# The Climate Solutions Map

*A census of climate solutions, their technical variations, and the companies implementing them. Data as of June 11, 2026.*

**4069 company entries** (3267 unique) · **63 solution areas** · **638 variations** · 7 sectors.

**Legend:** 🟢 mature · 🟡 scaling · 🟠 demonstration · 🔵 pilot · ⚪ lab — rated per variation. ⚠️/☠ = shut down or bankrupt (kept as data). *(audit add)* = added by verification pass.

---

## Does the claim hold? — "The solutions already exist, we just need to deploy faster"

**Verdict: Mostly true for the near term, misleading for the endgame.** For roughly the next decade, the claim is well supported. The IEA's 2023 Net Zero Roadmap update finds that ramping up renewables, efficiency, electrification and methane cuts with technologies *available today* delivers more than 80% of the emissions reductions needed by 2030 [2]. Project Drawdown's entire thesis is that the solutions "already exist" and need scaling, not invention [3]. But the claim quietly overreaches when stretched to 2050. The same IEA roadmap states that technologies not yet commercially available still account for about **35% of the cumulative reductions needed in 2050** — and that figure is the *good news*: in the 2021 edition it was "almost half" (~46–50%), at demonstration or prototype stage [1][2]. So the honest framing is: deployment is the binding constraint now; innovation remains decisive for the hard last third. Bill Gates / Breakthrough Energy push the opposite emphasis — that we lack cost-competitive tools for heavy industry, long-haul transport and removal, and must erase the "green premium" before deployment alone can finish the job [4]. The DOE Commercial Liftoff reports occupy the sensible middle: several key technologies (clean hydrogen, advanced nuclear, long-duration storage) are real but *pre-liftoff*, needing investment to scale from ~$40B to ~$300B/year by 2030 [5]. Both camps are right about different sectors.

| Sector | Constraint type | Key evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Power** | Deployment | Solar/wind/batteries are mature and cheapest-in-history. The world added ~600 GW of solar in 2024 and ~605 GW in 2025; battery storage hit a record 108 GW in 2025, up ~40% YoY [6][7]. The bottleneck is grid, not gear: >2,000 GW sits in US interconnection queues — twice the existing fleet — and only ~13% of requested capacity historically reaches operation [12]. |
| **Transport** | Both (deployment-led) | Light-duty EVs are commercial: 20.7M sold in 2025, >25% of new cars [8]. Charging buildout and grid are deployment problems. But aviation and shipping lack scaled solutions — sustainable fuels are ~0.1–1% of demand today and projected to reach only ~15% by 2030/2035; these are innovation-and-scale constrained [14]. |
| **Buildings** | Deployment (demand-signal-led) | Heat pumps are a mature technology, yet European sales *fell ~23% in 2024* after subsidy changes and cheap gas [9]. The hardware exists; the failure is policy stability, financing and consumer economics — pure deployment/demand barriers. |
| **Industry** | Both (innovation-led) | Green steel exists at pilot scale (HYBRIT, H2-DRI) but abatement runs ~$500/t CO₂ via hydrogen vs ~$70/t with CCS retrofits, needing $300/t tax credits to deploy [10]. Cement clinker substitutes, high-temperature heat and many chemical processes are not yet commercial. This is where Gates' innovation-gap argument is strongest [4]. |
| **Food & land** | Both | Land-use, diet-shift and food-waste solutions exist and are deployment/behaviour-constrained [3]. Enteric methane inhibitors (e.g., 3-NOP/Bovaer) are entering early commercial use with subsidy support [13], but vaccines, breeding and scaled alternative proteins remain in R&D — a mixed picture. |
| **Carbon removal** | Innovation/scale | The clearest innovation gap. ~19 operating DAC plants capture ~0.01 Mt CO₂/yr against an IEA need of ~1,000 Mt/yr by 2050, at $400–1,000/tonne [11]. The technology works but is nowhere near commercial scale or cost. "Deploy faster" is not yet a coherent instruction here. |

**Reading the table:** Power and light-duty transport — the largest near-term wedges — are genuinely deployment-bound, which is why the headline claim survives for 2030. Buildings and food are a mix of mature tech blocked by weak demand signals and genuinely immature options. Industry and carbon removal are where "just deploy" breaks down: the commercial product does not yet exist at the right cost, and the IEA's residual ~35% lives largely here [2][5]. The claim is therefore directionally honest but rhetorically convenient — it lets the listener skip the hardest 35%.

### What "deploying faster" actually requires

Even where the tech exists, "faster" is not free. The real constraints:

- **Permitting reform** — siting and environmental review routinely outlast the technology timeline for transmission, wind and DAC; this is now the dominant delay in the US and EU.
- **Grid interconnection** — >2,000 GW queued in the US, with median wait times now exceeding four years; without transmission and queue reform, built panels and turbines sit idle [12].
- **Finance** — high interest rates, tariff and policy uncertainty drove a record 112 GW of solar/storage *withdrawals* from US queues in 2024 [12]; DOE puts the liftoff financing gap at hundreds of billions per year [5].
- **Supply chains** — transformers, grid equipment, critical minerals and skilled labour are emerging chokepoints even as module costs fall.
- **Demand signals** — the heat-pump collapse shows mature tech stalls without stable subsidies, carbon pricing or mandates [9]; demand creation (e.g., green-steel procurement) is what pulls pre-liftoff industrial tech across the line.

**Bottom line:** Reframe the slogan as *"For most of this decade's emissions, deployment is the binding constraint — and even that requires fixing permitting, grids, finance and demand. For the last third of the job, especially heavy industry and removal, we still need innovation to make deployment possible."* That is both more accurate and more actionable than the original claim.

## Clean Energy Supply

How we make and move zero-carbon electricity: every generation source, every storage chemistry and form factor, and the grid hardware that connects them. Solar, wind, and lithium batteries are the mature deployment engine of the whole transition; advanced nuclear, fusion, next-gen geothermal, and long-duration storage are the frontier.

*9 solution areas · 84 variations · 574 company entries (515 unique companies; 28 marked dead, 18 acquired, 34 unverified)*

**Maturity at a glance (variations per stage):** Solar (3 mature, 4 scaling, 4 demonstration, 1 pilot) · Wind — All wind electricity generation format... (3 mature, 1 scaling, 1 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Geothermal (2 mature, 1 scaling, 2 demonstration, 3 pilot) · Hydro & Marine Energy (1 mature, 1 scaling, 4 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Nuclear Fission (1 mature, 1 scaling, 4 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Fusion — all confinement approaches plus fusi... (1 scaling, 2 demonstration, 7 lab) · Electrochemical Storage (2 mature, 1 scaling, 6 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Thermal & Mechanical Long-Duration Storage (2 mature, 3 scaling, 3 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Grid & Transmission Hardware (3 mature, 6 scaling, 1 demonstration)

#### Verification audit notes

Status corrections/nuances found by the audit pass:
- **SkySails Power** — Census lists 'operating' with official start of sales; in fact filed for insolvency Dec 9, 2025 (Hamburg District Court, provisional administrator Tjark Thies, ~120 employees) after a failed financing round. Operations continuing while it seeks rescue investors; status should be distressed/uncertain, not clean operating. ([evidence](https://deutschlandinenglish.com/p/skysails-power-gmbh-files-for-insolvency-amid-financial-challenges))
- **AW-Energy** — Census lists 'operating' with USD 19.1M 2024 revenue; the company filed for bankruptcy (~2025) and is now marked inactive/'deadpooled' by PitchBook, Tracxn and CB Insights. Status should be bankrupt-shutdown — a major correction since it was the longest-running wave-energy player with real revenue. ([evidence](https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/are-thiel-funded-floating-data-centers-enough-to-make-wave-energy-pencil/ (also https://tracxn.com/d/companies/awenergy/__wbtjMrsggUKjOpPiITiZk4F_rab1yP39CB6W4zh6tDw)))
- **EnerVenue** — Operating status correct, but the signal 'Kentucky gigafactory built' is misleading: EnerVenue vacated/abandoned the Kentucky plant in Nov 2024 without ramping (site taken over by Canadian Solar) and moved all high-volume manufacturing to Changzhou, China — which creates FEOC/domestic-content exposure worth noting alongside the $300M Series B. ([evidence](https://www.energy-storage.news/canadian-solar-to-manufacture-bess-and-cells-at-kentucky-plant-after-enervenue-backs-out/))
- **Aptera Motors** — Needs update and nuance: no longer purely pre-production — first vehicle came off its low-volume validation line Mar 3, 2026, with first customer deliveries targeted late 2026. But Q1 2026 10-Q discloses ~$17.7M cash vs $1.7-2.0M/month burn, management states cash is insufficient for the next 12 months, and it needs another $45-50M for low-volume production ($140-160M for high volume). Operating but with explicit going-concern risk. ([evidence](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/SEV/10-q-aptera-motors-corp-quarterly-earnings-report-c9afe8127b02.html))
- **ESS Tech (ESS Inc.)** — 'Uncertain' status remains apt but the evidence is stale: as of May-June 2026 ESS is still operating after a ~$31M financing injection, reported Q2 2025 revenue up 578% YoY, won a $9.9M USAF/CTC contract, and acquired insolvent German rival VoltStorage's IP — yet going-concern doubt persists and it says it needs additional debt/equity. ([evidence](https://www.energy-storage.news/flow-battery-startup-ess-tech-inc-looks-to-acquisitions-big-name-us-partnerships-for-hope-in-future-profitability/))
- **AgriSolar** — Census flags 'uncertain' — verification supports going further: no primary evidence the company exists (no website, press release, or independent coverage found); the $15M Series A claim traces only to the same Market Research Future agrivoltaics report. Likely a market-report artifact; recommend removing or annotating as unverifiable. ([evidence](https://www.marketresearchfuture.com/reports/agrivoltaics-market-33648 (sole circulating source; no corroboration found)))

Notable omissions the audit flagged (not yet incorporated into tables):
- *Solar / Utility-scale crystalline silicon PV*: JA Solar and Canadian Solar — two of the global top-5 module suppliers (Canadian Solar also a top-10 BESS integrator via e-STORAGE); their absence from the module-maker roster is the most obvious gap a PV analyst would catch.
- *Solar (missing variation): upstream polysilicon/ingot/wafer supply chain*: Tongwei (world's largest cell/polysilicon maker), GCL Technology, Daqo, Wacker, Hemlock — the census covers no upstream at all, even though polysilicon/wafer is where Chinese concentration risk and the 2024-25 price collapse live (and where REC Silicon's US restart just failed).
- *Solar / distributed & utility-scale (missing variation): PV inverters & power conversion*: Huawei — the world's No. 1 inverter supplier by shipments — appears nowhere; Sungrow appears only via floating/BESS arms. Inverters/PCS are the decisive electrical BOS layer and a census of solar supply without the Huawei-Sungrow duopoly is visibly incomplete.
- *Wind (missing variation): blade & drivetrain component manufacturing*: TPI Composites — world's largest independent wind-blade maker, Chapter 11 Aug 2025 (Türkiye plants sold, Vestas stalking-horse for the rest) — plus LM Wind Power (GE) and gearbox makers (ZF/Winergy). The census covers OEMs and blade recycling but skips the component tier whose distress defined 2024-25 wind economics.
- *Electrochemical Storage / Lithium-ion grid BESS*: EVE Energy (top-2 global ESS cell supplier), HyperStrong (China's No. 1 and a global top-3 BESS integrator), and Wärtsilä ES&O (leading Western integrator alongside Fluence) — all bigger players than several names listed.
- *Electrochemical Storage (missing variation): battery recycling & materials circularity*: Redwood Materials, Li-Cycle (CCAA May 2025, acquired by Glencore Aug 2025), Ascend Elements, Cirba Solutions — census covers PV recycling, blade recycling and second-life packs but not cell recycling, the largest circularity industry in the sector.
- *Nuclear Fission / Large light-water reactors*: Framatome (EPR co-builder and one of the West's two major fuel/reactor-services firms) and AtkinsRéalis/CANDU Energy (only heavy-water reactor vendor; Candu Monark, Cernavoda units, and the global CANDU refurbishment franchise) are both absent.
- *Nuclear Fission / Fuel cycle & enrichment*: Kazatomprom — the world's largest uranium producer (~20%+ of mined supply); listing Cameco alone hides where front-end supply concentration actually sits.
- *Thermal & Mechanical LDES / High-temperature thermal batteries*: Hyme Energy (Denmark, Seaborg spin-out) — molten hydroxide salt heat storage with industrial pilots (Esbjerg/Bornholm); one of the few credible European molten-salt thermal startups and a natural peer to Kyoto Group/Malta.
- *Fusion / Fusion supply chain (tritium handling)*: Marathon Fusion (San Francisco; tritium fuel-processing/pumping components, venture-funded 2024-25) — directly relevant because the variation's white-space claims tritium handling has 'almost no independent players.'

### Solar

**Utility-scale crystalline silicon PV (TOPCon, HJT, back-contact) incl. trackers & BOS** · `🟢 mature`

Gigawatt-scale fields of advanced n-type silicon modules (TOPCon, heterojunction, back-contact) on single-axis trackers with balance-of-system hardware; it is the workhorse of decarbonization and the cheapest bulk electricity in most of the world.

**Thin-film PV (CdTe, CIGS, amorphous silicon)** · `🟢 mature`

Deposits micron-thin semiconductor layers (cadmium telluride or copper-indium-gallium-selenide) directly onto glass or flexible foil, enabling high-throughput, low-cost manufacturing outside the Chinese silicon supply chain and good hot-climate performance.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

**Emerging PV materials (organic, quantum dot, dye-sensitized, kesterite)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Printable carbon-based semiconductors, quantum dots and earth-abundant compounds make ultralight, flexible, colored or indoor-optimized solar, unlocking surfaces and supply chains that rigid silicon cannot serve.

> **White space:** Kesterite (CZTS) has essentially zero commercial players — defect chemistry caps lab efficiency near ~15%, so it survives only as an earth-abundant research bet (e.g., as an indium-free tandem partner); broadly, emerging materials win where weight, flexibility, aesthetics or indoor light matter, not on $/W against silicon, leaving an opening for application-specific products with consumer/IoT margins.

**Agrivoltaics** · `🟡 scaling`

Co-locates elevated, vertical or dynamically tracking solar panels with crops or grazing so land produces food and power simultaneously, easing land-use conflict and often improving crop resilience to heat and drought.

Mounts PV on floats over reservoirs, hydropower dams and increasingly the open sea, saving land, cutting evaporation, and piggybacking on existing grid connections — with offshore variants now co-locating inside wind farms.

**Concentrated solar power (power tower, parabolic trough, linear Fresnel, dish)** · `🟡 scaling`

Mirrors concentrate sunlight to heat a fluid (molten salt, sodium, steam) that drives a turbine, with hours of cheap thermal storage built in — solar that can deliver firm, dispatchable power after sunset.

**Concentrator PV (CPV)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Lenses or mirrors focus sunlight hundreds of times onto tiny ultra-high-efficiency multijunction cells; it only pencils out where the concentrated waste heat is also captured and sold, or in high-DNI niches.

| [RayGen](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/press-releases/raygen-completes-127-million-series-d-investment-round/) | scaleup | Tower-mounted 'PV Ultra' receivers (multijunction cells at ~1000 suns) whose co-captured heat feeds water-based 17-hour 'thermal hydro' storage — the only CPV player scaling today. | A$127M Series D (Apr 2025: SLB, Quanta Services, Oxy, Breakthrough Victoria); 4 MW + 2.8 MW/17h plant operating at Carwarp; 150 MW Yadnarie project in development |
| [Saint-Augustin Canada Electric (STACE)](https://stace.ca/) | incumbent | Quebec industrial group that absorbed Soitec's CPV module technology and lines; current CPV activity appears minimal. | Acquired Soitec CPV assets (2016); little public CPV deployment since · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Classic dual-axis CPV died a decade ago (Soitec exit, Amonix/SunPower C7 shutdowns) because flat silicon got too cheap and CPV cannot use diffuse light; the only opening left is hybrid electric+thermal concentration that monetizes heat for long-duration storage or industrial use (RayGen's model), or multijunction cells for space.

**Space-based solar power** · `🔵 pilot`

Collects solar energy in orbit, where sunlight is constant and stronger, and beams it to Earth (or to other spacecraft) via laser or microwave — potentially baseload solar, if launch costs and beaming efficiency cooperate.

| [Aetherflux](https://techcrunch.com/2025/04/02/space-solar-startup-aetherflux-raises-50m-to-launch-first-space-demo-in-2026/) | startup | Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt's LEO constellation beaming power by infrared laser to small ground stations; first commercial-track orbital demo. | $50M Series A Apr 2025 (Index, Interlagos, a16z, BEV, NEA; $60M total) plus US DoD OECIF funding; Mission 1 demo targeted 2026 |
| [Virtus Solis](https://payloadspace.com/four-startups-race-to-make-space-based-power-a-reality/) | startup | Michigan startup designing robotically assembled km-scale arrays in high orbits with microwave power beaming. | Mostly grant-funded to date; in-space power demo planned 2027 with Orbital Composites |
| [Space Solar](https://payloadspace.com/four-startups-race-to-make-space-based-power-a-reality/) | startup | UK company developing the CASSIOPeiA helical satellite with 360-degree beam steering, targeting grid-scale delivery (first markets incl. Iceland) in the early 2030s. | UK government-backed; partnership with Transition Labs/Reykjavik Energy targeting 30 MW ~2030 |
| [Star Catcher Industries](https://payloadspace.com/four-startups-race-to-make-space-based-power-a-reality/) | startup | Building a space-to-space power grid that beams concentrated solar energy to other satellites rather than to Earth. | $12.25M seed (2024); beaming demos underway |
| [Reflect Orbital](https://www.reflectorbital.com/) | startup | Orbital mirror constellation that reflects sunlight onto terrestrial solar farms after dusk — adjacent route to 'solar at night' without beaming. | Series A raised 2025 (Lux Capital-led); first mirror satellite planned 2026 |

> **White space:** No one has delivered commercial power from orbit — the physics works (Caltech's 2023 MAPLE demo) but launch mass, thermal management and end-to-end beaming efficiency (<20%) keep $/MWh far above terrestrial solar+storage; near-term openings are defense, disaster relief and powering other satellites, with terrestrial baseload a 2030s bet riding on Starship-class launch costs.

### Wind — All wind electricity generation formats plus wind-asset life extension and circularity (Clean Energy Supply)

**Onshore utility-scale turbines** · `🟢 mature`

Large three-blade horizontal-axis turbines (3-8+ MW) on land farms convert bulk wind into grid electricity and are among the cheapest sources of new generation worldwide; ~117 GW was installed globally in 2025 alone.

**Fixed-bottom offshore wind (incl. foundations & installation tech)** · `🟢 mature`

Turbines of 11-20 MW mounted on monopile or jacket foundations in waters under ~60 m capture stronger, steadier sea winds; a specialized chain of foundation fabricators and jack-up installation vessels is as decisive as the turbines themselves.

**Floating offshore wind platforms & mooring systems** · `🟠 demonstration`

Turbines mounted on moored buoyant platforms (spar, semi-submersible, barge, TLP) unlock deep-water sites (>60 m) that hold most of the offshore wind resource near Japan, Korea, California and the Mediterranean; cost is still ~2-3x fixed-bottom.

> **White space:** Many platform designers but almost no commercial-scale buyers yet: LCOE is still ~2-3x fixed-bottom and ports, dynamic cables, moorings and serial fabrication are the bottleneck — the EUR 126M bet on BW Ideol's foundation factory shows the opening is industrialized floater/mooring manufacturing and anchor/mooring supply chains rather than yet another platform geometry.

**Airborne wind energy (kites, tethered drones)** · `🔵 pilot`

Tethered kites, rigid wings or drone-craft harvest the stronger, steadier winds at 200-800 m altitude using ~90% less material than a tower turbine, generating power via a ground winch (yo-yo cycle) or onboard rotors — attractive for off-grid, island and mobile uses.

> **White space:** The field consolidated from ~22 players (2017) to ~8 after Makani and Ampyx proved utility-scale AWE needs hundreds of millions that single-digit-MW unit economics cannot yet justify; the credible near-term opening is 100-500 kW mobile/off-grid systems competing with diesel on islands, mines and defense sites, with autonomy and tether reliability as the gating technologies.

Turbines from sub-kW micro units to ~100 kW serve homes, farms, telecom towers and buildings on-site — valuable where grid power is expensive or absent — though cheap solar has pushed the segment into off-grid and hybrid niches.

**Vertical-axis & novel rotor designs (incl. bladeless/oscillating)** · `🔵 pilot`

Alternative architectures — vertical-axis rotors, bladeless oscillating masts, track-mounted wings, multi- and single-rotor floaters — trade the mature three-blade format for lower height, lower center of gravity, denser packing or cheaper manufacture.

### Geothermal

**Conventional hydrothermal (dry steam, flash, binary ORC)** · `🟢 mature`

Taps naturally occurring underground reservoirs of steam or hot water and runs them through steam turbines or, for cooler resources, binary organic Rankine cycle (ORC) units — the workhorse supplying roughly 16-17 GW of always-on power globally, but limited to sites with natural hydrothermal resources.

**Enhanced geothermal systems (EGS)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Creates artificial reservoirs by drilling into hot dry rock and hydraulically fracturing it with shale-oilfield tools, letting geothermal work far beyond natural hot springs; Fervo's plants and DOE's Utah FORGE testbed have cut drilling times and costs sharply since 2023, making EGS the highest-momentum next-gen pathway.

Southern California Edison |

| [Chevron New Energies](https://www.chevron.com/newsroom/2022/q4/chevron-and-baseload-capital-create-joint-venture-to-explore-geothermal-development-opportunities) | incumbent | Oil supermajor bringing subsurface, drilling, and completions competencies to next-gen geothermal via a US development JV with Baseload Capital, starting at Weepah Hills, Nevada. | JV formed Dec 2022; advancing pilot-to-commercial pathway for novel geothermal in Esmeralda County, NV |

> **White space:** Despite Fervo's proof points there are almost no credible EGS fast-followers — project capex (~$1B+ for 500 MW), long permitting, and induced-seismicity management keep entry barriers high while DOE's FORGE absorbs much of the R&D; openings exist for international EGS developers (Europe, Japan, Latin America), oilfield-service firms productizing stimulation-as-a-service, and east-of-Rockies sedimentary EGS plays.

**Closed-loop / advanced geothermal systems (AGS)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Circulates a working fluid through sealed deep wellbores that gather heat by conduction alone — no fracking, no water consumption, and siting almost anywhere — but the physics of conduction-limited heat transfer means economics hinge on drilling very long laterals very cheaply.

| [Eavor Technologies](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/12/04/3200069/0/en/Eavor-Technologies-Achieves-First-Electricity-Production-at-Geretsried-Site.html) | scaleup | Canadian inventor of the multilateral 'Eavor-Loop'; its Geretsried, Germany plant delivered the world's first grid electricity from a fully closed-loop system in December 2025 (target 8.2 MWe + 64 MWth from four loops). | First grid power Dec 4, 2025 (initial ~0.5 MW, second loop drilling 2026); €91.6M EU Innovation Fund grant; backed by BP, Chevron, OMV and Canada Growth Fund; follow-on heat projects incl. Hannover |
| [XGS Energy](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250612778008/en/XGS-Energy-and-Meta-to-Partner-on-150-MW-Advanced-Geothermal-Project) | startup | Water-free conductive closed-loop design using a proprietary thermally conductive grout around steel casing, suited to arid regions. | 150 MW project agreement with Meta in New Mexico (June 2025; first ~5 MW by 2027, full by 2030); Baker Hughes development partnership (Mar 2026); >$40M raised |
| [GreenFire Energy](https://www.greenfireenergy.com/series-a-financing/) | startup | GreenLoop coaxial closed-loop retrofits that revive idle, dry, or underperforming geothermal wells rather than drilling new ones. | Series A led by Baker Hughes with Helmerich & Payne and Vallourec; building closed-loop test capability at Baker Hughes' Oklahoma facility (Wells2Watts consortium) |

> **White space:** Only ~3 funded players because conduction-limited heat extraction caps per-well output and analysts question scalability versus EGS; the opening is for radical drilling-cost reduction (longer/cheaper laterals), hybrid conduction-convection designs, and closed-loop retrofit services for the thousands of existing underperforming geothermal and oil wells.

**Superhot rock geothermal** · `🔵 pilot`

Targets rock above ~374°C where water becomes supercritical and each well can deliver 5-10x the power of a conventional well, potentially making geothermal cost-competitive almost anywhere on Earth — but drilling, casing, and downhole electronics at those temperatures are still unproven.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Mazama Energy](https://www.opb.org/article/2025/10/06/super-hot-rocks-geothermal-technology-renewable-energy-three-rivers-mazama/) | startup | Founded out of AltaRock and Blade Energy Partners to drill superhot (>374°C) enhanced geothermal wells on the flank of Oregon's Newberry Volcano, with up to 200 MW site potential. | $20M DOE superhot rock demonstration grant (Nov 2024); drilled the hottest EGS pilot to date at Newberry in 2025 with three national labs |
| [Quaise Energy](https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/07/22/1120545/geothermal-drilling-quaise/) | startup | MIT spinout using gyrotron-powered millimeter-wave energy to vaporize rock, aiming to reach 500°C rock at depths conventional bits cannot touch. | First open-field millimeter-wave drilling (100 m, central Texas, 2025); $21M Series A1; seeking ~$200M (incl. $100M Series B) for a 50 MW Oregon plant by 2030 |
| [Hephae Energy Technology](https://www.thinkgeoenergy.com/hephae-energy-raises-4-million-funding-to-support-field-trials-of-high-t-drilling-technology/) | startup | Builds the missing high-temperature downhole toolchain — its Pandora 210 measurement-while-drilling system is rated to 210°C with a roadmap to 300°C by 2030. | $4M round led by Underground Ventures with Nabors, Future Ventures, and Grantham Foundation; first tool in the ground in 2025 |

> **White space:** Nobody has produced commercial power from supercritical wells: Iceland's IDDP wells hit magma and corrosive superheated steam, ST1's 6+ km Finnish wells found uneconomic flow, and casing/cement/electronics above 400°C remain the binding constraint — so the nearest-term opening is high-temperature well hardware and instrumentation (Hephae is nearly alone) and government-backed demonstration programs rather than full-stack plant developers.

**Advanced drilling & exploration tech (millimeter-wave, plasma, AI prospecting)** · `🔵 pilot`

New drilling physics (millimeter-wave, plasma), high-temperature tools, and AI-driven subsurface prospecting attack the two biggest geothermal cost drivers — drilling (roughly half of deep-project capex) and exploration dry-hole risk — to unlock resources that are invisible or uneconomic today.

**Oilfield co-produced, geopressured & sedimentary-basin geothermal** · `🔵 pilot`

Reuses oil and gas wells, hot produced water, and deep pressurized sedimentary formations to generate power or heat with standard oilfield rigs and crews — leveraging millions of existing wellbores (an estimated ~40 GW US co-production potential) and Gulf Coast geopressured resources proven but never commercialized in the 1990s.

**Geothermal district heating & direct use** · `🟢 mature`

Pipes hot water from wells directly into city heating networks, greenhouses, aquaculture, and industry — the oldest and cheapest use of geothermal, dominant in Iceland and the Paris Basin and now scaling fastest in China and Denmark as a gas-heating replacement.

### Hydro & Marine Energy

**Conventional & run-of-river hydropower (incl. modernization/uprating)** · `🟢 mature`

Flowing river water, impounded behind dams or diverted run-of-river, spins turbines; at roughly 1,400 GW installed it is the world's largest renewable electricity source, and re-powering 50+ year-old fleets adds clean capacity and grid flexibility without building new dams.

**Small & modular hydro (low-head, fish-safe turbines)** · `🟡 scaling`

Compact, standardized turbines — including fish-safe runners, submersible units and vortex/screw designs — extract power from low dams, locks, weirs and conduits, unlocking the tens of GW sitting at existing non-powered dams without new impoundments.

> **White space:** Per-kW costs and site-specific civil works keep small hydro above solar+storage in most markets; the opening is standardization plus retrofit of the ~90,000 US non-powered dams under streamlined FERC licensing, where fish-safe turbines (Natel) collapse the cost of environmental compliance.

**Hydrokinetic river & canal turbines** · `🟠 demonstration`

Submerged turbines harvest kinetic energy from free-flowing rivers and irrigation canals with no dam at all; output per unit is small but highly predictable, making it ideal for displacing diesel in remote communities and monetizing existing canal infrastructure.

> **White space:** Slow rivers carry little extractable energy density and debris/ice drive O&M costs, so per-kWh economics lose to solar+storage almost everywhere; the credible wedges are Arctic and remote diesel-dependent communities (ORPC's niche, with diesel at $0.50+/kWh) and irrigation canals where interconnection, water rights and civil works already exist (Emrgy's niche) — two startups effectively own these openings today.

**Tidal stream turbines (seabed, floating, kite)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Underwater turbines — bottom-mounted, hung from floating platforms, or flown on subsea kites — convert fast, astronomically predictable tidal currents into electricity, providing forecastable renewable power that complements variable wind and solar.

**Tidal range, barrages & lagoons** · `🟠 demonstration`

Dams or artificial lagoons across high-tide-range estuaries impound seawater and release it through bulb turbines, delivering utility-scale, century-lifetime, perfectly predictable generation — at multi-billion upfront cost and with estuarine ecosystem impacts.

| [K-water (Korea Water Resources Corp)](https://www.ice.org.uk/news-views-insights/inside-infrastructure/tidal-power) | incumbent | Operates the 254 MW Sihwa Lake plant (2011), the world's largest tidal power station, built into an existing seawall. | One of only two large tidal range plants operating worldwide; piggybacked on existing infrastructure to manage cost. |

> **White space:** The resource is enormous and perfectly predictable (the Severn alone could supply ~7% of UK electricity), but no private balance sheet can carry multi-billion, 120-year assets with 20+ year paybacks plus habitats-directive litigation — which is why only two large plants exist and the lone venture-backed attempt (Swansea) died. The Severn Estuary Commission (March 2025) recommended a government-enabled demonstration lagoon over any barrage; the opening is for sovereign/pension capital and EPC consortia under regulated-asset-base style financing, not startups.

**Wave energy converters (point absorber, OWC, attenuator, overtopping)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Devices spanning point absorbers, oscillating water columns, hinged flaps/attenuators and overtopping designs convert wave motion into electricity; the global resource is vast and winter-peaking, complementing solar, but survivability in storms has historically destroyed both devices and companies.

**Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC)** · `🔵 pilot`

Exploits the 20-25°C temperature difference between warm tropical surface water and 4°C deep ocean water to run a closed Rankine cycle around the clock — thermodynamically inefficient but tapping an enormous baseload resource best matched to island grids paying diesel prices.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Makai Ocean Engineering](https://www.makai.com/renewable-energy/otec/) | incumbent | Hawaii engineering firm with 40+ years in OTEC; operates one of the world's only grid-connected OTEC plants (105 kW at NELHA) and builds Thin-Foil Heat Exchangers attacking OTEC's largest cost component. | 2025 MoU to integrate its TFHX into Global OTEC's modular 500 kW Power Module scalable to 50 MW. |
| [Global OTEC](https://globalotec.co/global-otec-and-makai-ocean-engineering-sign-mou-for-heat-exchanger-technology/) | startup | UK startup commercializing floating OTEC barges for island states — the 1.5 MW 'Dominique' for São Tomé and Príncipe, upscalable to 10 MW. | Lloyd's Register Approval in Principle; UNIDO-supported ESIA underway; Horizon Europe/UKRI-funded PLOTEC storm-resilient platform; Makai heat-exchanger partnership (2025). |
| [Bluerise](https://www.rechargenews.com/technology/otec-start-up-snapped-up-by-swiss-offshore-contractor-allseas/2-1-635687) | startup | Dutch OTEC and seawater air-conditioning pioneer (Curaçao projects) spun out of TU Delft. | Acquired by offshore contractor Allseas (2019), which absorbed the technology to develop OTEC at offshore-industry scale. · **acquired** |
| [Ocean Thermal Energy Corporation (OTE)](https://environment.sciencearray.com/ocean-thermal-energy-conversion-otec-clean-power) | startup | Long-running US developer of OTEC and SWAC projects (Bahamas resorts), publicly framing the sector's 'Innovation Valley of Death.' | States a first 5-10 MW plant needs $200-300M that no one has funded; little visible project construction. · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Physics caps OTEC at ~3-4% thermal efficiency from a ~22°C delta, so gigantic water flows, kilometer-scale cold-water pipes and heat-exchanger area dominate cost — no plant above 1 MW has ever run, and the $200-300M first commercial unit has no natural funder. The opening: small island states burning diesel at $0.25-0.40/kWh, with desalination and seawater air-conditioning co-products, plus defense interest in island bases; a verified heat-exchanger/cold-pipe cost breakthrough (e.g., Makai's TFHX in Global OTEC's barge) is the unlock, leaving the field to essentially two credible players.

**Salinity-gradient / osmotic power** · `🔵 pilot`

Mixing fresh and salt water releases free energy ('blue energy') that membranes capture via reverse electrodialysis or pressure-retarded osmosis at estuaries, salt caverns and desalination outfalls — a 24/7, weather-independent resource estimated in the thousands of TWh per year.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Sweetch Energy](https://www.aquatechtrade.com/news/water-treatment/osmotic-energy-sweetch-25-million-investment) | startup | French CNRS spin-off whose INOD nanofluidic electrodes/membranes deliver order-of-magnitude higher power density for reverse electrodialysis at river mouths. | ~€50M raised (Crédit Mutuel Impact, EDF Pulse, CNR, EIC); OsmoRhône 1 pilot operating at the Rhône delta with CNR since end-2024; WEF Technology Pioneer 2025; targets ~500 MW Rhône potential. |
| [SaltPower](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/954045) | startup | Danish company running pressure-retarded osmosis on saturated salt-cavern brine, whose extreme gradient (10x seawater) sidesteps the power-density problem that killed estuary PRO. | ~100 kW commercial unit operating at a Nobian salt site; EU Horizon 2020 scale-up project; founded 2015. |
| [REDstack](https://www.dutchwatersector.com/news/redstack-nears-first-green-hydrogen-production-at-its-salt-fresh-water-blue-energy-plant) | startup | Dutch reverse-electrodialysis developer operating the 'Blue Energy' pilot on the Afsluitdijk mixing Wadden Sea and IJsselmeer water since 2014. | ~€5M Waddenfonds grant for scale-up; exploring green hydrogen co-production at the plant. |
| [Statkraft](https://earth.org/osmotic-power-the-next-wave-of-renewable-energy/) | incumbent | Built the world's first pressure-retarded-osmosis prototype plant (Tofte, Norway, 2009) — then shut the program down circa 2013-14 when membrane power density made costs hopeless. | The sector's defining cautionary tale: an incumbent with cheap capital exited because membranes delivered ~1 W/m² against a ~5 W/m² breakeven. |

> **White space:** Classical membranes produce under 1-3 W/m² versus a ~5 W/m² economic threshold — that physics killed Statkraft's pioneer plant and kept the field empty for a decade. New nanomaterial electrodes (Sweetch) and extreme-gradient siting (SaltPower's saturated brines) reopen it; the white space is co-location with desalination outfalls and salt/chlor-alkali industries where the gradient is free and water pretreatment already exists — only ~3 credible companies worldwide are pursuing a resource theoretically worth a fifth of global electricity.

### Nuclear Fission

**Large light-water reactors (GW-scale new build & restarts)** · `🟢 mature`

Conventional gigawatt-class pressurized/boiling-water reactors (AP1000, EPR, APR1400, VVER, Hualong One) that split uranium to raise steam at grid scale, plus the new business of restarting recently retired US plants — the workhorse supplying ~9% of world electricity and most of its firm carbon-free power.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Westinghouse Electric Company](https://www.klgates.com/US-Government-Announces-Historic-80-Billion-Nuclear-Partnership-with-Westinghouse-Electric-Company-Cameco-Corporation-and-Brookfield-Asset-Management-to-Construct-AP1000-Reactor-Fleet-10-30-2025) | incumbent | OEM of the AP1000, the only Gen III+ design recently completed in the US (Vogtle 3&4); leading a new US large-reactor build wave. | $80B partnership with US government/Brookfield/Cameco (Oct 2025) targeting 10 new AP1000s under construction by 2030; export pipeline in Poland, Bulgaria, Ukraine. |
| [EDF](https://www.ans.org/news/article-7625/flamanville3-reaches-full-power/) | incumbent | Builds and operates the 1,650 MWe EPR; runs the French fleet and the UK's two flagship new-build projects. | Flamanville-3 EPR reached full power in 2025; Hinkley Point C under construction; Sizewell C (2 EPRs, >$30B) approved with UK government backing in 2025; EPR2 domestic program launched. |
| [KHNP (Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power)](https://www.powermag.com/three-nuclear-giants-will-vie-for-czech-republics-dukovany-expansion/) | incumbent | Exports the APR1400 with a track record of roughly on-time delivery (UAE Barakah 4-unit plant). | Signed ~$18B contract in mid-2025 for two new units at Czech Dukovany, beating EDF and Westinghouse; Korea restarting domestic new build. |

| [Holtec International](https://www.energy.gov/edf/holtec-palisades) | incumbent | Executing the first-ever restart of a fully retired US nuclear plant — the 800 MW Palisades PWR in Michigan. | $1.52B DOE loan guarantee closed; reactor returned to operating temperature/pressure late 2025 with grid return in early 2026 — first recommissioning in US history. |

**Light-water small modular reactors (SMRs)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Shrunken, factory-built versions of proven water-cooled reactors (roughly 30-470 MWe) that trade economies of scale for series manufacturing, simpler passive safety, easier siting and smaller per-project capital risk.

Helium-cooled reactors fueled with meltdown-tolerant TRISO particle fuel (pebbles or prisms) that run at 565-750°C, opening industrial process-heat and steam markets that water-cooled reactors physically cannot serve.

> **White space:** Only China operates a commercial HTGR, and two Western players (USNC, U-Battery) died in 2023-24 — high-temperature materials and TRISO fuel cost have outrun venture timelines; the opening is decarbonized industrial steam (500-600°C for chemicals/refining) that LWRs can't reach, now de-risked by the rebuilding US TRISO supply chain.

**Molten salt reactors (incl. thorium fuel cycles)** · `🔵 pilot`

Reactors cooled — or directly fueled — by molten fluoride/chloride salts at near-atmospheric pressure, including thorium breeding cycles, promising walk-away safety, high-temperature output and eventual waste burning, but still proving salt chemistry and fuel qualification at small scale.

Liquid-metal-cooled reactors with fast neutron spectra that extract dramatically more energy from uranium and can burn plutonium and nuclear waste; the flagship US advanced build (Natrium) pairs one with molten-salt thermal storage so output can flex around renewables.

**Fuel cycle & enrichment (HALEU, TRISO, fabrication)** · `🟡 scaling`

The mining-to-fabrication supply chain — especially uranium enrichment and the HALEU (10-20% enriched) and TRISO particle fuels that advanced reactors require — being urgently rebuilt in the West after the 2024 US ban on Russian uranium imports.

**Waste disposal & recycling** · `🟠 demonstration`

Engineered disposal of spent fuel (deep geological repositories, deep boreholes, dry-cask interim storage) and chemical recycling that recovers the ~95% of energy still in used fuel — the unsolved back end that gates public acceptance and now doubles as a domestic HALEU feedstock source.

Estonia) and IAEA engagement. |

> **White space:** Disposal is a government-monopoly market where the US has had no repository path since Yucca Mountain stalled, and recycling has historically lost to cheap fresh uranium plus proliferation concerns; the opening is recycling reframed as HALEU feedstock and waste-liability relief (Oklo/Curio model), plus borehole disposal for countries too small to afford a mined repository.

### Fusion — all confinement approaches plus fusion-specific supply chain (sector: Clean Energy Supply)

**Tokamaks (high-field HTS, spherical, conventional)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Donut-shaped magnetic bottles — the most-studied fusion configuration — confine 100-million-degree plasma, and new high-temperature-superconductor (HTS) magnets shrink the machines dramatically, turning ITER-scale physics into venture-fundable power plants.

| [Tokamak Energy](https://tokamakenergy.com/2024/11/20/tokamak-energy-raises-125m-to-commercialise-transformative-fusion-and-magnet-technologies/) | scaleup | UK spherical-tokamak pioneer; its ST40 was the first private machine to hit 100M °C ion temperature, and its TE Magnetics division sells HTS magnet systems into other markets. | $125M round Nov 2024 (East X, Lingotto, Furukawa Electric); $335M total since 2009; $52M ST40 upgrade with US DOE/UK government through 2026 |

**Stellarators** · `⚪ lab`

Twisted 3D magnet coils hold plasma in steady state without the driven current that causes tokamak disruptions, trading harder engineering for intrinsically stable always-on operation — the fastest-growing confinement race since Germany's W7-X validated the physics.

**Laser / inertial confinement fusion (ICF)** · `⚪ lab`

Banks of lasers implode peppercorn-sized fuel capsules to ignition — the only fusion approach with demonstrated net energy gain (NIF, December 2022) — with commercialization now hinging on high-repetition-rate lasers and cheap mass-produced targets.

**Magneto-inertial & magnetized target fusion (MTF/MIF)** · `⚪ lab`

A pre-magnetized plasma target is crushed to fusion conditions by liquid-metal liners, pulsed electromagnetic drivers, or converging plasma jets — a middle path needing far less driver power than lasers and far less magnet than tokamaks, but one whose milestone-or-die economics have already produced the sector's most visible financial distress.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [General Fusion](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/21/struggling-fusion-power-company-general-fusion-gets-22m-lifeline-from-investors/) | scaleup | Canadian MTF pioneer (Bezos-backed, founded 2002) compressing magnetized plasma with pistons and a liquid-lithium liner in its LM26 machine, chasing scientific breakeven. | Hit cash crisis May 2025 (~25% layoffs, open letter seeking $125M); rescued with $22M Aug 2025 + $51M SAFE Nov 2025 (Segra Capital, PenderFund); ~$440M+ lifetime funding |
| [Pacific Fusion](https://www.ans.org/news/article-6523/whats-different-about-pacific-fusions-pulsed-magnetic-concept/) | startup | Founded by NIF-ignition alumni and Eric Lander; uses ~150 impedance-matched Marx generator pulser modules to electromagnetically implode magnetized targets (scaled MagLIF), targeting net facility gain ~2030. | $900M committed Series A (out of stealth Nov 2024); 100+ consecutive pulser-module validation tests; $1B New Mexico R&D/manufacturing campus announced Sept 2025; General Atomics partnership |
| [Helicity Space](https://spacenews.com/lockheed-martin-ventures-invests-in-helicity-space/) | startup | Berkeley startup applying magneto-inertial fusion (merging helical plasma jets) to in-space propulsion rather than grid power, a niche where even modest gain is transformative. | ~$5M seed plus Lockheed Martin Ventures investment Apr 2024; four-plasma-gun Helicity Drive prototype testing |
| [HyperJet Fusion](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/227351-17) | startup | Chantilly, VA developer of plasma-jet-driven magneto-inertial fusion (spherical array of plasma guns imploding a target), ARPA-E ALPHA-funded; team and technology merged into NearStar Fusion. | ~$2M private + ARPA-E/DOE funding since 2017; absorbed by NearStar Fusion (PitchBook records merger/acquisition) · **acquired** |
| [Compact Fusion Systems](https://www.fusionenergybase.com/organization/compact-fusion-systems) | startup | Santa Fe startup designing liquid-metal-liner MTF power cores (50–500 MWe) for utilities; ARPA-E supported but with little public activity in recent years. | ARPA-E grant; minimal public news since — viability unclear as of mid-2026 · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** MTF promised the cheapest path (mechanical drivers, no giant lasers/magnets) yet General Fusion's 2025 near-collapse after 23 years shows the milestone-vs-runway squeeze; the opening is modern pulsed-power electronics (Pacific Fusion's pulser modules) and non-grid niches like propulsion, where smaller gain still sells.

**Field-reversed configuration (FRC, incl. pulsed)** · `🟠 demonstration`

A self-organized plasma 'smoke ring' confines itself with its own internal currents inside a simple linear machine, enabling either pulsed merging-and-compression with direct electricity recovery (Helion) or steady beam-driven operation aimed at aneutronic fuels (TAE).

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Helion Energy](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260604740624/en/Helion-Raises-$465-Million-Series-G-Funding-Round-to-Meet-Surging-Global-Demand-for-Power) | scaleup | Pulsed FRC machines that merge two plasmoids and recover electricity directly from the expanding magnetized plasma (no steam cycle), on a deuterium/helium-3 fuel path; building Orion, the world's first contracted commercial fusion plant, in Malaga, WA for Microsoft's 2028 PPA, plus a 500 MW Nucor deal. | $465M Series G June 2026; $425M Series F Jan 2025 ($5.4B valuation); Polaris became first private machine to demonstrate measurable D-T fusion (early 2026); Orion groundbreaking July 2025 |
| [TAE Technologies](https://tae.com/tae-technologies-raises-150-million-in-latest-funding-round/) | scaleup | Longest-running private fusion company (1998); sustains FRCs with neutral particle beams aiming ultimately at aneutronic proton-boron fuel; its 2025 'Norm' simplification cut machine size/cost up to 50%, feeding the Copernicus net-energy-capability machine and Da Vinci plant design. | >$150M round June 2025 (Chevron, Google, NEA); >$1.3B total raised; Copernicus targeting net-energy validation before 2030 |
| [Princeton Fusion Systems (Princeton Satellite Systems)](https://www.princetonfusionsystems.com/) | startup | Small PPPL-linked team developing the PFRC — a clean, kW-to-MW-scale FRC heated by odd-parity rotating magnetic fields — for compact power and space propulsion; PFRC-2 holds the FRC plasma-duration record. | ARPA-E and DOE grant funded; PFRC-3 next-step device planned |

> **White space:** Only ~3 credible players because FRC stability at reactor scale remains unproven physics and beam/pulsed machines are capital-hungry, yet the two leaders are among the best-funded in fusion; openings are second-source pulsed-FRC plays leveraging cheap modern power electronics and the helium-3 fuel supply chain Helion's D-He3 cycle will need.

**Z-pinch / sheared-flow** · `⚪ lab`

An electric current driven through a plasma column pinches it to fusion density with no external magnets or driver lasers — an approach killed for 50 years by kink instabilities and revived by sheared-flow stabilization — offering the cheapest, most compact hardware in fusion.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Zap Energy](https://www.zapenergy.com/news/zap-attracts-130m-as-demo-system-begins-operations) | scaleup | Seattle company behind sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch (no magnets, no lasers); its Century platform demonstrated >1,000 consecutive plasmas into flowing liquid-metal walls and FuZE-3 reached record ~1.6 GPa plasma pressures (Nov 2025) en route to breakeven on FuZE-Q. | $130M round (led by Soros Fund Management) as Century began operations; >$450M total raised |
| [Fuse (Fuse Energy Technologies)](https://thebusinessdownload.com/nuclear-startup-fuse-valued-at-over-200-million-in-new-funding/) | startup | Founded by JC Btaiche; sells pulsed-power X-ray/neutron radiation-effects testing to defense customers today (TITAN, the first high-energy impedance-matched Marx generator) as a revenue bridge toward Z-pinch fusion energy. | $32M Series A valuing the company >$200M (2025); US Air Force and defense contracts |
| [MIFTI (Magneto-Inertial Fusion Technologies)](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mifti-patented-staged-z-pinch-fusion-technology-launches-early-adopter-program-for-groundbreaking-electric-energy-and-radioisotope-production-302363852.html) | startup | Tustin, CA company developing the Staged Z-Pinch — a gas liner imploding onto a fusion fuel core to suppress instabilities — claiming national-lab-verified record neutron yields and launching an early-adopter program for radioisotope production. | Early adopter program launched Jan 2025; 20+ years of staged Z-pinch R&D, largely grant/private funded |
| [LPP Fusion](https://www.lppfusion.com/2025-fusion-in-review/) | startup | Eric Lerner's dense-plasma-focus venture chasing direct proton-boron 'focus fusion'; a 2,000-investor crowdfunded outlier that set its own yield record (0.26 J) in 2025 but operates on minimal cash. | ~$11M raised over two decades from retail investors; ~$240k cash on hand Feb 2025 — financially marginal |

> **White space:** Sparse because classic m=0/m=1 instabilities killed the pinch for half a century; Zap's sheared-flow results plus magnet-free, fast-iteration hardware reopen a low-capex lane, and the Fuse model (defense radiation-testing revenue while maturing the pinch) shows how new entrants can self-fund the physics risk.

**Magnetic mirrors** · `⚪ lab`

Plasma is bottled in a straight tube between two high-field magnetic 'plugs'; the approach was abandoned in the 1980s over end losses (MFTF was mothballed on completion day) but is being revived because 20T+ HTS end magnets transform confinement, and the simple linear geometry suits near-term industrial heat and neutron sources.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Realta Fusion](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/realta-fusion-raises-36-million-series-a-to-advance-compact-scalable-modular-fusion-energy-302452726.html) | startup | UW–Madison WHAM experiment spinout commercializing HTS-plugged axisymmetric tandem mirrors (Anvil demo), explicitly targeting industrial process heat as the first market; published a Q>5 tandem mirror plant design. | Oversubscribed $36M Series A June 2025 (Future Ventures, Khosla); strategic partnership and HTS magnet supply agreement with Commonwealth Fusion Systems (2026) |
| [Novatron Fusion Group](https://www.novatronfusion.com/news/2025-novatron-fusion-group-secures-new-partners-in-recent-funding-roundnbsp) | startup | Stockholm company whose NOVATRON mirror-cusp geometry is claimed to be inherently MHD-stable (plasma sits in a magnetic 'bowl' rather than on a 'hilltop'); N1 testbed hosted at KTH. | €10M Series A1 (2025) led by energy company St1; EIC backing |
| [⚠️ Lockheed Martin (Compact Fusion Reactor program)](https://aviationweek.com/defense/aircraft-propulsion/skunk-works-halted-nuclear-fusion-effort-2021) | incumbent | Skunk Works' high-beta cusp/mirror-hybrid CFR, hyped in 2014 as a truck-sized reactor within a decade; the program was quietly halted before 2021 (publicly confirmed Aug 2024) after successive T4/T5 prototypes failed to scale as promised — the company itself continues, but the fusion effort is dead. | Program shut down ~2020 after ~10 years; cautionary tale for compact-mirror claims · **☠ shut down** |

> **White space:** Only two active companies worldwide: mirrors carry the stigma of the 1980s end-loss failures and the modern HTS revival is barely four years old, but the linear geometry is the cheapest credible route to fusion-grade neutrons and industrial heat — an opening for heat-first business models and for hyperscaler/industrial offtakers wanting small, serviceable units.

**Electrostatic & exotic approaches (IEC, magneto-electrostatic, muon-catalyzed, levitated dipole)** · `⚪ lab`

A grab-bag of unconventional schemes — electrostatic wells (IEC), hybrid magneto-electrostatic orbit traps, muon-catalyzed 'cold' fusion, and levitated dipoles — that trade mainstream plasma physics for radically smaller, cheaper devices, with most survivors monetizing fusion neutrons (isotopes, materials testing) long before net energy.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [OpenStar Technologies](https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/openstar-demonstrates-dipole-fusion-reactor-concept) | startup | Wellington, NZ startup building levitated-dipole reactors (an 'inside-out tokamak' with a floating HTS magnet); its Junior device achieved the first commercial levitated-dipole plasma in late 2024. | ~$12M raised; NZ$35M New Zealand government loan (Regional Development Fund) Feb 2026 for a new research facility |
| [SHINE Technologies](https://www.shinefusion.com/blog/shine-technologies-showcases-flare-tm-the-worlds-most-powerful-continuous-fusion-neutron-system) | scaleup | Wisconsin company running the world's brightest steady-state D-T beam-target fusion neutron sources (FLARE, ~5×10^13 n/s) as a profitable business today — medical isotopes (Mo-99, Lu-177) and radiation testing, incl. supplying UKAEA's LIBRTI — as phase 3 of an explicit four-phase staircase to fusion energy. | Hundreds of millions raised; FLARE showcased 2024; UKAEA neutron-source contract; isotope plants in commissioning |

> **White space:** Thin for a physics reason — Todd Rider's thermodynamic limits on non-equilibrium electrostatic plasmas and the muon alpha-sticking problem have stood for decades — so the credible play is the one survivors already run: profitable neutron/isotope/testing products (Astral, SHINE, Avalanche's FusionWERX) that fund the long-shot energy claim, plus picks-and-shovels licensing of tritium-capable test infrastructure.

**Projectile / impact fusion** · `⚪ lab`

A hypervelocity projectile is fired into a target whose internal geometry amplifies the impact shock to ignition pressures — mechanically simple with no lasers or large magnets — but single-shot gain and repetition-rate economics pushed even the category leader out of power-plant ambitions in 2025.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [First Light Fusion](https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/first-light-fusion-switches-strategy-drops-plans-to-develop-power-plant) | startup | Oxford pioneer of projectile-driven fusion and pressure-multiplying 'amplifier' targets; in March 2025 it scrapped its own power-plant route (Machine 4 cancelled, valuation cut >60% by IP Group from £236M to £100M) and pivoted to supplying amplifier/velocity-multiplication technology to other fusion and HED programs, including work on Sandia's Z machine. | £25M first close led by East X Ventures with strategic investment from UKAEA; first commercial VIPER III amplifier shipment to Texas A&M announced Apr 2026 |
| [NearStar Fusion](https://climateinsider.com/2025/03/07/vipc-invests-in-nearstar-fusion-to-advance-clean-energy-and-virginias-nuclear-fusion-ecosystem/) | startup | Chantilly, VA startup whose 'Hypervelocity Gradient Field Fusion' fires gun-launched fuel projectiles into a magnetized plasma target — a gun-driven MTF hybrid designed for cheap, replaceable drivers; absorbed the HyperJet Fusion (PJMIF) team. | ~$10.5M raised incl. Virginia VIPC/Virginia Venture Partners investments (2025) and NSF SBIR; StartEngine crowdfunding open |

> **White space:** Effectively a two-player niche, and the leader's 2025 retreat is the clearest market evidence in fusion that single-shot impact economics (driver rep-rate, target cost, gain) don't yet close for power; the remaining opening is exactly First Light's new shape — selling amplifier/target physics as a supply-chain product to laser ICF, pulsed-power, and defense HED customers — rather than standalone plants.

### Electrochemical Storage

Containerized lithium iron phosphate (and some NMC) battery plants — cells integrated with inverters, thermal management, and control software — are the workhorse of grid storage, shifting solar and wind output and beating gas peakers on cost in many markets (~460 GWh shipped globally in 2025).

> **White space:** Western sodium-ion collapsed in 2025 (Natron shut down, Northvolt gone, Tiamat delayed) just as Chinese giants committed gigafactories — sodium's cost edge only appears at scale and when lithium is expensive. The opening is Western capacity anchored to niches lithium serves poorly (data-center UPS, cold climates, fire-code-constrained sites) or molten-sodium routes that sidestep li-ion's cost curve.

**Iron-air & other metal-air** · `🟠 demonstration`

Cells charge by 'unrusting' iron (or another metal) and discharge by re-oxidizing it with air, storing 100+ hours of energy at very low cost per kWh but only ~40-50% round-trip efficiency — built for multi-day wind/solar droughts rather than daily cycling.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Form Energy](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/iron-air-battery-developer-long-duration-storage-form-energy-collaboration-ge-vernova/730633/) | scaleup | 100-hour iron-air systems manufactured at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV; the category-defining player | $405M Series F (Oct 2024, T. Rowe Price + GE Vernova), >$1.2B raised; first project (1.5 MW/150 MWh with Great River Energy, Cambridge MN) online ~late 2025, more in MN/CO/CA/NY/GA/VA through 2026 |
| [Ore Energy](https://www.ess-news.com/2025/07/30/ore-energy-brings-first-grid-connected-iron-air-battery-online-in-the-netherlands/) | startup | TU Delft spinout that connected the world's first grid-connected, operational iron-air battery (Delft, NL, operating since May 2025) | ~€10M seed (2024) plus grants, ~€20M total; piloting 100-hour BESS with EDF lab in France; 4.2 MWh containers planned |
| [Phinergy](https://phinergy.com/) | scaleup | Israeli aluminum-air (primary, non-rechargeable) systems for telecom and backup power | Tel Aviv-listed; commercial backup deployments with telecom operators |

> **White space:** Effectively a one-company category: Form's $1.2B war chest dwarfs everyone, and physics (low round-trip efficiency and power density) confines metal-air to multi-day markets that today's tariffs and capacity products barely remunerate, deterring followers. Openings: non-US iron-air champions (Ore in the EU), and market-design/revenue-stack work that creates paid multi-day reliability products.

**Flow batteries (vanadium, iron, zinc-bromine, organic)** · `🟡 scaling`

Energy is stored in liquid electrolytes pumped through a reactor stack, decoupling power from energy so duration stretches cheaply to 4-12+ hours with 20,000+ cycles and no fire risk; vanadium leads (scaling fast in China), while iron, zinc-bromine, and organic chemistries chase cheaper electrolytes.

**Zinc-based non-flow batteries (zinc-bromine static, zinc-air, zinc-ion, nickel-zinc)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Zinc anodes in static (non-pumped) cells — zinc-bromine gel, zinc-air, zinc-manganese alkaline, nickel-zinc — deliver non-flammable, lithium-free storage from abundant materials, trading lower efficiency and energy density for safety and indoor/urban siting flexibility.

The opening is anchoring to fire-code-driven demand — data-center UPS, urban and defense sites — rather than fighting LFP head-on per kWh, as ZincFive's data-center traction and Eos's DOE-backed onshore story show.

**High-temperature liquid-metal & sodium-sulfur** · `🟠 demonstration`

Cells operate at 250-700C with molten electrodes or ceramic electrolytes (sodium-sulfur, calcium-antimony liquid metal), offering long calendar life and cheap materials for 6-12 hour storage — but the only mass producer is now exiting after losing the economics race to LFP.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [BASF Stationary Energy Storage](https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2024/06/p-24-216) | incumbent | Global sales/development partner for NAS since 2019; co-developed NAS MODEL L24 with <1%/year degradation (June 2024) | Partnership discussions with NGK discontinued Sept 2025; unit's future unclear · *status unverified* |
| [Ambri](https://www.energy-storage.news/liquid-metal-startup-ambri-back-in-business-after-chapter-11-bankruptcy/) | startup | Calcium-antimony liquid-metal cells (Sadoway/MIT) with no degradation mechanism, now targeting data centers | Chapter 11 May 2024; emerged Aug 2024 under lender consortium (Gates Frontier, Paulson); first containerized systems shipping, ~$35M revenue reported 2025 |

> **White space:** The non-lithium chemistry with the longest real grid track record (NAS, ~5 GWh over two decades) is being abandoned by its only manufacturer, and the flagship liquid-metal startup went bankrupt — high operating temperature plus bespoke manufacturing simply lost to LFP's cost curve. Openings: acquiring/licensing NGK's proven NAS IP and servicing its installed fleet, or intermediate-temperature sodium-halide designs (e.g., Inlyte) that reuse the supply chain at lower temperature and cost.

**Nickel-hydrogen & novel aqueous chemistries (lead-carbon, aluminum-ion)** · `🔵 pilot`

Space-proven nickel-hydrogen pressure vessels and water-based chemistries (aqueous sodium/manganese oxide, lead-carbon, aluminum-ion) promise 20,000-30,000 cycles, wide temperature tolerance, and zero fire risk, betting that lifetime and safety can beat lithium's upfront cost.

| [Alsym Energy](https://www.ess-news.com/2025/10/22/alsym-energy-launches-na-series-claiming-safe-low-cost-sodium-ion-battery-storage/) | startup | Non-flammable, non-toxic aqueous metal-oxide chemistry; launched Na-Series sodium-based stationary line Oct 2025 | ~$78M raised (General Catalyst, Tata); product launch but no large deployments yet |

> **White space:** EnerVenue is nearly alone at scale: pressure-vessel capex and low volumetric energy density deter entrants, and Aquion's 2017 collapse still shadows aqueous chemistries. The opening is ultra-long-life niches where 30k cycles, wide temperature range, and zero fire suppression beat LFP on total cost — AI data centers, desert and off-grid sites — plus licensing models that avoid building gigafactories alone.

**Solid-state & advanced lithium for stationary use** · `🔵 pilot`

Solid or semi-solid electrolytes and advanced electrodes (lithium-sulfur, lithium-titanate/niobium anodes) aim to bring fire safety, very long cycle life, or cheaper electrode manufacturing to stationary lithium storage — though most solid-state developers chase EVs first and the grid gets their tech second.

> **White space:** Solid-state's headline advantage — energy density — is nearly worthless for stationary storage, so no major solid-state player targets the grid first and the segment is thin. The opening is chemistry chosen FOR stationary economics: semi-solid electrode cost cuts, LTO/niobium cycle life for high-throughput grid services, and fire-code-friendly cells that unlock indoor, urban, and data-center siting.

**Supercapacitors & hybrid ion capacitors** · `🟠 demonstration`

Electrostatic storage in high-surface-area carbon delivers millions of cycles and sub-second response but tiny energy capacity, suiting grid-forming inertia, power smoothing, and AI data-center peak shaving (usually hybridized with batteries) rather than energy shifting.

### Thermal & Mechanical Long-Duration Storage

**High-temperature thermal batteries (molten salt, bricks, sand, carbon blocks + TPV)** · `🟡 scaling`

Electric resistance heating charges cheap media — firebricks, crushed rock, sand, molten salt or carbon blocks — to 500–2,400 C, then discharges as industrial steam/heat (or electricity via thermophotovoltaics), attacking the ~20% of global emissions from industrial process heat with dirt-cheap storage materials.

| [Antora Energy](https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/antoras-150-million-cash-infusion-will-boost-manufacturing/) | scaleup | Modular carbon-block batteries reaching >1,500 C with optional thermophotovoltaic electricity output | $150M Series B (Feb 2024, BlackRock/Temasek's Decarbonization Partners), ~$244M total; 50 MW / 5 GWh system commissioning at POET bioprocessing plant, South Dakota |

**Pumped thermal / Carnot batteries** · `🔵 pilot`

Heat pumps convert cheap electricity into a hot store (often paired with a cold store) and a heat engine reverses the cycle to regenerate power, promising multi-day storage from steel, rock and salt — but ~50-60% round-trip efficiency has kept it behind Li-ion and pushed players toward selling heat instead.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Malta Inc](https://www.ess-news.com/2025/06/17/malta-inc-launches-spanish-thermal-energy-storage-pilot-site/) | startup | Google X spinout storing electricity in molten salt via a heat-pump/heat-engine cycle; now also selling 300-550 C industrial heat pumps | 14 MW Puertollano (Spain) LDES pilot launched Jun 2025 with BBVA revenue agreement; first commercial Advanced Heat Pump at Proman methanol plant, Texas |
| [Stiesdal Storage](https://www.stiesdal.com/) | startup | GridScale crushed-basalt pumped thermal storage from wind pioneer Henrik Stiesdal | 4 MW / 10 MWh demonstrator at Rodby, Denmark since 2023; commercial rollout has been slow since |
| [Echogen Power Systems](https://echogen.com/) | startup | Supercritical-CO2 heat-engine cycles for electro-thermal energy storage and waste heat recovery | ARPA-E DAYS awardee; licenses sCO2 power cycle technology to OEMs |
| [MAN Energy Solutions](https://www.man-es.com/) | incumbent | ETES electro-thermal storage and very large industrial heat pumps (e.g., 50 MW Esbjerg seawater heat pump) plus Carnot-cycle turbomachinery | Volkswagen Group subsidiary; ETES reference plants in Denmark/Norway |
| [Siemens Gamesa (ETES program)](https://www.siemensgamesa.com/) | incumbent | Built the world's first large rock-bed electric thermal storage demo (130 MWh, Hamburg, 2019) then shelved the program — the sector's key failure datapoint | Demo operated ~2019-2022; program discontinued as parent retrenched |

> **White space:** Thin field for physics reasons — heat-pump/heat-engine round trips lose ~40-50% of energy, and Li-ion cost declines killed the pure power-to-power case (Siemens Gamesa quit; Malta pivoted toward industrial heat); the opening is hybrid heat-plus-power offtake and repowering retiring coal plants whose steam turbines a Carnot battery can reuse.

**Phase-change & thermochemical storage** · `🟡 scaling`

Stores energy in a material's melting transition (PCM — ice, salt hydrates, metal alloys) or a reversible chemical reaction (thermochemical metal oxides/salts), giving compact, low-loss heat and cooling batteries for buildings and industry rather than bulk electricity.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Sunamp](https://sunamp.com/) | scaleup | Plentigrade salt-hydrate PCM 'Thermino' heat batteries replacing hot-water cylinders in homes | ~$28.6M raised; tens of thousands of UK/EU installs; launched low-power models for the Italian market Mar 2025 |
| [CALMAC (Trane Technologies)](https://www.calmac.com/) | incumbent | IceBank ice-storage tanks shifting commercial-building cooling load off-peak — the mature workhorse of PCM storage | Thousands of buildings worldwide; acquired by Ingersoll Rand/Trane in 2016 · **acquired** |
| [Nostromo Energy](https://nostromo.energy/technology/icebrick) | startup | IceBrick modular ice-cell arrays retrofitted to commercial buildings for peak cooling demand response | Installed at flagship California hotels (e.g., Beverly Hilton); TASE-listed, pursuing US utility programs |
| [Phase Change Solutions](https://phasechange.com/) | startup | BioPCM plant-derived phase-change materials tunable from -75 C to 175 C for buildings and cold chain | Commercial sales across 40+ countries; partnerships in building retrofit |

| [RedoxBlox](https://www.thermalbatteryalliance.com/thermalbatteryallianceannouncement) | startup | Metal-oxide redox thermochemical modules storing heat plus chemical energy, discharging above 1,100 C for industrial heat and gas-turbine decarbonization | ARPA-E and Khosla Ventures-backed; founding member of the Thermal Battery Alliance (Jan 2025) |

> **White space:** Building-side ice/PCM is commercial, but high-temperature thermochemical storage has only a couple of credible players because reaction reversibility and cycling degradation are hard chemistry; an opening exists above ~1,000 C where sensible-heat bricks lose energy density and industrial gas users need both heat and storable chemical energy.

**Gravity storage (towers, mine shafts, rail, cranes)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Lifts mass — composite blocks in towers, weights in disused mine shafts, rail cars on slopes, water-filled pistons — with surplus power and recovers electricity on descent; the physics is simple and degradation-free, but low energy density and high structural cost have kept it above battery prices.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Energy Vault](https://www.energyvault.com/projects/cn-rudong) | scaleup | EVx gravity towers raising/lowering 24-tonne composite blocks; the only public pure-play, though US revenue has pivoted to conventional BESS | NYSE: NRGV; 25 MW / 100 MWh Rudong (China) system commissioned, ~9 licensed China deployments totaling 3.7+ GWh; $150M convertible note closed Mar 2026 |
| [Gravitricity](https://www.energy-storage.news/gravitricity-and-energy-vault-move-forward-with-commercialising-gravity-energy-storage/) | startup | Weights of 500-5,000 tonnes raised and lowered in abandoned mine shafts | 250 kW Edinburgh demonstrator proven; agreements for projects at former mines (Finland's Pyhasalmi, US, India), still pre-commercial |
| [Green Gravity](https://greengravity.com/) | startup | Australian developer repurposing legacy mine shafts with ore-filled weights | Agreements with mine owners (e.g., Woodlawn); government grant-backed, pilot stage |
| [ARES North America](https://aresnorthamerica.com/) | startup | GravityLine — chains of weighted rail cars on a Nevada slope providing grid regulation | Broke ground on 50 MW merchant Pahrump Valley plant (2023) targeting Q4 2025 operation; little public confirmation since · *status unverified* |
| [Gravity Power](https://www.gravitypower.net/) | startup | Hydraulic piston-in-shaft concept (massive piston atop a sealed water column) | Long-gestating; no commercial plant after a decade-plus · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Sparse for physics reasons: lifted-mass energy density is tiny (a 1,000-tonne weight dropped 500 m stores ~1.4 MWh) so steel and civil works dominate cost, and Li-ion's price collapse erased the niche — Energy Vault's own pivot to batteries is the tell; the credible opening is brownfield mine shafts where the structure, grid connection and workforce already exist.

**Compressed air energy storage (adiabatic & underground caverns)** · `🟡 scaling`

Uses cheap power to compress air into salt caverns, rock caverns or engineered vessels and re-expands it through turbines — modern adiabatic/advanced designs store the compression heat too, eliminating gas burn — enabling 100 MW-to-GW, 6-12+ hour storage at very low cost per kWh.

**Liquid air & CO2 battery cycles** · `🟠 demonstration`

Liquefies air (or compresses CO2 between a gas dome and liquid tanks in a closed loop) using surplus power, then expands it through turbines to regenerate electricity — siteable anywhere with no caverns or mountains, built from mature industrial-gas hardware.

**Pumped storage hydro (conventional, closed-loop, high-density fluid, subsea)** · `🟢 mature`

Pumps water uphill (or a 2.5x-denser fluid up small hills, or out of pressurized subsea spheres) when power is cheap and runs it back through turbines when needed — at ~180 GW installed it is >90% of the world's storage energy and still the cheapest bulk option where geography allows.

**Geomechanical / subsurface pressurized-water storage** · `🔵 pilot`

Pumps water under high pressure into engineered underground rock formations or proppant-held fractures and releases it back through hydropower turbines — using oil-and-gas drilling techniques to put 'pumped hydro' on flat land anywhere, with near-zero standing losses.

| [Quidnet Energy](https://cleantechnica.com/2025/06/27/new-long-duration-energy-storage-system-deploys-underground-hydropower/) | startup | Geomechanical Pumped Storage in shallow rock lenses; the category creator | $10M ARPA-E SCALEUP award; 1 MW / 10 MWh project under 15-year deal with CPS Energy (San Antonio) — demonstrated 35 MWh discharge after six months of pressurized storage with no loss (Jun 2025); backed by Hunt Energy and Breakthrough Energy Ventures |
| [Sage Geosystems](https://www.hartenergy.com/exclusives/sage-geosystems-advances-commercial-scale-energy-storage-facility-209044) | startup | EarthStore — pressurized water stored in fracture domains of hot dry rock wells, doubling as geothermal generation | 3 MW commercial facility with San Miguel Electric Cooperative (TX); >$97M Series B led by Ormat Technologies (2025); separate 150 MW geothermal deal with Meta |

> **White space:** Essentially two players: reservoir geomechanics is the moat and the risk — fracture containment, cycling fatigue and round-trip efficiency (~50-70%) are unproven at scale, so generalist investors stay away; if Quidnet's CPS project validates economics, oilfield-services firms (Halliburton, SLB-class drilling and pressure-pumping crews) could industrialize deployment almost overnight, making this a natural O&G-transition play.

**Flywheels** · `🟢 mature`

Stores electricity as rotational kinetic energy in magnetically levitated rotors that charge and discharge in milliseconds with million-cycle life — a power (not energy) technology that owns UPS and frequency-regulation niches but has repeatedly failed commercially as grid energy storage.

| [Amber Kinetics](https://cleantechnica.com/2026/04/19/from-beacon-to-amber-flywheels-missed-the-grid/) | startup | Four-hour steel-rotor flywheels (32 kWh KESS) — the only long-duration flywheel attempt | 17 years old with only ~$25-47M disclosed funding; US military microgrid evaluations (Miramar Q3 2025, Viejas 2026) but living on grants, not sales · *status unverified* |
| [VYCON (Calnetix)](https://vyconenergy.com/) | incumbent | Kinetic-energy UPS flywheels widely deployed in data centers, hospitals and crane regeneration | Thousands of units fielded; profitable power-quality niche |
| [Piller Power Systems (incl. ex-Active Power)](https://www.piller.com/) | incumbent | Rotary UPS and flywheel ride-through systems; absorbed distressed flywheel maker Active Power (2016) | Langley Holdings unit; standard kit for mission-critical facilities |
| [Revterra](https://greyb.com/blog/advanced-flywheel-energy-storage-startups/) | startup | Passive magnetic-bearing 'kinetic batteries' (100 kWh / 400 kW) buffering EV fast-charging on weak grids | $6M seed (2022); pilot deployments with charging developers |
| [QuinteQ Energy](https://www.quinteqenergy.com/) | startup | Lightweight Boeing-derived flywheels for port cranes, military microgrids and peak shaving | Dutch; deployments at ports and defense sites, early commercial |

> **White space:** As energy storage the physics is unforgiving — self-discharge and the $/kWh of spinning steel confine flywheels to seconds-to-minutes, and the corporate graveyard (Beacon Ch.11, Active Power distressed sale, Pentadyne liquidation, Temporal Power) proves grid arbitrage never penciled; the live opening is power-quality hybrids that shield batteries from cycling (Torus's model) and inertia-as-a-service on inverter-heavy grids.

**Hydrogen power-to-power LDES (electrolyzer + cavern/tank + fuel cell or turbine)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Converts surplus renewable electricity to hydrogen via electrolysis, stores it in salt caverns, tanks or metal hydrides for days to seasons, and converts it back through fuel cells or hydrogen-capable turbines — the only practical seasonal storage, though sub-40% round-trip efficiency makes it expensive without mandates.
