| [Chevron](https://www.chevron.com/newsroom/2024/q3/aces-hydrogen-project-to-advance-lower-carbon-future) | incumbent | Acquired Magnum Development (owner of the Utah salt-cavern site) in 2023 to co-own ACES Delta — an oil major buying into H2 storage | Holds majority interest in ACES Delta alongside Mitsubishi Power |
| [HDF Energy](https://fuelcellsworks.com/2025/04/07/fuel-cells/hdf-energy-installs-fuel-cells-at-ceog-project-in-french-guiana-advancing-24-7-renewable-power-supply) | scaleup | Renewstable baseload plants combining solar, 16 MW electrolysis, 128 MWh H2 storage and fuel cells for island grids | Euronext-listed; CEOG French Guiana — the world's first multi-MW hydrogen power plant — in final equipment installation 2025, serving ~10,000 households |
| [Energy Vault (Calistoga Resiliency Center)](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/energy-vault-pge-announce-successful-completion-of-the-calistoga-resiliency-center-the-worlds-first-ultra-long-duration-hybrid-battery--hydrogen-energy-storage-microgrid-302567475.html) | scaleup | Owns/operates the world's first ultra-long-duration hybrid hydrogen-fuel-cell + battery microgrid (8.5 MW / 293 MWh) replacing diesel for PG&E wildfire shutoffs | Commercial operation Sep 2025 under 10.5-year PG&E tolling agreement |
| [Plug Power](https://www.plugpower.com/) | scaleup | PEM electrolyzers, fuel cells and stationary power for hydrogen P2P chains | NASDAQ-listed; closed $1.66B DOE loan guarantee (Jan 2025) amid sustained losses, layoffs and cash concerns |
| [GKN Hydrogen](https://www.langleyholdings.com/news/2024/08/01/langley-acquires-gkn-hydrogen/) | startup | Metal-hydride solid-state H2 storage (16x density of compressed gas, 30-year life) packaged as power-to-power microgrid systems | Acquired by Langley Holdings from Dowlais Group (Aug 2024) into its Power Solutions division; 7,000+ cycles proven at 99% efficiency · **acquired** |
| [Siemens Energy](https://www.siemens-energy.com/) | incumbent | Silyzer electrolyzers plus hydrogen-capable gas turbines; ran HYFLEXPOWER, the first integrated industrial power-to-H2-to-power demo at 100% hydrogen | 100% H2 turbine operation demonstrated in France (2023); H2-ready turbine line shipping |

> **White space:** Round-trip efficiency of ~30-40% plus electrolyzer capex means no merchant business case exists — every operating project leans on a mandate (Calistoga wildfire resilience), an island grid with diesel-price competition (CEOG), or policy-backed utility offtake (LADWP/IPP); the structural opening is pairing existing or cheap-to-mine salt caverns with the H2-capable turbine fleets utilities are already buying, rather than greenfield fuel-cell plants.

### Grid & Transmission Hardware

**HVDC converter stations & interconnectors** · `🟢 mature`

Power-electronic converter stations turn AC into high-voltage DC so bulk renewable power can travel thousands of kilometers over land or under sea with low losses, forming the backbone for offshore wind and inter-regional grid links.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Hitachi Energy](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/articles/key-companies-in-high-voltage-direct-current-converter) | incumbent | Market leader in voltage-source-converter HVDC (HVDC Light) stations for offshore wind and interconnectors | Disclosed ~$4.2B HVDC backlog incl. Dogger Bank and North Sea links; top-3 vendors held ~60-65% of 2025 order intake |
| [Siemens Energy](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/articles/key-companies-in-high-voltage-direct-current-converter) | incumbent | HVDC PLUS converter technology for offshore grid connections and energy islands | Booked ~$3.8B in 2025 across Bornholm, East Anglia THREE and Middle East schemes |
| [GE Vernova](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/articles/key-companies-in-high-voltage-direct-current-converter) | incumbent | HVDC converter systems; re-entered offshore HVDC after a four-year hiatus | $1.4B Ostwind 4 offshore HVDC award in 2025 |
| [Mitsubishi Electric](https://www.sphericalinsights.com/blogs/top-15-companies-in-hvdc-transmission-market-worldwide-in-2025-market-research-report-2024-2035) | incumbent | HVDC converter and frequency-converter stations, especially for Japan's 50/60 Hz interties | Ranked among top global HVDC transmission suppliers in 2025 |
| [NR Electric](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/articles/key-companies-in-high-voltage-direct-current-converter) | incumbent | Chinese converter-valve and control supplier expanding internationally with 20-30% price discounts vs Western OEMs | Part of Chinese vendor push (with C-EPRI, Xian XD) into export HVDC markets in 2025 |
| [Sun Cable](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/2025/07/07/federal-government-keeps-faith-in-suncable-project/) | scaleup | Developing AAPowerLink, a ~4,300 km Australia-Singapore HVDC link exporting Northern Territory solar | Entered administration Jan 2023, relaunched under Grok Ventures; Australian major-project status renewed July 2025 and Singapore conditional import approval for 1.75 GW; FID expected 2027 |
| [Xlinks](https://www.newcivilengineer.com/latest/developer-bitterly-disappointed-as-government-calls-off-25bn-uk-morocco-interconnector-27-06-2025/) | startup | Proposed 3.6 GW, 3,800 km Morocco-UK HVDC interconnector delivering Saharan solar and wind to Britain | UK government declined CfD support in June 2025 calling the megaproject too risky; company exploring private routes · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Western converter supply is a three-firm oligopoly sold out into the 2030s with 24+ month converter-transformer lead times, while Chinese rivals face security barriers in Western markets — the opening is standardized/modular converter designs, valve components, and new factory capacity rather than yet another merchant-link developer (Xlinks' rejection shows mega-project FOAK risk).

**High-voltage submarine & underground cable systems** · `🟢 mature`

Extruded XLPE and mass-impregnated cables rated up to 525 kV carry offshore wind and interconnector power under seas and cities, and global decarbonization plans hinge on a handful of factories that make them.

| [NKT](https://www.offshore-mag.com/renewable-energy/article/55240474/shortage-of-submarine-power-cables-poses-threat-to-offshore-wind-market) | incumbent | Danish pioneer of 525 kV extruded HVDC cable for European interconnectors and German corridor projects | Record high-voltage backlog with ~45% from offshore wind; one of three Europeans controlling ~75% of HVDC cable supply |
| [Nexans](https://www.offshore-mag.com/renewable-energy/article/55240474/shortage-of-submarine-power-cables-poses-threat-to-offshore-wind-market) | incumbent | French HV subsea cable maker (Halden, Norway and Charleston, SC plants) plus cable-laying vessels | Among the top-3 suppliers holding ~75% of the HVDC cable market; multi-year sold-out backlog |
| [LS Cable & System](https://www.offshore-mag.com/renewable-energy/article/55240474/shortage-of-submarine-power-cables-poses-threat-to-offshore-wind-market) | incumbent | Korean cable giant building LS Greenlink in Chesapeake, Virginia — slated to be the largest HVDC subsea cable plant in the US | ~$680M plant, construction from 2025, completion expected 2027, supported by IRA 48C credits |
| [Sumitomo Electric](https://sumitomoelectric.com/press/2024/05/prs018) | incumbent | Japanese cable maker building the UK's first HVDC cable factory at Port of Nigg, Scotland | £350M factory broke ground May 2024 with production from ~Q3 2026; preferred bidder for SSEN's Shetland 2 525 kV cable |
| [XLCC](https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2025/11/267293/morocco-uk-project-halt-stalls-xlcc-cable-plant/) | startup | UK startup attempting a greenfield HVDC cable factory at Hunterston, Scotland, originally anchored to the Xlinks project | Plant plans stalled after the Morocco-UK project lost government backing in 2025 · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Backlogs quoted at 10+ years and ~75% of HVDC cable capacity in three European firms; $500M-class plants plus decade-long qualification track records deter entrants, so the realistic opening is regional factories anchored by national grid programs (the LS Greenlink and Sumitomo Nigg model) and specialist installation vessels — XLCC's stall shows the risk of anchoring a plant to a single merchant project.

**Advanced conductors & reconductoring** · `🟡 scaling`

Replacing steel-core conductors with carbon-composite-core wires on existing towers can roughly double a line's capacity with no new right-of-way, making reconductoring the fastest, cheapest way to expand transmission for clean energy.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [TS Conductor](https://www.prweb.com/releases/ts-conductor-raises-60-million-from-industry-leading-investors-to-expand-us-production-of-high-capacity-power-lines-302207238.html) | scaleup | Makes encapsulated carbon-core aluminum conductors (AECC) that install with standard hardware and crews | $60M growth round led by Wellington (July 2024) with Quanta, NextEra, Edison, BEV and National Grid Partners; building a $134M South Carolina plant with DOE backing |
| [CTC Global](https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2025/06/30/google-aims-to-boost-transmission-capacity-with-advanced-conductor-upgrades/) | scaleup | Inventor of the ACCC composite-core conductor, the most widely deployed advanced conductor globally | Raised growth capital from Endeavour and Greenbelt Capital Partners (2025); chosen technology for Google's 2025 utility reconductoring partnership program |
| [Southwire](https://www.southwire.com/) | incumbent | Largest North American wire and cable maker; manufactures and distributes high-capacity and composite-core conductor products at scale | Key domestic manufacturing partner as US reconductoring demand accelerates |
| [3M](https://www.3m.com/3M/en_US/p/c/b/accr/) | incumbent | Pioneered the ACCR aluminum-matrix composite conductor, an early high-temperature low-sag design | Legacy advanced-conductor line deployed by utilities since the 2000s |
| [Quanta Services](https://www.renewableenergyworld.com/power-grid/grid-conductor-company-raises-60-million-for-second-us-production-facility/) | incumbent | Largest US T&D contractor performing live-line reconductoring; strategic investor in TS Conductor | Participated in TS Conductor's 2024 round to lock up advanced-conductor installation capability |

> **White space:** Only two pure-play composite-core makers (CTC Global, TS Conductor) face a DOE-identified opportunity to roughly double capacity on existing corridors; the binding constraints are core manufacturing capacity and utility incentives that favor rate-based new builds, so openings exist for new core suppliers, installation tooling, and third-party financing models like Google's 2025 reconductoring program.

**Superconducting cables & fault current limiters** · `🟠 demonstration`

High-temperature superconducting (HTS) wire carries 5-10x more current than copper in a tiny footprint and can self-limit fault currents, letting utilities push huge power through dense cities or constrained rights-of-way.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [MetOx International](https://www.manufacturing.net/operations/news/22924307/metox-secures-80m-in-doe-funding-to-build-advanced-hts-wire-facility-in-us) | startup | Scaling US manufacturing of Xeus HTS wire, the key feedstock for superconducting cables, FCLs and fusion magnets | $25M Series B extension (Sep 2024) plus selection for $80M DOE funding for a new HTS wire plant breaking ground in 2025 |
| [AMSC (American Superconductor)](https://www.custommarketinsights.com/report/fault-current-limiter-market/) | incumbent | Amperium HTS wire, resilient electric grid (REG) city cables, superconducting fault current limiters and D-VAR systems | NASDAQ-listed; installed an SFCL in a US military-grade power system in Feb 2025; REG system operating in Chicago's grid |
| [Nexans](https://www.custommarketinsights.com/report/fault-current-limiter-market/) | incumbent | Builds turnkey superconducting cable systems and HTS fault current limiters (using AMSC wire) | Released an HTS fault current limiter for offshore wind platforms in Feb 2025 after North Sea testing |
| [THEVA](https://www.modernpowersystems.com/analysis/hts-technology-expands-in-usa-and-germany/) | scaleup | German HTS tape producer supplying the Munich SuperLink, the world's longest planned urban superconducting cable | Expanding German tape production alongside US HTS capacity growth |
| [SuperNode](https://supernode.energy/) | startup | Irish developer of superconducting cable systems aimed at bulk offshore-wind grid connections | Privately backed (founded by Mainstream Renewable's Eddie O'Connor); still pre-commercial |

> **White space:** Physics is proven but HTS tape supply (a handful of producers, high $/kA-m cost) and cryogenic O&M keep deployments at demonstration scale; near-term openings are tape capacity scale-up (MetOx's DOE-backed plant) and right-of-way-impossible niches — dense cities, substation interties, and AI data-center campuses — where conventional conductors simply cannot fit.

**Dynamic line rating & transmission monitoring sensors** · `🟡 scaling`

Sensors on or near power lines measure real conductor temperature, sag and weather so operators can safely run lines 20-40% above static ratings and spot failures before they spark outages or wildfires.

|---|---|---|---|
| [LineVision](https://www.aes.com/newsroom/aes-and-linevision-release-results-study-assessing-largest-single-deployment-dynamic-line) | scaleup | Non-contact LiDAR/electromagnetic sensors plus analytics for dynamic line ratings and asset health | Largest single US DLR deployment with AES (Indiana/Ohio); National Grid expanding UK use to 585 km after a successful 275 kV trial |
| [Heimdall Power](https://www.renewableenergyworld.com/power-grid/transmission/startup-behind-magic-ball-for-boosting-transmission-capacity-raises-25-million/) | scaleup | Norwegian maker of drone-installed 'magic ball' Neuron sensors clamped directly on conductors | $25M raise (2024); 52 sensors at Great River Energy delivered avg 42.8% capacity gain — largest US DLR install at the time; TIME Best Inventions 2025 |
| [Ampacimon](https://www.ampacimon.com/) | scaleup | Belgian pioneer of sag/vibration-based DLR sensors, deployed on Elia's grid since 2008 | Longest-running commercial DLR vendor; 2025 partnership with AP Sensing and new drone-installed HV sensors |
| [Gridware](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251117004576/en/Gridware-Raises-$55-Million-Growth-Round-to-Accelerate-U.S.-Deployments-and-Support-Global-Expansion) | startup | Pole-mounted Gridscope sensors detecting mechanical/electrical faults for wildfire prevention and outage response | $55M Series B (Nov 2025) led by Tiger Global and Generation IM; tens of thousands of poles deployed, utility partners serving ~40% of US customers |
| [Prisma Photonics](https://www.powermag.com/prisma-photonics-deploys-grid-monitoring-equipment-in-california/) | startup | Turns existing fiber (OPGW) on transmission lines into a distributed sensor — no on-line hardware needed | PG&E trial in California and statewide Great River Energy deployment in Minnesota (2025) |
| [Reactive Technologies](https://reactive-technologies.com/news/reactive-technologies-raises-25m/) | scaleup | GridMetrix measures grid inertia in real time by injecting signals via grid-connected modulator hardware | £25M Series D (May 2024) led by M&G, BGF and Breakthrough Energy Ventures; NYISO and Taiwan Power deployments |

**Power-flow control devices (FACTS, SSSC, modular power flow controllers)** · `🟡 scaling`

Power-electronic devices push or pull power between parallel lines, rerouting flows around congested circuits so existing grids carry more renewables without new wires; classic FACTS is mature while modular, redeployable units are the fast-growing wave.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Smart Wires](https://investor.pgecorp.com/news-events/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/PGE-and-Smart-Wires-Enhance-Grid-Reliability-Capacity-for-Data-Centers-in-San-Jose/default.aspx) | scaleup | Created the modular static synchronous series compensator (SmartValve) category — truck-delivered, redeployable power-flow control | $65M raised to scale 2025 operations; PG&E San Jose data-center project adding 100+ MW, 24-device Eles (Slovenia) deployment, first Brazil project with ISA |
| [Hitachi Energy](https://www.hitachienergy.com/products-and-solutions/facts) | incumbent | Full FACTS portfolio — SVCs, series compensation and STATCOMs — for transmission operators worldwide | Decades-deep installed base; FACTS demand surging with renewables and data-center load |
| [Siemens Energy](https://www.siemens-energy.com/global/en/home/products-services/product-offerings/grid-forming.html) | incumbent | SVC PLUS and UPFC-class series/shunt compensation systems | Major FACTS supplier with growing grid-stabilization order book |
| [GE Vernova](https://www.gevernova.com/grid-solutions/systems/flexible-ac-transmission-systems-facts/synchronous-condenser) | incumbent | FACTS and series compensation systems integrated with its grid solutions business | One of three Western FACTS majors |
| [AMSC (American Superconductor)](https://www.amsc.com/gridtec/) | incumbent | Transportable D-VAR dynamic reactive power (STATCOM) systems popular for wind/solar interconnection | Hundreds of D-VAR installations; profitable grid segment driving record revenue |

> **White space:** Smart Wires is essentially the only pure-play modular series-compensation vendor (Faraday Grid's 2019 collapse thinned the field); the barrier is not physics but utility rate-base incentives that reward large capital builds over cheap grid-enhancing fixes — shared-savings business models, distribution-level flow control, and FERC-mandated GET consideration are the openings.

**Grid-forming inverters, STATCOMs & synchronous condensers** · `🟡 scaling`

As coal and gas plants retire, these devices replace the voltage, inertia and fault current that spinning generators once provided — via grid-forming battery inverters, power-electronic STATCOMs, or spinning synchronous condensers — keeping renewable-heavy grids stable.

| [Siemens Energy](https://www.tdworld.com/reliability-and-resiliency/article/55361853/virtual-inertia-in-the-real-world) | incumbent | E-STATCOMs, synchronous condensers and hybrid stability plants | Energized world-first supercapacitor E-STATCOM with TenneT (Mehrum, Dec 2025); building syncon+flywheel+160 MWh BESS hybrid at Shannonbridge, Ireland |
| [GE Vernova](https://www.gevernova.com/news/press-releases/ge-vernova-provide-grid-stabilizing-technology-transgrid-support-renewables-rollout) | incumbent | Synchronous condenser systems and rotating stabilizers for inertia and short-circuit strength | Contracted for synchronous condensers at five Transgrid sites stabilizing the New South Wales grid |

**Transformers (conventional supply, mobile/modular, solid-state)** · `🟢 mature`

Transformers step voltage up and down at every grid interface; a global shortage with multi-year lead times is now the single biggest hardware bottleneck for connecting clean energy and data centers, driving new factories plus mobile and solid-state alternatives.

| [Ionate](https://www.eu-startups.com/2025/02/deeptech-ionate-raises-e16-3-million-to-modernise-global-power-systems/) | startup | UK maker of the Hybrid Intelligent Transformer — solid-state control wrapped around conventional magnetics for power-flow control and grid visibility without full-SST fragility | $17M Series A (Feb 2025) led by AlbionVC with In-Q-Tel and JGC; launching US operations targeting data-center constraints |
| [⚠️ Faraday Grid](https://www.greentechmedia.com/articles/read/transformer-technology-hopeful-faraday-grid-goes-bust) | startup | Edinburgh startup that promised the 'Faraday Exchanger' power-flow-controlling transformer replacement | Raised ~£25M from Adam Neumann's family office (Jan 2019), then collapsed into administration by August 2019 after overexpansion · **☠ shut down** |

> **White space:** Wood Mackenzie pegged the 2025 supply deficit near 100% (shrinking below 10% only by 2030), with large power transformer lead times of 3-5 years; openings are new domestic capacity (grain-oriented steel remains scarce), amorphous-core efficiency plays, standardized modular substations, and solid-state designs for data-center/EV duty — though Faraday Grid's collapse shows how capital-unforgiving novel transformer ventures can be.

**SF6-free switchgear & substation equipment** · `🟡 scaling`

SF6, the insulating gas in conventional switchgear, is the most potent greenhouse gas known (~25,000x CO2), so vendors are replacing it with clean air, fluoronitrile blends and vacuum interrupters as EU F-gas rules phase SF6 out from 2026 onward.

| [GE Vernova](https://www.gevernova.com/grid-solutions/hvmv_equipment/catalog/sf6-free-hv-switchgear/) | incumbent | g3 fluoronitrile-based SF6-free GIS with the same footprint as SF6 equipment, 72.5 kV and up | g3 substations operating across Europe; full SF6-free HV range commercialized |
| [Siemens Energy](https://www.siemens-energy.com/global/en/home/products-services/product-offerings/gas-insulated-switchgear.html) | incumbent | Blue portfolio using clean air insulation plus vacuum interrupters — zero F-gas at all | Blue GIS commercially deployed up to transmission voltages |
| [Schneider Electric](https://www.se.com/ww/en/work/products/product-launch/sf6-free-switchgear/) | incumbent | SM AirSeT and related pure-air medium-voltage switchgear for distribution networks | MV SF6-free range scaling across utility and commercial installs as EU F-gas regulation bites |
| [Nuventura](https://www.enlit.world/library/lucy-group-acquires-nuventura-to-expand-into-primary-sf6-free-switchgear) | startup | Berlin startup that commercialized the first SF6-free 36 kV GIS using dry air | €25M Series A (>€35M total) led by Mirova; acquired by UK's Lucy Group in April 2026 to scale globally · **acquired** |

> **White space:** High-voltage SF6-free is locked up by incumbents because type-testing costs and utility installed-base trust create steep barriers — Nuventura, the lone notable VC-backed entrant, exited to an incumbent in April 2026; remaining startup ground is medium-voltage/secondary distribution, retrofit and SF6 leak-monitoring niches as EU bans phase in 2026-2032.

## Transport

Moving people and freight without oil. Light-duty EVs and their battery supply chain are commercially won and scaling; the open battles are heavy trucking, charging at scale, and the hard physics of aviation and shipping fuels.

*9 solution areas · 95 variations · 710 company entries (648 unique companies; 53 marked dead, 31 acquired, 21 unverified)*

**Maturity at a glance (variations per stage):** Passenger & Light-Duty EVs (1 mature, 4 scaling, 2 demonstration, 1 pilot) · Electric Two/Three-Wheelers & Micromobility (5 mature, 3 scaling, 1 demonstration) · Commercial, Heavy-Duty & Off-Road EVs (1 mature, 7 scaling, 3 demonstration, 1 pilot) · EV Charging & Grid Integration (3 mature, 6 scaling, 1 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries (1 mature, 4 scaling, 3 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Battery Materials, Components, Powertrain & R... (6 mature, 2 scaling, 2 demonstration) · Aviation Decarbonization (2 scaling, 5 demonstration, 5 pilot) · Maritime Decarbonization (1 mature, 3 scaling, 5 demonstration, 1 lab) · Rail, Hydrogen for Transport & E-fuels (1 mature, 4 scaling, 7 demonstration)

**Solution areas:** [Passenger & Light-Duty EVs](#passenger-light-duty-evs) · [Electric Two/Three-Wheelers & Micromobility](#electric-twothree-wheelers-micromobility) · [Commercial, Heavy-Duty & Off-Road EVs](#commercial-heavy-duty-off-road-evs) · [EV Charging & Grid Integration](#ev-charging-grid-integration) · [Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries](#battery-cells-next-gen-chemistries) · [Battery Materials, Components, Powertrain & Recycling](#battery-materials-components-powertrain-recycling) · [Aviation Decarbonization](#aviation-decarbonization) · [Maritime Decarbonization](#maritime-decarbonization) · [Rail, Hydrogen for Transport & E-fuels](#rail-hydrogen-for-transport-e-fuels)

| [Sono Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sono_Motors) | startup | Canceled its crowdfunded Sion solar car after insolvency and pivoted to retrofit solar kits for buses and trucks (customers include Mitsubishi Europe, CHEREAU, Scania, MAN). | Sion program scrapped Feb 2023 with ~45k reservations; relaunched post-insolvency as a solar-retrofit supplier; Sion prototypes auctioned Aug 2025 |

> **White space:** Both flagship solar-car startups failed (Lightyear bankrupt, Sono's Sion canceled) and Aptera is still pre-revenue after years — physics caps on-vehicle PV near 1 kW, so a standalone 'solar carmaker' only pencils with extreme lightweighting. The credible opening is solar as a feature: OEM roof options, retrofit kits for fleets, and sun-rich-market microcars/LSVs where 20-40 km/day of free range covers most trips.

| [Stellantis (Citroën Ami / Fiat Topolino / Opel Rocks-e)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_Ami_(electric_vehicle)) | incumbent | Mass-produced ~€8k L6e quadricycle drivable from age 14 in France, sold through vending-machine-simple retail. | 75,000+ units across 18 markets since 2020; France's best-selling quadricycle |
| [Micro Mobility Systems (Microlino)](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/first-drive-the-2025-microlino-is-a-euro-friendly-ev-with-throwback-good-looks/) | scaleup | Swiss kick-scooter maker building the premium bubble-car-styled Microlino L7e quadricycle in Turin. | ~3,700 vehicles produced in 2024, first full production year; ~£20k price point |
| [Renault Mobilize (Duo)](https://cleantechnica.com/2025/10/20/amsterdams-tiny-electric-cars-are-not-just-golf-carts-that-went-to-design-school/) | incumbent | 80 km/h two-seat quadricycle sold partly by subscription, Renault's bet on sub-car urban mobility. | Launched 2025 in Europe as the Ami's direct upmarket competitor |
| [Eli Electric (Eli Zero)](https://newatlas.com/automotive/eli-zero-electric-micro-car) | startup | Builds a $11,990 neighborhood electric vehicle (NEV/LSV) targeting US suburbs, already sold as an L6e in Europe. | US deliveries to reservation holders began 2025 after regulatory delays |
| [NIU Technologies](https://electrek.co/2025/11/04/nius-scooter-sized-electric-microcar-is-actually-headed-for-production/) | scaleup | Chinese smart-scooter maker moving up into a scooter-priced enclosed electric microcar. | Microcar confirmed headed to production (Nov 2025); leverages existing two-wheeler retail network |
| [⚠️ ElectraMeccanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ElectraMeccanica) | startup | Canadian maker of the single-seat Solo three-wheeler — recalled and bought back every vehicle in 2023, ending the program. | All ~400 Solos repurchased Feb 2023; vehicle business wound down and shell merged with Xos in 2024 · **☠ shut down** |
| [Arcimoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcimoto) | startup | Oregon maker of the three-wheeled 'Fun Utility Vehicle' tandem EV that could never get unit costs below price. | Production halted since 2023 amid funding collapse, mass layoffs and delisting threats; no credible restart · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Crowded in Europe and China but nearly empty in the US, where no federal quadricycle class exists and the 25 mph low-speed-vehicle rule strands products between golf carts and cars — a regulatory void that helped kill Arcimoto and ElectraMeccanica. An opening exists for whoever cracks US homologation (a 35-45 mph 'medium-speed' class or state-level carve-outs) with a sub-$12k product like Eli's.

**EV skateboard platforms & contract manufacturers** · `🟠 demonstration`

Companies that sell modular EV rolling chassis ('skateboards') or assemble complete EVs under contract, letting brands launch vehicles without owning factories or full-stack engineering — attempting to do for cars what Foxconn did for phones.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Foxconn / Foxtron](https://evxl.co/2025/12/19/foxconn-foxtron-acquires-luxgen/) | incumbent | Electronics giant's EV arm offering the open MIH platform and contract assembly; its Model C sells as the Luxgen n7 in Taiwan. | Acquired Luxgen brand for ~$25M Dec 2025; MOU to supply Mitsubishi-badged EVs for Oceania from H2 2026; n7 was Taiwan's #2 EV at launch |
| [Magna Steyr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna_Steyr) | incumbent | Veteran full-vehicle contract manufacturer in Graz (built Jaguar I-Pace and Fisker Ocean) with its own EV platform engineering services. | Lost anchor EV client when Fisker went bankrupt 2024; Graz capacity underutilized, actively courting new EV programs |
| [REE Automotive](https://www.greencarreports.com/news/1141987_ree-electric-truck-by-wire-us-certified) | startup | Israeli developer of REEcorner x-by-wire modules packing motor, steering, brakes and suspension into the wheel corners of a flat skateboard. | P7-C was first fully by-wire vehicle FMVSS-certified in the US; ~$60M order book; pivoting toward licensing its software-defined-vehicle stack amid cash constraints |
| [U Power Technology](https://www.upincar.com/) | startup | Chinese 'UP Super Board' skateboard chassis venture aiming to supply niche brands and ride-hailing OEMs. | Nasdaq-listed 2023 (UCAR) but minimal vehicle revenue; little verified commercial traction since · *status unverified* |
| [⚠️ Canoo](https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/17/ev-startup-canoo-files-for-bankruptcy-and-ceases-operations/) | startup | Built lifestyle vans and pickups on a steer-by-wire skateboard it once pitched as a platform for Hyundai and others. | Chapter 7 liquidation Jan 2025, ceased operations immediately; ~$164M liabilities vs $126M assets · **☠ shut down** |
| [Geely (SEA architecture)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainable_Experience_Architecture) | incumbent | Licenses and shares its Sustainable Experience Architecture across Zeekr, Volvo EX30, smart, Polestar and external partners — the closest thing to a high-volume third-party EV platform. | SEA underpins millions of vehicles across 6+ brands; smart JV with Mercedes built entirely on it |
| [⚠️ VDL Nedcar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VDL_Nedcar) | incumbent | The Netherlands' only large contract car plant; after BMW pulled the MINI contract it failed to land a replacement EV client (talks with Rivian and Canoo collapsed). | Car assembly ended March 2024 with thousands of layoffs; site repurposed away from vehicles (parent VDL Groep remains solvent) · **☠ shut down** |
| [CATL (CIIC / Panshi chassis)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_Amperex_Technology) | incumbent | World's largest battery maker selling an integrated cell-to-chassis skateboard so new entrants and legacy brands can skip platform R&D. | Panshi/Bedrock chassis unveiled Dec 2024; first applications with Avatr; pitching international licensees |

> **White space:** Pure skateboard startups keep dying (Canoo Ch7 2025, Arrival 2024) and contract plants keep losing anchors (Magna-Fisker, VDL-MINI) because credible volume customers barely exist — incumbents own factories and startups die before reaching volume. The model that works is Foxconn's: regional assembly inside tariff walls plus white-label platforms for legacy brands that lack EV R&D (Mitsubishi-Foxtron), and Chinese platform licensing (Geely SEA, CATL) is the likely consolidation path.

**ICE-to-EV passenger conversions & classic-car retrofits** · `🟠 demonstration`

Specialists that remove combustion drivetrains from existing or classic cars and install electric ones, extending vehicle life and avoiding the embodied emissions of a new car — economically viable today mainly at luxury restomod price points.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Everrati](https://www.drivingelectric.com/electric/1819/electric-classic-cars-costs-companies-and-conversions) | startup | OEM-grade 'redefined' electric conversions of icons (Porsche 911 964, Land Rover Series, GT40) with reversible installs preserving originality. | Operating since 2019 with US build partners; six-figure price points and order books across UK/US |
| [Electrogenic](https://electrek.co/guides/ev-conversion/) | startup | Sells type-tested drop-in conversion kits (Land Rover Defender, Jaguar E-Type, Citroën DS) and holds UK defense contracts for electrified Land Rovers. | Kit network expanded to US installers in Vermont and Texas; one of the few converters with a scalable kit model |
| [Lunaz Design](https://www.electrive.com/2024/03/19/lunaz-applied-technologies-goes-into-administration/) | startup | Beckham-backed luxury electrification of Rolls-Royce, Bentley, Aston Martin and Range Rover classics at Silverstone. | Sister company Lunaz Applied Technologies (electric bin lorries) entered administration Mar 2024, pausing the group; Lunaz Design resumed restructured operations May 2024 |
| [⚠️ Transition-One](https://journalauto.com/services/retrofit-clap-de-fin-pour-transition-one/) | startup | French pioneer of certified low-cost (~€5-8k) retrofit kits for mass-market cars like the Twingo and Fiat 500; helped write France's retrofit regulation. | Judicial liquidation Mar 2023 after a €5M raise failed — founder blamed lack of industrialization financing · **☠ shut down** |
| [R-FIT](https://www.r-fit.fr/) | startup | Sells Renault-endorsed homologated retrofit kits for classic Renault 4, 5 and Twingo, installed through the Renault network. | Partnership unveiled with Renault in 2023; kits from ~€12k including battery |
| [Rev Mobilities](https://www.autoactu.com/actualites/la-societe-transition-one-pionniere-du-retrofit-electrique-liquidee) | startup | French retrofit integrator converting passenger cars and light fleets, one of the survivors consolidating the French retrofit market. | Secured new investment after pioneer Transition-One was liquidated |
| [EV West](https://www.topspeed.com/ice-cars-to-ev-conversion-companies/) | startup | Long-running California shop supplying conversion components and Tesla-crate-motor swaps that seeded the US DIY conversion ecosystem. | Operating since 2010s with multi-year build backlog; parts business serves hundreds of independent converters |

> **White space:** Mass-market retrofit has repeatedly failed (Transition-One liquidated despite French subsidies and a regulation written around it) because kit-plus-labor cost rivals a used BEV; only luxury restomods clear margins. The opening is standardized, type-approved kits for a handful of iconic high-volume models installed through OEM dealer networks (the Renault/R-FIT pattern), or subsidy-backed fleet retrofits where duty cycles are predictable.

Smartphone and internet giants entering passenger EVs by leveraging brand, retail networks, software ecosystems and electronics supply-chain mastery instead of automotive heritage — compressing development cycles to ~3 years.

### Electric Two/Three-Wheelers & Micromobility

**Electric motorcycles (on-road and off-road)** · `🟡 scaling`

Battery-electric motorcycles replace petrol bikes for commuting, sport and off-road riding, eliminating tailpipe emissions and noise — but high prices and limited highway range have kept Western consumer demand thin, while India and profitable off-road niches grow.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Zero Motorcycles](https://techcrunch.com/2024/10/24/zero-motorcycles-is-raising-120-million/) | scaleup | Longest-running dedicated electric motorcycle OEM (US), full street/dual-sport lineup on its Z-Force powertrain | Raised $120M (Oct 2024); sales declined from 3,979 units (2022) to ~1,944 in first 9 months of 2025 |
| [LiveWire](https://www.theautopian.com/electric-motorcycle-companies-are-dying-left-and-right-as-people-just-arent-buying-enough-bikes/) | incumbent | Harley-Davidson's NYSE-listed electric spinoff selling premium S2/Del Mar models | Sold just 33 motorcycles in Q1 2025 (-72% YoY); kept afloat by Harley-Davidson backing, far from profitability |
| [Stark Future](https://electrek.co/2025/05/14/how-one-of-the-only-profitable-electric-motorcycle-companies-got-there-with-street-legal-e-dirtbikes/) | scaleup | Barcelona maker of the Varg electric motocross/supermoto bike; vertically integrated and one of the only profitable e-moto OEMs | 2025 revenue ~EUR 115M (+77% YoY) with profitable months (Apr 2025: $20.5M revenue, +$3.1M EBITDA); 400 retail locations in 50+ countries |

| [Oben Electric](https://india.entrepreneur.com/news-and-trends/oben-electric-bags-inr-85-cr-in-pre-series-b-round/501044) | startup | Bengaluru OEM of affordable LFP-battery commuter electric motorcycles (Rorr) built for Indian heat | Total funding ~INR 285 crore after INR 85 Cr pre-Series B (2025) |

| [Energica](https://electrek.co/2025/07/19/its-true-high-performance-electric-motorcycle-brand-energica-is-back/) | scaleup | Italian pioneer of high-performance electric sportbikes (Ego, Experia); former MotoE supplier | Filed bankruptcy Oct 2024 under Ideanomics ownership; taken over by Singapore investor group in 2025 with relaunch underway · **acquired** |

| [⚠️ Fuell](https://www.theautopian.com/electric-motorcycle-companies-are-dying-left-and-right-as-people-just-arent-buying-enough-bikes/) | startup | Erik Buell-founded e-motorcycle/e-bike startup (Fllow motorcycle, Flluid e-bikes) | Went out of business in 2024 leaving crowdfunding backers without products · **☠ shut down** |
| [⚠️ Sondors](https://www.theautopian.com/electric-motorcycle-companies-are-dying-left-and-right-as-people-just-arent-buying-enough-bikes/) | startup | Crowdfunded budget e-bike maker that attempted the Metacycle low-cost electric motorcycle | Ceased operations/went out of business (2023-24) after Metacycle quality and delivery failures · **☠ shut down** |

> **White space:** Player count is high but financial credibility is thin: Western consumer demand never materialized at premium prices (Energica, Cake, Fuell, Sondors all failed 2023-25) because range/price economics at highway speed favor ICE; the proven openings are profitable performance niches with vertical integration (Stark model) and low-cost commuter bikes in motorcycle-first markets (India, SE Asia, LatAm).

**Two-wheeler electric conversion & retrofit kits** · `🟠 demonstration`

Type-approved retrofit kits convert existing petrol scooters/motorcycles (and ordinary bicycles) to electric drive at a fraction of new-vehicle cost, decarbonizing the installed fleet instead of waiting for replacement cycles.

Hero Splendor, Honda Activa) | ARAI-approved kits from ~INR 35,000 (to ~INR 95,000 with battery); installation network across 36 RTOs |
| [Swytch](https://www.cnn.com/cnn-underscored/reviews/swytch-electric-bike-conversion-kit) | scaleup | UK maker of compact wheel-swap kits that convert any pedal bicycle into an e-bike | 80,000+ bikes converted worldwide; claims 1 in 14 new UK e-bikes is a Swytch conversion; MAX+ kit rolled out 2025 |

> **White space:** Genuinely sparse: per-model homologation (RTO/ARAI type approval) is slow and expensive, kit-plus-battery cost approaches a cheap used EV, and liability/battery certification scares installers — so only a handful of credible players exist; the opening is B2B fleet retrofits (delivery fleets, boda-boda cooperatives, municipal fleets) where one approved model covers thousands of identical vehicles and TCO math is decisive.

The credible openings are standardized kits for captive high-utilization fleets whose chassis outlive powertrains (refuse, terminal tractors, transit buses), retrofit-friendly regulatory regimes (France's décret rétrofit, India), and battery-swap conversions like Janus where charging infrastructure is the binding constraint.

**Electrified trailers & range-extending add-ons** · `🔵 pilot`

Powered e-axles, battery dollies and electric trailer hubs add traction or power to the trailer itself, cutting a diesel tractor's fuel 20-40% or extending a BEV tractor's range — electrifying freight without replacing the truck.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Range Energy](https://www.ttnews.com/articles/range-energy-new-financing) | startup | Powered eTrailer with a force-sensing smart kingpin that assists any tractor — no truck modification — cutting fuel use roughly a third. | $31.5M raised (incl. $23.5M round Feb 2024 with Yamaha, UP.Partners); fleet pilots moving to production |
| [Revoy](https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/revoy) | startup | Swappable-battery 'EV dolly' inserted between tractor and trailer with corridor swap stations, sold per-mile so diesel trucks run as near-EVs on set lanes. | Venture-backed; commercial corridor service live in the US South-Central since 2024 |
| [ConMet eMobility](https://conmet.com) | incumbent | PreSet Plus eHub in-wheel motors on trailer axles that regenerate braking energy to power electric refrigeration units (TRUs). | Commercial pilots with major reefer fleets |
| [ZF](https://www.zf.com) | incumbent | Trailer e-axles (AxTrax LF) and eTrailer systems supplied to trailer OEMs for recuperation and traction assist. | Tier-1 scale supplier bringing trailer electrification to series production |

> **White space:** Very few credible players because powered trailers sit in a regulatory grey zone (weight allowances, braking rules) and the industry splits incentives — tractor owners buy fuel while trailer owners buy trailers. An opening exists for per-mile leased range-extension that leaves the tractor and its warranty untouched, bridging fleets to electrification years before Class 8 BEVs and megawatt charging are ubiquitous.

**Battery-swap heavy trucks & swap ecosystems** · `🟡 scaling`

Heavy trucks with standardized swappable packs decouple the battery from the vehicle purchase and refuel in ~5 minutes, which is why roughly a third of China's surging electric heavy-truck sales are swap-capable — the fastest route to diesel parity in 24/7 freight.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CATL (Qiji Energy)](https://carnewschina.com/2025/12/23/catl-launched-longest-1250-km-battery-swap-route-in-china/) | incumbent | Built the #75 standardized swappable heavy-truck pack and a national swap-station network, including a 1,250 km Chengdu-Shanghai corridor opened Dec 2025. | Stations compatible with 95% of mainstream Chinese HDT models; 300-station target; CEO projects 50% HDT electrification by 2028 |
| [SPIC (Qiyuan)](https://english.news.cn/20250528/c9dfae07666647ebb347f0e1abdb6583/c.html) | incumbent | State Power Investment Corp arm that pioneered battery-as-a-service financing and operates one of China's largest swap-truck/station fleets. | Battery-swap models were ~32% of China's Q1 2025 new-energy heavy truck sales |
| [XCMG](https://thedriven.io/2025/08/05/sales-of-battery-electric-heavy-trucks-surge-in-china-to-nearly-one-quarter-of-market/) | incumbent | Among the top sellers of new-energy heavy trucks in China, including swap-capable tractors for mines, ports and steel logistics. | China NEV heavy truck sales hit ~25% penetration mid-2025 and >30% by Nov 2025 (28,000 units that month) |
| [SANY](https://thedriven.io/2025/08/05/sales-of-battery-electric-heavy-trucks-surge-in-china-to-nearly-one-quarter-of-market/) | incumbent | Leading electric heavy truck OEM offering both charge and swap variants plus its own swap stations. | Consistently top-3 in China NEV HDT sales |
| [FAW Jiefang](https://govt.chinadaily.com.cn/s/202505/28/WS6836d6d5498eec7e1f737f84/next-generation-battery-swap-ecosystem-empowers-chinas-heavy-duty-truck-sector.html) | incumbent | China's biggest truck maker; J6-based swap-capable e-tractors integrated with the Qiji standardized-pack ecosystem. | Among a dozen OEMs with 30+ truck models compatible with CATL's 75# pack |

> **White space:** Outside China this approach is nearly empty (Australia's Janus Electric is the lone notable player) because swap needs pack standardization across OEMs — a chicken-and-egg no western truck maker will start. The opening is corridor consortia (drayage lanes, mining/port shuttles) adopting a standard pack with battery-as-a-service financing, potentially importing CATL's proven 75# model.

### EV Charging & Grid Integration

**Public DC fast-charging networks & CPOs** · `🟡 scaling`

Companies that build, own and operate public DC fast-charging stations and sell electrons to drivers; they are the backbone that makes road trips and EV ownership without home charging viable.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Tesla Supercharger](https://www.tesla.com/supercharger) | incumbent | World's largest and most reliable DCFC network; its NACS connector became the de facto North American standard and is now open to other brands. | ~65,000-70,000 connectors globally; nearly all major OEMs adopted NACS 2023-2025 |
| [EVgo](https://electrek.co/2024/12/13/evgo-closes-a-1-25b-federal-loan-to-build-7500-dc-fast-chargers/) | scaleup | US owner-operator of urban-focused public fast charging with dense metro coverage and autonomous-fleet charging contracts. | Closed $1.25B DOE loan guarantee Dec 2024 to add ~7,500 stalls, reaching 10,000+ stalls by 2029; NYSE-listed |
| [Electrify America](https://www.electrifyamerica.com) | incumbent | VW-funded open DCFC network created after Dieselgate; largest open ultra-fast network in the US. | ~1,000 stations / 4,500+ ultra-fast chargers across US and Canada |
| [Ionity](https://ionity.eu) | scaleup | European highway HPC joint venture of BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Ford, VW and Hyundai focused on 350 kW corridor charging. | 600+ stations / thousands of 350 kW points in 24 countries; ~EUR 700M round led by BlackRock (2021) |
| [Fastned](https://fastnedcharging.com) | scaleup | Dutch listed pure-play CPO building canopy-covered fast-charging hubs, profitable at station level; co-founded the Spark Alliance roaming pact. | Euronext-listed; 350+ stations across Europe; Spark Alliance with Ionity, Electra and Atlante (2025) |
| [Electra](https://www.electrive.com/2025/07/24/electra-secures-e433-million-loan-for-european-hpc-rollout/) | startup | French urban/metro fast-charging hub developer with app-led UX, expanding across Western Europe. | Raised over EUR 1B total including EUR 433M green loan (Jul 2025) |

**Megawatt charging systems (MCS) for heavy trucks** · `🟠 demonstration`

Megawatt Charging System hardware and hubs deliver 1 MW+ so long-haul electric trucks can recharge during the driver's mandated 30-45 minute break, removing the core objection to battery freight; first real deployments began 2024-2025.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [WattEV](https://wattev.com/mcs-charging-technology-for-heavy-duty-trucks/) | startup | Builds solar-microgrid electric truck stops in California and sells trucking-as-a-service; early public MCS deployer. | Multiple CA freight-corridor depots including Bakersfield solar microgrid; megawatt-ready design across network |
| [ABB E-mobility](https://www.electrive.com/2025/09/24/man-and-abb-refine-reliability-of-mcs-charging-sessions/) | incumbent | MCS1200 delivering a full 1.2 MW continuously, validated in long-duration sessions with MAN trucks. | Continuous 1.2 MW charge sessions demonstrated with MAN (2025); pilot deliveries underway |
| [Kempower](https://www.evinfrastructurenews.com/ev-fleet-charging/megawatt-charging-for-trucks-the-complete-guide-to-mcs-charging-infrastructure-in-2026) | scaleup | Launched a modular megawatt charging product line aimed at truck stops and depots. | MCS hardware at early multi-MW public truck hubs in EU/US |
| [Power Electronics](https://www.evcandi.com/news/milence-and-power-electronics-successfully-test-new-megawatt-charging-system) | incumbent | Co-developed and field-tested a new MCS unit with Milence for public truck hubs. | Successful MCS system test with Milence (2025) |
| [Tesla (Semi Megacharger)](https://www.tesla.com/semi) | incumbent | Proprietary ~1.2 MW Megachargers for the Tesla Semi, with a corridor network planned alongside Semi volume production. | Megachargers live at PepsiCo/Tesla sites; Semi volume ramp targeted 2026 |
| [BYD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYD_Auto) | incumbent | 1,000 kW 'flash charging' Super e-Platform for passenger cars and a planned national megawatt charging buildout in China. | Launched 1 MW flash charging Mar 2025; thousands of stations planned across China |
| [Huawei Digital Power](https://www.evinfrastructurenews.com/ev-fleet-charging/megawatt-charging-for-trucks-the-complete-guide-to-mcs-charging-infrastructure-in-2026) | incumbent | 1.5 MW liquid-cooled megawatt charger aimed at Chinese electric heavy trucks and highway freight corridors. | 1.5 MW truck charger unveiled 2025; deployments with Chinese CPO partners |

> **White space:** Hardware now exists, but multi-megawatt grid interconnections take 3-7 years in the US/EU — the opening is in battery-buffered or flexible-interconnect MCS hubs and in financing structures that de-risk utilization before electric long-haul truck volumes arrive.

**Battery swapping (cars and 2/3-wheelers)** · `🟡 scaling`

Robotic stations exchange a depleted pack for a full one in 3-5 minutes, decoupling refueling speed from battery chemistry; it is scaling rapidly in China and for Asian two/three-wheelers while repeatedly failing in Western passenger-car markets (Better Place 2013, Ample 2025).

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [Battery Smart](https://blume.vc/commentaries/hidden-in-plain-sight-how-two-iitians-electrified-indias-last-mile-one-battery-swap-at-a-time) | startup | India's largest swap network for electric two/three-wheelers on a franchise, battery-as-a-service model. | ~1,500 stations across 50 cities, 125,000+ swaps/day; $65M Series B (2024) plus 2026 follow-on |

> **White space:** Passenger-car swapping only works where one player controls pack standardization at scale — China's CATL/NIO advantage; the Western opening is not consumer cars (Ample's failure confirms it) but standardized commercial fleets and 2/3-wheeler markets in emerging economies.

Inductive pads in pavement — static or dynamic 'electric roads' — charge vehicles without plugs, promising hands-free top-ups for transit and future autonomous fleets, but cost-per-kW, alignment and efficiency still trail cables badly and the sector just consolidated.

| [HEVO](https://hevo.com) | startup | Brooklyn startup making compact wireless charging pads with utility and DOE/national-lab pilot projects. | Small DOE/Oak Ridge-linked pilots; early commercial product |

> **White space:** Physics and cost keep this thin: inductive transfer adds $/kW and efficiency loss versus a cable, and no OEM factory-fits at volume; the credible opening is hands-free static charging for autonomous and transit fleets where eliminating charging labor justifies the premium — not consumer cars or long highway segments (Sweden postponed its permanent e-road).

**V2G/bidirectional & managed-charging software** · `🟡 scaling`

Software and bidirectional hardware that times millions of EV charging sessions against grid needs and can discharge vehicle batteries to homes or the grid, turning the EV fleet into the cheapest grid battery available; unidirectional managed charging is commercial at scale while true V2G is in early deployment.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [WeaveGrid](https://chargedevs.com/newswire/lg-technology-ventures-invests-in-weavegrid-to-advance-ev-grid-integration/) | startup | Telematics-based managed-charging software sold to utilities (PG&E, DTE, Xcel) integrating directly with automakers' vehicle APIs. | $28M round (Dec 2024) plus strategic investments from Hyundai/Kia (Jan 2025) and LG (Sep 2025); named a VPP leader by Wood Mackenzie 2025 |
| [ev.energy](https://ev.energy) | startup | Driver-app-led managed charging platform running utility programs across the US, UK and Europe. | Series B ~$33M (2023, National Grid Partners); dozens of utility programs live |
| [ChargeScape](https://www.utilitydive.com/spons/chargescape-and-the-future-of-energy-management/744270/) | startup | Automaker-owned (BMW, Ford, Honda, Nissan) vehicle-grid-integration platform connecting OEM telematics to utilities for V1G today and V2X programs next. | Four-OEM JV; live utility enrollments (e.g., 1,400 DTE customers by mid-2025); V2G/V2H programs launching |
| [Kaluza](https://www.kaluza.com) | scaleup | OVO-spun energy flexibility platform orchestrating smart tariffs, EV charging and V2G for retailers like OVO and AGL. | AGL took a ~20% stake (2023); powers UK smart/V2G tariffs |
| [The Mobility House](https://www.mobilityhouse.com) | scaleup | German aggregator monetizing EV and stationary batteries in power markets; runs commercial V2G with Renault Mobilize in France. | Backed by Mercedes-Benz, Renault and Mitsubishi; trading EV flexibility in EU markets |
| [Nuvve](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/NVVE/) | scaleup | V2G pioneer focused on electric school buses and fleet hubs. | Deeply distressed: Q4 2025 revenue $1.95M, $5.5M cash; pivoting to stationary battery aggregation and BaaS |
| [Fermata Energy](https://fermataenergy.com) | startup | Bidirectional charger hardware plus software platform monetizing parked fleet vehicles (demand-charge shaving, utility programs). | UL-certified bidirectional chargers; utility programs including Duke Energy |
| [dcbel](https://www.dcbel.energy) | startup | Home bidirectional DC station (Ara) combining solar inverter, V2H and home energy management. | Tens of millions raised; UL-listed home V2X hardware rolling out in North America |
| [Sunrun](https://www.sunrun.com) | incumbent | Largest US residential solar installer turned EV-grid player: installs Ford F-150 Lightning V2H systems and runs vehicle-battery VPP pilots. | Ford Home Integration System partner; PG&E vehicle-to-home/VPP pilots |
| [EnergyHub](https://www.energyhub.com) | incumbent | Alarm.com-owned DERMS that folds EV managed charging into broader demand-response portfolios for dozens of utilities. | EV programs live across 60+ utility clients |

**Battery-buffered, off-grid, solar-canopy & mobile chargers** · `🟡 scaling`

Chargers with integrated battery storage — fixed cabinets, solar canopies or trucks/trailers — deliver fast charging where the grid is weak or interconnection is years away, and can stack revenue from demand-charge avoidance and grid services; FreeWire's collapse shows the unit economics are unforgiving.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [ADS-TEC Energy](https://www.energy-storage.news/ads-tec-battery-buffered-ev-fast-chargers-put-into-ancillary-services-market-in-austria/) | scaleup | German-Irish maker of battery-buffered ChargeBox/ChargePost cabinets that deliver 300 kW+ from low-power grid connections, now also selling grid services. | NASDAQ-listed (ADSE); units earning ancillary-service revenue in Austria; partnership with Jolt targeting 5,000 fueling stations |
| [Jolt Energy](https://www.electrive.com/2024/10/10/jolt-energy-to-build-50-battery-buffered-hpcs-in-and-around-stockholm/) | startup | Munich CPO deploying ad-financed, battery-buffered street fast chargers in city centers (free first kWhs funded by screens). | Building 50 battery-buffered HPCs around Stockholm (2024); BlackRock-backed rollouts in DACH/US |
| [⚠️ FreeWire Technologies](https://electrek.co/2024/05/05/freewire-closes-its-hq-and-lays-off-just-about-everyone/) | startup | Pioneered the battery-integrated Boost Charger for sites without grid upgrades. | Raised $200M+, then closed HQ May 2024, terminated ~113 staff and sold assets in distress · **☠ shut down** |
| [SparkCharge](https://www.sparkcharge.io/post/sparkcharge-raises-30-5-million-in-capital-to-accelerate-mobile-ev-charging-expansion) | startup | Mobile charging-as-a-service: battery-equipped vans and portable units deliver charging to fleets with no infrastructure. | $30.5M raised (Series A-1 + venture debt, 2025); operations across US, Mexico, Canada |
| [Beam Global](https://beamforall.com) | scaleup | EV ARC transportable solar-canopy-plus-storage chargers requiring no grid connection, sold mainly to government and municipal buyers. | NASDAQ-listed (BEEM); hundreds of EV ARC units deployed but revenue declined sharply 2024-25 |
| [Electric Era](https://electricera.tech) | startup | SpaceX-alumni startup building battery-buffered PowerNode fast-charging stations with high-uptime software for convenience retailers. | Venture-backed; dozens of battery-buffered stations live across the US |
| [ElectricFish](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/443277-01) | startup | 350 kW battery-integrated charging cubes that double as community resilience/microgrid assets. | Seed/grant-funded; early deployments |

> **White space:** Demand charges and multi-year interconnection queues create the niche, but hardware capex plus battery degradation crushed FreeWire even with $200M+ raised — the viable models pair the battery with a second revenue stack (ADS-TEC's ancillary services, Jolt's ad financing) rather than selling boxes alone.

**Charging software platforms, roaming & payments** · `🟢 mature`

The back-office layer — charge-point management systems, roaming hubs, Plug&Charge identity and payments — that lets any driver use any charger and any operator bill for it; standards (OCPP/OCPI/ISO 15118) make this a consolidating platform game.

| [Gireve](https://www.gireve.com) | incumbent | French roaming hub connecting CPOs and eMSPs across Europe, backed by EDF, Renault and Caisse des Depots. | Hundreds of thousands of connected charge points across Europe |

| [Driivz](https://driivz.com) | scaleup | White-label charging management platform powering major networks including EVgo. | Acquired by Vontier (2022); runs some of the largest CPO back-ends · **acquired** |
| [AMPECO](https://www.ampeco.com/us/press_release/ampeco-and-hubject-announce-a-global-strategic-partnership-to-deliver-plugcharge-and-roaming-services-to-ev-charging-providers/) | startup | White-label, hardware-agnostic charging management platform for CPOs in 65+ countries. | $26M Series B (2024); global strategic partnership with Hubject (2025) |

**Curbside & pole-mounted urban charging** · `🟡 scaling`

Compact L2 (and now compact DC) chargers on lampposts, utility poles and detachable-cable curb posts serve the huge population of drivers without driveways — often piggybacking on existing streetlight or building power to dodge utility interconnection costs; the UK has scaled it, the US is just starting.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [ubitricity](https://www.ubitricity.com) | incumbent | Shell-owned lamppost-charging operator; the UK's largest public charging network by point count. | ~10,000 lamppost/bollard charge points, mostly in London |
| [itselectric](https://www.evcandi.com/news/itselectric-gets-funding-accelerate-curbside-ev-charging-across-us) | startup | Brooklyn startup whose detachable-cable curb posts draw spare capacity from adjacent buildings and share revenue with property owners — no utility interconnection needed. | $6.5M seed extension (total ~$11.8M, Uber among backers); expanding to seven US cities; first curbside V2G pilot in California |
| [Voltpost](https://electrek.co/2026/04/30/washington-dc-street-poles-ev-chargers-voltpost/) | startup | Retrofits existing lampposts into modular L2 chargers in about an hour. | NYC deployments; won Washington DC DOEE public-charging grant (2026) |
| [Gravity](https://insideevs.com/news/765318/new-york-curbside-ev-charger-voltpost/) | startup | Ultra-compact 500 kW curbside DC 'trees' and fast fleet hubs that fit a fast charger in a parking-meter footprint. | Google-backed; 200 kW Manhattan fleet hub plus 500 kW curbside units deployed in NYC |
| [Trojan Energy](https://chargedevs.com/newswire/curbside-charger-maker-trojan-energy-secures-26-million-in-investment/) | startup | Scottish maker of flat-and-flush in-pavement connectors that leave no street furniture when not in use. | GBP 26M raised (BGF and Scottish National Investment Bank) |
| [char.gy](https://char.gy) | startup | UK lamppost and on-street charging operator winning council-wide concessions under the government's LEVI fund. | Thousands of on-street chargers across UK boroughs; multiple LEVI contract wins |
| [Connected Kerb](https://www.connectedkerb.com) | scaleup | UK on-street charging infrastructure with below-ground electronics designed for 25-year life. | GBP 110M from Aviva Investors (2022); thousands of sockets installed, though growth has lagged plan |

> **White space:** Outside the UK this is wide open: US curbside barely exists because utility make-ready costs and curb permitting kill L2 economics — models that bypass interconnection via building or streetlight power (itselectric, Voltpost) are the wedge, and no one yet owns the US city-franchise playbook.

**Robotic & automated charging** · `🔵 pilot`

Robot arms or mobile robots plug in and charge vehicles autonomously, eliminating charging labor for ports, depots and robotaxi fleets and enabling 24/7 asset utilization — the conductive, near-term alternative to wireless for hands-free charging.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Rocsys](https://rocsys.com) | startup | Dutch leader retrofitting soft-robotics arms onto standard CCS chargers for hands-free charging of terminal tractors, trucks and autonomous fleets. | ~$36M raised; deployments at US container terminals and truck depots |
| [Hyundai Motor Group](https://www.hyundai.com/worldwide/en) | incumbent | Developed an Automatic Charging Robot (ACR) deployed in pilots including its Singapore smart factory and robotaxi operations. | ACR demonstrations and pilot deployments since 2023 |
| [Mob-Energy](https://www.mob-energy.com) | startup | French startup whose 'Charles' mobile robot roams parking garages delivering battery-buffered charging to parked cars. | ~EUR 10M raised; deployments in French parking structures |
| [EV Safe Charge](https://evsafecharge.com) | startup | Developed ZiGGY, a mobile charging robot for hotels and venues. | Prototype and pilot announcements 2022-23; little public traction since · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Almost nobody is at commercial stage here — Rocsys is nearly alone — yet the demand driver is compounding: robotaxi fleets (Waymo et al.) still charge with human labor, and autonomous trucking depots will need hands-free megawatt charging; a focused player that standardizes robot-ready connectors with OEMs could own the category.

### Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries

**Incumbent giga-scale cell makers** · `🟢 mature`

Vertically integrated giants mass-produce lithium-ion EV cells (NMC and LFP) at tens-to-hundreds of GWh per year, driving the cost declines that make EVs competitive with combustion cars.

New entrants and OEM-backed ventures build gigafactories outside the China-Korea-Japan oligopoly to localize EV cell supply in Europe and North America — a capital-intensive race where several flagship players have already failed.

**Solid-state batteries** · `🟠 demonstration`

Replacing the flammable liquid electrolyte with a solid (sulfide, oxide-ceramic or polymer) promises higher energy density and safety, and is now moving from lab to B-samples in demo vehicles and first giga-level plants.
