| [Toyota](https://eepower.com/tech-insights/solid-state-batteries-race-to-mass-production/) | incumbent | Largest corporate solid-state program (with Idemitsu on sulfide electrolyte), targeting first production vehicles around 2027-28 | Re-confirmed 2027 rollout target on its battery roadmap |
| [Samsung SDI](https://eepower.com/tech-insights/solid-state-batteries-race-to-mass-production/) | incumbent | Sulfide all-solid-state (ASB) pilot line in Suwon producing samples for automakers | Targeting 2027 mass production of all-solid-state cells |
| [WeLion New Energy](https://sustainableskies.org/even-more-solid-state-batteries/) | scaleup | Chinese maker of semi-solid (hybrid electrolyte) cells already shipping in NIO's 150 kWh swappable pack | Semi-solid packs in commercial use with NIO since 2024 — the first road-going 'solid-state-adjacent' EV cells |
| [Blue Solutions (Bolloré)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_battery) | incumbent | Only company with years of commercial polymer solid-state cells in service (Mercedes eCitaro buses), now developing a gen-4 EV cell | Decade of fleet deployment in buses and car-sharing; gen-4 plant planned in France |

**Lithium-metal & anode-free cells** · `🔵 pilot`

Replacing the graphite anode with thin lithium metal — or no anode at all — can boost energy density 50-100%, but dendrite growth and manufacturing yield have killed or redirected most ventures.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [SES AI](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/SES/ses-ai-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-k7p7atr3lj0a.html) | startup | MIT spinout whose Li-metal EV A-sample program morphed into an AI materials-discovery platform (Molecular Universe) plus drone and ESS battery sales | NYSE-listed; pivoted factories to drones; ~10x sales growth with 2025 revenue guidance of $15-25M — EV li-metal effectively deprioritized |
| [Ion Storage Systems](https://chargedevs.com/newswire/ion-storage-systems-qualifies-its-solid-state-battery-cells-with-a-customer-production-to-start-this-year/) | startup | Anode-free, compression-free ceramic solid-state cell using a 3D garnet electrolyte structure (University of Maryland spinout) | First multilayer cells off semi-automated Beltsville line March 2025; $20M ARPA-E SCALEUP award; first customer qualification with production starting 2025 |
| [Pure Lithium](https://purelithium.io/) | startup | Vertically integrated lithium-metal-on-LFP cell with a brine-to-anode extraction process that skips conventional lithium refining | 150+ patents/applications; claims Gen-1 Li-LFP cell with 2x LFP energy density and 6,500+ cycles |
| [Sion Power](https://sionpower.com/) | startup | Arizona developer of large-format Licerion lithium-metal cells for EV and defense applications | Long-running program (ex Li-S pioneer); current commercial traction unclear as of 2026 · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** This space is thinning, not crowding: Northvolt shut its Cuberg li-metal unit (2024) and SES pivoted to software/drones, evidence that dendrite suppression plus manufacturable yield remains unsolved economics; the opening is defense- and aviation-funded niches where $/kWh matters less than Wh/kg, and anode-free architectures that piggyback on solid-state separators (Ion Storage, QuantumScape).

**Silicon-anode cell makers** · `🟡 scaling`

Swapping graphite for silicon-dominant anodes stores far more lithium per gram, yielding 20-80% higher energy density and faster charge — first commercialized in drones, defense and wearables where buyers pay premiums.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Amprius Technologies](https://dronelife.com/2025/05/05/amprius-launches-450-wh-kg-sicore-lithium-ion-battery-targeting-aviation-and-defense/) | startup | Highest-energy-density commercial cells (SiCore/SiMaxx, up to 450-500 Wh/kg) built on a silicon nanowire/silicon-dominant platform for UAVs, e-aviation and defense | NYSE-listed; $15M UAV purchase order Feb 2025; GWh-scale contract-manufacturing network; 450 Wh/kg SiCore launched May 2025 |
| [Enovix](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828318/000182831825000293/envx8-kxq3x90525exh991pr.htm) | startup | 3D-stacked cell architecture with 100% active silicon anode, ramping in Malaysia (Fab2) for smartphones/wearables with EV as a later market | AI-1 smartphone cell (900+ Wh/L) in commercial qualification; raised $232M via warrants in 2025 to accelerate Fab2 |
| [Ionblox](https://www.evcandi.com/news/ionblox-receives-us32m-funding-high-power-battery-cells) | startup | Pre-lithiated silicon-oxide pouch cells delivering both high power and fast charge, aimed at eVTOL aircraft and extreme-fast-charge EVs | Series B expanded to $32M with Temasek, Applied Ventures and Lilium; ~$60M total raised |
| [NanoGraf](https://www.batterytechonline.com/battery-manufacturing/nanograf-s-silicon-anode-technology-powers-critical-defense-equipment) | startup | Chicago maker of silicon-anode 18650 cells (M38, 3.8 Ah) for US military radios and equipment, onshoring the full cell supply chain | ~$45M cumulative DoD funding incl. $15M Army contract; tens of thousands of M38 cells produced 2024, scaling to hundreds of thousands in 2025; Thales design win |

> **White space:** Full silicon-anode cells at EV scale remain open territory — current players profitably serve drones/defense/consumer niches while EV silicon arrives mainly as anode-material blends from suppliers (Sila, Group14, in the Components bucket); whoever cracks automotive-grade cycle life and GWh cost first inherits a large premium-EV and eVTOL market.

**Lithium-sulfur cells** · `🔵 pilot`

Sulfur cathodes are dirt-cheap, abundant and free of nickel/cobalt, with 2-3x theoretical energy density of lithium-ion, but polysulfide shuttling has historically destroyed cycle life — a physics problem several startups now claim to have engineered around.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Lyten](https://cleantechnica.com/2025/08/07/us-startup-lyten-is-still-determined-to-make-a-lithium-sulfur-ev-battery-happen/) | startup | 3D-graphene-caged sulfur cathode Li-S cells; now also owns Northvolt's Swedish plants for dual lithium-ion/Li-S production | A-samples shipped to US/EU automakers from San Jose pilot line; >$1B Reno gigafactory (10 GWh) planned with phase 1 targeted 2027; Stellantis strategic investor |
| [Zeta Energy](https://www.electrive.com/2024/12/06/stellantis-and-zeta-energy-develop-lithium-sulfur-batteries/) | startup | Houston startup pairing a sulfurized-carbon cathode with a lithium-metal anode, claiming ~3x energy density at half the cost of li-ion | Joint development agreement with Stellantis (Dec 2024) targeting EV application by 2030 |
| [Theion](https://battery-tech.net/lithium-sulfur-battery-companies/) | startup | Berlin startup using monoclinic sulfur crystal cathodes grown directly, targeting 3x energy density at a fraction of cell cost | Founded 2020; venture-stage with aerospace/mobility sample ambitions |
| [Li-S Energy](https://battery-tech.net/lithium-sulfur-battery-companies/) | startup | ASX-listed Australian developer of semi-solid-state Li-S cells with boron-nitride nanotube stabilization, focused on drones and defense aviation | ASX:LIS; 45 Ah cells produced on its Geelong pilot line |
| [⚠️ OXIS Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium%E2%80%93sulfur_battery) | startup | UK Li-S pioneer with aviation and marine programs that ran out of cash before commercialization | Entered administration May 2021; IP sold (largely to Gelion) — the sector's cautionary tale · **☠ shut down** |
| [Stellantis](https://sustainableskies.org/stellantis-zeta-and-lytens-lithium-sulfur-battery/) | incumbent | Only major automaker betting on Li-S twice over — strategic investor in Lyten (2023) and JDA partner of Zeta Energy | Targets Li-S EV batteries around 2030 to cut pack cost and weight |

> **White space:** Barely a handful of credible players because polysulfide shuttle and lithium-metal anodes compound two unsolved problems; OXIS's collapse and Lyten's pivot toward conventional li-ion (via Northvolt assets) show the funding gap — the opening is weight-critical aviation, drone and defense markets that tolerate 200-500 cycle lives while cycle life improves.

**Sodium-ion for mobility** · `🟠 demonstration`

Sodium-ion cells swap lithium for abundant sodium, promising lower cost, no lithium/cobalt/copper exposure and excellent cold-weather and fast-charge behavior at ~10-20% lower energy density — now entering first mass production for cars in China.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CATL](https://carnewschina.com/2025/12/28/catl-confirms-2026-large-scale-sodium-ion-battery-deployment-in-multiple-sectors/) | incumbent | Naxtra sodium-ion brand (175 Wh/kg, -40°C operation) plus hybrid sodium-lithium packs via dual-power architecture | Naxtra launched April 2025, mass production from Dec 2025; first sodium EV (Changan Nevo A06) due mid-2026 |
| [HiNa Battery](https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/list-of-global-top-sodium-na-ion-sib-battery-manufacturers-makers-companies-producers-suppliers-in-the-world) | startup | Chinese Academy of Sciences spinout that put sodium-ion cells in the first test EV (Sehol E10X) and supplies low-speed vehicles and ESS | Small-batch production since 2023; among China's sodium-ion leaders |
| [BYD](https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/list-of-global-top-sodium-na-ion-sib-battery-manufacturers-makers-companies-producers-suppliers-in-the-world) | incumbent | Building a dedicated sodium-ion plant (Xuzhou) targeting small EVs and micromobility alongside its LFP empire | Confirmed sodium-ion development; deployment expected in select models behind CATL's timeline |
| [Faradion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodium-ion_battery) | startup | UK sodium-ion pioneer with layered-oxide cathode chemistry now owned by Reliance Industries for the Indian market | Acquired by Reliance Industries 2022 (~£100M); no automotive-scale production announced · **acquired** |
| [Tiamat Energy](https://www.tiamat-energy.com/) | startup | French CNRS spinout making high-power polyanionic sodium-ion cells (power tools first, mobility next) with a planned Amiens gigafactory | Backed by Stellantis Ventures, Arkema, MBDA; third funding round closed June 2025; 5 GWh plant construction starting late 2025, output ~2027 |
| [Farasis Energy](https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/list-of-global-top-sodium-na-ion-sib-battery-manufacturers-makers-companies-producers-suppliers-in-the-world) | incumbent | Chinese pouch-cell maker that put first-gen sodium-ion cells into JMEV city EVs and is shipping gen-2 | Sodium-ion EVs on Chinese roads since 2023; gen-2 cells at ~160 Wh/kg |
| [⚠️ Natron Energy](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/sodium-ion-battery-natron-energy-shutters-halts-NC-factory-plans/759479/) | startup | US Prussian-blue sodium-ion maker (industrial/data-center power, adjacent to mobility) that could not bridge to scale | Ceased all operations Sept 2025; 95 laid off; $1.4B North Carolina gigafactory cancelled · **☠ shut down** |

> **White space:** Outside China the field is nearly empty — Natron's liquidation and Faradion's quiet absorption into Reliance show sodium-ion's cost advantage only materializes at giga-scale when lithium prices are high; the opening is Western low-cost regional EVs, two/three-wheelers and cold-climate fleets if anyone can finance a plant before CATL's exports set the price floor.

**LFP/LMFP & manganese-rich cell innovation** · `🟡 scaling`

Iron- and manganese-based cathodes trade some energy density for major cost, safety and longevity gains; adding manganese (LMFP, LMR) claws back 15-33% energy density, making this the chemistry battleground for mass-market EVs.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CATL](https://www.batterytechonline.com/lithium-ion-batteries/latest-lfp-battery-projects-driving-safety-sustainability-and-savings) | incumbent | Shenxing superfast-charge LFP family (4C, later 800 km/12C peak versions) mass-produced for dozens of Chinese models | Shenxing in volume production since 2024 across major Chinese OEMs |
| [BYD FinDreams](https://www.batterytechonline.com/lithium-ion-batteries/latest-lfp-battery-projects-driving-safety-sustainability-and-savings) | incumbent | Blade 2.0 LFP cells and the Super e-Platform claiming 10C megawatt 'flash charging' (~400 km in 5 minutes) | 1,000 kW flash-charge platform unveiled March 2025, rolling out on Han L/Tang L |
| [Gotion High-Tech](https://en.gotion.com.cn/) | incumbent | First mover in LMFP with the Astroinno L600 cell (240 Wh/kg, ~1000 km pack range) headed for series production | Astroinno LMFP validated and slated for volume production; VW-backed |
| [Ultium Cells (GM + LG Energy Solution)](https://news.gm.com/home.detail.html/Pages/news/us/en/2025/may/0513-GM-LG-Energy-Solution-pioneer-LMR-battery-cell-technology.html) | incumbent | First Western program to commercialize lithium-manganese-rich (LMR) prismatic cells — 33% higher energy density than best LFP at comparable cost — for electric trucks/SUVs | Pre-production at LG facility late 2027, US commercial production 2028 |
| [Ford](https://www.techbrew.com/stories/2025/05/15/gm-lg-energy-solution-emerging-battery-cell-chemistry) | incumbent | Ion Park team developing its own LMR chemistry and licensing CATL LFP tech for the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan plant | Declared intent to put LMR cells in EVs this decade; Michigan LFP plant ramping 2026 |
| [Our Next Energy (ONE)](https://www.autonews.com/technology/an-our-next-energy-abandons-auto-batteries-rail-and-defense-0108/) | startup | Michigan startup behind Aries LFP packs and the Gemini dual-chemistry (LFP + anode-free range extender) architecture | Lost key EV contract; 45% workforce cut Jan 2026; abandoned automotive to focus on rail, defense and grid storage with $35M in new contracts |
| [Integrals Power](https://integralspower.com/) | startup | UK developer of high-manganese (up to 80% Mn) LMFP cathode materials and prototype cells for automotive customers | Seed/early-stage; supplying LMFP samples to OEM and cell-maker evaluations |

> **White space:** Chinese incumbents own LFP innovation end-to-end; the Western gap is stark — ONE's retreat from automotive leaves GM/LG's 2028 LMR program as the main non-Chinese bet, so an opening exists for US/EU LFP-LMFP cell capacity insulated by tariffs and defense/rail demand rather than head-on EV price competition.

**Extreme-fast-charge & niobium/LTO cells** · `🟠 demonstration`

Niobium- and titanium-oxide anodes (and silicon-dominant XFC designs) charge in under 10 minutes and survive tens of thousands of cycles, targeting vehicles and machines where uptime beats energy density.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [StoreDot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StoreDot) | startup | Israeli silicon-dominant '100in5' XFC cells (100 miles in 5 minutes), with prismatic samples produced with Flex\|N\|Gate and EVE Energy as manufacturing partner | 15 OEM test programs incl. 5 of top-10 automakers; Andretti SPAC merger signed Dec 2025 then cancelled in 2026 over a $30M cash shortfall — reportedly months of runway left · *status unverified* |
| [Nyobolt](https://techfundingnews.com/nyobolt-60m-series-c-1b-valuation-symbotic-battery-tech/) | startup | Cambridge (UK) niobium-tungsten-oxide anode cells charging in under 5 minutes with very long cycle life, first commercialized in warehouse robotics | $60M Series C led by Symbotic at ~$1B valuation (2025); ~$160M total raised; EV demonstrator charged 10-80% in 4m37s |
| [Echion Technologies](https://echiontech.com/) | startup | Cambridge maker of XNO niobium-oxide anode materials that drop into partner cells for 6-minute-charge mining trucks, buses and industrial EVs | GWh-scale XNO supply partnership with niobium giant CBMM; commercial cells shipping via partners |
| [Toshiba](https://www.global.toshiba/ww/products-solutions/battery/scib.html) | incumbent | SCiB lithium-titanate (LTO) cells with 20,000+ cycle life powering buses, trains, ships and grid buffers for nearly two decades; next-gen NTO (niobium-titanium-oxide) cell with CBMM/Sojitz | SCiB commercially deployed since 2008 across transport fleets; NTO samples demonstrated |
| [Microvast](https://microvast.com/) | scaleup | Fast-charging cell and pack maker for commercial vehicles (buses, trucks, port equipment) with plants in China, Germany and Tennessee | NASDAQ-listed; thousands of commercial fleets equipped; >$300M annual revenue scale |

> **White space:** Standalone XFC startups are being squeezed from above — CATL's 4C-6C Shenxing and BYD's 10C flash-charge LFP now ship at giga-scale, which is exactly why StoreDot is on the brink; the surviving opening is high-cycle-count niche duty cycles (robotics, mining, ports, charging buffers) where niobium/LTO chemistry's 10x cycle life justifies its $/kWh premium, as Nyobolt and Echion are proving.

**High-power specialty cells for e-aviation & performance** · `🟡 scaling`

Electric aircraft, eVTOLs and motorsport need cells that discharge at 10-20C (and recharge between flights) without overheating — a low-volume, high-margin niche dominated by one Taiwanese supplier after the leading startup died.

| [Amprius Technologies](https://dronelife.com/2025/05/05/amprius-launches-450-wh-kg-sicore-lithium-ion-battery-targeting-aviation-and-defense/) | startup | Silicon-anode cells with the highest specific energy in flight use — powering HAPS (high-altitude pseudo-satellites), military UAVs and eVTOL prototypes | Airbus Zephyr heritage; $15M UAV order 2025; SiCore 450 Wh/kg launched for aviation/defense |
| [EaglePicher Technologies](https://www.eaglepicher.com/) | incumbent | US defense/aerospace battery house (Missouri) building qualified high-power and thermal cells for missiles, aircraft and space programs | Decades of DoD/NASA flight heritage; expanding lithium-ion aviation lines |

> **White space:** Cuberg's shutdown and the insolvency of anchor customers like Lilium left e-aviation cell supply concentrated in Molicel; aerospace certification costs and tiny volumes deter giga-scale incumbents, so the opening is defense- and certification-funded specialty lines (the Amprius/NanoGraf playbook) selling Wh/kg and C-rate at 5-10x automotive cell prices.

### Battery Materials, Components, Powertrain & Recycling

**Cathode active materials & precursors** · `🟢 mature`

Producing the lithium-bearing crystal powders (NMC, NCA, LFP/LMFP) and precursor chemicals that store energy on the positive electrode — the single most valuable material in a battery and the key lever on cost, range and critical-mineral dependence.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Umicore](https://cen.acs.org/energy/energy-storage-/Cathode-projects-advance-North-America/100/i41) | incumbent | Belgian materials group making high-nickel NMC CAM and precursors in Europe/Asia with a paused Ontario plant | One of the largest Western CAM makers; cut battery-materials capex ~50% and delayed plants in 2024-25 amid weak EV demand and <40% Western plant utilization |
| [BASF](https://cen.acs.org/energy/energy-storage-/Cathode-projects-advance-North-America/100/i41) | incumbent | Runs the Schwarzheide (Germany) high-nickel CAM plant plus Harjavalta precursors, but has put parts of the battery materials business under review | Schwarzheide began production 2023 targeting ~100 kt/yr; investment scaled back ~50% with facilities delayed in 2024-25 |
| [EcoPro BM](https://www.ecopro.co.kr/eng/) | incumbent | Korea's high-nickel NCA/NCM cathode leader supplying Samsung SDI and SK On, expanding into Canada (with Ford/SK) | Multi-hundred-kt/yr capacity across Korea; KOSDAQ-listed large cap |
| [POSCO Future M](https://www.poscofuturem.com/en/) | incumbent | Korea's only integrated cathode-plus-anode materials maker, vertically tied to POSCO lithium/nickel | GM Ultium CAM JV; tens of kt/yr NCMA capacity ramping |
| [Hunan Yuneng](https://www.datamintelligence.com/research-report/cathode-materials-market) | incumbent | World's largest LFP cathode producer, anchor supplier to CATL and BYD | Largest global LFP CAM market share; Shenzhen-listed |

**Anode materials: graphite, synthetic & silicon** · `🟢 mature`

Making the carbon or silicon powders for the negative electrode — graphite is a mature, China-dominated commodity being onshored for supply security, while silicon-rich anodes promise 20%+ more energy density and faster charging and are just reaching automotive scale.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|

Regenerating cathode powder while preserving its engineered crystal structure (plasma, relithiation or direct precursor synthesis) instead of dissolving everything to metal salts — promising far lower cost and emissions, but only if feedstock chemistry is known and still in demand.

| [Aqua Metals](https://ir.aquametals.com/press-releases/detail/310/aqua-metals-reports-milestone-advancements-strategic) | startup | Electrochemical Li AquaRefining that plates metals back out of black mass with electricity instead of chemical reagents | Nasdaq micro-cap; pilot ran 24/7 for over a year producing >99.5% lithium carbonate and signed a supply agreement with 6K Energy, but capital constraints stalled its Sierra ARC campus |

> **White space:** Direct recycling stays thin because it needs clean, single-chemistry feedstock and the regenerated cathode must still match market demand — recovered NMC risks obsolescence as the fleet shifts to LFP. The opening is LFP and manufacturing scrap: metal values there are too low for hydromet to pencil, so structure-preserving regeneration is the only route that creates value, which is why PNE's LFP-capable SC plant matters.

### Aviation Decarbonization

**HEFA sustainable aviation fuel** · `🟡 scaling`

Hydrotreats waste fats, used cooking oil, and vegetable oils into drop-in jet fuel; it supplies ~80% of all SAF today and is the only pathway producing at large commercial scale, making it the workhorse of near-term aviation decarbonization despite a hard ceiling on waste-lipid feedstock.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Neste](https://www.privatecharterx.blog/sustainable-aviation-fuel-market-2025/) | incumbent | World's largest SAF producer; converted refineries in Singapore and Rotterdam dedicate ~1.5 Mt/yr to SAF capability | Rotterdam SAF line (500 kt/yr) started April 2025, bringing global SAF capability to 1.5 Mt/yr; long-term offtakes with Lufthansa, United, Air France-KLM |
| [World Energy](https://worldenergy.net/press-release/world-energy-department-of-energy-loan-guarantee/) | scaleup | First commercial SAF supplier (Paramount, CA since 2016); converting its Houston biorefinery into a 250M gal/yr SAF hub | DOE invited Part II application for ~$2B loan guarantee (2024); 70M-gallon SAF supply pact with Montana Renewables (2025) |
| [Montana Renewables (Calumet)](https://calumet.com/montana-renewables-announces-closing-of-1-44-billion-doe-loan-facility-for-renewable-fuels-and-biomass-energy-facility/) | scaleup | Great Falls, MT refinery conversion; one of North America's largest SAF producers, expanding via the MaxSAF project to ~300M gal/yr | Closed $1.44B DOE loan facility Jan 2025 ($1.67B program); first $782M tranche drawn in 2025 despite federal funding freeze delay |
| [EcoCeres](https://biofuels-news.com/news/ecoceres-inaugurates-first-saf-plant-in-malaysia/) | scaleup | Hong Kong-based waste-feedstock biorefiner (used cooking oil) with HEFA plants in Zhangjiagang, China and Pasir Gudang, Malaysia | Malaysia plant (420 kt/yr HVO/SAF/naphtha) commissioned Oct 2025, inaugurated Jan 2026; ~770 kt/yr combined renewable fuels capacity; Bain Capital-backed |

| [Phillips 66](https://farmdocdaily.illinois.edu/2025/01/estimates-of-sustainable-aviation-fuel-production-capacity-at-u-s-renewable-diesel-plants-through-2026.html) | incumbent | Converted its Rodeo, CA oil refinery to one of the world's largest renewable fuels plants with SAF output | Rodeo Renewed (~50,000 bpd renewable fuels) ramped 2024-25 with SAF trains; supplying California airports |

**Alcohol-to-jet SAF** · `🟠 demonstration`

Chemically dehydrates and oligomerizes ethanol or isobutanol into jet fuel, unlocking the huge existing ethanol industry (and future CO2- or biogas-derived alcohols) as SAF feedstock far beyond the limited supply of waste fats.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [LanzaJet](https://www.lanzajet.com/news-insights/lanzajet-makes-history) | scaleup | Built and operates the world's first commercial-scale ethanol-to-jet plant (Freedom Pines Fuels, Soperton, GA — 10M gal/yr) and licenses its ATJ process globally | First commercial-scale ethanol-based jet fuel produced Nov 2025; backers include Suncor, Mitsui, Shell, Airbus, Microsoft Climate Fund; license projects in UK, Japan, Uzbekistan |
| [Gevo](https://esgnews.com/gevo-secures-1-46-billion-doe-loan-for-worlds-first-net-zero-aviation-fuel-plant/) | scaleup | Isobutanol/ethanol-to-jet developer; Net-Zero 1 (Lake Preston, SD) designed for ~60M gal/yr SAF with on-site CCS | $1.46B DOE loan commitment (Oct 2024); acquired Red Trail Energy ethanol+CCS plant; NZ1 FID still pending — economics strained by denied Summit CO2 pipeline permits |

| [Summit Next Gen](https://www.resources.org/common-resources/the-promise-of-ethanol-to-jet-for-sustainable-aviation-fuel-in-the-united-states/) | startup | Developing a large Houston-area ethanol-to-SAF conversion plant using licensed technology, fed by Midwest ethanol | Part of Summit Agricultural Group; planned ~250M gal/yr facility, among the largest announced US ATJ projects |

**Gasification & Fischer-Tropsch SAF from waste/biomass** · `🟠 demonstration`

Gasifies municipal solid waste or woody biomass into syngas and synthesizes Fischer-Tropsch jet fuel — promising effectively unlimited cheap feedstock, but historically plagued by feedstock-handling failures, syngas cleanup problems, and capex blowouts.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [⚠️ Fulcrum BioEnergy](https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2608211-fulcrum-bioenergy-files-for-chapter-11-relief) | startup | Built the world's first municipal-waste-to-fuels plant (Sierra, NV) feeding FT synthesis | Chapter 11 in September 2024 after ~$1B raised from airlines and oil majors; Sierra plant disabled by nitric acid corrosion and feedstock sludge buildup · **☠ shut down** |
| ⚠️ Red Rock Biofuels | startup | Attempted a woody-biomass gasification + FT SAF plant in Lakeview, Oregon | Construction stalled ~2022 after cost overruns; unfinished plant sold at auction — a second high-profile gasification-FT failure alongside Fulcrum · **☠ shut down** |
| [DG Fuels](https://dgfuels.com) | startup | Developing a ~$4-5B cellulosic (bagasse/wood waste) FT SAF plant in St. James Parish, Louisiana (~180M gal/yr), one of the largest announced SAF projects | Strategic investment from Airbus; offtakes with Delta and Air France-KLM; FID targeted mid-2020s |
| [Velocys](https://velocys.com/fischer-tropsch-reactor-technology/) | scaleup | Supplies microchannel Fischer-Tropsch reactors that make small-scale FT economic; technology behind the UK Altalto waste-to-SAF project | Taken private in 2024 in a ~$40M rescue (Carbon Direct, Lightrock, GenZero, Kibo); UK government SAF funding supports its black-bag-waste project |
| [Aether Fuels](https://aetherfuels.com) | startup | Temasek/Xora-incubated startup with 'Aether Aurora' flexible syngas-to-liquids platform tolerant of mixed waste-carbon feedstocks | Venture-stage (~$35M+ raised); pilot-scale technology development in Singapore and US |
| [Enerkem](https://www.ieabioenergy.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/IEA-Bioenergy-Task-39-SAF-report.pdf) | scaleup | Canadian MSW gasification company (Edmonton pioneer plant; Varennes Carbon Recycling project in Québec) producing methanol/ethanol convertible toward jet | Edmonton plant closed and major restructuring 2024-25; Varennes project continuing with government backing · *status unverified* |
| [Johnson Matthey (with bp)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fischer%E2%80%93Tropsch_process) | incumbent | Co-developed FT CANS fixed-bed Fischer-Tropsch technology licensed to waste-to-SAF developers (was selected by Fulcrum, DG Fuels, Strategic Biofuels) | Established catalysis incumbent monetizing SAF via licensing rather than project risk |

> **White space:** Two flagship failures (Fulcrum 2024, Red Rock ~2022) prove the chokepoint is feedstock prep and syngas cleanup at scale, not FT chemistry — yet waste feedstock remains the largest untapped SAF resource; the opening is for modular FT (Velocys/Ineratec-style) paired with already-proven gasifiers or with clean point-source syngas, and for developers who de-risk the front end before scaling.

**Power-to-liquid e-SAF** · `🟠 demonstration`

Synthesizes jet fuel from green hydrogen and captured CO2 (via Fischer-Tropsch, methanol, or direct CO2 electrolysis routes); feedstock is effectively unlimited and lifecycle carbon lowest of any pathway, but cost hinges on cheap clean electricity — EU/UK e-SAF sub-mandates from 2030 create guaranteed demand.

**Emerging SAF routes: pyrolysis, HTL, algae, CO2-to-ethanol chains** · `🔵 pilot`

Earlier-stage chemistry — fast-pyrolysis oil upgrading, hydrothermal liquefaction of wet wastes like sewage biosolids, engineered algae oils, and waste-gas fermentation to ethanol — aimed at unlocking cheap, abundant feedstocks the mainstream pathways cannot use.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [LanzaTech](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843724/000162828025026378/lnzaex991-pressrelease1q25.htm) | scaleup | Gas fermentation converting industrial waste gases and CO2 into ethanol that feeds LanzaJet's ATJ plants — the front half of the CO2-to-jet chain | NASDAQ-listed but distressed: going-concern doubt despite $40M preferred equity (May 2025), 1-for-100 reverse split (Aug 2025) for Nasdaq compliance; licensing deals continue (e.g., Uzbekistan ethanol+SAF complex) |
| [Firefly Green Fuels](https://biofuels-news.com/news/firefly-green-fuels-and-synagro-to-unlock-saf-production-from-biosolids-in-north-america/) | startup | Hydrothermal liquefaction of sewage biosolids into SAF — a negative-cost, city-scale feedstock nobody else uses | Wizz Air offtake; Synagro partnership for North American biosolids; Builders Vision backing; first UK plant targeted 2028/29 |
| [Alder Renewables](https://www.alderrenewables.com/latest-news-research/alder-saf100-accelerating-development-for-next-generation-sustainable-fuels) | startup | Upgrades biomass pyrolysis oil into 'Alder SAF100', a 100% drop-in fuel candidate from woody residues | Backed by United Airlines Ventures, Boeing and Avfuel; pilot-scale production and SAF100 testing underway |
| [Viridos](https://elevenflo.com/blog/viridos-bankruptcy) | startup | Engineered high-lipid algae strains for algal jet fuel (the former ExxonMobil algae program) | ExxonMobil exited 2023 calling algae 'too difficult and expensive'; Chapter 11 April 2025; assets sold to Breakthrough Energy Ventures in a 64-day sale completed Nov 2025 · **acquired** |

> **White space:** Algae has now failed twice at corporate scale (Exxon exit 2023, Viridos Chapter 11 2025) — biology plus harvesting economics remain unsolved physics-of-cost; meanwhile wet-waste HTL has gate-fee-negative feedstock at every city wastewater plant and essentially one credible player (Firefly), so process developers that partner with water utilities face an almost empty field.

**Battery-electric fixed-wing aircraft** · `🟠 demonstration`

Replaces turbines with battery packs and electric motors for true zero-emission flight; today's cell energy density caps useful range at roughly 100-400nm, so the market is flight training, cargo feeders, and 9-90 seat regional designs that bet on future batteries.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [BETA Technologies](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/16/beta-technologies-ipo-value-evtol.html) | scaleup | ALIA CX300 fixed-wing electric (plus A250 eVTOL) with a build-the-charging-network strategy along the US East Coast | IPO'd on NYSE Oct-Nov 2025 (sought ~$825M at up to $7.2B valuation); $300M GE Aerospace investment; customers include UPS, Bristow, Air New Zealand |
| [Eviation](https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/air-transport/2025-02-18/eviation-pauses-alice-electric-aircraft-while-seeking-new) | startup | Alice 9-passenger clean-sheet electric commuter (flew once in 2022); claimed $5B order book from Cape Air, DHL and others | Laid off most staff and paused Alice development indefinitely in Feb 2025 while seeking strategic partners · *status unverified* |
| [Elysian](https://www.flightglobal.com/air-transport/2026/04/elysian-tweaks-e9x-design-boosting-weight-and-wingspan-of-battery-powered-aircraft/) | startup | Dutch startup designing the E9X, a 90-seat battery-electric airliner premised on ~400 Wh/kg cells and ~400nm range | Design refined April 2026 (larger wing, more weight); scale model in 2-3 years, full prototype ~2030, service ~2033; Panta Holdings-backed |
| [Pipistrel (Textron eAviation)](https://www.pipistrel-aircraft.com) | incumbent | Velis Electro — the world's only EASA type-certified electric airplane, in serial production for flight schools | Hundreds delivered globally; acquired by Textron in 2022 as its eAviation anchor · **acquired** |
| [Diamond Aircraft](https://www.diamondaircraft.com) | incumbent | Developing the eDA40 electric trainer with quick-charge capability; parent Wanfeng also absorbed Volocopter's assets | eDA40 in flight test toward certification; established GA manufacturing base |
| [Bye Aerospace](https://byeaerospace.com) | startup | eFlyer 2/4 electric trainers pursued since the mid-2010s | Certification repeatedly delayed amid persistent funding gaps; program continuation unclear · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** The 9-19 seat pure-battery commuter segment has been gutted (Eviation paused, Bye stalled) because ~250-300 Wh/kg pack-level density cannot close the payload-range business case; trainers (Pipistrel) and cargo feeders work today, and the opening reopens only when 400+ Wh/kg cells (solid-state/silicon-anode) reach aviation qualification — battery suppliers, not airframers, hold the bottleneck.

**Hybrid-electric propulsion & retrofits** · `🔵 pilot`

Pairs combustion engines or turbogenerators with electric motors and batteries to cut fuel burn ~30-50% on regional aircraft, and de-risks certification by retrofitting existing airframes — the pragmatic bridge while batteries and hydrogen mature.

> **White space:** Incumbent engine makers have retreated (Rolls-Royce sold off its electric-propulsion unit; Pratt & Whitney slowed its Dash 8 hybrid demo), and Heart's downsizing shows clean-sheet regional hybrids strain venture funding — certification cost versus a small regional market is the chokepoint, so retrofit STCs on existing airframes (Ampaire-style) are the nearest-term wedge and remain thinly contested.

**Hydrogen fuel-cell & H2-combustion aircraft plus airport H2 fueling** · `🔵 pilot`

Uses hydrogen in fuel cells driving electric props (or burned directly in turbines) for zero-carbon flight beyond battery range; requires cryogenic or high-pressure storage on board and entirely new airport fueling infrastructure, creating a chicken-and-egg scaling problem.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|

> **White space:** Universal Hydrogen's collapse and the Airbus ZEROe slip to the 2040s froze airline and airport H2 investment — the chicken-and-egg between aircraft and fueling infrastructure is the binding constraint, not the fuel cell; the credible near-term openings are sub-regional retrofits certified under existing rules and airport cryogenic ground equipment (Fabrum is nearly alone), which monetize before any H2 airliner exists.

**eVTOL & urban air mobility** · `🟠 demonstration`

Battery-powered vertical-takeoff air taxis replacing helicopters and congested car trips; zero operational emissions and far quieter, though net climate benefit depends on displacing higher-carbon modes at scale — and the sector just went through a brutal shakeout separating certifiers from the rest.

**Flight-ops efficiency & contrail avoidance** · `🟡 scaling`

Software that optimizes routes, climb profiles, taxiing and fuel decisions — and now reroutes flights around ice-supersaturated air to avoid warming contrails — cutting 1-5% of fuel burn and potentially a large share of aviation's non-CO2 forcing at near-zero hardware cost.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [OpenAirlines](https://www.openairlines.com/) | scaleup | SkyBreathe — the most widely used airline fuel-efficiency analytics platform, mining flight-data-recorder data for savings and coaching pilots | 80+ airline customers; claims up to 5% fuel reduction with no aircraft modification |
| [SATAVIA](https://aviationweek.com/air-transport/aircraft-propulsion/ge-aerospace-takes-over-contrail-prevention-startup-satavia) | startup | DECISIONX:NETZERO contrail forecasting and flight-plan optimization, converting avoided warming into tradable climate units; worked with Etihad, KLM and 12 operators | Acquired by GE Aerospace (Aerospace Carbon Solutions unit) Sept 2024 — first contrail-startup exit · **acquired** |
| [Google Research / Breakthrough Energy](https://www.rdworldonline.com/googles-ai-cut-contrails-62-on-american-airlines-flights-getting-the-whole-industry-to-follow-could-be-a-harder-problem/) | incumbent | AI contrail-risk maps from satellite + weather data, proven in the largest operational avoidance trial to date | 2025 American Airlines trial across 2,400+ transatlantic flights cut observable contrails ~62% with no statistically significant fuel penalty |
| [Flightkeys](https://news.aa.com/sustainability/environment/contrail-avoidance/) | scaleup | Vienna-based 5D flight-planning system embedding contrail forecasts and cost-optimal trajectories directly into dispatch | Integrated Google/Breakthrough contrail data for the American Airlines trial; growing share of tier-1 airline flight planning |
| [Estuaire](https://www.blue-lines.org/airline-index) | startup | French analytics startup quantifying and monitoring airline non-CO2 emissions and route-level climate impact | Engaged by Vueling and Wizz Air (2025) for contrail data analysis and disclosure |
| [SITA](https://www.sita.aero) | incumbent | OptiFlight (acquired from Safety Line) — machine-learning climb-profile and in-flight fuel optimization sold through its huge airline IT footprint | Deployed across dozens of carriers as part of SITA's digital day-of-operations suite |
| [Airspace Intelligence](https://airspace-intelligence.com) | startup | Flyways AI — dynamic ATC-aware route re-optimization first deployed fleet-wide with Alaska Airlines | Multi-year Alaska Airlines deployment; venture-backed Series B |

> **White space:** Fuel-efficiency software is crowded, but contrail avoidance — arguably the cheapest large climate lever in all of aviation — has almost no independent commercial players left after SATAVIA sold to GE: there is still no regulatory or market mechanism that pays airlines for avoided contrails (EU non-CO2 MRV only began 2025), so whoever builds the verification-and-credit layer when regulation lands inherits the category.

**Ultra-efficient airframes & next-gen engines (BWB, open fan, laminar flow)** · `🔵 pilot`

Redesigns the aircraft itself — blended-wing bodies, open-fan engines, truss-braced and laminar-flow wings — to cut fuel burn 20-50% regardless of what fuel is burned; the single biggest efficiency lever for the 2030s fleet and a multiplier on every SAF gallon.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [JetZero](https://www.flightglobal.com/airframers/all-wing-aircraft-developer-jetzero-raises-175m-for-demonstrator-advancement/165942.article) | startup | Z4 blended-wing-body 200-250 seat airliner claiming ~50% lower fuel burn; using a US Air Force demonstrator to leapfrog the duopoly | $235M USAF contract (2023); $175M Series B (Jan 2026, B Capital) with United/Alaska equity and conditional orders; $4.7B Greensboro, NC factory announced; demonstrator flight planned 2027 |
| [CFM International (GE Aerospace + Safran)](https://www.flightglobal.com/airframers/airbus-still-sees-blended-wing-body-design-as-possible-for-larger-jets/164450.article) | incumbent | RISE open-fan engine demonstrator targeting ~20% lower fuel burn and full SAF/H2 compatibility for the next narrowbody generation | Airbus plans RISE-derived open-fan flight tests for its next-generation single-aisle; ground tests progressing |
| [Airbus](https://www.flightglobal.com/airframers/airbus-still-sees-blended-wing-body-design-as-possible-for-larger-jets/164450.article) | incumbent | Next-gen single-aisle program (~2035+) wrapping open-fan propulsion, long folding wings, and new materials; keeps BWB on the shelf for larger jets | CEO confirms open-fan baseline studies; 'Wing of Tomorrow' composites program complete |
| [Boeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_X-66) | incumbent | X-66 truss-braced-wing NASA demonstrator exploring ~30% fuel-burn reduction for narrowbodies | Paused the X-66 build in 2025 to refocus on thin-wing research amid company-wide strain — evidence of incumbent slow-walking |
| [Otto Aviation](https://www.ottoaviation.com) | startup | Phantom 3500 business jet using super-laminar-flow fuselage to claim ~50-60% lower fuel burn per trip | First flight targeted ~2027; announced Jacksonville, FL production site (2025) |
| [Natilus](https://www.natilus.co) | startup | Blended-wing-body freighters (Kona) and a 200-seat passenger BWB concept (Horizon) pitched at 30%+ efficiency gains | Claims multi-billion-dollar pre-order book for cargo BWB; sub-scale prototypes flown |

> **White space:** The Boeing-Airbus duopoly has no clean-sheet aircraft before ~2035 and Boeing even paused its own X-66 efficiency demonstrator, leaving a rare structural opening that JetZero is testing via military-funded demonstrators — but the $10B+ certification-and-industrialization moat means the realistic startup path is defense/cargo first, and almost no one else is attempting it.

**Low-emission airships & hybrid lighter-than-air cargo** · `🔵 pilot`

Helium-buoyed hybrid and rigid airships trade speed for ~75-90% lower fuel burn (with electric or hydrogen variants planned), targeting remote-area cargo, surveillance, and short-haul passenger niches that need no runways or road infrastructure.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Hybrid Air Vehicles](https://aerospaceamerica.aiaa.org/year-in-review/airships-in-2025-orders-booked-production-sites-selected-and-flight-tests-progressing/) | scaleup | Airlander 10 hybrid airship (10-tonne payload) with hydrogen-electric zero-emission variant planned with ZeroAvia | Doncaster UK factory planned for 24 aircraft/yr; ~35 reservations incl. Air Nostrum (20) and a first military order; service entry ~2029 |
| [LTA Research](https://aerospaceamerica.aiaa.org/year-in-review/airships-in-2025-orders-booked-production-sites-selected-and-flight-tests-progressing/) | startup | Sergey Brin-funded builder of Pathfinder 1, the first new rigid airship in 85 years, aimed at humanitarian cargo | Pathfinder 1 flew over the Golden Gate Bridge Oct 2025 in expanding flight-test campaign begun 2024 |
| [Flying Whales](https://aerospaceamerica.aiaa.org/year-in-review/airships-in-2025-orders-booked-production-sites-selected-and-flight-tests-progressing/) | scaleup | French-Québécois LCA60T rigid airship for 60-tonne outsize cargo lift to roadless regions (forestry, grid, remote communities) | French/Québec government backing; binding lease contract with France's National Forest Agency (Jul 2025); Laruscade factory site unveiled |

> **White space:** A century of failed revivals (CargoLifter, Lockheed's exited LMH-1) plus helium cost, weather sensitivity, and unsolved variable-buoyancy ground handling keep credible players to three; the opening is narrow but real in remote logistics where the alternative is building roads or flying helicopters — and certification authorities have no modern airship rulebook, so the first type certificate effectively defines the category.

### Maritime Decarbonization

**Green methanol vessels, engines & fuel supply** · `🟠 demonstration`

Ships burn e-methanol (from renewable power) or bio-methanol (from waste) in dual-fuel diesel engines, cutting greenhouse gas up to ~75-95% with a liquid fuel that is easy to store and bunker — vessels and engines are commercial, but green fuel supply is the binding constraint.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [MAN Energy Solutions](https://www.man-es.com/) | incumbent | Dominant supplier of ME-LGIM two-stroke dual-fuel methanol engines that power Maersk's fleet and most of the global methanol orderbook. | Methanol dual-fuel engine of choice for hundreds of ordered vessels since the Laura Maersk (2023) |
| [A.P. Moller - Maersk](https://www.offshore-energy.biz/maersks-green-methanol-containership-fleet-is-now-complete/) | incumbent | First-mover container line: world's first methanol-fueled boxship (Laura Maersk), first large dual-fuel series, and first big-ship methanol retrofit conversion. | Completed world's first series of large dual-fuel methanol vessels (Axel Maersk, 2025); ~25 methanol-enabled ships ordered |
| [European Energy](https://europeanenergy.com/2025/05/13/kasso-e-methanol-facility-officially-inaugurated/) | scaleup | Built and operates Kassø (Denmark), the world's first commercial-scale e-methanol plant (42,000 t/yr, 51/49 with Mitsui), supplying Maersk, LEGO and Novo Nordisk. | Kassø inaugurated May 2025; first e-methanol bunkering of Laura Maersk; green bridge financing with Mitsui Jan 2026 |
| [⚠️ Liquid Wind](https://maritime-executive.com/article/e-methanol-producer-liquid-wind-enters-bankruptcy-administration) | startup | Swedish developer of standardized ~100,000 t/yr e-methanol plants (FlagshipONE, sold to Ørsted and later cancelled). | Raised ~€64M but filed for bankruptcy May 2026 after failing to secure offtakes/financing; subsidiaries put up for sale · **☠ shut down** |
| [C2X](https://shipandbunker.com/news/world/173661-eneos-and-maersk-boost-c2x-with-100-million-green-methanol-investment) | scaleup | A.P. Moller Holding spin-out developing multi-megaton green methanol production in Egypt, Spain and the US Gulf (Beaver Lake, Louisiana). | $100M investment from ENEOS alongside APMH/Maersk; ambition of 3 Mt/yr capacity by 2030 |
| [WasteFuel](https://maritime-executive.com/article/bp-invests-in-wastefuel-s-bio-methanol-and-signs-offtake-agreement) | startup | Converts municipal and agricultural waste into bio-methanol for marine fuel. | Backed by Maersk Growth and BP ($10M plus offtake MoU); launched biomethanol sales |
| [Methanex](https://www.methanex.com/) | incumbent | World's largest methanol producer and marine methanol supplier; operates the methanol-fueled Waterfront Shipping tanker fleet. | Acquired OCI Global's international methanol business (~$2B deal closed 2025), consolidating fuel supply |
| [X-Press Feeders](https://www.x-pressfeeders.com/news/x-press-feeders-starts-europes-first-feeder-network-powered-by-green-methanol-ushering-in-new-era-of-sustainable-shipping) | incumbent | Operates Europe's first green-methanol-powered container feeder network (Rotterdam-Baltic GFX/GBX routes) with ISCC-certified fuel. | 3 dual-fuel feeders operating, 14 ordered (deliveries through 2026) |

> **White space:** Ships have outrun fuel: one commercial e-methanol plant (42 kt/yr) versus megaton-scale fleet demand, and developers die without bankable offtakes (Liquid Wind bankruptcy, Ørsted's FlagshipONE cancellation). The opening is for producers who can lock long-term offtakes and shrink the green premium, plus FuelEU-compliance structures that monetize it.

**Ammonia propulsion & ammonia-to-power** · `🟠 demonstration`

Ammonia is a carbon-free hydrogen carrier that can be burned in dual-fuel engines or cracked into hydrogen for fuel cells, promising zero-CO2 deep-sea shipping if toxicity, N2O slip and bunkering infrastructure are solved.

| [MAN Energy Solutions](https://www.lloydslist.com/LL1152410/MAN-to-deliver-first-ammonia-dual-fuel-engines-in-early-2026) | incumbent | Developing the two-stroke ammonia engine (ME-LGIA) expected to power the deep-sea ammonia fleet. | First ammonia dual-fuel engine deliveries scheduled early 2026 |

| [Wärtsilä](https://maritime-executive.com/article/norwegian-timber-ship-will-be-first-to-use-wartsila-s-ammonia-engine) | incumbent | Launched the first commercial four-stroke ammonia engine (Wärtsilä 25 Ammonia) for short-sea vessels. | First newbuild installations for Viridis Bulk Carriers and Skarv Shipping; equipment deliveries from Q4 2026 |
| [Amogy](https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/15/amogy-raises-80m-to-power-ships-and-data-centers-with-ammonia/) | scaleup | Cracks ammonia onboard into hydrogen for fuel cells; sailed the world's first ammonia-powered vessel (NH3 Kraken tug, 2024) and now targets ships plus floating power. | Raised $80M in 2025 (~$300M total), led by Korea Development Bank; Asia maritime expansion |
| [Azane Fuel Solutions](https://www.yara.com/corporate-releases/yara-clean-ammonia-and-azane-granted-safety-permit-to-build-worlds-first-low-emission-ammonia-bunkering-terminal/) | startup | Builds containerized and floating ammonia bunkering terminals — the missing fueling infrastructure layer. | World-first ammonia bunkering terminal safety permit in Norway; 15 units pre-ordered by Yara Clean Ammonia |
| [Yara Clean Ammonia](https://www.worldcargonews.com/environment/2025/09/steel-cut-for-worlds-first-ammonia-powered-container-ship-yara-eyde/) | incumbent | World's largest ammonia trader, building Yara Eyde — the first ammonia-powered container ship (with North Sea Container Line) — plus bunkering supply. | Yara Eyde steel cut Sept 2025 at Qingdao Yangfan; delivery ~mid-2026 for Oslo-Rotterdam route |
| [Exmar](https://exmar.com/en/news-center/worlds-first-ocean-going-ammonia-dual-fuel-vessels-named-in-south-korea/) | incumbent | First shipowner to take delivery of ocean-going ammonia dual-fuel gas carriers (which can burn their own cargo). | World's first ammonia dual-fuel midsize gas carriers named/delivered in South Korea in 2025 |
| [Fortescue](https://fortescue.com/) | incumbent | Converted the Green Pioneer, the world's first ammonia dual-fuel demonstration vessel, to force regulatory and port acceptance. | Demonstrated ammonia operation in Singapore (2024) and showcased the vessel internationally |

> **White space:** Engine supply is consolidating with the three incumbent engine houses; the open gaps are port-side bunkering networks, crew safety/training systems and N2O abatement — whoever industrializes safe ammonia transfer owns the bottleneck.

**Hydrogen & fuel-cell vessels** · `🟠 demonstration`

Compressed or liquid hydrogen feeding PEM fuel cells gives genuinely zero-emission propulsion for ferries, harbor craft and inland barges, but low energy density and high green-hydrogen cost confine it to short, subsidized routes — and the sector has suffered heavy attrition.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

> **White space:** Capture is proven but the loop is open: there is no standardized port CO2 offload/storage chain and IMO/EU accounting for captured CO2 is still pending, so value hinges on regulation — first movers locking port logistics and cement/CCU offtake (the Seabound-Heidelberg model) own the gap.

Small modular and molten-salt reactors aboard ships or floating power plants would deliver years of zero-carbon operation without refueling, but no commercial nuclear merchant vessel exists — today's work is reactor design, class rules and feasibility studies.

HD Hyundai, TerraPower and Wan Hai; targets $10B orderbook by 2030 and floating plants by mid-2030s |
| [Seaborg Technologies](https://www.neimagazine.com/news/korean-shipbuilder-joins-nuclear-shipping-project-11502161/) | startup | Danish compact molten salt reactor (CMSR) for power barges, partnered with Samsung Heavy Industries and KAERI. | SHI partnership for barges of up to 8x100 MWe; company downsized and refocused in 2023-24 |

> **White space:** Physics is proven by navies, but civilian port access, insurance/liability frameworks and IMO rules don't yet exist, so credible players are few and capital-heavy; the near-term opening is floating nuclear power for ports and islands (regulated like land assets) before propulsion, plus licensing/class-rule tooling.

### Rail, Hydrogen for Transport & E-fuels

**Battery-electric trains & locomotives** · `🟡 scaling`

Lithium-ion battery packs replace or supplement diesel engines in multiple-unit passenger trains and freight locomotives, charging from overhead wires or regenerative braking to eliminate diesel on non-electrified track at lower infrastructure cost than full electrification.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Wabtec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wabtec_FLXDrive) | incumbent | FLXdrive heavy-haul battery locomotive (up to ~7 MWh) for freight and mining railroads | Orders from Union Pacific, CN, Rio Tinto, BHP, Roy Hill and Vale; BHP units arrived at Port Hedland Nov 2025 |
| [Stadler Rail](https://railway-news.com/germany-stadler-to-deliver-19-flirt-akku-battery-trains-in-central-thuringia/) | incumbent | FLIRT Akku battery multiple-unit, the European volume leader for replacing diesel railcars on partially electrified lines | 55 units in service in Schleswig-Holstein and 44 in Rhineland-Palatinate; new orders from ODEG (14) and DB Regio Thuringia (19, service 2028) |
| [Siemens Mobility](https://www.mobility.siemens.com/global/en/portfolio/rolling-stock/commuter-and-regional-trains/mireo/mireo-plus.html) | incumbent | Mireo Plus B battery EMU platform sold across German regional networks | In revenue service in Germany with multiple follow-on fleet orders |
| [Progress Rail (Caterpillar)](https://www.trains.com/trn/railroads/locomotives/battery-powered-locomotives-continue-to-gain-momentum/) | incumbent | EMD Joule battery-electric switcher and line-haul locomotives | Joule units delivered for long-term demonstration at Pacific Harbor Line, California; battery locomotive momentum building across Class I demos |
| [Alstom](https://www.railjournal.com/technology/alstom-shelves-hydrogen-development/) | incumbent | Coradia battery-electric multiple units (BEMUs) for German regional lines; pivoting rolling-stock R&D from hydrogen to battery | BEMU fleets ordered in Germany while hydrogen train development was paused in 2025 |
| [Hitachi Rail](https://www.hitachi.com/en/press/articles/2025/04/0403/) | incumbent | Battery-hybrid and tri-mode (electric/battery/diesel) intercity trains, including the Trenitalia 'Blues' fleet and UK intercity battery trains | April 2025 UK contract for 45 intercity battery-hybrid cars worth ~£300M including 10-year maintenance |

**Autonomous battery railcars & rail freight innovation** · `🟠 demonstration`

Self-propelled, battery-electric railcars that move individually or in small platoons without a locomotive or crew, aiming to win short-haul container and bulk freight back from diesel trucks by making rail economical at small batch sizes.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Parallel Systems](https://www.builtinla.com/articles/parallel-systems-raises-38m-electric-rail-pilot-20250414) | startup | Autonomous battery-electric intermodal railcars that platoon; second-generation vehicle FRA-approved for pilot on two Genesee & Wyoming short lines in Georgia | $38M Series B extension April 2025 (~$100M total raised); 300+ railcar backlog; commercial launch targeted 2026 |
| [Intramotev](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/autonomous-rail-intermodal-cars-to-begin-testing-this-month) | startup | TugVolt self-propelled battery railcars that convert existing freight cars; first mover in revenue industrial service | Autonomous railcars in commercial operation at a Missouri calcium mine; near deal for intermodal cars with an international customer |

> **White space:** Effectively a two-startup US field: FRA certification, railroad operating-rule conservatism, and Class I labor agreements make entry brutal, while the prize (the ~70% of US freight ton-miles on trucks) is huge. Openings exist for European/Asian equivalents on lighter-regulated networks and for retrofit propulsion/automation kits for existing railcar fleets.

**Hydrogen trains** · `🟠 demonstration`

Fuel-cell multiple units and locomotives store compressed hydrogen onboard to replace diesel on long non-electrified routes where batteries lack range, but early fleets have hit reliability and fuel-supply problems and several buyers are reverting to battery trains.

**Rail electrification & discontinuous catenary technology** · `🟢 mature`

Overhead catenary electrification is the proven, lowest-emission way to decarbonize heavy rail traffic; the new 'discontinuous' approach wires only sections of a route and lets battery-hybrid trains bridge the gaps, cutting capital cost on bridges, tunnels and rural stretches.

| [Hitachi Rail](https://www.hitachi.com/en/press/articles/2025/04/0403/) | incumbent | Tri-mode (25kV/battery/diesel) and battery-hybrid intercity trains designed specifically to exploit partial electrification | £300M UK battery-intercity order April 2025; East West Rail's £2.5B 'partial-discontinuous electrification' decision (Nov 2025) validates the model |

**Locomotive repowering & hybrid retrofits** · `🟠 demonstration`

Replacing or augmenting the diesel engines in existing locomotives with hybrid-electric, dual-fuel RNG, or battery modules cuts fuel use 30-50% at roughly half the cost of new locomotives, attacking the long-lived legacy fleet that full replacement can't reach for decades.

| [Wabtec](https://www.wabteccorp.com/locomotive/alternative-fuel-locomotives/FLXdrive) | incumbent | Locomotive modernization programs (DC-to-AC conversions) that cut fuel burn across legacy fleets, alongside FLXdrive hybridization | Thousands of modernizations delivered; modernization is a core profit segment |
| [⚠️ First Mode](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000026172/000002617225000010/cmi2025q18-kex99.htm) | startup | Hybrid hydrogen-battery retrofit powertrains for mining haul trucks and rail | Filed Chapter 11 in December 2024 after Anglo American pulled back; assets and technology portfolio bought by Cummins (announced Feb 2025) · **☠ shut down** |

Transit buses are hydrogen's strongest road niche because depot-based fueling solves the station problem and duty cycles favor fast refueling; European fuel-cell bus registrations grew ~163% in 2025 even as truck players collapsed.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Solaris Bus & Coach](https://www.sustainable-bus.com/news/solaris-results-2025/) | incumbent | European fuel-cell bus market leader (Urbino hydrogen family), owned by Spain's CAF Group | Delivered 306 hydrogen buses in 2025 for a 58% European FC-bus share; €1.18B revenue 2025 |
| [Wrightbus](https://www.sustainable-bus.com/news/wrightbus-record-2025/) | scaleup | Northern Irish maker of the world's first hydrogen double-decker and Kite Hydroliner single-deckers, expanding fast in Germany | 1,200+ buses produced in 2025 (+20% YoY); ~130 hydrogen buses on German roads by end-2025 (Saarbahn 28, Cottbus 46, WestVerkehr 12) |
| [⚠️ Van Hool](https://www.sustainable-bus.com/news/van-hool-vdl-crisis-future/) | incumbent | Belgian bus/coach maker that was an early fuel-cell bus pioneer in Europe and the US | Declared bankrupt April 2024; bus activities taken over by VDL/Schmitz Cargobull; De Lijn retired its Van Hool H2 buses and dismantled the Antwerp H2 station · **☠ shut down** |
| [CaetanoBus](https://www.sustainable-bus.com/fuel-cell-bus/fuel-cell-bus-hydrogen/) | incumbent | Portuguese builder (Toyota/Mitsui-backed) of the H2.City Gold fuel-cell bus using Toyota stacks | Fuel-cell bus fleets delivered across Spain, Portugal, Germany and UK |
| [New Flyer (NFI Group)](https://www.compositesworld.com/news/new-flyer-selects-hexagon-purus-h2-tanks-for-fifth-consecutive-year) | incumbent | North America's largest transit bus maker, building Xcelsior CHARGE FC hydrogen buses | Selected Hexagon Purus hydrogen tanks for the fifth consecutive year; growing US FC bus orders under FTA Low-No grants |

**Hydrogen passenger cars (light-duty FCEVs)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Fuel-cell sedans and SUVs refuel in minutes with zero tailpipe emissions, but collapsing station networks and $30+/kg retail hydrogen have shrunk the market to a few OEM flagships and fleet niches, making this a contrarian bet on future infrastructure.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Toyota](https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/is-hydrogen-the-future-for-cars-manufacturers-havent-given-up-on-it-yet/4020674.article) | incumbent | Mirai, the highest-volume FCEV car ever, plus third-generation fuel-cell systems licensed to other OEMs | Mirai sales slumped with California's station closures, but Toyota continues FC development and supplies BMW's 2028 program |
| [Hyundai Motor](https://evmagazine.com/top10/top-10-hydrogen-cars) | incumbent | Nexo FCEV SUV, refreshed with a new generation launched 2025 (from the Initium concept) | One of only two FCEV cars in series production globally; Korea remains the largest FCEV car market |
| [Honda](https://evmagazine.com/top10/top-10-hydrogen-cars) | incumbent | CR-V e:FCEV, a US-built plug-in hybrid fuel-cell SUV using a co-developed GM fuel-cell system | Low-volume lease program in California; keeps Honda's FC supply chain alive for trucks/stationary |
| [BMW](https://fortune.com/2025/07/27/bmw-ix5-hydrogen-car-production-2028-battery-electric-vehicle/) | incumbent | iX5 Hydrogen pilot fleet, with the brand's first series-production FCEV due 2028 using Toyota's gen-3 stack | 1M+ km of pilot-fleet testing complete; 2028 series launch confirmed for Germany/France first |
| [Riversimple](https://drivinghydrogen.com/2025/08/15/riversimple-to-launch-all-inclusive-hydrogen-car-subscription/) | startup | Welsh maker of the ultra-light two-seat Rasa FCEV offered only via all-inclusive subscription (insurance, fuel, servicing bundled) | Beta testing in Abergavenny with subscription launch announced August 2025 — still pre-commercial after 20+ years |
| [HysetCo](https://www.hysetco.com) | scaleup | Paris operator of Europe's largest hydrogen taxi fleet (Hype legacy) with its own urban refueling stations — the fleet-plus-depot model that makes FCEV cars pencil | Raised ~€200M in 2024 led by Hy24 to scale Paris-region fleet and stations |
| [Hopium](https://www.hopium.com) | startup | French startup that abandoned its Machina hydrogen sedan after near-collapse and pivoted to selling fuel-cell stacks | Went through judicial reorganization in 2023; survival as a component supplier unproven · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Retail FCEV cars are in retreat — Shell closed all California light-duty stations in 2024 and Mirai resale values cratered — because chicken-and-egg station economics fail at low vehicle density. The viable opening is captive fleets with depot fueling (taxis, government fleets) as HysetCo demonstrates, not retail.
