| [Steffes](https://steffes.com/) | incumbent | Grid-enabled water heating controls and ETS systems long deployed by rural co-ops and municipal utilities for load management. | Decades-long incumbent in utility-controlled water heating |
| [Mixergy](https://www.mixergy.co.uk/) | startup | UK smart stratified hot-water cylinders that heat only the water needed and respond to tariff/grid signals. | Tens of thousands of UK installs via housing providers and energy suppliers |

> **White space:** Despite being the cheapest flexible storage on the grid, this space has almost no venture activity: water heaters are sold through plumbers on burnout replacement, and the flexibility value accrues to utilities rather than the homeowner (split incentives). State CTA-2045 mandates (WA, OR) and 15-minute wholesale settlement create an opening for fleet aggregators and OEM-embedded software, as consumer retrofit plays (e.g., Aquanta) never reached scale.

**Smart ventilation, HRV/ERV and IAQ-driven HVAC load reduction** · `🟡 scaling`

Demand-controlled and heat-recovery ventilation plus sorbent air cleaning deliver required fresh air with far less conditioning energy — attacking the ventilation share of HVAC load while improving indoor air quality.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Zehnder](https://www.zehndergroup.com/) | incumbent | European leader in high-efficiency HRV/ERV (ComfoAir) recovering up to ~90% of heat from exhaust air in tight, electrified homes. | Listed Swiss group; the default ventilation spec for Passive House projects |
| [enVerid](https://enverid.com/) | startup | Sorbent-based HVAC Load Reduction modules that scrub CO2/VOCs indoors so buildings can cut outside-air intake up to 80% and HVAC energy up to 40% under ASHRAE 62.1 IAQP. | $20M round (2020) plus DOE cost-shared development; effectively alone in sorbent OA-reduction |
| [Airthings](https://www.airthings.com/) | scaleup | Radon/CO2/IAQ sensors whose 'Airthings for Business' data drives demand-controlled ventilation and HVAC optimization. | Oslo Bors-listed; millions of sensors sold |
| [Kaiterra](https://www.kaiterra.com/) | startup | Commercial IAQ monitoring integrated with BMS to balance ventilation energy against air-quality targets (RESET/WELL compliance). | Enterprise IAQ deployments across global CRE |
| [Broan-NuTone](https://www.broan-nutone.com/) | incumbent | Largest North American residential ventilation maker; Overture system links IAQ sensors to fresh-air appliances for automated ventilation. | Madison Air portfolio company with dominant retrofit channel |
| [Panasonic](https://na.panasonic.com/) | incumbent | WhisperGreen/ERV lines plus IAQ sensing bring spot and balanced ventilation with efficiency controls to mainstream homebuilding. | Global appliance incumbent in residential IAQ/ventilation |
| [Aldes](https://www.aldes.com/) | incumbent | French ventilation group behind demand-controlled ventilation (humidity-sensitive extract) standard in EU dwellings. | Decades-deployed DCV incumbent across Europe |
| [Minotair](https://www.minotair.com/) | startup | Canadian heat-pump ventilator combining HRV, dehumidification and supplemental heating/cooling in one cold-climate unit. | Niche but shipping product in North American cold climates |

> **White space:** Ventilation energy is governed by code minimums rather than economics, so few startups can monetize savings — enVerid is nearly alone in load-reduction hardware and most innovation sits inside European incumbents. Post-COVID IAQ expectations plus electrification (ventilation loads on heat pumps) create an opening for controls that co-optimize air quality and energy, and for US adoption of EU-style demand-controlled ventilation.

**Lighting and plug-load controls (networked LED, occupancy-driven)** · `🟢 mature`

Networked luminaire-level controls, occupancy/daylight sensing and smart plug-load management squeeze the remaining 30-60% savings beyond the LED conversion and add a sensor backbone for building optimization.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Lutron](https://www.lutron.com/) | incumbent | Private lighting-controls leader spanning residential (Caseta/RadioRA) to commercial wireless systems (Vive, Athena). | Dominant specification share in US lighting control |
| [Signify](https://www.signify.com/) | incumbent | World's largest lighting maker; Interact connected-lighting platform turns LED networks into IoT sensing/energy systems. | Euronext-listed; millions of connected light points on Interact |
| [Acuity Brands](https://www.acuitybrands.com/) | incumbent | nLight networked lighting controls plus Distech Controls building automation make it the most controls-integrated US luminaire maker. | NYSE-listed; nLight embedded across its fixture portfolio |
| [Legrand](https://www.legrand.us/) | incumbent | Wattstopper occupancy/daylight controls and plug-load management meeting Title 24-style code requirements. | Global electrical incumbent; code-driven controls volume |
| [Enlighted](https://www.enlightedinc.com/) | scaleup | Luminaire-level sensor network using lighting as a data backbone for occupancy analytics and HVAC optimization. | Acquired by Siemens (2018); now part of Siemens' smart-buildings stack · **acquired** |
| [Casambi](https://www.casambi.com/) | scaleup | Finnish Bluetooth-mesh lighting control ecosystem embedded by hundreds of fixture/driver OEMs as a wireless retrofit standard. | Fast-growing OEM ecosystem across Europe/US |
| [Sapient Industries](https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/sapient-industries) | startup | AI plug-load management that learns device behavior at the outlet and automatically de-energizes idle equipment. | ~$24.9M raised (incl. $20M round, 2021); one of few pure plug-load players |

> **White space:** Post-LED, lighting-control value consolidated into incumbent ecosystems (Enlighted into Siemens, Digital Lumens into OSRAM), leaving little room for fixture-side startups. The genuine gap is plug loads — now approaching a third of commercial building electricity and largely uncontrolled — where Sapient is among the only venture-backed players.

### Low-Carbon Structural Materials & Industrialized Construction

**Mass timber manufacturing (CLT, glulam, DLT/NLT)** · `🟡 scaling`

Factories laminate dimensional lumber into large structural panels and beams (CLT, glulam, DLT/NLT) that replace much of a building's concrete and steel frame while storing biogenic carbon in the structure for decades.

| [Binderholz](https://www.binderholz.com/en-us/) | incumbent | Family-owned Austrian group that is among the world's largest integrated solid-wood processors, producing CLT and glulam at scale with US capacity via the Klausner mill acquisitions. | 60+ sites across Europe and US; among largest global sawmill/CLT groups |
| [KLH Massivholz](https://www.klh.at/en/) | incumbent | Austrian CLT pioneer producing cross-laminated timber since 1999 and exporting panels worldwide. | 25+ years of CLT production; one of the original European CLT brands |
| [Mercer Mass Timber](https://mercermasstimber.com/) | incumbent | Largest North American mass-timber producer after buying Structurlam's plants; runs one of the world's largest CLT presses in Spokane Valley, WA plus glulam capacity. | Acquired Structurlam assets for ~$81M (2023); ~45,000 m3 glulam plus large-format CLT capacity |
| [⚠️ Structurlam](https://mercerint.com/our-operations/mercer-mass-timber/) | incumbent | Pioneer North American CLT/glulam maker (founded 1962, CLT since 2011) that supplied landmark projects like Brock Commons before collapsing. | Filed Chapter 11 in April 2023 after losing the Walmart HQ contract; BC and Arkansas plants sold to Mercer International for ~$81M · **☠ shut down** |

**Engineered bamboo and fast-growing-fiber structural products** · `🟠 demonstration`

Bamboo and other fast-growing grasses are laminated or pressed into structural studs, beams and wall panels that match timber strength while regrowing in 3-5 years and sequestering carbon faster per acre than trees.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [BamCore](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/bamcore/__5KNsLjCiiK76evwVIpux5HS3xnLjIyspNC6SZgmE0ZE) | startup | Hollow-core bamboo-hybrid panelized wall system (Prime Wall) that replaces stud framing in low-rise housing with higher insulation and lower carbon. | Series B raised May 2024; Tracxn reports ~$142M cumulative funding across 10 rounds; selected for a federal low-carbon building materials grant (Jul 2024) |
| [Rizome](https://www.bworldonline.com/economy/2023/05/30/525904/100-m-engineered-bamboo-facility-to-rise-in-cagayan-de-oro/) | startup | Grows giant bamboo in the Philippines and Florida and manufactures engineered bamboo lumber, building the supply chain end to end. | $100M engineered-bamboo facility in Cagayan de Oro; won 2024 US Secretary of State's Award for Corporate Excellence (Climate Resilience) |
| [ReNuTeq](https://www.renuteq.com/) | startup | St. Louis maker of structural engineered bamboo (SEB) glulam-style frames and components, fire-tested for commercial projects. | Commercial installs including the Danforth Plant Science Center Farm Pavilion (2024) |
| [MOSO International](https://www.moso-bamboo.com/) | incumbent | Dutch market leader in industrial bamboo products (beams, panels, decking, cladding) with global distribution, mostly semi-structural applications. | 25+ years in bamboo products; distribution across 50+ countries |

> **White space:** Almost no code-approved structural bamboo exists in Western markets: the fiber supply sits in the tropics, ICC/Eurocode certification is slow and expensive, and lamination plants are capital-intensive. The opening is code-certified bamboo studs/panels produced near equatorial fiber with US production-builder distribution, sold on hurricane and fire performance plus carbon — the path BamCore's builder partnerships and Rizome's $100M plant are testing.

**Carbon-storing and bio-based boards, blocks and finishes** · `🟠 demonstration`

Agricultural fibers (grass, straw, hemp) and recycled cellulose are pressed into drop-in replacements for OSB, drywall and masonry blocks, storing biogenic carbon in walls instead of emitting it from gypsum, cement and clear-cut timber.

| [IsoHemp](https://www.isohemp.com/en) | scaleup | Belgian manufacturer of hempcrete masonry blocks with an automated plant, the European volume leader for hemp-lime construction. | Factory capacity ~5M blocks/yr; thousands of projects across Europe |
| [JustBioFiber](https://justbiofiber.com/) | startup | Alberta maker of interlocking Lego-style structural hempcrete blocks with an integrated load-bearing frame. | Built the zero-carbon Trent University forensics building; pandemic-era financial struggles reported (2024) and little recent commercial activity visible · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Distribution is the moat, not chemistry: gypsum and OSB incumbents (USG, Knauf, Saint-Gobain, LP) own contractor channels and price points, so bio-boards historically die in the 'green premium' boutique niche. Plantd's national-builder offtake model (D.R. Horton) is the template — winning one production homebuilder beats a thousand one-off architect specs.

**Bio-based and carbon-storing insulation** · `🟡 scaling`

Wood fiber, hemp, cellulose and wool are manufactured into batt, board and blown insulation that matches mineral and foam R-values with a fraction of the embodied carbon, often storing more carbon than production emits.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Steico](https://www.steico.com/en) | incumbent | World's largest wood-fibre insulation manufacturer (Germany/Poland), supplying batts, boards and blown fiber across Europe. | Listed German leader at hundreds of millions of euros in revenue; Kingspan acquired a 51% majority stake (announced 2023) |
| [Gutex](https://gutex.de/en/) | incumbent | Century-old Black Forest wood-fibre insulation board maker now pushing into North American distribution. | One of Europe's oldest and largest wood-fibre board producers |
| [TimberHP (GO Lab)](https://www.centralmaine.com/2025/06/25/madisons-timberhp-emerges-from-chapter-11-bankruptcy-with-eye-on-sustainable-future/) | startup | First and only North American wood-fiber insulation plant, a retrofit of the Madison, Maine paper mill producing TimberFill, TimberBatt and TimberBoard. | Filed Chapter 11 Mar 2025 after $30M+ construction overruns; emerged in 77 days (Jun 2025) with bondholders led by BlackRock affiliates converting to equity and ~$29M new financing |
| [Hempitecture](https://www.ornl.gov/news/innovation-crossroads-company-hempitecture-receives-84-million-doe-funding) | startup | Idaho manufacturer of HempWool batt insulation and PlantPanel exterior boards, building a second East Coast plant in Tennessee. | $8.4M DOE MESC grant; ~$6M equity crowdfunding (2025); $1.1M NYSERDA grant |

> **White space:** North American wood-fiber capacity is effectively a one-plant monopoly (TimberHP) versus a dozen mature European mills, and TimberHP's Chapter 11 reflected first-of-a-kind mill-retrofit cost risk rather than demand risk — products kept selling through bankruptcy. The opening: second and third NA plants sited on existing sawmill residue streams, financed with project debt rather than venture equity, plus straw/hemp lines feeding code-friendly batt formats.

**Prefab/modular low-energy construction and SIP systems** · `🟡 scaling`

Factory-built panels and volumetric modules — often structural insulated panels or insulated composite skins — compress build schedules and cut both material waste and operational energy through tight, well-insulated envelopes.

> **White space:** Single-family economics remain unproven — printing replaces one trade among thirty, and two capex-heavy players failed in 18 months (Diamond Age, Mighty Buildings). The defensible openings are commercial/retail printing where schedule is the value (Alquist-Walmart), printer-as-product OEM models (COBOD), and genuinely low-cement printable mixes, since the material — not the robot — is the carbon story.

Openings: robotic processing that collapses labor cost (Urban Machine's wedge), salvage-to-engineered-product upgrading (Cambium's salvaged-wood CLT), and material passports positioned ahead of EU enforcement deadlines.

### Refrigerants & Commercial Refrigeration

**Low-GWP refrigerant chemistry and production (HFOs, low-GWP blends)** · `🟢 mature`

Fluorochemical producers synthesize hydrofluoroolefins (HFOs) and low-GWP blends that drop into air conditioning and refrigeration equipment with 90-99% lower warming potential than the HFCs being phased down under the AIM Act and EU F-gas rules, making this the fastest lever for cutting refrigerant emissions at scale.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Chemours](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001627223/000095017025103204/cc-ex99_1.htm) | incumbent | Produces the Opteon HFO refrigerant family (R-1234yf, R-454B etc.) and is the US market leader in AIM Act transition chemistry. | Opteon refrigerant revenue +80% YoY in Q3 2025, now ~80% of total refrigerant sales; completed neat-Opteon capacity expansion at Corpus Christi in 2025. |
| [Honeywell](https://advancedmaterials.honeywell.com/us/en/products/air-conditioning-refrigeration-and-heating/solstice-hfos) | incumbent | Makes the Solstice HFO portfolio (1234yf, 1234ze, R-454B) — the other half of the global HFO patent duopoly with Chemours. | Multi-billion-dollar cumulative Solstice sales; doubled Baton Rouge 1234ze capacity; in May 2025 began supplying HFO blends to Arkema for resale. |
| [Koura (Orbia)](https://www.kouraglobal.com/) | incumbent | Orbia's fluorine business; vertically integrated from its own fluorspar mine into Klea-brand low-GWP refrigerants and propellants. | One of the few non-US/Japan HFO/low-GWP producers; mine-to-molecule integration gives feedstock cost advantage. |
| [Arkema](https://www.achrnews.com/articles/164662-arkema-to-offer-r-454b-and-other-low-gwp-refrigerants) | incumbent | Sells Forane-brand refrigerants and in May 2025 struck a commercial arrangement with Honeywell to offer R-454B and other low-GWP HFO blends. | Forane R-454B (GWP 466) specified by multiple HVAC OEMs as the R-410A successor; deal announced May 2025. |
| [Daikin (Daikin Chemical)](https://www.hpac.com/columns/engineering-green-buildings/article/21118831/refrigerants-energy-efficiency-air-conditioning) | incumbent | Only company that is both a refrigerant chemical producer and the world's largest AC OEM; champions mildly-low-GWP R-32 and develops HFO blends. | R-32 now the default in residential AC globally; partnered with Honeywell to expand Solstice use in Japan. |
| [Zhejiang Juhua](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/refrigerants-market/companies) | incumbent | China's largest fluororefrigerant producer by volume, building HFO-1234yf/ze capacity as Chinese HFC quotas tighten under Kigali. | Among top global refrigerant producers by tonnage; multiple HFO capacity additions announced 2024-2025. |

> **White space:** No startup layer exists and likely cannot: fluorochemical plants cost hundreds of millions, HFO process IP is locked up by the Chemours-Honeywell patent estate, and growing PFAS/TFA scrutiny of HFOs in Europe makes new fluorinated molecules a liability; the real opening is on the natural-refrigerant side (equipment, not chemistry) and in TFA-risk analytics.

**Natural-refrigerant equipment (CO2 transcritical racks, R290 self-contained cases, ammonia systems)** · `🟡 scaling`

Equipment OEMs replace HFC systems entirely with refrigerants that have near-zero warming potential — CO2 (GWP 1) rack systems for supermarkets, propane/R290 (GWP ~3) sealed display cases, and low-charge ammonia for industrial cold storage — eliminating refrigerant emissions at the source rather than managing them.

**Refrigerant recovery, reclamation and destruction (incl. carbon-credit-financed models)** · `🟡 scaling`

Companies collect used or stockpiled refrigerant and either purify it back to spec for resale (reclamation, now mandated for servicing under EPA's ER&R rule) or incinerate it for carbon credits, preventing gases up to 10,000x more potent than CO2 from venting to the atmosphere.

> **White space:** The US reclaim market is consolidating around a few incumbents, but recovery rates remain ~5-10% of theoretical and the Global South has almost no collection infrastructure — Recoolit's Google deal shows corporate buyers will fund technician-network models in Article 5 countries, and EPA's 2026-2029 reclaim mandates plus state rules (CARB) create room for tech-enabled aggregation of the fragmented contractor recovery chain.

**Refrigerant leak detection and monitoring hardware** · `🟢 mature`

Fixed and networked gas sensors continuously sniff machine rooms, sales-floor cases and chillers for refrigerant leaks — supermarkets typically leak ~25% of their charge annually — and new EPA AIM Act rules mandating automatic leak detection on large systems from 2026-2027 are turning a safety product into a compliance requirement.

> **White space:** Hardware is incumbent-dominated with essentially no venture-backed entrants — sensing physics (infrared/semiconductor cells) is commoditized and channels run through HVAC distribution — but the EPA's automatic-leak-detection mandate (effective 2026-2027) plus natural-refrigerant safety sensing (CO2/R290 in occupied spaces) creates an opening for cheap networked per-case sensors fused with software analytics, which is currently being attacked from the software side (e.g., Axiom Cloud's sensorless leak detection) rather than by new hardware players.

**Refrigerant compliance and lifecycle management software** · `🟡 scaling`

SaaS platforms track every cylinder, charge, leak event and repair across an equipment fleet to automate EPA Section 608/AIM Act and EU F-gas recordkeeping — newly urgent because the EPA ER&R rule's leak-repair, ALD and reporting requirements took effect January 2026 and pull thousands of previously exempt systems into regulation.

| [Facilio](https://www.nexuslabs.online/content/grocery-facility-software-silos-refrigerant-compliance) | scaleup | Connected-CMMS platform adding refrigerant compliance to unify the siloed FM tools grocers run today. | ~$35M Series B (2023, Dragoneer); pitching grocery chains on consolidating refrigerant, energy and work-order software. |

> **White space:** The category is fragmented between legacy enterprise tools and tiny contractor apps with no clear venture-scale winner; the Jan 2026 ER&R reporting wave, 2027 ALD mandates and EU F-gas 2024 recast force every operator of >15-lb systems into auditable digital records, an opening for a modern system-of-record that fuses sensor data, work orders and Scope 1 emissions reporting — currently being approached sideways by CMMS (Fexa, Facilio) and monitoring (Axiom) players rather than head-on.

**Grocery and building refrigeration optimization (AI monitoring/controls, case doors, anti-sweat, thermal storage)** · `🟡 scaling`

Software, controls and retrofit hardware squeeze 10-40% energy and leak reductions out of existing refrigeration fleets — AI that watches rack telemetry to catch leaks and tune setpoints, retrofitted glass doors and adaptive anti-sweat heater controls, and phase-change thermal storage that shifts compressor load off peak — delivering emissions cuts without replacing the refrigeration system.

**Solid-state and novel-cycle refrigeration (thermoelectric, magnetocaloric, elastocaloric)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Replaces the vapor-compression cycle entirely — thermoelectric chips, magnetocaloric alloys cycled through magnetic fields, or elastocaloric shape-memory metals — to make refrigerant-free, quiet, precisely controlled cooling for merchandisers and cold cases, eliminating both refrigerant emissions and compressor losses if efficiency and cost can match incumbents.

EUR 6.3M round); May-Sep 2025 supermarket pilot measured 15% better energy efficiency than a comparable R290 unit; won ATMO Europe 2025 refrigeration innovation award. |

## Industry & Manufacturing

The hardest-to-abate sector: steel, cement, chemicals, hydrogen, ammonia, process heat, and the minerals supply chain that everything else depends on. This is where the innovation gap is widest and where first-of-a-kind plant financing decides who survives.

*9 solution areas · 105 variations · 600 company entries (564 unique companies; 16 marked dead, 8 acquired, 24 unverified)*

**Maturity at a glance (variations per stage):** Green Iron, Steel & Metals (1 mature, 5 demonstration, 4 pilot) · Low-Carbon Cement & Concrete (1 mature, 4 scaling, 2 demonstration, 4 pilot) · Clean Hydrogen Production (1 mature, 3 scaling, 3 demonstration, 5 pilot) · Green Ammonia & Fertilizers (1 mature, 2 scaling, 4 demonstration, 2 pilot, 1 lab) · Green Chemicals & Bio/CO2-Based Materials (4 scaling, 5 demonstration, 1 pilot) · Plastics & Polymer Circularity (4 scaling, 9 demonstration, 3 pilot) · Industrial Heat & Process Electrification (1 mature, 6 scaling, 5 demonstration) · Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining (3 scaling, 7 demonstration, 3 pilot) · Battery & Materials Recycling (2 mature, 4 scaling, 5 demonstration)

**Solution areas:** [Green Iron, Steel & Metals](#green-iron-steel-metals) · [Low-Carbon Cement & Concrete](#low-carbon-cement-concrete) · [Clean Hydrogen Production](#clean-hydrogen-production) · [Green Ammonia & Fertilizers](#green-ammonia-fertilizers) · [Green Chemicals & Bio/CO2-Based Materials](#green-chemicals-bioco2-based-materials) · [Plastics & Polymer Circularity](#plastics-polymer-circularity) · [Industrial Heat & Process Electrification](#industrial-heat-process-electrification) · [Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining](#critical-minerals-extraction-refining) · [Battery & Materials Recycling](#battery-materials-recycling)

### Green Iron, Steel & Metals

**Hydrogen direct reduced iron (H2-DRI) plants and green iron/HBI developers** · `🟠 demonstration`

Green hydrogen replaces coal/coke to strip oxygen from iron ore in shaft or fluidized-bed furnaces, yielding direct reduced iron (DRI/HBI) that is melted in electric furnaces — the leading route to near-zero primary steel, cutting ~90% of blast-furnace CO2.

**Molten oxide electrolysis (MOE) of iron ore** · `🔵 pilot`

Electricity is passed through iron ore dissolved in a ~1,600°C molten oxide bath using an inert anode, splitting ore directly into liquid iron and oxygen with zero process CO2 when run on clean power.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Boston Metal](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/03/12/3041404/0/en/Boston-Metal-Commissions-Industrial-Scale-Cell-in-Crucial-Green-Steel-Milestone.html) | scaleup | MIT spinout running inert-anode MOE cells for green steel in Woburn, MA, plus a Brazilian subsidiary applying MOE to recover high-value metals (Nb, Ta, Sn) from mining waste as an early revenue wedge. | ~$370M raised including $262M Series C (ArcelorMittal, Microsoft, BHP among investors); industrial-scale green-steel cell commissioned March 2025; Brazil 10 ktpa high-value-metals plant slated for 2026; first steel demonstration plant planned 2026 |

> **White space:** Effectively a one-company field: inert anodes must survive 1,600°C corrosive oxide melts and the process needs very cheap firm clean power, so nobody else has followed Boston Metal out of the lab. Openings are alternative anode materials/chemistries and Boston Metal's own playbook — monetizing high-margin ferroalloys and critical metals first, where $/tonne tolerance is far higher than commodity steel.

**Low-temperature aqueous/electrochemical ironmaking (iron electrowinning)** · `🔵 pilot`

Iron ore is dissolved in acid or alkaline solution and pure iron is electroplated out at 60-110°C, letting intermittent renewables make iron without coke ovens, DR-grade pellets, or hydrogen infrastructure.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Electra](https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/green-steel/electra-clean-iron-investment-electrowinning) | startup | Acid-based electrowinning at ~60°C that accepts low-grade ores and produces 99% pure iron plates for EAF steelmaking. | $186M Series B April 2025 co-led by Capricorn and Temasek (BHP, Rio Tinto, Nucor, Breakthrough Energy among investors), >$214M total plus $30M follow-on; 500 tpy demonstration plant in Jefferson County, Colorado by early 2026; Meta bought its first green-iron EACs and Nucor partnership signed |
| [ArcelorMittal + John Cockerill (Volteron)](https://johncockerill.com/en/press-and-news/news/arcelormittal-john-cockerill-announce-volteron/) | incumbent | Industrializing the EU Siderwin alkaline iron-electrowinning process into Volteron, the first industrial-scale low-temperature iron electrolysis plant. | Siderwin pilot completed under Horizon 2020; first 40,000-80,000 tpa plant targeted to start production in 2027, with 0.3-1 Mtpa expansion intended |
| [Element Zero](https://www.mining.com/fortescue-ends-bitter-green-iron-battle-with-element-zero/) | startup | Australian startup (ex-Fortescue scientists) using electrochemical reduction with ionic-liquid electrolytes to make green iron and other metals from ores. | Survived a two-year Fortescue trade-secrets lawsuit settled November 2025 with damages claims dismissed and cost orders vacated; described in court reporting as financially strained |

> **White space:** Electrowinning's low current densities mean enormous cell area and capex per tonne — the physics that kept it out of ironmaking for a century — so only three credible players exist. The opening is pairing cells with cheap curtailed renewables (the process tolerates intermittency, unlike furnaces) and selling ultra-pure iron into premium niches like powders and electrical steel before attacking bulk steel.

**Flash and single-step novel ironmaking reactors** · `🔵 pilot`

Fine iron ore concentrate reacts in seconds with hydrogen, methane, or concentrated laser/electric heat in a single vessel, skipping the pelletizing/sintering and multi-unit flowsheets that add cost and emissions to conventional and H2-DRI routes.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Hertha Metals](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250722728868/en/Hertha-Metals-Unveils-Breakthrough-Process-to-Accelerate-American-Made-Steel-and-High-Purity-Iron-Production) | startup | Single-step reactor converting ore fines directly to molten steel and high-purity iron using methane today and hydrogen-ready chemistry, in Conroe, Texas. | >$17M from Khosla Ventures, Breakthrough Energy Fellows, Pear VC, Clean Energy Ventures; continuous 1 tonne/day pilot running since late 2024; 9,000 tpa plant groundbreaking January 2026 |
| [Limelight Steel](https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/green-steel/us-awards-28m-for-cutting-edge-tech-to-clean-up-iron-and-steel) | startup | Oakland, CA startup building a laser furnace that reduces iron ore to molten iron with roughly half the energy and >80% lower emissions than a blast furnace. | $2.9M ARPA-E award (part of a 2025 $28M federal iron/steel tech package); pre-seed/seed stage |
| [Calix](https://www.esgtoday.com/rio-tinto-invests-23-million-in-green-iron-plant-pauses-bioiron-project/) | scaleup | ASX-listed company whose ZESTY electric flash calciner makes hydrogen-DRI directly from iron ore fines without agglomeration. | Rio Tinto signed a joint development agreement and invested $23M (Nov 2025) in the proposed ZESTY green iron demonstration plant at Kwinana, WA, alongside ARENA support |

> **White space:** Only ~4% of seaborne ore is DR-pellet grade, so fines-tolerant single-step reactors attack a real $50-80/t pellet-premium gap — yet the field is tiny because high-temperature fines handling and product consistency are unforgiving, and the University of Utah flash-ironmaking lineage (DOE-funded since the 2010s) still has no commercial operator. Room remains for new reactor entrants with capital-light pilots, as Hertha's $17M-to-1tpd economics demonstrated.

**Hydrogen plasma, smelting reduction and electric smelting furnaces (ESF)** · `🔵 pilot`

Electrically powered smelting vessels or hydrogen plasma arcs melt and finish reducing ore or low-grade DRI, letting abundant mid-grade ores (which H2-DRI shaft furnaces cannot take) feed clean steelmaking without blast furnaces.

| [Primetals Technologies (with Mitsubishi Corp)](https://www.primetals.com/en/news/2025083472-construction-begins-on-hydrogen-based-ironmaking-plant-in-linz-austria/) | incumbent | Supplies HYFOR — the first fluidized-bed hydrogen reduction of ore fines, piloted at Donawitz since 2021 — paired with its electric 'Smelter' furnace producing hot metal plus cement-grade slag. | Building the Hy4Smelt industrial-scale demonstration plant in Linz with voestalpine, Mitsubishi and Rio Tinto; startup planned end-2027 |
| [NeoSmelt (BlueScope, BHP, Rio Tinto, Woodside, Mitsui JV)](https://www.riotinto.com/en/news/releases/2025/neosmelt-welcomes-federal-government-support-and-signs-two-new-participants-for-groundbreaking-steel-decarbonisation-project) | incumbent | Consortium building Australia's largest ironmaking electric smelting furnace pilot at Kwinana, WA to prove DRI-ESF steelmaking from mid-grade Pilbara ores. | Expanded to five equal partners June 2025 with Australian federal government support; pilot targeted ~2028; DRI-ESF route claims up to 80% CO2 reduction |
| [Fortescue](https://www.gem.wiki/Fortescue_Christmas_Creek_Green_Metal_Project) | incumbent | Christmas Creek Green Metal Project combining on-site green hydrogen DRI with an electric smelting furnace to make green iron at an operating Pilbara mine. | US$50M project, >1,500 tpa capacity; first hot metal anticipated in the June quarter 2026 per its March 2026 quarterly report |
| [Tata Steel (HIsarna)](https://www.tatasteeleurope.com) | incumbent | Developed the HIsarna coal-based smelting reduction reactor at IJmuiden (20% CO2 cut, capture-ready), piloted since 2011. | HIsarna deprioritized as Tata Steel Nederland chose the DRI-EAF route for IJmuiden's transition; technology's future deployment unclear |

> **White space:** No startups operate here — smelting furnaces only pencil when bolted onto existing mills and need hundreds of MW of firm power, so the field is incumbent consortia. The strategic opening (and why BHP/Rio/BlueScope fund it) is unlocking mid-grade Pilbara ores for green steel; a licensable, ore-flexible ESF design would ride that need.

**Alternative chemical reduction routes: sodium-cycle ironmaking and biocarbon/biochar reductants** · `🟠 demonstration`

Coke is replaced with alternative reductants — recyclable sodium metal at 250-350°C oven temperatures, or sustainably grown charcoal/biomass in conventional-style furnaces — so iron can be made with little or no fossil CO2.

| [Aço Verde do Brasil (AVB)](https://www.spglobal.com/commodityinsights/en/market-insights/latest-news/agriculture/032521-brazils-avb-receives-carbon-neutral-steel-certificate) | scaleup | 600 ktpa integrated Brazilian mill running mini blast furnaces entirely on captive eucalyptus charcoal from 50,000 ha of plantations. | SGS-certified carbon-neutral steel producer (since 2021, ~0.06-0.10 tCO2/t steel); recognized by the World Economic Forum among near-zero steel pioneers |
| [Aperam](https://www.aperam.com) | incumbent | Stainless/specialty steelmaker whose BioEnergia unit supplies FSC-certified eucalyptus charcoal that fully fuels its Brazilian blast furnaces. | Charcoal-based ironmaking at Timóteo, Brazil for over a decade with >100,000 ha of plantations |
| [Rio Tinto (BioIron)](https://www.miningweekly.com/article/rio-tinto-pauses-bioiron-partners-on-new-low-emissions-steel-pilot-2025-11-17) | incumbent | BioIron process uses raw biomass and microwave energy instead of coal to reduce Pilbara ore fines, with net-negative potential when paired with CCS. | $143M R&D facility planned in WA after successful German pilot, but further furnace design work paused November 2025 pending technical de-risking; capital redirected to Calix ZESTY demo |

> **White space:** Sodium-cycle ironmaking has exactly one player (Helios) — alkali-metal handling risk and the energy round-trip of regenerating sodium deter investors, but a proven closed loop at oven temperatures could enable small modular iron plants. Biocarbon is land-constrained (Brazil-style charcoal cannot scale to 2 Gt of global steel), so it stays a regional niche — Rio Tinto's BioIron pause underlines the engineering risk.

**Scrap-EAF steelmaking expansion and DRI-EAF hybrid clean steel mills** · `🟢 mature`

Electric arc furnaces melt recycled scrap (or scrap blended with DRI), cutting roughly 70-90% of emissions versus blast furnaces — the only clean-steel route that is already mainstream, profitable, and expanding worldwide.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Nucor](https://www.nucor.com) | incumbent | Largest US steelmaker, 100% EAF-based, selling Econiq net-zero steel (renewable power plus offsets) to GM, and expanding sheet capacity. | ~$3.1B Apple Grove, WV sheet mill under construction; Econiq shipped since 2022 |
| [Steel Dynamics](https://www.steeldynamics.com) | incumbent | EAF flat-rolled leader whose 3 Mtpa Sinton, Texas mill is the template for low-carbon greenfield EAF sheet capacity. | ~$22B revenue EAF producer; Sinton ramped through 2023-25 |
| [U.S. Steel (Big River Steel)](https://www.ussteel.com) | incumbent | Built the Big River 2 EAF mega-mill in Arkansas (started late 2024), shifting its footprint toward low-emissions EAF steel. | Acquired by Nippon Steel in June 2025 (~$14.9B with US government golden share); BR2 operating · **acquired** |
| [Hyundai Steel](https://www.recyclingtoday.com/news/hyundai-kia-steel-mill-louisiana-danieli-technology-land-purchase-development-award/) | incumbent | Building a $5.8B, 2.7 Mtpa DRI-EAF integrated low-carbon mill in Ascension Parish, Louisiana to supply US auto plants. | Announced March 2025; 1,700-acre site purchased; construction from 2026, online ~2029-30 |
| [Tata Steel UK](https://www.letsrecycle.com/news/tata-steel-begins-construction-on-1-25bn-port-talbot-eaf/) | incumbent | Replacing Port Talbot's closed blast furnaces with a 3 Mtpa scrap-EAF — cutting ~90% of site emissions and ~7% of total UK industrial CO2. | £1.25B project with £500M UK government support; construction began July 2025, commissioning targeted end-2027 |
| [Algoma Steel](https://algoma.com) | incumbent | Completed Canada's highest-profile BF-to-EAF conversion at Sault Ste. Marie, producing its first EAF steel in 2025. | First EAF steel April 2025; full transition cuts ~70% of emissions; navigating US tariff pressure with Canadian government support |
| [Hybar](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/hybar-produces-its-first-steel-rebar-302470801.html) | startup | Greenfield 700 ktpa scrap-EAF rebar mill in Osceola, Arkansas powered by the largest behind-the-meter solar-plus-storage array in US industry. | ~$1B financing from a 2023 standing start; first rebar June 2025, grand opening November 2025; second mill planned |

| [British Steel](https://www.gem.wiki/British_Steel_Scunthorpe_plant) | incumbent | Scunthorpe blast furnaces seized under the UK's April 2025 Steel Industry (Special Measures) Act after Chinese owner Jingye moved to close them; EAF decarbonization plan unresolved. | Under effective nationalization since April 2025; EAF transition plans remain undecided · *status unverified* |

**CCUS retrofits on BF-BOF/DRI, top-gas recycling, and steel offgas-to-products** · `🟠 demonstration`

The CO/CO2-rich offgases of existing blast furnaces and DRI plants are captured, recycled back as reductant, or fermented/catalyzed into ethanol and chemicals — decarbonizing the ~2-billion-tonne installed fleet without rebuilding it.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [ADNOC / Emirates Steel (Al Reyadah)](https://www.adnoc.ae) | incumbent | Operates the world's only commercial-scale steel CCUS — capturing ~0.8 Mtpa of CO2 from gas-based DRI in Abu Dhabi for enhanced oil recovery since 2016. | Nearly a decade of continuous commercial operation; cornerstone of ADNOC's CCUS buildout |
| [LanzaTech](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843724/000162828025026378/lnzaex991-pressrelease1q25.htm) | scaleup | Gas fermentation (Carbalyst) converting steel offgas CO into ethanol — flagship Steelanol plant with ArcelorMittal Gent plus commercial JV plants with Shougang in China. | Steelanol (80 ML/yr) ramped with first ethanol barge December 2024, but severe financial distress: going-concern doubt, $40M Carbon Direct preferred (May 2025), 1-for-100 reverse split (Aug 2025), and a $0.02/share take-private proposal · *status unverified* |
| [ArcelorMittal](https://corporate.arcelormittal.com/media/news/non-regulatory-news/arcelormittal-and-lanzatech-announce-first-ethanol-samples-from-commercial-flagship-carbon-capture-and-utilisation-facility-in-ghent-belgium) | incumbent | Hosts the €200M Steelanol offgas-to-ethanol plant at Gent and the 3D/DMX amine capture pilot at Dunkirk on blast furnace gas. | Steelanol producing and shipping ethanol; ~125 ktpa CO2 reduction at Gent |
| [China Baowu](https://worldsteel.org/case-studies/environment/china-baowu-development-and-application-of-low-carbon-metallurgical-technology-based-on-hycrof/) | incumbent | World's largest steelmaker; its HyCROF hydrogen-enriched, top-gas-recycling oxygen blast furnace (with CO2 separation) is the leading BF retrofit demonstration, plus a 1 Mt hydrogen shaft furnace at Zhanjiang. | 2,500 m3 HyCROF commercial demonstration at Bayi Steel operating since September 2023 with ~16-21% CO2 cuts (~1 Mtpa avoided); group-wide rollout could cut >40 Mtpa |
| [thyssenkrupp (Carbon2Chem)](https://www.thyssenkrupp.com) | incumbent | Carbon2Chem pilot at Duisburg converts steel-mill gases into methanol and ammonia with partners including Fraunhofer and Covestro. | Pilot operating since 2018 with German federal funding across two project phases |
| [Nippon Steel (COURSE50)](https://www.nipponsteel.com) | incumbent | COURSE50/Super COURSE50 program injects hydrogen into blast furnaces and captures CO2 from top gas, proven on a test blast furnace in Japan. | Test furnace demonstrated >30% CO2 reduction; deployment planned on commercial furnaces around 2030 |
| [Carbon Clean](https://www.carbonclean.com) | scaleup | Modular CycloneCC capture units small enough to retrofit inside steel plants — piloted on Tata Steel Jamshedpur blast furnace gas (5 tpd) since 2021. | Backed by Chevron, Samsung Ventures and CEMEX; >$190M raised; multiple industrial pilots |

> **White space:** Only one commercial-scale capture system exists on steel worldwide (Al Reyadah — and on clean DRI gas, not dirty dilute BF gas), because thin steel margins cannot absorb capture costs without strong carbon pricing. The opening is modular capture plus utilization on Asia's young blast-furnace fleet (Baowu's HyCROF shows incumbent appetite), while LanzaTech's distress is a warning that offgas-to-chemicals must work without subsidy.

**Green aluminum: inert-anode smelting, low-carbon alumina refining, and low-carbon smelting/remelt** · `🟠 demonstration`

Inert anodes replace the consumable carbon anodes that burn into CO2 and PFCs (emitting only oxygen), while electrified alumina refining and renewable-powered or recycled-feed smelters attack the rest of aluminum's ~2% share of global emissions.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [ELYSIS (Alcoa + Rio Tinto JV)](https://elysis.com/en/elysis-achieves-breakthrough-with-commercial-size-cell-a-first-in-aluminium-production-using-the) | scaleup | JV (with Apple, Canada and Quebec backing) industrializing carbon-free inert-anode smelting cells. | First commercial-size 450 kA inert-anode cell started up at the Alma, Quebec smelter in November 2025 — a world first; demonstration plant under construction at Arvida |
| [Rio Tinto](https://www.riotinto.com/en/news/releases/2025/elysis-achieves-breakthrough-with-commercial-size-cell) | incumbent | Hosting and scaling ELYSIS cells at its hydro-powered Quebec smelters and leading construction of the Arvida inert-anode demonstration plant. | Alma 450 kA cell live November 2025; ELYSIS positioned as a core pillar of its aluminum decarbonization strategy |
| [Alcoa](https://www.alcoa.com) | incumbent | ELYSIS co-founder and inventor of its base technology; also piloting mechanical vapor recompression (MVR) to electrify alumina refining in Australia and selling Sustana low-carbon products. | ELYSIS milestone reached 2025; MVR refinery pilot backed by Australian government funding |
| [Rusal](https://www.lightmetalage.com/news/industry-news/smelting/rusal-produces-low-carbon-aluminum-using-inert-anode-technology/) | incumbent | Developed its own inert-anode cells at Krasnoyarsk producing aluminum with the world's lowest smelting footprint (<0.01 tCO2e/t scope 1-2), branded ALLOW INERTA. | Confirmed operational stability of inert-anode technology September 2025; commercial batches shipped to Chinese foil makers in 2025 |
| [Norsk Hydro](https://www.hydro.com/en/global/sustainability/our-roadmap-to-net-zero-emissions-in-aluminium-production/halzero-zero-emission-electrolysis-from-hydro) | incumbent | Developing HalZero — a chloride-route, fully decarbonized smelting process emitting only oxygen — alongside commercial CIRCAL 100R recycled and REDUXA low-carbon aluminum lines. | HalZero process steps maturing at its Porsgrunn test center; industrial concept pilot targeted toward end of the decade |
| [Emirates Global Aluminium](https://www.ega.ae) | incumbent | CelestiAL — the first aluminum smelted commercially with solar power (via Dubai's grid solar park), supplied to BMW and other customers since 2021. | Tens of thousands of tonnes of CelestiAL sold annually; expanding US recycling/remelt footprint |

> **White space:** Inert anodes are a 40-year graveyard of failed attempts (anode materials corrode at ~960°C in cryolite), so only deep-pocketed incumbents and state champions play — there is essentially no startup presence in primary aluminum. The under-explored opening is low-carbon alumina refining (MVR, electric calcination), which is ~25% of aluminum's footprint and has almost no dedicated companies.

**Other low-carbon structural metals: magnesium from brines, low-carbon titanium, green silicon/ferroalloys** · `🟠 demonstration`

Electrolytic and hydrogen/biocarbon chemistry is applied to other energy-intensive structural metals — magnesium from seawater/brines instead of China's coal-fired Pidgeon process, titanium powder without the energy-hungry Kroll process, biocarbon-reduced silicon — cutting emissions and import dependence together.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Magrathea Metals](https://www.magratheametals.com/news/100million) | startup | Electrolytic magnesium from seawater and brines with a proprietary low-cost dehydration step, claiming ~50% lower capex per tonne than competing routes. | >$100M total backing as of May 2026, including a $24M Series A (March 2026) and $19.6M from the US Department of Defense; pilot foundry operating; JV term sheet with TETRA Technologies for an Arkansas magnesium plant (Nov 2025) |
| [⚠️ US Magnesium](https://grist.org/business/us-magnesium-shutdown-supply-chain-mineral/) | incumbent | Was North America's only primary magnesium producer (Great Salt Lake brines, Utah) before halting production and collapsing. | Filed for bankruptcy September 2025 with the plant shuttered and no clear restart path — leaving the US with zero primary magnesium output · **☠ shut down** |
| [Latrobe Magnesium](https://latrobevalleyexpress.com.au/news/2025/12/09/us-backing-to-make-latrobe-great-again/) | startup | ASX-listed company extracting magnesium from brown-coal fly ash via a hydromet/thermal-reduction process in Victoria, Australia. | 1,000 tpa demonstration plant commissioned September 2025 (~A$70M spent); production temporarily halted by an equipment defect; raised A$10M and pursuing US government support for a 10,000 tpa stage 2 |
| [IperionX](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001898601/000114036126002866/ef20064210_ex99-1.htm) | scaleup | Produces titanium powder and parts from scrap and minerals in Virginia using the low-energy HAMR/HSPT processes (licensed from Univ. of Utah), bypassing the Kroll process. | NASDAQ-listed; 200 tpa powder capacity online in 2025 (up 60% without new capex), seven-fold scale-up to 1,400 tpa planned for 2027; $47.1M US DoD IBAS award fully obligated; EBITDA-positive inflection targeted end-2026 |
| [Metalysis](https://www.metalysis.com) | startup | UK company using the solid-state FFC Cambridge electrolytic process to make titanium and alloy powders directly from oxides without Kroll. | Bought out of administration in 2019 by Power Resources Group; continues niche powder production — a cautionary tale on scaling novel metal electrolysis · **acquired** |
| [Elkem](https://www.elkem.com) | incumbent | Norwegian silicon/ferrosilicon leader systematically substituting fossil coal with biocarbon in its smelting furnaces, targeting ~50% biocarbon in Norway. | Biocarbon used at industrial scale across Norwegian and Brazilian plants; pilot biocarbon production facilities operating |
| [Ferroglobe](https://www.ferroglobe.com) | incumbent | Largest western silicon-metal and ferroalloy producer marketing lower-carbon silicon (hydropower-heavy assets, partial biocarbon) for solar and battery supply chains. | NASDAQ-listed incumbent positioned as the non-Chinese low-carbon silicon source amid US/EU trade measures |

> **White space:** China produces ~90% of world magnesium via coal-fired Pidgeon retorts, and the 2025 US Magnesium bankruptcy erased North America's only primary supply — a wide-open, DoD-subsidized lane for electrolytic brine magnesium where Magrathea is nearly alone. The same import-dependence logic (and Kroll-process energy intensity) keeps low-carbon titanium underpopulated despite IperionX's traction.

### Low-Carbon Cement & Concrete

**Clinker substitution and engineered SCMs (calcined clays/LC3, tailings, glass, ashes)** · `🟡 scaling`

Swaps a large share of CO2-intensive Portland clinker for reactive minerals engineered from calcined clays, mine tailings, glass, ashes and slags — the cheapest, most code-compatible decarbonization lever (30-85% footprint cuts) and increasingly urgent as legacy fly ash and blast-furnace slag supplies shrink.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Terra CO2](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250702426008/en/Terra-CO2-Announces-Additional-Series-B-Funding-to-Scale-Sustainable-Cement-Production) | startup | Makes OPUS SCM from abundant local rock and mine tailings using a proprietary reactor, drop-in replacing up to 40% of cement | Series B totaling ~$124.5M (2025; BEV, Eagle Materials, GenZero, Just Climate, Cemex); $52.6M DOE award for 240kt/yr Magna, Utah plant using Rio Tinto Kennecott tailings |
| [Material Evolution (Mevo)](https://www.materialevolution.com/ultra-low-carbon-cement-plant/) | scaleup | Kiln-free alkali-fusion process turning industrial byproducts into MevoCem ultra-low-carbon cement (up to 85% CO2 reduction) | Mevo A1 plant in Wrexham, UK (120kt/yr) operational since Oct 2024 — UK's largest ultra-low-carbon cement producer; 2025 Constructing Excellence National Innovation Award |
| [Queens Carbon](https://www.cemnet.com/News/story/177292/queens-carbon-secures-us-14-5m-for-carbon-neutral-scms.html) | startup | Hydrothermal ~500C reactor producing carbon-neutral SCMs and cementitious materials that replace up to 50% of conventional cement | $10M seed (2024, Clean Energy Ventures; Buzzi Unicem USA strategic partner) plus $14.5M ARPA-E SCALEUP award; pilot system at a partner cement plant |
| [Carbon Upcycling Technologies](https://sustainablebiz.ca/carbon-upcycling-integrates-carbon-capture-cement-plant) | scaleup | CO2-activates steel slags, fly ash and clays in pressurized reactors to make enhanced SCMs while sequestering kiln CO2 | ~$54M raised ($26M 2023, $18M+$10M 2025); broke ground on Carbon 1 commercial CCU unit at Ash Grove's (CRH) Mississauga cement plant |

**Non-Portland and alternative binder chemistries (geopolymers, CSA, Mg- and brine-based, silicate-rock OPC)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Abandons limestone clinker altogether for binders made from alkali-activated slags and clays, calcium sulfoaluminate, magnesium or brine chemistry — cutting most process CO2 but fighting prescriptive concrete codes, supply logistics and conservative buyers.

**Electrochemical and low-temperature cement/lime synthesis** · `🔵 pilot`

Replaces the 1,450C fossil-fired kiln with electrochemical cells or sub-600C reactors that extract reactive calcium from non-carbonate rocks and wastes, eliminating both fuel and process emissions when powered by clean electricity.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Sublime Systems](https://www.constructiondive.com/news/sublime-pauses-factory-construction-funding-pullback/807835/) | startup | Ambient-temperature electrochemical process making ASTM C1157 'Sublime Cement' from non-carbonate feedstocks | >$200M raised including $75M from CRH and Holcim (2024) and a Microsoft EAC offtake (~622kt); DOE's $87M rescinded May 2025 forced a pause of the 30kt/yr Holyoke plant and ~10% layoffs (late 2025) |
| [Chement](https://www.chement.co) | startup | Room-temperature electrochemical route to clinker chemistry, ARPA-E backed | Lab-scale; little public activity since early grants — viability unconfirmed as of mid-2026 · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Physics works but economics are brutal — these routes trade cheap coal heat for electricity plus first-of-a-kind capex against a ~$100-130/t commodity, and the May 2025 DOE rescissions removed the leading US demonstrations; the opening is small modular plants sited on cheap clean power and underwritten by green-premium offtakes (Microsoft-style EAC deals from data-center builders) rather than head-to-head commodity competition.

**Biogenic and microbial cements** · `🔵 pilot`

Uses bacteria or microalgae to biomineralize calcium carbonate that binds aggregates at ambient temperature, growing masonry, tiles and blocks with near-zero kiln emissions.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Biomason](https://biomason.com/news) | scaleup | Microbially-grown bioLITH precast tiles and biocement, with licensed production in Europe (IBF, Denmark) | ~$104M+ raised including $36.7M Series D (Jan 2025; Novo Holdings, 2150); products commercially available and used in US/EU projects |
| [Prometheus Materials](https://prometheusmaterials.com) | startup | Photosynthetic microalgae bio-cement for zero-carbon masonry units and panels (CU Boulder spinout) | Series A/B backed by Sofinnova Partners and Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund; pilot masonry production in Colorado |
| [Minus Materials](https://www.minusmaterials.com) | startup | Grows biogenic limestone from coccolithophore microalgae as a carbon-negative feedstock for clinker | CU Boulder spinout; pre-seed/lab stage with little public activity since 2023 · *status unverified* |
| [BioZeroc](https://biozeroc.com) | startup | UK startup producing bio-concrete via microbial calcium carbonate precipitation in place of cement | Pre-seed and Innovate UK funded; lab/prototype stage, current commercial status unverified · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Biology's slow precipitation rates and nutrient/water logistics cap biocement at premium precast, masonry and defense niches rather than ready-mix; the opening is high-margin architectural products, coastal/erosion hardening, and DoD expeditionary construction where cost-per-ton matters less than logistics.

**Kiln decarbonization hardware (electric kilns/calciners, solar calcination, oxyfuel, micro-modular kilns)** · `🔵 pilot`

Re-engineers kiln heat itself — rotodynamic electric heaters, concentrated-solar receivers, pure-oxyfuel combustion and micro-modular vertical kilns — to cut fuel CO2 and deliver concentrated, capture-ready process CO2 streams.

| [Heliogen](https://mercomcapital.com/zeo-energy-completes-acquisition-heliogen/) | startup | AI-steered heliostat fields for ~1,000C industrial heat, once pitched for cement calcination | SPAC'd 2021 near $2B valuation, collapsed, and was acquired by Zeo Energy in an all-stock deal (closed Aug 11, 2025) — cautionary tale for solar-heat-for-cement · **acquired** |
| [Coolbrook](https://coolbrook.com) | scaleup | RotoDynamic Heater electrifying kiln/calciner heat to ~1,000C using renewable electricity | Demonstrated ~1,000C electric heating at Brightlands (NL) pilot; partnerships with Cemex, UltraTech and ABB |

> **White space:** Kilns are 40-year assets needing 24/7 ultra-high-grade heat, so few startups attack the hardware directly and Heliogen's distressed sale shows pure-play solar heat struggled; the opening is electrified calciners that double as capture enablers by producing pure process-CO2 streams, sold through incumbent EPCs.

**CCUS on cement and lime plants** · `🟠 demonstration`

Captures the roughly 60% of cement CO2 that is unavoidable limestone process chemistry — via amine post-combustion, indirectly heated calcination, oxyfuel or cryogenic separation — and sends it to geological storage; the only route that decarbonizes the existing clinker fleet.

**CO2 mineralization and curing in concrete and aggregates** · `🟡 scaling`

Injects CO2 into fresh concrete, cures precast with flue gas, or reacts it with demolition concrete, olivine and Ca/Mg-rich industrial wastes so it permanently mineralizes as carbonate — turning the built environment into a carbon sink while often improving strength.

**Recycled cement and concrete circularity** · `🔵 pilot`

Recovers value from demolished concrete — reactivating old cement paste as clinker feed (including melting it as flux in steel-recycling electric arc furnaces) and smart-crushing waste into clean aggregates and reactive fines — avoiding new limestone calcination entirely.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Cambridge Electric Cement](https://www.enterprise.cam.ac.uk/news/cambridge-electric-cement-raises-2-25m-to-industrialise-low-carbon-circular-cement-production/) | startup | Uses recovered cement paste as the flux in steel-recycling EAFs, yielding recycled Portland clinker as a co-product of steel | £2.25M seed (2025, Zero Carbon Capital, L&G); £6.5M Innovate UK 'Cement 2 Zero' trials showing 50-75% CO2 reduction vs conventional clinker |
| [CemVision](https://group.vattenfall.com/press-and-media/pressreleases/2025/vattenfall-and-cemvision-sign-new-commercial-agreement-for-near-zero-carbon-cement) | startup | Swedish startup firing 'Re-ment' clinker from recycled concrete and mine waste in electrified/hydrogen kilns for near-zero cement | Commercial offtake agreement with Vattenfall signed 2025; pilot production and Nordic industrial partnerships |
| [Holcim](https://www.holcim.com) | incumbent | ECOCycle recycling platform feeding construction demolition materials back into cement, including a world-first 100% recycled-clinker production run (Altkirch, 2023) | Recycles ~10Mt/yr of construction demolition materials with expansion targets |
| [Heidelberg Materials](https://www.heidelbergmaterials.com) | incumbent | ReConcrete selective separation and recycled-paste re-clinkering R&D, including CO2 uptake in recycled fines | Industrial trials across European plants; part of its 2030 circularity targets |
| [Sika](https://www.sika.com) | incumbent | reCO2ver smart-crushing process separating old concrete into clean aggregate, sand and CO2-binding cement fines | Pilot/demonstration units with recyclers; part of Sika's circular concrete portfolio |

> **White space:** Hardened paste is only ~20-30% of demolition concrete, its reactivity is low, and virgin aggregate is nearly free, so standalone economics are weak and pure-plays are scarce; EU end-of-waste rules, rising landfill costs and the EAF steel boom create the opening — steel-cement symbiosis (the CEC model) and carbonation of recycled fines integrated into existing recycler networks.

### Clean Hydrogen Production

**Alkaline electrolyzers (incl. pressurized and advanced-membrane designs)** · `🟢 mature`

Century-old technology that splits water in a liquid potassium hydroxide electrolyte using cheap nickel-based electrodes, making it the lowest-capex and most widely deployed route to green hydrogen at gigawatt scale.

**Stimulated (orange) and subsurface-biological hydrogen** · `🔵 pilot`

Rather than hunting existing accumulations, these players manufacture hydrogen underground — injecting catalyst-bearing fluids into iron-rich rock to accelerate serpentinization, or feeding microbes in depleted oil reservoirs — turning geology itself into the reactor.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Vema Hydrogen](https://www.axios.com/pro/climate-deals/2025/02/18/vema-seed-stimulated-geologic-hydrogen) | startup | Injects catalyst-bearing brine into shallow iron-rich formations to stimulate hydrogen generation at claimed <$1/kg | $13M seed (Feb 2025, Extantia + Propeller); developing first full-scale stimulated-hydrogen pilot wells in North America |
| [Gold H2 (Cemvita spinout)](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220927005409/en/Cemvitas-Successful-Field-Test-Demonstrates-Gold-Hydrogen-Production-in-Situ) | startup | Injects engineered microbes into depleted oil wells to bioconvert residual hydrocarbons into hydrogen in situ | Permian Basin field trial measured H2 three orders of magnitude above baseline; spun out of Cemvita as dedicated subsidiary |
| [Eden GeoPower](https://www.edengeopower.com) | startup | Electrical reservoir stimulation to enhance permeability and reaction rates in iron-rich rock for hydrogen generation | ARPA-E-funded serpentinization work; core stimulation business spans geothermal and mining |

> **White space:** Barely three credible players because the chemistry is unproven at field scale: serpentinization kinetics are slow, catalyst delivery and hydrogen recovery from the same wellbore is an unsolved engineering loop, and there is no offtake infrastructure at remote sites. ARPA-E seeded the science in 2024; the opening is for oilfield-services-grade execution (drilling, stimulation, downhole separation) married to geochemistry — a natural play for service majors or well-capitalized spinouts.

| [Mote](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250304282371/en/Mote-Secures-$7-Million-Funding-in-First-Close-of-Series-A-Round-to-Advance-Companys-Carbon-Negative-Biomass-to-Energy-Technology) | startup | Gasifies forestry waste into hydrogen while geologically sequestering the biogenic CO2 (carbon-negative BECCS-H2) | $7M Series A first close (Mar 2025); Bakersfield and SMUD/Sacramento projects targeting operations 2027-28 |
| [Babcock & Wilcox](https://www.babcock.com) | incumbent | BrightLoop chemical-looping process converting biomass or waste fuels to hydrogen with inherent CO2 separation | First commercial-demonstration BrightLoop plant built in Massillon, Ohio; Wyoming and Louisiana projects in development |
| [Ways2H](https://ways2h.com) | startup | Japanese-licensed thermochemical conversion of MSW and medical waste to hydrogen in modular units | Tokyo and California pilots circa 2020-2022; little public activity since — status unclear · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Waste gasification has a 20-year graveyard (capex blowouts, feedstock contamination, syngas cleanup), and the two US flagships illustrate it — SGH2 stalled post-permit and Ways2H went quiet. The economics only close when tipping fees, LCFS/45V credits and hydrogen revenue stack; the opening is modular, non-combustion designs at existing landfill/utility sites with a creditworthy waste partner (the Raven SR–Republic–Chevron template).

**Biological, photocatalytic, solar-thermochemical and metal-water hydrogen routes** · `🔵 pilot`

Frontier routes that skip electrolysis entirely — engineered microbes fermenting crop waste, sunlight-driven photocatalysts splitting water directly, high-temperature solar redox cycles, and aluminum-water reactions that release hydrogen from scrap metal.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [HydGene Renewables](https://www.hydgene.com/post/hydgene-awarded-nsw-government-cti-funding-to-scale-on-farm-hydrogen-innovation) | startup | Engineered biocatalyst (dark fermentation) converting agricultural residues into on-site, on-demand carbon-negative hydrogen | A$6M seed (Agronomics, CEFC) plus A$2.5M NSW grant (2025); pilot ran continuously >2 years, producing high-purity H2 from wheat straw (Mar 2026) |
| [Sparc Hydrogen](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2025/12/16/sparc-hits-production-milestone-at-hydrogen-pilot-plant-in-australia/) | startup | JV (Sparc Technologies, Fortescue, Univ. of Adelaide) running the world's first on-sun photocatalytic water-splitting pilot using concentrated solar | Roseworthy pilot opened Jun 2025; sustained hydrogen production achieved Dec 2025; A$2.75M federal AEA grant |
| [SunHydrogen](https://www.sunhydrogen.com) | startup | Photoelectrochemical nanoparticle panels generating hydrogen directly from sunlight and water | OTC-listed; square-meter-scale demonstration modules with university and industrial partners (incl. Honda R&D collaboration); pre-revenue |
| [Found Energy](https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/10/23/1126397/startup-aluminum-zero-carbon-fuel/) | startup | Catalytically reacts scrap aluminum with water to deliver hydrogen plus steam/heat for industry, using waste metal as an energy carrier | $12M seed; switched on the largest-ever aluminum-water reactor in 2025 (MIT Technology Review); US Army funding ecosystem ($20M Georgia Tech-led program) validating the route |

> **White space:** Sparse because the physics is brutal: photocatalysis sits at ~1-5% solar-to-hydrogen versus ~10% needed to beat PV-plus-electrolysis, fermentation rates cap out on microbial kinetics, and solar thermochemical cycles (Sandia/DLR-class) remain lab projects with no dedicated commercial player after Heliogen's collapse. Credible openings are niche-first: distributed ag-waste hydrogen for fertilizer-dependent farms (HydGene's wedge) and aluminum-water systems for defense/remote power where logistics, not $/kg, set the bar — evidenced by the US Army's $20M program.

### Green Ammonia & Fertilizers

**Gigascale green ammonia (electrolytic H2 + Haber-Bosch)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Couples large renewable-powered water electrolysis to conventional Haber-Bosch synthesis to make fossil-free ammonia at million-tonne scale for fertilizer, shipping fuel, and hydrogen export, decarbonizing the single largest chemical CO2 source.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [NEOM Green Hydrogen Company (ACWA Power / Air Products / NEOM)](https://acwapower.com/en/projects/neom-green-hydrogen-project/) | scaleup | Building the world's largest single-site green ammonia plant (1.2 Mtpa) on ~4 GW of solar+wind+storage with thyssenkrupp electrolyzers; Air Products is exclusive offtaker. | ~$8.4B financed; under construction, commissioning slipped from 2025 to 2027 |
| [AM Green (Greenko)](https://ammoniaenergy.org/articles/am-green-production-nears-at-indias-first-renewable-ammonia-mega-project/) | scaleup | Retrofitting India's Nagarjuna/Kakinada fertilizer complex with electrolytic H2/ammonia backed by pumped-hydro-firmed renewables; 1 Mtpa phase one. | FID reached on first 1 Mtpa; Uniper offtake up to 500k tpy + Yara/Keppel; first shipments now targeted 2028 |
| [ACME Group](https://www.mercomindia.com/acme-secures-%E2%82%B940-billion-for-green-project-in-oman) | scaleup | Developing green ammonia in India (Tamil Nadu) and Oman for export and domestic fertilizer auctions. | Won ~370k tpy of India's fertilizer-producer auction volume; secured ~INR 40B for Oman; Yara offtake 100k tpa from Oman phase 1 (start 2027) |
| [Fertiglobe / Scatec (Egypt Green Hydrogen)](https://oci-global.com/news-stories/press-releases/fertiglobe-partners-with-scatec-and-the-sovereign-fund-of-egypt-to-develop-green-ammonia-project-in-egypt/) | incumbent | 100 MW electrolyzer feeding renewable H2 into Fertiglobe's existing Ain Sokhna ammonia plant — Africa's first integrated green H2 plant. | Phase one commissioned 2022; 20-year H2Global-backed offtake at EUR1000/ton; FID on full project targeted H1 2025 |
| [Yara International](https://www.yara.com/corporate-releases/yara-and-acme-signed-a-binding-agreement-for-supply-of-green-ammonia/) | incumbent | World's largest ammonia trader/producer; operating green ammonia at Porsgrunn (Heroya) and signing binding offtakes (ACME, AM Green) to green its fertilizer book. | Heroya renewable ammonia unit operating; multiple long-term green NH3 offtake agreements |
| [CF Industries](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001324404/000132440426000003/cf-02182026_ex991xearnings.htm) | incumbent | Largest North American ammonia producer; ran an electrolytic green ammonia project at Donaldsonville but pivoted capital to blue (CCS). | Dec 2025 management dropped the incremental electrolyzer investment for inadequate returns, favoring CCS |
| [⚠️ Australian Renewable Energy Hub (BP / InterContinental Energy / CWP Global)](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2025/07/28/bp-backs-out-of-26-gw-green-hydrogen-plan-in-australia/) | incumbent | Up to 26 GW Pilbara renewables for green hydrogen/ammonia export — emblem of the gigascale thesis. | BP exited as operator and equity holder July 2025 from the ~$55B hub; project's lead developer gone · **☠ shut down** |
| [Murchison Green Hydrogen (CIP / Mineral Resources)](https://politics-government.news-articles.net/content/2026/03/02/murchison-green-ammonia-plant-paused-by-shipping-deal-collapse.html) | scaleup | ~$15B Western Australia green ammonia export project. | Effectively paused after NYK shipping deal collapsed (2026); FID now pushed to 2027 · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Economics, not physics: green ammonia lands at roughly 2-3x grey cost, so projects live or die on subsidized offtake and dedicated shipping. A wave of 2025-26 FID failures (BP exiting AREH, Fortescue abandoning Queensland, Murchison's shipping deal collapsing) shows the bottleneck is bankable long-term buyers and logistics, not technology. Opening: aggregated demand/offtake vehicles (H2Global-style auctions) and merchant import terminals that de-risk the buyer side.

**Modular & distributed ammonia synthesis (relaxed Haber-Bosch)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Shrinks Haber-Bosch into containerized, intermittency-tolerant units running at lower temperature/pressure via advanced catalysts or sorbent-enhanced loops, so farmers and ports can make green ammonia on-site instead of shipping it from gigafactories.

| [Tsubame BHB](https://tsubame-bhb.co.jp/en/news-en/4552/) | scaleup | Low-temperature/low-pressure Haber-Bosch using Hosono's ruthenium-on-electride (C12A7:e-) catalyst for distributed plants. | Series C ~JPY5.3B; 2025 Global Cleantech 100; tech running at INPEX Kashiwazaki Hydrogen Park (~500 t/yr) and a Brazil (Atvos) LOI |

**Electrochemical & lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction** · `⚪ lab`

Skips Haber-Bosch entirely by reducing N2 to ammonia in an electrolyzer at ambient conditions — often via a lithium-mediated cycle (Li metal -> Li3N -> NH3) — promising direct coupling to renewable electricity but still fighting low efficiency and selectivity.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Jupiter Ionics](https://www.hydrocarbonprocessing.com/news/2024/03/jupiter-ionics-raises-9-mm-to-progress-their-electrochemical-green-ammonia-technology/) | startup | Australian modular reactor doing continuous lithium-mediated electrochemical N2 reduction from water, air and renewable power. | Raised ~US$9M (incl. A$2.5M seed led by Tenacious Ventures + ~$2M government); reactor scale-up, pre-commercial |
| [NitroVolt (formerly NitroFix / Nitrofix Solutions)](https://www.esgtoday.com/nitrovolt-raises-e3-5-million-to-produce-green-fertilizers-for-farmers/) | startup | Danish continuous-flow lithium-mediated electrolyzer aimed at on-farm distributed green ammonia/fertilizer. | EUR3.5M seed (EUR750K pre-seed before); investors incl. EIFO, EQT Foundation; moving lab tech to a farm demo unit |
| [Atmonia](https://ammoniaenergy.org/organization/atmonia/) | startup | Icelandic one-step electrochemical ammonia synthesis from air/water using a proprietary precious-metal-free catalyst (co-developed catalyst search with Fujitsu HPC/AI). | ~$16.7M raised (ReykVC, Landvaettir); achieved lab-scale ammonia production Oct 2025; further funding scheduled 2026-27 |

> **White space:** Physics-limited: lithium-mediated and direct N2 reduction still post low Faradaic efficiency, modest rates, and energy use that trails optimized Haber-Bosch, so all credible players remain lab-to-bench. The opening is a continuous, high-current-density, stable electrolyzer (especially Li recovery/regeneration) — whoever cracks durability at industrially relevant rates first leapfrogs the field.

**Plasma nitrogen fixation & on-farm nitrate** · `🔵 pilot`

Uses non-thermal plasma to split air's N2 and O2 into NOx that dissolves into water as plant-available nitrate (or enriches manure/slurry), enabling electricity-and-air fertilizer made at the farm with no Haber-Bosch and no CO2.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [N2 Applied](https://n2applied.com/) | scaleup | Norwegian on-farm plasma units that fix air N into nitrate and lock nitrogen into livestock slurry/digestate, cutting ammonia emissions while boosting fertilizer value. | ~15 years of development; commercial-pilot units across European farms |
| [VitalFluid](https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/836896) | startup | Dutch plasma-activated-water (PLAN2FIX) units extracting N from air directly into irrigation water as nitrate. | EU Horizon (Plan2fix) supported; field pilots |
| [Nitricity](https://www.esgtoday.com/nitricity-raises-50-million-to-scale-sustainable-low-carbon-fertilizer-technology/) | startup | US firm that built plasma-activated-water nitrate pilots, then pivoted to electrified organic fertilizer from almond-shell waste. | $50M raised; Delhi, California plant (~100x scale-up) breaking ground, sold out through 2028 — but now organic-fertilizer, not plasma nitrate |

> **White space:** Energy efficiency is the wall: plasma N-to-NOx still consumes far more energy per kg N than Haber-Bosch, which is why Nitricity pivoted from plasma nitrate to waste-derived organic fertilizer. Plasma survives where the value isn't bulk N but logistics/co-benefits (slurry enrichment, on-site liquid nitrate, ammonia-emission abatement); the opening is selling the avoided-transport and manure-management value, not commodity N.

**Biological nitrogen fixation displacing synthetic N** · `🟡 scaling`

Engineers or formulates soil microbes (often gene-edited to keep fixing nitrogen even when synthetic fertilizer is present) that colonize roots and convert atmospheric N2 into ammonia in-field, shaving synthetic fertilizer use and N2O emissions.

| [Kula Bio](https://agfundernews.com/kula-bio-closes-50m-series-a-to-further-develop-its-low-emission-biofertilizer) | startup | Energizes a naturally occurring microbe (Xanthobacter) into a high-output nitrogen biofertilizer applied to the root zone. | ~$86.7M raised across 6 rounds (incl. $50M Series A); latest round Nov 2025 |

**Blue ammonia with CCS (retrofit and new-build)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Keeps natural-gas-based ammonia but captures and sequesters the process CO2 (via autothermal reforming or capture on existing steam reformers), giving a lower-carbon, lower-cost-than-green bridge molecule that monetizes US 45Q credits.

**N2O abatement & low-carbon nitric acid** · `🟢 mature`

Installs tertiary/secondary catalysts in nitric acid plants that destroy nitrous oxide (a ~265x-CO2 greenhouse gas) and NOx, the cheapest large-scale lever to cut the fertilizer industry's non-CO2 climate footprint.

**Green urea & alternative nitrogen products (green AN, CO2-to-urea)** · `🔵 pilot`

Takes green/low-carbon ammonia downstream into the actual products farmers and miners use — urea (made with captured or direct-air-captured CO2), low-carbon ammonium nitrate for fertilizer and explosives — closing the loop on finished-product, not just feedstock, decarbonization.

| [Orica](https://www.orica.com/news-media/2024/first-low-carbon-ammonium-nitrate-blast) | incumbent | Global explosives maker buying low-carbon AN to offer decarbonized blasting products to mining customers. | Completed first low-carbon AN blast in Spain (2024); building low-emission ammonia feedstock supply |
| [Yara International](https://www.yara.com/industrial-nitrogen/civil-explosives/low-carbon-footprint-ammonium-nitrate/) | incumbent | Markets Low-Carbon Footprint Ammonium Nitrate and develops green urea pathways off its renewable ammonia output. | Low-carbon AN product line launched; green NH3 feedstock from Heroya |
| [CSIRO (green urea synthesis program)](https://research.csiro.au/sct/mineralization/green-urea-synthesis/) | incumbent | Public-research effort developing carbon-neutral green urea routes coupling green ammonia with DAC/captured CO2 (Australia perspective). | Research/techno-economic stage; base-case green urea ~US$989/t with renewables at $71/MWh |

> **White space:** Green urea carries a double penalty — it needs both green ammonia AND a clean CO2 source — so levelized costs (~$1000/t with DAC) sit far above grey until ~2030, leaving almost no pure-play. Green ammonium nitrate is further along because miners/explosives buyers (Orica) will pay a green premium and volumes are smaller. Opening: green AN for mining and civil works as the beachhead, with green urea waiting on cheap captured CO2 co-located with green ammonia.

| [Uniper](https://ammoniaenergy.org/articles/uniper-thyssenkrupp-uhde-demonstration-scale-ammonia-cracker-plant-under-construction-in-germany/) | incumbent | Energy major standing up ammonia import + cracking infrastructure to supply ~10-20% of Germany's 2030 hydrogen demand via Wilhelmshaven. | Demo cracker under construction; licensed thyssenkrupp tech for commercial terminal |

**Low-carbon phosphate/potash processing & recovered-nutrient fertilizers** · `🟡 scaling`

Recovers phosphorus (and nitrogen) from wastewater, manure and process streams as struvite or calcium phosphate, and valorizes phosphogypsum waste, reducing reliance on mined, energy-intensive phosphate/potash and the eutrophication footprint of nutrient runoff.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Ostara Nutrient Recovery Technologies](https://www.ostara.com/nutrient-recovery/nutrient-recovery-solutions/) | scaleup | Recovers phosphorus from municipal/industrial wastewater as struvite, sold as Crystal Green slow-release fertilizer; also treats phosphogypsum pond water. | Deployed at wastewater plants worldwide since 2005; launched next-gen Crystal Green (CG P2X) and EU-organic-approved struvite (2025) |
| [Schwing Bioset](https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/229483-18) | incumbent | Biosolids handling and nutrient-recovery (struvite/Bioset) systems for municipal and industrial sludge. | Acquired by Metawater (Apr 2025), folding into a larger water-tech platform · **acquired** |
| [NPHarvest](https://www.startus-insights.com/innovators-guide/new-fertilizer-solutions/) | startup | Aalto-spinout membrane system that extracts pure ammonia and calcium phosphate from wastewater without heat or high pressure. | Commercializing energy-efficient nutrient recovery; integrates with existing WWTPs |
| [Seraplant](https://www.startus-insights.com/innovators-guide/new-fertilizer-solutions/) | startup | Produces recycled phosphorus fertilizer from sewage-sludge ash via reactive-bonding, granulation and fractionation. | Operating recycled-P fertilizer production |
| [Mosaic / OCP (phosphate-potash majors)](https://www.fertilizer.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2025_IFA_Phosphogypsum_From_Waste_to_Inventory.pdf) | incumbent | Mined-phosphate/potash incumbents pursuing lower-carbon processing and phosphogypsum reuse rather than nutrient recovery. | Global reuse of phosphogypsum ~35% (2024 IFA report); majors exploring valorization and rare-earth co-recovery |

> **White space:** Recovered nutrients are real but tiny against mined phosphate/potash, and phosphogypsum valorization is mostly still research; struvite economics depend on wastewater-plant gate fees and local fertilizer offtake. Opening: regulatory tailwinds (EU nutrient-recovery mandates, P-runoff limits) plus rare-earth co-recovery from phosphogypsum could turn waste liabilities into byproduct revenue.
