### Green Chemicals & Bio/CO2-Based Materials

**Fermentation & synbio platform chemicals from sugars** · `🟡 scaling`

Engineered microbes ferment plant sugars directly into high-volume chemical building blocks (diols, diacids, monomers, solvents) that drop into existing supply chains at up to ~90% lower greenhouse-gas emissions than petrochemical routes.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|

| [Cathay Biotech (Cathay Industrial Biotech)](https://www.plastmatch.com/news/cathay-biotech-profit-soars-by-51-long-chain-ciixgavx-detail) | incumbent | Large-scale fermentation of bio-based long-chain diacids (DDDA) and PA56 bio-nylon (TERRYL/ECOPENT) from sugar feedstocks. | STAR-listed; ~$456M trailing-12-mo revenue (Sep 2025); 2024 net profit ~487M yuan; partnering CATL on polyamide composites. |
| [Visolis](https://www.synbiobeta.com/read/why-the-department-of-war-is-backing-visolis-to-scale-bio-based-solvents) | startup | Ferments biomass to mevalonic acid, then chemically converts it to bio-isoprene (rubber monomer), SAF and specialty solvents. | Zeon partnership toward a commercial bio-isoprene plant (announced 2025); >$5M U.S. DoD/DBIMP funding for bio-based solvents. |
| [ZymoChem](https://pulse2.com/zymochem-21-million-in-funding/) | startup | Carbon-efficient fermentation platform that avoids CO2 loss to make bio-based monomers (e.g., adipic acid, biodegradable superabsorbents). | $21M Series A led by Breakout Ventures with Lululemon and Toyota Ventures. |

**Chemo-enzymatic & cell-free biomanufacturing** · `🟠 demonstration`

Uses immobilized enzymes and/or metal catalysis (not whole living cells) to convert sugars and feedstocks into chemicals and ingredients, enabling higher yields, continuous operation and fewer purification steps than classical fermentation.

| [Debut Biotech](https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/debut-biotech-picks-up-22m-series-a-for-cell-free-biomanufacturing-facility) | startup | Cell-free (immobilized-enzyme) biomanufacturing of high-value cosmetic actives and ingredients from low-value feedstocks. | ~$88M total raised incl. Series B led by L'Oréal BOLD; partners L'Oréal, DSM, DIC; ~80 employees. |
| [EnginZyme](https://www.enginzyme.com/) | startup | Cell-free biomanufacturing using engineered enzymes on solid supports to run metabolic pathways outside living cells. | Swedish cell-free platform company; current 2026 status not independently re-confirmed in this research. · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Cell-free and chemo-enzymatic routes are hard at commodity scale because of enzyme cost, cofactor regeneration and stability; the credible opening is high-value specialty/cosmetic actives, or pairing enzymes with cheap metal catalysis as Solugen does to reach larger commodity volumes.

Anaerobic acetogen and methanotroph microbes ferment industrial off-gases, syngas, captured CO2+H2 or methane into ethanol, acetic acid/acetate and single-cell protein, recycling carbon that would otherwise be emitted.

Platforms that electrify chemical synthesis (replacing heat and stoichiometric redox reagents with electrons) or use high-throughput experimentation and AI to discover catalysts and greener electrochemical routes.

> **White space:** Electro-organic synthesis at scale and AI catalyst discovery are nascent: few standalone companies exist because incumbents capture most value through internal R&D and economics hinge on cheap clean power and proven electrode durability. The opening is modular electrochemical reactors for high-value pharma/specialty intermediates and AI catalyst-discovery offered as a service to chemical majors.

### Plastics & Polymer Circularity

**Enzymatic depolymerization of PET, nylon and polyolefins** · `🟠 demonstration`

Engineered enzymes (increasingly AI-designed) selectively break condensation polymers like PET and nylon back into their pure monomers under mild conditions, enabling true bottle-to-bottle / fiber-to-fiber circularity at lower energy than thermal routes.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Carbios](https://www.carbios.com/newsroom/en/carbios-maintains-its-commitment-to-build-the-longlaville-plant-and-adjusts-its-timeline/) | scaleup | PET-hydrolase enzymatic depolymerization; building a 50kt/yr flagship plant at Longlaville, France in JV with Indorama | Public funding EUR42.5M secured; Longlaville financing being finalized, commissioning pushed to ~2028; offtakes with L'Oreal, L'Occitane and beverage majors |
| [Samsara Eco](https://www.thechemicalengineer.com/news/samsara-eco-unveils-commercial-textile-recycling-plant-using-ai-engineered-enzymes/) | startup | AI-designed enzymes (EosEco) for nylon 6,6 and polyester; opened first plant in Jerrabomberra, Australia (Sep 2025) | ~US$100M+ raised; KBR engaged for a 20kt/yr nylon 6,6 plant targeted early 2028; partnerships with lululemon |
| [Protein Evolution](https://workinbiotech.com/companies/protein-evolution) | startup | AI-designed enzymes (Biopure) depolymerizing polyester/poly-blend textile waste in New Haven, CT | Launched from stealth with ~$25M; partnerships with Basecamp Research (PU/nylon) and Stella McCartney garment debut |
| [Epoch Biodesign](https://www.eu-startups.com/2026/03/epoch-biodesign-raises-e10-3-million-to-use-ai-and-enzymes-to-recycle-plastic-and-textile-waste-at-commercial-scale/) | startup | London-based; AI+enzyme platform targeting nylon 6,6 and textile/plastic waste at commercial scale | Raised EUR10.3M (Mar 2026), total >EUR43M; scaling toward commercialization of recycled nylon |
| [Birch Biosciences](https://www.birchbiosciences.com/) | startup | Engineering enzymes for plastic (incl. polyurethane) depolymerization using AI/ML enzyme discovery | Early stage; DOE SBIR Phase II grant for enzymatic PU recycling; small seed funding to date |

> **White space:** Enzymes work well on ester/amide bonds (PET, nylon) but struggle with carbon-carbon backbones of polyolefins (PE/PP), which dominate plastic waste; an enzyme or hybrid system that economically cracks polyolefins remains the major open prize.

**Chemical depolymerization of PET via methanolysis** · `🟡 scaling`

Methanol reacts with PET under heat/pressure to cleave it into purified monomers (DMT and MEG) that re-polymerize to virgin-grade PET, handling colored and contaminated feedstock that mechanical recycling cannot.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Eastman](https://resource-recycling.com/plastics/2025/08/01/eastman-to-delay-texas-plant-appeal-loss-of-doe-grant/) | incumbent | Operates commercial methanolysis (Polyester Renewal Technology) at Kingsport, TN; planned a second $1.2B plant at Longview, TX | Kingsport running and debottlenecking toward 130% nameplate; Texas plant delayed ~2 yrs after DOE cancelled a $375M grant in 2025 |
| [Loop Industries](https://loopindustries.com/loop-industries-and-ester-industries-india-joint-venture-awards-detailed-engineering-contract-to-toyo-for-infinite-loop-india/) | startup | Low-energy depolymerization (Infinite Loop) producing DMT/MEG; building 70kt JV plant in Gujarat, India with Ester Industries | India JV ELITe acquired ~93 acres, awarded detailed engineering to Toyo (Dec 2025), capex cut to ~$165-170M, ops targeted 2028; Nike offtake; European site (with Reed/Societe Generale) in selection |
| [Indorama Ventures](https://www.carbios.com/newsroom/en/carbios-maintains-its-commitment-to-build-the-longlaville-plant-and-adjusts-its-timeline/) | incumbent | Global PET producer; JV partner with Carbios at Longlaville and a major adopter/offtaker of depolymerized rPET | World's largest PET producer; strategic recycling investments across regions |

**Chemical depolymerization of PET via glycolysis** · `🟡 scaling`

Ethylene glycol breaks PET into BHET monomer that is purified and re-polymerized, a lower-temperature route that is among the most commercially advanced chemical-recycling methods for polyester.

**Microwave-assisted and room-temperature PET depolymerization** · `🟠 demonstration`

Novel low-energy routes break PET faster or at ambient conditions, including microwave-assisted depolymerization and solvent systems that avoid high heat/pressure, lowering both capex and energy cost for chemical recycling.

| [Gr3n](https://tech.eu/2026/06/05/gr3n-raises-eur155m-series-b-to-scale-pet-chemical-recycling/) | startup | Microwave-assisted depolymerization (MADE) of PET/polyester incl. textiles; building MODUS, a 40kt/yr first-of-a-kind plant in Spain | Closed EUR15.5M Series B (Jun 2026); signed EUR35M EU Innovation Fund grant; commercial operation targeted Q2 2030 |
| [DePoly](https://packagingeurope.com/news/depolys-showcase-plant-to-turn-500-tonnes-of-pet-into-raw-materials-yearly/12775.article) | startup | Swiss room-temperature, solvent-based PET depolymerization to virgin-grade monomers (TPA + MEG) without heat/pressure | Building a showcase plant to process ~500 t/yr of PET into raw materials; backed by strategic and VC investors |

> **White space:** These are first-of-a-kind energy-saving angles on a crowded PET-chemolysis field; the bet is that lower energy intensity finally beats virgin PET on cost, but none has yet proven full commercial-scale economics.

**PMMA, polycarbonate and polyurethane chemolysis** · `🔵 pilot`

Chemical depolymerization tailored to non-PET condensation/addition polymers - cracking acrylic (PMMA) back to MMA monomer, polycarbonate to BPA, and polyurethane foam back to polyols - recovers high-value monomers from streams that otherwise have no circular route.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [Trinseo](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001519061/000110465925107750/tse-20251106xex99d1.htm) | incumbent | PMMA (acrylic) depolymerization back to MMA monomer; opened a depolymerization pilot at Rho, Italy and scaling PC + PMMA recycling | Recycled-content product sales +47% YoY (2025); progressing commercial scale-up of PC and PMMA recycling |
| [Dow (RENUVA)](https://cen.acs.org/materials/polymers/LyondellBasell-buys-plastics-recycling-technology/102/i27) | incumbent | RENUVA process chemically breaks end-of-life polyurethane mattress foam back into polyol for new flexible foam | Operating mattress-recycling programs in Europe; representative incumbent route for PU circularity |
| [Birch Biosciences](https://www.birchbiosciences.com/) | startup | Enzymatic (not chemical) PU depolymerization - a biological alternative to PU chemolysis | DOE SBIR Phase II grant for enzymatic polyurethane recycling |

> **White space:** Beyond PET, monomer-recovery chemistry is fragmented and mostly pre-commercial; PMMA-to-MMA is closest to viability while PU and PC chemolysis remain economics-challenged, leaving room for a player that nails feedstock logistics and monomer purity.

**Pyrolysis and catalytic cracking of mixed polyolefins** · `🟠 demonstration`

Heating mixed PE/PP/PS waste in the absence of oxygen cracks the polymer chains into pyrolysis oil (naphtha-like feedstock) that refineries and crackers turn back into new plastic, the dominant 'advanced recycling' route for hard-to-recycle polyolefins - but one plagued by weak economics and plant failures.

| [Alterra Energy](https://resource-recycling.com/plastics/2025/12/15/alterra-licenses-tech-for-two-new-recycling-sites/) | scaleup | Liquefaction/pyrolysis technology licensor; operates a plant in Akron, OH and licenses to partners (Freepoint, others) | Licensed two new sites (Dec 2025) plus a 192-288kt/yr Gulf Coast Freepoint license; withdrew its own PA plant plan (Aug 2025) |
| [Nexus Circular](https://resource-recycling.com/plastics/2023/02/21/chemical-recycling-licensing-deals-partnerships-announced/) | scaleup | Pyrolysis of landfill-bound film/flexibles into circular feedstock; Atlanta-based with expansion plans | Contracted to supply ~24,000 t/yr of pyrolysis feedstock to LyondellBasell |
| [⚠️ Brightmark](https://www.plasticsnews.com/news/brightmark-subsidiaries-file-bankruptcy-over-ashley-chemical-recycling-plant/) | startup | Operated a $260M mixed-plastics pyrolysis 'Circularity Center' in Ashley, Indiana | Subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 (Mar 2025) after defaulting on $172.5M green bonds; plant reached only ~5% of nameplate; parent retained assets for ~$14.3M at auction · **☠ shut down** |
| [⚠️ Freepoint Eco-Systems](https://cen.acs.org/business/freepoint-eco-systems-shuts-down-plastics-pyrolysis-plant/104/web/2026/06) | startup | Operated a large pyrolysis plant in Hebron, Ohio (Alterra-licensed) supplying oil to Shell's Norco refinery | Suspended/shut down the Hebron plant (reported 2026) amid activist and Ohio EPA pressure · **☠ shut down** |
| [⚠️ Quantafuel (Viridor)](https://www.euwid-recycling.com/news/business/viridor-proposes-shutdown-of-quantafuel-chemical-recycling-activities-130526/) | scaleup | Operated a plastics-to-liquids pyrolysis plant at Skive, Denmark plus activities in Malmo and Oslo | Owner Viridor proposed shutting all European chemical-recycling ops (May 2026), calling them 'commercially uninvestable' despite 70-75% dry yields · **☠ shut down** |

> **White space:** Despite heavy investment, polyolefin pyrolysis is the epicenter of sector failures (Brightmark default, Freepoint shutdown, Viridor/Quantafuel exit) because virgin plastic is cheaper and feedstock prep is hard; the surviving model appears to be asset-light technology licensing plus tight integration with a downstream cracker/offtaker.

**Microwave-assisted pyrolysis and depolymerization to monomers** · `🔵 pilot`

Electrified, microwave-driven reactors heat polyolefins or polystyrene faster and more controllably than conventional pyrolysis, enabling modular, lower-carbon units and - for polystyrene - direct recovery of styrene monomer rather than mixed oil.

| [Pyrowave](https://www.pyrowave.com/en/blog/news/iw_06e3cbe0bfe43cf24d5d25437f67a818) | startup | Microwave catalytic depolymerization of polystyrene back to virgin-grade styrene monomer; Quebec-based | JV with Michelin to industrialize PS-to-styrene; Michelin produced a 4-tonne SBR prototype batch; backed by Fonds de solidarite FTQ |
| [Resynergi](https://www.ptonline.com/news/resynergi-raises-64-million-to-scale-microwave-assisted-pyrolysis) | startup | Continuous Microwave Assisted Pyrolysis (CMAP) modules cracking HDPE/LDPE/PP/PS into pyrolysis oil; modular, rapid-deploy | Raised ~$6.4M Series B + $18M extension (Taranis-led, with Lummus); Lummus to fabricate and supply modules globally; first commercial-scale site planned |

> **White space:** Microwave/electrified pyrolysis promises modularity and lower carbon but is unproven at commercial scale; polystyrene-to-styrene is the most differentiated niche (clean monomer recovery) and the least crowded.

**Hydrothermal and supercritical-water recycling** · `🟠 demonstration`

Supercritical or near-critical water/steam acts as 'molecular scissors' to depolymerize mixed and contaminated plastics into hydrocarbon feedstock, tolerating dirtier streams than dry pyrolysis and producing more consistent yields.

| [Mura Technology](https://www.muratechnology.com/news/mura-technology-opens-doors-to-worlds-first-commercial-scale-hydroprs-advanced-plastic-recycling-site-in-teesside-uk/) | scaleup | HydroPRS supercritical-steam recycling (licensing Licella's Cat-HTR); opened world's first commercial-scale plant at Teesside/Wilton, UK | Wilton ~20kt/yr in commissioning, ops ~Q1 2026; Dow partnership to scale up to ~600kt/yr across Europe/US by 2030, incl. a large Bohlen, Germany facility |
| [Licella](https://www.licella.com/2025/02/01/first-mura-technology-commercial-facility-enters-commissioning-phase-in-the-uk/) | scaleup | Developer of the Cat-HTR catalytic hydrothermal platform (16+ yrs R&D) licensed to Mura and others | Australian parent technology behind Mura's HydroPRS; multiple global licensing projects |
| [Aduro Clean Technologies](https://www.ainvest.com/news/aduro-clean-technologies-updates-hydrochemolytic-technology-pilot-plant-expansion-2508/) | startup | Hydrochemolytic Technology (HCT) using water chemistry to convert waste plastics/heavy oils at lower temperatures; Nasdaq-listed (ADUR) | Next-Gen Process pilot plant commissioning Sep-Oct 2025 (Siemens automation); site selection Jan 2026, ~8,000 t/yr demo targeted early 2027 |

> **White space:** Only a handful of players hold viable hydrothermal IP (Licella's Cat-HTR underpins Mura; Aduro is independent); high-pressure reactor capex and scale-up risk are the barrier, so the opening is a partner with deep petrochemical engineering and offtake (as Dow is for Mura).

**Dissolution and purification recycling (without depolymerization)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Selective solvents dissolve a target polymer (PP, PS, multilayer films) out of mixed/contaminated waste and strip away color, additives and contaminants, recovering a near-virgin polymer without breaking it into monomers - lower energy than chemolysis but limited to compatible streams.

| [PureCycle Technologies](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PCT/10-k-pure-cycle-technologies-inc-files-annual-report-557244abf1d0.html) | scaleup | Solvent-based purification of polypropylene to near-virgin PP (UPRP-licensed); flagship plant in Ironton, Ohio | Ironton 107M lb/yr design ramping; raised $300M Series B preferred + ~$75M equity/bonds in 2025; planning Augusta GA (300M lb/yr by 2030, EUR40M EU grant) plus Thailand/Belgium |
| [UpSolv (formerly Polystyvert)](https://polystyvert.com/en/polystyvert-expands-its-technology-platform-to-thermoplastics-and-becomes-upsolv/) | startup | Dissolution of polystyrene (incl. contaminated PS) in an essential-oil solvent; rebranded UpSolv and extending platform to other thermoplastics | Demonstrated contaminated-PS recycling; first commercial plant under development as of 2025 |
| [APK AG](https://cen.acs.org/materials/polymers/LyondellBasell-buys-plastics-recycling-technology/102/i27) | startup | Newcycling solvent-based delamination/dissolution of multilayer LDPE flexible films | Entered insolvency mid-2024; fully acquired by LyondellBasell (deal announced Aug 2024, completed) and folded into LYB's Circular & Low Carbon Solutions · **acquired** |
| [Saperatec](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mame.202400414) | startup | German delamination process separating multilayer film/composite packaging into component materials via a proprietary separation liquid | Cited in 2025 multilayer-recycling reviews; commercial status unclear · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Dissolution is energy-light but solvent recovery and feedstock purity drive economics; the field thinned after APK's insolvency, so a player that proves cheap, recyclable solvent loops on high-value streams (PP, multilayer flexibles) has room.

**Polyolefin upcycling to higher-value products** · `🟠 demonstration`

Rather than returning waste plastic to the same low-value polymer, these processes chemically convert it into higher-value materials - polyols/TPU, surfactants, waxes and additives - improving the economics of recycling polyolefins by selling up the value chain.

|---|---|---|---|

Bata family office |
| [GreenMantra Technologies](https://www.closedlooppartners.com/closed-loop-partners-deploys-10-million-loan-to-greenmantra-technologies/) | startup | Molecular (thermal-catalytic) recycling of waste PE/PP into specialty waxes and polymer additives; Brantford, Ontario | >$10M loan from Closed Loop Infrastructure Group to expand equipment, expected to lift specialty-product output ~50% |

> **White space:** Upcycling sidesteps the 'cheaper-than-virgin' trap by targeting premium chemicals, but each product market is small; scaling requires multiple offtakes and the field is thin, leaving room for platforms that flexibly tune output to whatever specialty market pays most.

**Textile fiber-to-fiber recycling** · `🟠 demonstration`

Chemical and hydrothermal processes regenerate polyester and cellulose (cotton) from end-of-life garments and polycotton blends back into virgin-grade fibers, closing the loop on fashion waste that is otherwise landfilled or incinerated.

**Tire and rubber recycling: recovered carbon black and devulcanization** · `🟡 scaling`

End-of-life tires are pyrolyzed to recover carbon black (rCB) and oil, or mechanically/thermally devulcanized to restore reusable rubber, displacing virgin carbon black and rubber in new tires - one of the more economically grounded circularity niches thanks to strong rCB demand.

**Carbon fiber and composite reclamation** · `🟠 demonstration`

Pyrolysis, solvolysis or plasma processes recover high-value carbon fiber from aerospace scrap, end-of-life parts and wind-blade composites, salvaging fiber worth far more than virgin alternatives from material that is otherwise landfilled.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Fairmat](https://www.fairmat.tech/) | startup | Recovers and reformats carbon-fiber composite scrap (aerospace, wind blades) into new high-performance recycled materials using a cold atmospheric-plasma process | Claims ~10x lower CO2 than conventional methods; collects aerospace parts, wind blades and manufacturing scrap; venture-backed, scaling in France/US |
| [Vartega](https://www.compositesworld.com/news/vartega-secures-10-million-to-promote-recycled-carbon-fiber) | startup | Recycles carbon fiber from aerospace, automotive and wind scrap into EasyFeed/Fenix recycled fiber for compounding and thermoset uses | Secured ~$10M to scale recycled carbon fiber supply; US-based (Colorado) |

> **White space:** Recovered fiber loses some mechanical performance and faces qualification hurdles in aerospace; supply of clean end-of-life feedstock is also lumpy, so the field is small - an opening exists for processes (like cold-plasma) that preserve fiber strength and for firms that lock up aerospace/wind scrap streams.

**Wind-blade and thermoset epoxy chemolysis for industrial composites** · `🔵 pilot`

Chemical processes break the epoxy resin in cured thermoset composites - notably wind-turbine blades - back into reusable virgin-grade materials, solving the long-standing problem that thermosets cannot be melted or remolded like thermoplastics.

Institute, Olin) demonstrated lab-scale; 2024 JEC Composites Innovation Award; scaling toward blade circularity |
| [Stena Recycling](https://www.stenarecycling.com/news-insights/newsroom/2024/stena-recycling-awarded-for-wind-turbine-blade-circularity-solution/) | incumbent | Recycling partner in the Vestas/Olin blade-circularity chain, handling disassembly and material recovery of wind-blade composites | Co-recipient of the 2024 JEC Global Innovation Award (Renewable Energies) for the blade-recycling solution |
| [Olin Corporation](https://www.vestas.com/en/media/company-news/2023/vestas-unveils-circularity-solution-to-end-landfill-for-c3710818) | incumbent | Epoxy producer supplying the chemistry/know-how to convert recovered blade epoxy back into virgin-grade resin materials | Founding CETEC partner with Vestas; provides the chemical-recycling chemistry for the consortium |

> **White space:** Epoxy chemolysis for blades is still lab-to-pilot and driven mainly by an OEM consortium (Vestas/Olin/Stena) rather than independent startups; with tens of thousands of tonnes of blades reaching end-of-life yearly, there is wide-open space for a dedicated commercial-scale operator once the chemistry proves out economically.

**AI/robotic sorting, digital markers and feedstock prep** · `🟡 scaling`

Computer-vision AI, robotic pickers, hyperspectral/NIR sensors and invisible digital watermarks identify and separate plastics by polymer, color and brand at material recovery facilities, dramatically improving the purity and yield of recyclate that all downstream recycling depends on.

**Mixed-plastic feedstock aggregation and pre-processing** · `🟠 demonstration`

Specialized 'circularity centers' collect, sort and engineer hard-to-recycle mixed plastics into consistent custom feedstock blends for both mechanical and advanced recyclers - solving the feedstock-supply bottleneck that has starved and sunk many chemical-recycling plants.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [Cyclyx International](https://www.wastedive.com/news/agilyx-leaves-chemical-recycling-operations-greendot/811474/) | scaleup | Feedstock-management JV (Agilyx, ExxonMobil, LyondellBasell) building Circularity Centers that engineer custom mixed-plastic feedstock blends | Houston CCC1 starting up 2025; Fort Worth CCC2 ($135M, ~300M lb/yr) targeted H2 2026; 2026 restructuring splits center ownership among the partners |
| [Agilyx](https://www.wastedive.com/news/agilyx-leaves-chemical-recycling-operations-greendot/811474/) | scaleup | Polystyrene depolymerization and feedstock pre-processing; co-founder of Cyclyx, taking ownership of the Dallas-area circularity center | 2026 unwinding of the Cyclyx JV reallocates assets; Agilyx to own the Dallas-area center while Exxon/LYB take Houston |

> **White space:** Feedstock prep is the quiet linchpin of the whole bucket: pyrolysis plants failed partly for lack of clean, consistent input. Cyclyx is nearly alone at scale, so there is white space for independent aggregators that de-risk advanced recyclers by guaranteeing engineered feedstock.

### Industrial Heat & Process Electrification

**Solid-media heat batteries delivering steam and hot air** · `🟡 scaling`

Electric resistance elements heat cheap solid media (firebrick, carbon blocks, slag granulate, sand, rock, alloy blocks) to 400-1,800C when renewable power is cheap, then discharge continuous steam or hot air (or power via thermophotovoltaics), letting factories run on intermittent electricity without boilers.

| [Rondo Energy](https://www.rondo.com/news-press/rondo-powers-up-worlds-largest-industrial-heat-battery) | startup | Refractory-brick heat battery (RHB) charged resistively, discharging high-pressure steam and hot air for fuels, food, chemicals and cement plants. | World's largest 100 MWh heat battery in daily commercial operation in California (Oct 2025); EUR 75M project funding from Breakthrough Energy Catalyst + EIB; 100 MWh Heineken/EDP brewery deal in Portugal. |
| [Antora Energy](https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/energy-storage/innovation-antora-massive-heat-battery) | startup | Solid carbon-block thermal batteries that emit heat as radiant light, plus thermophotovoltaic heat-to-power modules. | $150M Series B (Decarbonization Partners), >$230M total; ARPA-E $14.5M SCALEUP; 5 GWh system commissioning at POET ethanol plant, South Dakota; novel Otter Tail Power tariff. |
| [Kraftblock](https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/green-steel/global-giant-tata-steel-using-heat-battery) | startup | Granulate storage made from recycled steel-slag handling up to ~1,300C, packaged into power-to-heat systems. | EUR 20M Series B (Shell Ventures, 2023); 9 MW / 70 MWh system electrifying PepsiCo's Netherlands fryer lines with Eneco; Tata Steel pilot. |

**Molten-salt, molten-hydroxide, and phase-change industrial heat storage** · `🟠 demonstration`

Stores off-peak electricity in molten salts, hydroxides, concrete or phase-change materials at 250-700C and discharges on demand as process steam - more engineering complexity than bricks but compact, pumpable, and able to deliver steady isothermal output.

| [Hyme Energy](https://techcrunch.com/2024/12/19/after-raising-26m-hyme-energy-signs-global-deal-to-scale-thermal-storage/) | startup | Molten hydroxide salt storage above 500C (Seaborg spinout) with patented corrosion control, targeting 24/7 industrial steam. | $26M raised; global agreement with Arla incl. planned 200 MWh system at Holstebro dairy (target 2029); commercialization partnership with Sulzer (Mar 2025). |

> **White space:** Salts and PCMs carry corrosion, freeze-protection and balance-of-plant costs that dirt-cheap brick/rock/sand systems avoid - Azelio's 2023 bankruptcy and 1414 Degrees' slow grind show the squeeze; the defensible niche is compact isothermal discharge and direct >500C steam where solid media and steam quality struggle (Hyme's hydroxide bet), plus retrofit of existing CSP salt supply chains.

**Industrial and steam-generating heat pumps, MVR, and chemical heat transformers** · `🟡 scaling`

Compresses ambient or waste heat - via mechanical heat pumps, vapor recompression, or absorption chemistry - to deliver 100-200C hot water and steam at 2-6x boiler efficiency, the workhorse route for electrifying low- and mid-temperature process heat in food, beverage, paper and chemicals.

**Electric resistance and electrode boilers for process steam** · `🟢 mature`

Resistance and high-voltage electrode boilers convert electricity directly to steam or hot water at up to ~75 MW per unit with near-instant ramping - mature, low-capex hardware that pairs naturally with volatile power prices and hybrid gas-electric operation.

> **White space:** The hardware is commoditized century-old technology held by a handful of boiler makers, so differentiation has moved to economics: the open ground is grid-interactive 'boiler-as-battery' dispatch software, demand-charge management, and heat-as-a-service wrappers that make electric steam pencil against cheap gas - not new steel.

Taps hot water from conventional hydrothermal wells or engineered closed loops to feed district networks and low-temperature industrial processes with 24/7 carbon-free heat, avoiding the conversion losses of geothermal power.

### Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining

**Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from brines & brine co-production** · `🟠 demonstration`

Sorbents, membranes, solvents, or electrochemical cells pull lithium selectively out of salar, geothermal, and oilfield brines in hours instead of 18-month evaporation ponds, slashing land and water footprints and unlocking dilute resources (Smackover, Upper Rhine, Salton Sea) that conventional ponds cannot economically touch.

**Lithium from clay and unconventional hard-rock processing** · `🟠 demonstration`

Acid or CO2-based leaching flowsheets unlock lithium from claystone/sedimentary deposits and cut the energy and reagent intensity of spodumene conversion, adding a third supply pillar beyond brine ponds and conventional hard rock — critical because the biggest US lithium resources are clays.

> **White space:** Capital intensity ($1-3B per project) and unproven first-of-kind flowsheets restrict this to a handful of mega-projects that only advanced once DOE loans and automaker equity de-risked them; the open lane is low-capex, low-acid chemistry (CO2 or chloride leaching) that can work at smaller deposits without a billion-dollar acid plant.

**Copper extraction innovation (catalytic heap leaching, electrochemical reduction, in-situ recovery)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Catalysts, microbes, and electrochemistry break chalcopyrite's passivation layer so copper can be leached or plated from low-grade primary sulfide ore, waste dumps, and deep orebodies without building new smelters — the main lever for closing the forecast multi-Mt copper supply gap for electrification.

> **White space:** Chalcopyrite passivation defeated heap leaching for 40 years; catalytic leaching now has several funded players, but direct electrochemical reduction of concentrate has essentially one startup (Still Bright) — hard electrochemistry, but the prize is replacing the world's copper smelters (and their geographic concentration in China), so credible second entrants would find capital.

| [Graphjet Technology](https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:e5d0c57e6d53d:0-graphjet-technology-sec-10-k-report/) | startup | Malaysian palm-kernel-waste-to-graphite process, Nasdaq-listed via SPAC in 2024. | FY2025 10-K discloses going-concern doubt: ~$0.09M revenue, $22.5M operating loss, liabilities exceeding assets. · *status unverified* |
| [Syrah Resources](https://www.chemanalyst.com/NewsAndDeals/NewsDetails/syrah-resources-reports-positive-progress-on-balama-operations-42397) | scaleup | Vertically integrated natural graphite: Balama mine (Mozambique) plus the Vidalia, Louisiana active-anode-material plant — the first ex-China integrated natural graphite AAM producer. | Balama restarted May 2025 after a 9-month protest-driven shutdown; DOE/DFC loans plus ~$104M equity recapitalization; 67kt produced in 2025. |

> **White space:** China's Dec 2024 export controls exposed near-zero western anode capacity, yet Chinese price undercutting keeps margins brutal — Graphjet's going-concern and Syrah's force majeure are the cautionary tales; 2025 US anti-dumping duties (effective rates in the hundreds of percent) plus DOE loans finally give first-plant economics a floor, favoring whoever locks fixed-price automaker offtakes.

**Tailings and mine-waste reprocessing for metals recovery** · `🟠 demonstration`

Hydrometallurgy, novel separation, and bio-processes re-mine the world's billions of tonnes of tailings and slag for cobalt, copper, rare earths, and nickel — supply that needs no new mine permit and remediates legacy environmental liabilities at the same time.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Phoenix Tailings](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250430735778/en/Rare-Earth-Metals-Refining-Company-Phoenix-Tailings-Closes-on-Additional-$33M-in-Funding-From-Strategic-Investors-Bringing-the-Round-up-to-$76M-to-Support-Rare-Earth-Metal-Independence) | startup | Recovers rare earths and other metals from mining waste and produces finished Nd/NdPr, Dy, and Tb metal at US facilities with no Chinese inputs and no hazardous waste. | Series B closed at $76M (2025) plus $40M strategic capital; Exeter, NH metallization plant scaling from 200t toward 1,000+t; announced go-public via Plum Acquisition III SPAC (late 2025). |
| [Regeneration](https://www.resolve.ngo/projects/regeneration) | startup | RESOLVE-created enterprise that re-mines legacy sites and tailings for critical minerals and funds habitat restoration with the proceeds. | Rio Tinto invested $2M and screens its legacy sites for projects; Mejuri founding jewelry-sector investment. |
| [Jubilee Metals Group](https://jubileemetalsgroup.com/) | scaleup | AIM/JSE-listed processor recovering PGMs and chrome from South African tailings at commercial scale, with copper/cobalt waste processing built in Zambia. | Profitable multi-year chrome/PGM tailings operations; strategic review refocusing portfolio 2025. |
| [Eurasian Resources Group (Metalkol RTR)](https://www.eurasianresources.lu/) | incumbent | Reprocesses historic Kolwezi (DRC) copper-cobalt tailings into one of the world's largest cobalt outputs — the at-scale proof that tailings can be tier-one supply. | ~20kt+ cobalt capacity operating since 2019. |
| [Rio Tinto](https://www.riotinto.com/en/news/stories/a-new-model-for-mining) | incumbent | Extracts scandium from titanium-dioxide waste streams in Quebec and lithium from 90 years of borate tailings at Boron, California under its 'full value mining' program. | Commercial scandium oxide production since 2021; Boron lithium demonstration. |
| [Cobalt Blue Holdings](https://cobaltblueholdings.com/) | startup | Reprocessing pyrite (waste) streams at Broken Hill for cobalt and building a planned Kwinana cobalt-nickel refinery. | Demonstration plant produced mixed hydroxide; progress slowed by weak cobalt prices. |

> **White space:** The barrier is legal, not technical: acquiring tailings means acquiring perpetual environmental liability, and feedstock chemistry varies dam to dam, which scares generalist capital; DoD/DOE rare-earth-from-waste funding and liability-transfer deal structures with majors (the Regeneration model) are the wedge, and failures here are scarce because so few have tried.

**AI-driven exploration, geophysics, and drilling automation** · `🟡 scaling`

Machine learning over geoscience data, novel sensors (muon tomography, seismic micro-arrays, drill-core scanners), and autonomous rigs find and delineate deposits under cover faster and far cheaper than the <1% industry hit rate — discovery being the longest-lead bottleneck in minerals supply.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [KoBold Metals](https://me.smenet.org/kobold-raises-537-million-to-expand-ai-powered-critical-mineral-exploration-worldwide/) | scaleup | Full-stack AI explorer that takes its own discoveries to development; Mingomba (Zambia) is shaping up as one of the largest high-grade copper finds in decades. | $537M Series C (Jan 2025) at ~$3B valuation (Bezos/Gates-backed); 60+ projects on five continents. |
| [Earth AI](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/earth-ai-closes-oversubscribed-round-raising-20m-for-ai-driven-mineral-exploration-302360289.html) | startup | Pairs predictive targeting with its own low-cost drill rigs (~$100/m), verifying its AI targets by drilling them itself in Australia. | $20M oversubscribed round (Jan 2025); claimed ~75% drilling success rate on greenfield targets (Mo, Ni, PGE discoveries). |
| [Fleet Space Technologies](https://fleetspace.com/) | scaleup | ExoSphere: satellite-linked seismic node arrays plus AI for rapid 3D subsurface imaging, used by Rio Tinto, Barrick and hundreds of explorers. | Series D (2023) at ~A$800M valuation; hundreds of surveys delivered. |
| [VerAI Discoveries](https://posgeo.wordpress.com/2026/01/12/ai-in-mineral-exploration-2025-in-review/) | startup | AI targeting of concealed deposits under cover where conventional geophysics struggles, building a portfolio of staked discoveries. | $24M Series B (Feb 2025); 60+ mineral targets/projects. |
| [GeologicAI](https://posgeo.wordpress.com/2026/01/12/ai-in-mineral-exploration-2025-in-review/) | startup | Robotic multi-sensor drill-core scanners plus AI 'decision engineering' that re-logs core in real time for grade and recovery modeling. | $44M Series B (2024). |
| [Ideon Technologies](https://ideon.ai/) | startup | Muon tomography — cosmic-ray imaging from boreholes — producing density maps of orebodies hundreds of meters underground without drilling grids. | ~US$16M raised (Playground Global-led); trials with major miners. |

| [Ivanhoe Electric](https://www.ivanhoeelectric.com/) | scaleup | Friedland-led explorer pairing proprietary Typhoon high-power geophysics with AI inversion (Computational Geosciences) to find deep US copper, advancing Santa Cruz, Arizona. | NYSE-listed; Santa Cruz feasibility and construction decision path 2025-26; Saudi Ma'aden JV. |

**Bio-mining and phytomining** · `🔵 pilot`

Engineered microbes leach metals from low-grade ore and waste while hyperaccumulator plants literally farm nickel from metal-rich soils, offering near-zero-blast, low-energy metal recovery — and often stacking revenue with CO2 removal or remediation.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Genomines](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250917650939/en/Genomines-Raises-$45M-Series-A-to-Redefine-Global-Metal-Extraction-with-Plant-Based-Nickel) | startup | Genetically enhanced hyperaccumulator plants that concentrate nickel from soils and tailings, processed into battery-grade product after harvest. | $45M Series A (Sep 2025; Engine Ventures, Forbion BioEconomy); ~$62M total including French government grants. |
| [Metalplant](https://www.naturetechmemos.com/p/phytomining-growing-nickel-in-plants) | startup | Nickel phytomining farms in Albania using Odontarrhena hyperaccumulators, paired with olivine spreading so each tonne of nickel also sequesters CO2. | Seed-stage; pilot harvests producing nickel plus carbon-removal credits. |
| [Endolith](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/02/03/1132047/microbes-extract-metal-cleantech/) | startup | AI-monitored microbial consortia ('mining athletes') injected into copper heaps to boost chalcopyrite leach recovery; lithium biomining in development. | $13.5M seed (2025; Squadra-led) plus $16.5M (Nov 2025) to move from Denver lab onto operating heaps; validated in a BHP-led program. |
| [Cemvita](https://www.cemvita.com/) | startup | Houston synthetic-biology company whose biomining unit seeded the field (spun into Endolith); now focused on subsurface microbes including 'gold hydrogen' and bio-manufacturing. | Pivoted away from copper biomining — itself a datapoint that standalone biomining needed mine-operator pull. |
| [BacTech Environmental](https://bactechgreen.com/) | startup | Listed bioleaching developer applying proven arsenopyrite-oxidizing bacteria to clean up arsenic-laden concentrates while recovering metals (Ecuador project). | Decades-old proven tech base; Ponce Enriquez bioleach plant in development. |
| [Allonnia](https://allonnia.com/) | startup | Ginkgo Bioworks spinout (Gates Frontier-backed) applying engineered biology to mine tailings remediation and metal recovery from waste streams. | Partnerships in oil-sands tailings and mining waste; venture-backed. |

> **White space:** Microbial kinetics are slow and phytomining is land- and time-hungry, so economics only close on nickel-rich ultramafic soils and on waste streams where remediation budgets or CO2-removal credits stack with metal revenue; the field is thin enough that a player proving stacked-revenue unit economics at one site could own the category.

**Low-impact and precision mining (surgical extraction, ore sorting, clean process chemistry)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Borehole-scale 'surgical' extraction, sensor-based bulk ore sorting, and regenerated process reagents shrink the energy, waste rock, and chemical footprint per tonne of metal — making small, high-grade, or socially constrained deposits mineable at all.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Novamera](https://novamerainc.com/first-of-its-kind-surgical-mining-technology-positions-novamera-to-accelerate-production-of-critical-minerals-and-metals/) | startup | Surgical Mining: imaging-guided large-diameter drilling that extracts narrow high-grade veins with ~95% less waste and no open pit, sold as a service. | World-first commercial surgical-mining extraction at Golden Promise, Newfoundland (Nov 2025); Northstar services contract (US$1.5M advance); DIGITAL co-investments $3.5M + $4.0M; Series A underway. |
| [MineSense](https://minesense.com/minesense-closes-us-18-million-financing-to-drive-commercialization/) | scaleup | ShovelSense XRF sensors on shovels and belts classify ore vs. waste in real time, cutting hauling/processing of barren rock at operating copper mines (Teck Highland Valley, Copper Mountain). | US$42M (2022) and US$18M (2024) rounds; strategic investors include Caterpillar, ABB, Mitsubishi. |
| [NextOre](https://nextore.com.au/) | startup | CSIRO-spun magnetic resonance analyzers for bulk ore sorting on conveyors and trucks, measuring whole-stream copper grade in seconds. | Commercial deployments including Carmen Copper (Philippines) and trials in Chile/Australia. |
| [Travertine Technologies](https://www.prweb.com/releases/travertine-secures-8-5-million-to-reduce-waste-and-emissions-in-mining-fertilizer-and-cement-production-302179909.html) | startup | Electrochemical process regenerating sulfuric acid from gypsum/sulfate mine waste while mineralizing CO2 into carbonates — circular reagent chemistry for lithium, nickel, and REE extraction. | US$8.5M (Jun 2024) co-led by Holcim MAQER Ventures with Grantham Foundation and Clean Energy Ventures; piloting with critical-minerals projects. |

> **White space:** Mining's conservatism and first-of-kind operational risk keep adoption slow even when sensors are proven, and few startups survive the 5-10 year sales cycle; the opening is outcome-priced mining-as-a-service on stranded small/high-grade deposits (Novamera's model) and reagent circularity tied to acid supply security, both of which sidestep the 'sell tech to a skeptical miner' problem.

### Battery & Materials Recycling

**Hydrometallurgical lithium-ion recycling at scale (incl. LFP-specific routes)** · `🟡 scaling`

Shredded battery 'black mass' is leached in aqueous chemistry and refined back to battery-grade lithium, nickel and cobalt salts, creating a domestic secondary supply that displaces mining; LFP-specific flowsheets target lithium and phosphate recovery where contained-metal value is low.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Redwood Materials](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/lithium-ion-battery-recyclers-trump-doe-cirba-abtc-li-cycle/757376/) | scaleup | Largest North American recycler, integrating collection, hydromet refining and (planned) cathode production on one Nevada campus, plus LFP and copper streams | >$2B equity raised; processes the majority of North America's end-of-life lithium-ion volume; launched Redwood Energy second-life storage unit June 2025 |
| [Ascend Elements](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/lithium-ion-battery-recyclers-trump-doe-cirba-abtc-li-cycle/757376/) | scaleup | Hydro-to-Cathode process that converts black mass directly into pCAM without full elemental separation, with a Georgia plant operating and Kentucky Apex-1 under construction | ~$700M Series D (2023-24); Apex-1 Kentucky construction delayed after an offtaker withdrew and a $164M DOE grant was cancelled in 2025 |
| [Cirba Solutions](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/lithium-ion-battery-recyclers-trump-doe-cirba-abtc-li-cycle/757376/) | scaleup | Operates the broadest US collection-and-processing network (lead, NiMH, lithium) and is building hydromet refining capacity in South Carolina | EQT/Heritage-backed; $200M DOE grant for Columbia SC plant intact; Lancaster OH plant production up ~600% since 2022 |

| [tozero](https://www.tozero.solutions/) | startup | Munich startup recovering lithium and graphite from black mass via hydromet, targeting low-value chemistries | Seed-funded (~€11M plus grants); first industrial-scale plant in Germany came online March 2026 |

> **White space:** Crowded for NMC chemistries, but LFP, graphite anode and electrolyte recovery remain thin in the West because low contained-metal value breaks the leach-and-sell-salts revenue model — openings for LFP-tolerant flowsheets (cylib, tozero, Ace Green are early) and anode/electrolyte valorization; Li-Cycle's and Northvolt's failures show capex discipline and feedstock contracts matter more than nameplate capacity.

**Direct cathode recycling and upcycling to pCAM/CAM** · `🟠 demonstration`

Instead of dissolving cathodes to elemental salts, these processes regenerate or 'heal' cathode crystal structure (or convert black mass straight to precursor CAM), preserving embedded value and cutting energy, cost and emissions versus full hydromet.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Princeton NuEnergy](https://interestingengineering.com/energy/97-battery-recycling-yield-us-facility-turns-old-lithium-devices-into-new-energy-systems) | startup | Low-temperature plasma-assisted purification (LPAS) that relithiates and regenerates cathode powder directly from production scrap and end-of-life cells | >$55M raised incl. $30M Series A (Samsung Ventures) and ~$18M of DOE awards; commercial-scale McKinney TX line claims >97% yield |
| [Green Li-ion](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240618645137/en/Green-Li-ion-Marks-the-Opening-of-its-First-Commercial-Scale-Lithium-Ion-Battery-Recycling-Plant-in-Oklahoma) | startup | GREEN HYDROREJUVENATION modules that convert unsorted black mass directly into battery-grade pCAM in ~12 hours, sold as drop-in plant units | Opened North America's first commercial pCAM-from-black-mass plant (Atoka, OK, 2024; ~2 t/day); raised a bridge round May 2025 |
| [Ascend Elements](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/lithium-ion-battery-recyclers-trump-doe-cirba-abtc-li-cycle/757376/) | scaleup | Hydro-to-Cathode upcycling: impurity removal then co-precipitation of custom-ratio pCAM directly from leach solution, skipping elemental separation | ~$700M raised; pCAM produced at Covington GA; Kentucky Apex-1 pCAM plant delayed in 2025 |
| [OnTo Technology](https://www.onto-technology.com/) | startup | Oregon pioneer of 'cathode healing' direct recycling, primarily licensing IP and running DOE-funded pilots rather than owning plants | Long-running DOE/USABC project partner; licensing-stage with pilot demonstrations |

> **White space:** Few players because direct recycling needs chemistry-sorted, format-consistent feedstock and OEM re-qualification of regenerated powder, while target chemistries keep churning (NMC to high-Ni to LFP) — an opening for chemistry-agnostic regeneration tied to cell-maker production scrap, where feedstock is clean and qualification loops are short.

**Pyrometallurgical recovery and black-mass pre-processing/logistics** · `🟢 mature`

Established smelters recover nickel, cobalt and copper from batteries in furnaces (losing lithium and graphite to slag), while a parallel layer of shredding 'spoke' plants and reverse logistics turns packs into transportable black mass — the workhorse front end of the whole recycling chain.

| [Mercedes-Benz](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/company/news/recycling-factory-kuppenheim.html) | incumbent | First automaker with an in-house integrated mechanical + hydromet battery recycling plant, closing its own materials loop | Kuppenheim plant opened Oct 2024; 2,500 t/yr, >96% claimed material recovery, built with Primobius (SMS group/Neometals) technology |

**Electrochemical and novel-solvent metal recovery** · `🟠 demonstration`

Electricity (electrowinning/electro-extraction) or designer solvents (deep eutectics, fully-electric flowsheets) replace furnaces and acid-intensive solvent extraction, promising modular, low-emission metal refining that can sit close to scrap sources.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Nth Cycle](https://nthcycle.com/news/nth-cycle-closes-44-million-in-series-b-and-non-dilutive-financing-to-scale-clean-critical-metal-refining-technology/) | startup | 'Oyster' electro-extraction units that refine shredded scrap or black mass into nickel-cobalt MHP on-site, sold as modular systems | $44M Series B + non-dilutive (2024); first commercial facility in Fairfield, OH producing MHP since Sept 2024 |
| [Aqua Metals](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/AQMS/10-k-aqua-metals-inc-files-annual-report-15a825532efb.html) | startup | Electrolytic 'AquaRefining' of black mass to lithium carbonate and metals without furnace or heavy chemical consumption, piloted in Nevada | 5,000+ hours piloting and lithium carbonate produced, but FY2025 brought no revenue, a going-concern warning, asset sales and a pivot toward acquiring Lion Energy · *status unverified* |
| [DEScycle](https://rareearthexchanges.com/news/the-midstream-revolution-descycles-bet-on-distributed-metals-recovery-draws-e10-million/) | startup | UK developer using deep eutectic solvents to dissolve and selectively recover metals from e-waste and other feeds at near-ambient conditions | ~€10M raised (2025) to scale distributed metals-recovery units; pilot stage |
| [Ace Green Recycling](https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/ace-green-ceo-lfp-rising-star-recycling-market/) | startup | Fully-electric, zero-Scope-1 GREENLEAD lead recycling plus LithiumFirst process deliberately aimed at LFP batteries | 30,000-100,000 t/yr feedstock supply agreements signed for planned Texas flagship (production from 2026); announced plan to go public (Dec 2024) |

> **White space:** Sparse because electrochemical routes must beat brutally cheap incumbent solvent-extraction refining in China, and scale-up is capital-hungry (Aqua Metals' going-concern struggles are the cautionary tale) — the opening is modular, distributed refining that monetizes intermediates like MHP near scrap sources in tariff-protected markets, as Nth Cycle is attempting.

**Second-life EV battery systems, diagnostics, and state-of-health analytics** · `🟠 demonstration`

Retired EV packs with 70-80% remaining capacity are tested, re-certified and reassembled into stationary storage — supported by software that estimates state-of-health from field data — extracting more value per battery before recycling.

|---|---|---|---|
| [B2U Storage Solutions](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/12/17/3206992/0/en/B2U-Storage-Solutions-Launches-Fund-for-Second-Life-Battery-Energy-Storage-Systems.html) | scaleup | Pack-level 'plug and play' second-life BESS paired with solar plants in California, avoiding costly pack disassembly | Seven hybrid solar+storage projects (four grid-connected); launched a structured-finance fund Dec 2025; battery supply deal with Waymo |

| [Connected Energy](https://connected-energy.co.uk/) | scaleup | UK pioneer of containerized E-STOR second-life systems, moving into grid-scale second-life storage | Founded 2010; backed by Volvo Energy and Caterpillar Venture Capital; grid-scale second-life testing underway |
| [Voltfang](https://app.dealroom.co/companies/voltfang) | startup | German maker of industrial second-life storage systems from EV batteries with its own qualification line | €15M Series B (Jun 2025); opened a 6,000 m² Aachen plant billed as Europe's largest second-life battery factory, targeting 1 GWh/yr |
| [Element Energy](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/element-energy-commissions-53-mwh-second-life-battery-energy-storage-projec/734020/) | scaleup | Cell-level battery management that lets heterogeneous, partially-degraded modules run safely in large second-life arrays | Commissioned the world's largest second-life BESS (53 MWh, Texas, 2024); partnership with LG Energy Solution Vertech toward a 2 GWh pipeline |

| [TWAICE](https://www.electrive.com/2026/02/05/battery-analytics-startup-twaice-secures-e24-million/) | scaleup | Battery analytics platform whose digital-twin SOH models are used to qualify, warranty and operate second-life and grid storage assets | €24M EIB venture debt (Feb 2026); BESS analytics business roughly tripled in 2025 |

> **White space:** The economics are being squeezed from both sides — new LFP cell prices keep falling while recyclers bid up end-of-life packs — so pure repurposers struggle; the durable openings are cell-level electronics and bankable SOH certification (diagnostics + warranty + insurance) that make second-life assets financeable, plus captive OEM/fleet supply deals like Waymo-B2U.

**E-waste urban mining and precious-metal recovery** · `🟢 mature`

Circuit boards and electronics are 'mined' for gold, silver, palladium and copper — traditionally in giant copper smelters, now increasingly via clean chemistry (bioleaching, selective lixiviants) that recovers precious metals locally without cyanide or smelting.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Mint Innovation](https://www.mint.bio/news-and-press/mint-innovation-secures-site-for-first-us-e-waste-biotechnology-facility) | startup | Uses microbes (bioleaching) plus chemistry to recover gold and copper from shredded PCBs in city-scale 'biorefineries' | Commercial plant operating in Sydney; first US facility in Longview, TX slated for completion end-2025 |
| [Excir](https://www.royalmint.com/aboutus/press-centre/the-royal-mint-announces-investment-in-excir-to-strengthen-partnership-in-precious-metals-recovery/) | startup | Canadian selective-chemistry process that strips >99% of gold from circuit boards in minutes at room temperature | Technology deployed at The Royal Mint's Llantrisant plant (capacity 4,000 t PCBs/yr); Royal Mint took an equity stake April 2025 |
| [Umicore (Precious Metals Refining)](https://pmr.umicore.com/) | incumbent | Hoboken, Belgium smelter-refinery — the world benchmark for recovering 17+ metals from e-scrap and industrial residues | World's largest precious-metals recycler; ~500,000 t/yr feed capacity |
| [Boliden](https://www.boliden.com/) | incumbent | Rönnskär (Sweden) copper smelter is one of the world's largest e-scrap processors, integrated with mining feed | ~120,000 t/yr electronic scrap capacity at Rönnskär |
| [Sims Lifecycle Services](https://www.simslifecycle.com/) | incumbent | Global ITAD and e-scrap processing arm of Sims Ltd., feeding recovered boards to smelters and managing enterprise device reuse | Operations across dozens of sites globally; listed parent (ASX: SGM) |
| [ERI](https://eridirect.com/) | incumbent | Largest dedicated US electronics recycler with nationwide collection and certified data destruction | Eight US facilities; processes >100M lbs of e-waste annually |

> **White space:** Smelting capacity is ample; the real bottleneck is feedstock — only ~20% of global e-waste reaches formal recycling — so the opening is collection/reverse-logistics and automated PCB liberation rather than more refining chemistry; clean-chemistry players win where local processing avoids export of boards to distant smelters.

**Magnet and rare-earth recycling** · `🟠 demonstration`

End-of-life NdFeB magnets from motors, drives and electronics are recovered and either re-sintered magnet-to-magnet (e.g., via hydrogen decrepitation) or chemically refined to rare-earth oxides, building a Western supply of Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb outside China's near-monopoly.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Cyclic Materials](https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/10/06/1124287/2025-climate-tech-companies-to-watch-cyclic-materials-rare-earth-recycling/) | startup | MagCycle magnet harvesting plus REEPure hydromet refining to mixed rare-earth oxide, building hub-and-spoke plants in North America | US$53M Series B (2024; BMW i Ventures, Jaguar Land Rover, Microsoft CIF); Kingston, ON facility operating; magnet-waste deal with VACUUMSCHMELZE; MIT Tech Review 2025 'company to watch' |
| [HyProMag (Mkango/Maginito)](https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/rare-earth-magnet-recycling-technology-branches-out/) | startup | Hydrogen decrepitation (HPMS) that turns scrap magnets directly back into sintered-magnet powder with >90% energy savings vs virgin | Tyseley UK plant commissioned; ~100 tpy German plant in commissioning 2025 and 500 tpy US plant planned 2025-26 |
| [Noveon Magnetics](https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/rare-earth-magnet-recycling-technology-branches-out/) | scaleup | Texas magnet manufacturer running commercial magnet-to-magnet recycling, selling finished NdFeB magnets rather than oxides | San Marcos plant operating; ~2,000 t of 2025 magnet production supported by end-of-life recycled feed; DoD-backed |
| [Ionic Technologies](https://rareearthexchanges.com/news/rare-earth-recycling-in-2025-progress-promises-and-persistent-bottlenecks/) | startup | Belfast subsidiary of Ionic Rare Earths refining scrap magnets to separated high-purity rare-earth oxides | Leads £11M CREEM UK consortium with EMR, Ford and Bentley to recover magnets from end-of-life vehicles |
| [Carester (Caremag)](https://www.carester.fr/en/caremag-launch/) | startup | French separation specialist building Europe's first large-scale combined rare-earth recycling and heavy-RE refining plant at Lacq | €216M secured (€106M French state + €110M JOGMEC/Iwatani JV, 2025); plant to recycle 2,000 t magnets/yr and refine 5,000 t concentrate from end-2026 |

> **White space:** China refines ~90% of rare earths and its 2025 export controls turbo-charged demand for Western alternatives, yet collection of dispersed small magnets and the lack of Western sintering capacity keep the field thin — openings in automated magnet harvesting from motors/HDDs and OEM-backed closed loops (the VAC-Cyclic and CREEM models).

**Solar panel recycling and reuse** · `🟡 scaling`

End-of-life and damaged PV modules are de-framed, delaminated and separated to recover glass, aluminum, copper, silver and silicon (or resold as working used panels), heading off a multi-million-tonne waste wave arriving as 2000s-era installations retire.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [SOLARCYCLE](https://resource-recycling.com/e-scrap/2026/01/30/solarcycle-starts-up-georgia-recycling-plant/) | scaleup | US high-recovery recycling (glass, silver, silicon, copper) vertically integrating into recycled-content solar glass manufacturing | Cedartown, GA recycling plant started up Jan 2026 (5 GW/yr); up to $250M municipal-bond financing for co-located glass plant with >80% of capacity pre-committed |
| [ROSI](https://www.rosi-solar.com/news/rosi-secures-over-eu20-million-to-scale-solar-panel-recycling-across-europe) | startup | French high-value recovery of ultrapure silicon, silver and copper from modules using thermal/chemical delamination | >€20M raised (2025) to scale; Grenoble plant ramping toward 10,000 t/yr and a second 10,000 t/yr plant planned in Teruel, Spain |
| [We Recycle Solar](https://werecyclesolar.com/) | startup | Operates one of the largest US dedicated panel recycling plants (Yuma, AZ) plus a reuse/resale brokerage for working modules | Yuma plant can process thousands of panels per day; national decommissioning logistics network |
| [First Solar](https://www.firstsolar.com/) | incumbent | Runs in-house CdTe module recycling lines at its own factories — the longest-standing manufacturer take-back program in solar | Recycling at factory sites since 2005 with ~90% material recovery rates |
| [SecondSol](https://www.secondsol.com/) | startup | German online marketplace for used and refurbished PV modules, extending panel life before recycling | Largest European secondary-market platform for PV modules and spare parts |

> **White space:** Volumes are still early (the big end-of-life wave hits ~2030) and recycling margins lean on tipping fees plus tariff-protected glass demand — Solarcycle's 2025 construction pause over federal tax-credit uncertainty shows policy sensitivity; the open ground is high-purity silver/solar-grade silicon recovery at cost, and reuse certification for the booming used-panel trade.

**Wind blade and fiber-composite recycling** · `🟠 demonstration`

Decommissioned turbine blades (glass/carbon fiber in thermoset epoxy) are shredded for cement co-processing, mechanically converted into fiber additives, or broken down by pyrolysis/chemolysis to recover clean fibers and resin feedstock — solving wind power's most visible waste problem.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|

| [Continuum](https://www.compositesworld.com/news/continuum-targets-facility-capacity-transforms-composite-materials-to-advance-wind-blade-recycling) | startup | Danish mechanical recycler separating blades into fiber/resin fractions and pressing them into composite panels for construction | Esbjerg factory targeting minimum 36,000 t/yr blade capacity, with plans for multiple European plants |
| [Carbon Rivers](https://www.energy.gov/eere/wind/articles/carbon-rivers-makes-wind-turbine-blade-recycling-and-upcycling-reality-support) | startup | DOE-supported pyrolysis that recovers clean, mechanically-intact glass fiber from blades for reuse in new composites | Several thousand tonnes processed; scaling toward a >50,000 t/yr facility near Knoxville, TN |
| [Veolia](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251007527996/en/Wind-Turbine-Blade-Recycling-Market-Trends-and-Forecast-Report-2025-with-Veolia-Environnement-Groupe-Lapeyre-Global-Fiberglass-Solutions-Geocycle-Carbon-Rivers-Regen-Fiber-Vestas-Wind-Systems---ResearchAndMarkets.com) | incumbent | Cement-kiln co-processing of shredded blades (GE Renewable Energy partnership) — the lowest-cost route operating at scale today | Thousands of blades processed into kiln fuel/raw material since 2020 |
| [Vestas](https://cen.acs.org/environment/recycling/Wind-turbine-blade-recycling-picks/102/i31) | incumbent | CETEC epoxy chemolysis (with Olin and Stena) that breaks cured epoxy back to virgin-grade resin constituents, enabling recycling of existing blades without redesign | Chemical disassembly process unveiled 2023, in scale-up with partners |
| [Fairmat](https://www.fairmat.tech/) | scaleup | French deep-tech recycling carbon-fiber composite offcuts and parts into engineered chips for new high-performance products | >$50M raised (Series B 2023); plants in France and Salt Lake City with aerospace supply deals |
| [Global Fiberglass Solutions](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251007527996/en/Wind-Turbine-Blade-Recycling-Market-Trends-and-Forecast-Report-2025-with-Veolia-Environnement-Groupe-Lapeyre-Global-Fiberglass-Solutions-Geocycle-Carbon-Rivers-Regen-Fiber-Vestas-Wind-Systems---ResearchAndMarkets.com) | startup | Early US mover converting blades into composite pellets and panels | Drew attention for stockpiled blades in Texas/Iowa and has gone quiet; commercial activity unclear · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Recovered glass fiber is worth little relative to the cost of moving and cutting 70-meter blades, so cement co-processing wins on economics and high-value routes stay subscale (GFS's stockpiles are the cautionary tale) — openings in mobile/on-site blade sectioning logistics, resin-recovery chemolysis as repowering accelerates through 2030, and higher-value carbon-fiber streams.

**Advanced alloy scrap sorting and metals recovery** · `🟡 scaling`

Sensor fusion (LIBS, XRF, X-ray transmission) plus AI classifies and separates mixed metal scrap into specific alloy grades at belt speed, letting 'twitch' and zorba streams that were exported be re-melted domestically into high-value wrought alloys with ~95% energy savings versus primary.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Sortera Technologies](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sortera-scales-solution-to-the-mixed-aluminum-problem-with-45-million-in-funding-and-new-tennessee-facility-302620885.html) | startup | Only US pure-play operating its own AI+LIBS plants that upgrade mixed aluminum shred into furnace-ready, alloy-specific products | $45M round (Nov 2025; T. Rowe Price-advised accounts, VXI, Yamaha Motor Ventures); second plant announced in Lebanon, TN |
| [TOMRA Recycling](https://www.tomra.com/waste-metal-recycling/media-center/webcasts/2025/from-ai-to-dynamic-libs) | incumbent | Global sensor-sorting equipment leader; launched dynamic-LIBS AUTOSORT PULSE to split wrought aluminum into 5xxx/6xxx alloy families | Dynamic LIBS and deep-learning aluminum sorting products launched 2025 on an installed base of thousands of sorters |
| [STEINERT](https://steinertglobal.com/) | incumbent | German metals-sorting incumbent supplying LIBS, XRF and X-ray transmission lines used by major shredders to upgrade zorba/twitch | Family-owned incumbent with sorting systems deployed across global scrap yards |

> **White space:** Thin because it demands simultaneous depth in sensors, ML and physical metallurgy plus plant capex, and incumbents sell equipment rather than operate — Sortera is nearly alone as an operator; tightening scrap-export flows and aluminum tariffs create an opening for more own-and-operate alloy upgrading hubs and for copper/steel alloy-level sorting beyond aluminum.

**Materials traceability and battery-passport software** · `🟡 scaling`

Software (often blockchain-anchored) tracks critical materials from mine or recycler through manufacturing to end-of-life, underpinning the EU's mandatory digital battery passport (Feb 2027) and letting buyers verify recycled content, carbon footprint and ethical sourcing.

## Food, Agriculture & Land Use

Roughly a third of global emissions once land use is counted: alternative proteins, livestock and rice methane, fertilizer, precision and regenerative agriculture, food waste, forests, and blue carbon. Solutions here are unusually behavior- and policy-dependent, and the alt-protein shakeout of 2023–2025 is a live case study in hype-cycle risk.

*9 solution areas · 71 variations · 445 company entries (421 unique companies; 27 marked dead, 10 acquired, 15 unverified)*

**Maturity at a glance (variations per stage):** Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins (1 mature, 4 scaling, 4 demonstration) · Cultivated Meat & Novel Protein Sources (2 scaling, 4 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Livestock & Rice Methane (2 mature, 4 scaling, 1 lab) · Fertilizer & Crop Inputs (1 mature, 4 scaling, 1 demonstration) · Precision Ag, Robotics & Controlled-Environme... (1 mature, 6 scaling, 2 demonstration) · Regenerative Agriculture & Soil Carbon (4 scaling, 1 demonstration, 2 pilot) · Food Loss & Waste (1 mature, 4 scaling, 4 demonstration) · Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains (1 mature, 6 scaling, 2 demonstration) · Blue Carbon & Coastal Ecosystems (4 scaling, 1 demonstration, 2 pilot)

**Solution areas:** [Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins](#plant-based-fermentation-proteins) · [Cultivated Meat & Novel Protein Sources](#cultivated-meat-novel-protein-sources) · [Livestock & Rice Methane](#livestock-rice-methane) · [Fertilizer & Crop Inputs](#fertilizer-crop-inputs) · [Precision Ag, Robotics & Controlled-Environment Ag](#precision-ag-robotics-controlled-environment-ag) · [Regenerative Agriculture & Soil Carbon](#regenerative-agriculture-soil-carbon) · [Food Loss & Waste](#food-loss-waste) · [Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains](#forests-deforestation-free-supply-chains) · [Blue Carbon & Coastal Ecosystems](#blue-carbon-coastal-ecosystems)

### Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins

**Plant-based meat (ground, whole-cut, 3D-printed)** · `🟡 scaling`

Replicates ground, formed, or whole-cut meat from plant proteins (soy, pea, wheat) using extrusion, shear-cell, or 3D-printing to mimic muscle texture, cutting the land, water, and emissions footprint of livestock by roughly an order of magnitude.

**Plant-based dairy, cheese & yogurt** · `🟡 scaling`

Recreates milk, cheese, and yogurt from plant bases (oat, soy, nut, potato) plus plant proteins/fats and cultures, avoiding the methane and land use of dairy herds while targeting the harder functional challenge of meltable, stretchy cheese.

**Plant-based eggs & seafood** · `🟡 scaling`

Replaces eggs (mung-bean or other plant-protein liquid eggs) and fish/shellfish (konjac, soy, legume, algae) with plant analogues, easing pressure on caged hens and on overfished and bycatch-heavy wild stocks.

**Mycoprotein & filamentous-fungi / biomass fermentation** · `🟡 scaling`

Grows whole filamentous fungal biomass in fermenters (the cells themselves are the food), yielding a fibrous, high-protein, high-fiber ingredient that is the most cost-mature fermentation route to meat-like texture and is economically viable at industrial scale today.

**Precision fermentation of dairy proteins (whey, casein)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Engineers microbes (yeast/fungi) to brew the exact whey and casein proteins found in cow's milk without any animal, enabling animal-identical cheese, milk and protein powders with a fraction of dairy's emissions once production scales.

Brews specific functional proteins beyond dairy, egg white (ovalbumin), heme/myoglobin for meat flavor, and collagen for food and cosmetics, by fermenting engineered microbes, delivering animal-identical functionality without hens, cattle, or slaughterhouses.

**Animal-free fats & oils (fermented or synthetic)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Produces fats and oils, dairy-style butterfat, meat fat, and palm-oil replacements, either by fermenting microbes (precision/biomass) or by building triglycerides thermochemically from captured carbon, addressing the fat fraction that drives much of the flavor, melt and deforestation impact of animal and palm products.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Nourish Ingredients](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/nourish-ingredients-tastilux-fema-gras-us-precision-fermentation-fat/) | startup | Australian firm making precision-fermented animal-like fats (e.g. Tastilux) that mimic meat/dairy fat at low inclusion rates, sold B2B. | Cleared to sell animal-free meat fat in the US (FEMA GRAS); set up a European commercial hub in the Netherlands; courted by global food giants |
| [Savor](https://agfundernews.com/savor-unveils-first-of-its-kind-butter-made-without-cows-plants-or-microbes) | startup | Bill Gates-backed firm building fats thermochemically from captured CO2, hydrogen and methane, no animals, plants or microbes; launched a carbon-made butter. | Launched first commercial product (carbon butter) in March 2025; planning a large-scale facility to take on dairy and palm |
| [C16 Biosciences](https://www.genengnews.com/news/c16-biosciences-gears-up-to-go-palmless/) | startup | US firm fermenting a palm-oil alternative (Palmless / Torula-derived oil) to replace deforestation-linked palm in food and personal care. | Achieved commercial-scale production with revenue in personal care; received US DoD biomanufacturing award; expanding into food |
| [Melt&Marble](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/melt-and-marble-funding-precision-fermentation-fat-launch/) | startup | Swedish precision-fermentation firm making designer fats/lipids for food and personal care. | Closed ~$8.5M (SEK 80M) round in Dec 2025; reached commercial-scale production; first ingredients (personal care) in 2026, US food market in sight |

| [Yali Bio](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/melt-and-marble-funding-precision-fermentation-fat-launch/) | startup | California firm using synthetic biology and precision fermentation to design tailored fats and lipids. | Early-stage; cited among US precision-fermentation fat developers |

> **White space:** Fats are a high-value, under-served leverage point: a 1% animal-fat inclusion can transform plant-meat flavor, so B2B 'designer fat' suppliers win without needing to own the finished product. The constraint is fermentation cost; carbon-to-fat thermochemistry (Savor) is a novel, capacity-light alternative still proving cost at scale.

**B2B plant-protein ingredients, isolates & texturization tech** · `🟢 mature`

Supplies the upstream building blocks, pea/soy/wheat protein concentrates and isolates plus textured vegetable proteins made by high-moisture extrusion, that downstream brands turn into meat and dairy analogues; this layer is the most cost-mature and profitable part of the value chain.

**Fermentation scale-up infrastructure & contract manufacturing (CDMOs)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Builds and operates the large fermentation tanks and downstream processing that protein startups lack, providing commercial-scale (100,000 L+) capacity as a contract manufacturer; this is the single biggest bottleneck standing between precision-fermentation pilots and price-competitive supply.

| [Synonym](https://www.synbiobeta.com/read/protein-without-the-moo-brewing-the-future-of-food) | startup | US firm providing financing, engineering and project development to build out fermentation biomanufacturing capacity and match startups to capacity. | Cited as a key infrastructure/enablement player bridging startups to commercial fermentation capacity |
| [Cauldron](https://www.proteinproductiontechnology.com/post/fermentation-rises-as-alternative-proteins-hold-ground-amid-food-tech-vc-slowdown) | startup | Australian firm commercializing a continuous (hyper-fermentation) process and planning a network of 'smaller, smarter' precision-fermentation plants run as a CDMO. | Planning a 500,000-L facility; long-term CDMO network ambitions for functional lipids, enzymes and proteins |
| [ScaleUp Bio](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/articles/key-companies-in-precision-fermentation) | startup | Singapore-based precision-fermentation CDMO (Temasek/ADM-linked) offering pilot-to-commercial capacity for food-protein startups in Asia. | Cited as an interim CDMO path for startups bridging lab validation to commercial supply |
| [ABEC](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/articles/key-companies-in-precision-fermentation) | incumbent | Engineering firm designing and building large bioreactors and single-use/stainless fermentation systems used by food and biotech producers. | Established bioprocess-equipment supplier enabling large-scale fermentation buildouts |

> **White space:** Dedicated food-grade large-scale fermentation capacity is acutely scarce, only a handful of players have committed to 100,000 L+ food plants, so capital intensity and offtake risk keep entrants few. The opening is purpose-built food CDMOs (vs. repurposed pharma capacity) financed by sovereign and strategic capital with anchor offtake contracts.
