### Food Loss & Waste

**Shelf-life extension coatings, packaging & treatments** · `🟡 scaling`

Edible coatings, ripening-control treatments (e.g., 1-MCP), and active packaging slow respiration and moisture loss so produce survives longer in transit and on shelf, cutting spoilage-driven waste and the emissions embodied in lost food.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Apeel Sciences](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/apeel-technologies) | scaleup | Plant-derived edible coatings applied at packhouses that extend shelf life of avocados, citrus, cucumbers and more by days to weeks. | Raised ~$640M total incl. $250M Series E (2021, ~$2B valuation); deployed with major US/EU retailers; restructured 2023-24 amid slower-than-hoped commercialization |
| [Hazel Technologies](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/hazel-technologies) | scaleup | Drop-in sachets and packaging inserts that release vapor-phase ripening inhibitors inside produce boxes during transit. | ~$110M raised through Series C; used by hundreds of produce suppliers across dozens of crops |
| [AgroFresh](https://www.agrofresh.com/) | incumbent | Dominant supplier of 1-MCP post-harvest freshness treatments (SmartFresh) used on a large share of the world's stored apples, plus coatings and digital tools. | NASDAQ-listed until taken private by Paine Schwartz Partners (completed 2023); decades of global deployment · **acquired** |
| [Mori](https://www.mori.com/) | startup | Silk-protein (fibroin) edible coating with FDA GRAS status applied to produce and proteins to slow spoilage. | Raised >$80M venture funding (Series B 2022); commercial pilots with US produce and protein processors |
| [Ryp Labs](https://www.ryplabs.com/) | startup | StixFresh produce stickers that release natural antimicrobial vapors to delay mold and over-ripening on individual fruit. | Venture/grant-backed; retail and packer pilots in US and Europe |
| [RipeLocker](https://www.ripelocker.com/) | startup | Patented low-atmospheric-pressure storage containers that hold berries, hops, and flowers in suspended animation for weeks. | Commercial trials with major berry and hop shippers; named alongside Apeel/Hazel as a category leader |
| [Sufresca](https://www.sufresca.com/) | startup | Israeli developer of invisible, washable edible coatings tailored per-crop (cucumbers, peppers, citrus). | Seed-stage; pilots with European produce packers |
| [Saveggy](https://www.saveggy.com/) | startup | Swedish plant-based coating replacing plastic shrink-wrap on cucumbers and peppers. | Early commercial rollout with Nordic retailer ICA; seed/EU-grant funded |
| [Xampla](https://www.xampla.com/) | startup | Cambridge spinout making Morro-brand natural polymer coatings and films from plant protein as edible/compostable barriers for food. | Raised ~$20M+; commercial partnerships incl. Huhtamaki and food brands |

**Surplus food marketplaces, redistribution & dynamic pricing** · `🟡 scaling`

Apps and B2B platforms match soon-to-expire or surplus food with discount buyers, charities, or secondary channels — and dynamically mark down prices — so edible food gets eaten instead of landfilled.

|---|---|---|---|

| [Flashfood](https://www.thepacker.com/news/sustainability/how-food-waste-apps-are-reshaping-grocery-retail) | scaleup | App platform grocers use to sell near-dated meat, produce, and dairy at ~50% off for in-store pickup. | Partnered with thousands of stores (Meijer and other chains) across North America; 100M+ lbs of food diverted |
| [Misfits Market](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/misfits-market) | scaleup | Online grocer built on 'ugly' and surplus produce and short-coded pantry goods delivered to consumers. | Raised $526.5M (SoftBank, Accel, Valor); acquired rival Imperfect Foods in 2022 |

| [Phenix](https://wearephenix.com/) | scaleup | French anti-waste app plus donation logistics that routes retailer surplus to consumers and charities across Western Europe. | B Corp; thousands of partner merchants in France/Spain/Portugal/Italy/Belgium; raised ~EUR 15M+ |
| [OLIO](https://olioapp.com/) | scaleup | Neighbor-to-neighbor and store-to-community sharing app where volunteers redistribute retailer surplus for free. | Raised ~$43M Series B (2021, VNV Global); millions of users; Tesco volunteer partnership |
| [Goodr](https://goodr.co/) | startup | Atlanta-based surplus-food logistics company routing edible surplus from airports, stadiums, and corporates to nonprofits, with waste audits. | Venture-backed (raised ~$8M+); clients include major airports and arenas |
| [Spoiler Alert](https://www.spoileralert.com/) | scaleup | B2B private marketplace where CPG brands liquidate excess and short-dated inventory to discount/secondary channels. | Raised ~$32M; used by Kraft Heinz, Nestlé, Danone and other top food brands |

Turns high-volume food-processing byproducts (spent grain, okara, fruit peels, coffee waste, veg trim) into flours, proteins, snacks, and functional actives, capturing the nutrition and embedded emissions of food that would otherwise be discarded.

**Freshness sensing, smart labels & shelf-life prediction** · `🟠 demonstration`

Biosensors, time-temperature labels, and NIR scanners measure how fresh food actually is — instead of relying on conservative printed dates — enabling dynamic expiry, first-expired-first-out routing, and fewer premature discards across the cold chain and at home.

| [Sensitech](https://www.sensitech.com/) | incumbent | Carrier-owned market leader in cold-chain monitoring (TempTale) used across global perishable logistics. | Decades-deployed incumbent within Carrier's $20B+ portfolio |

Black soldier fly larvae and mealworms eat food waste and processing byproducts and are harvested as protein for animal feed, pet food, and aquaculture plus frass fertilizer, valorizing streams unsuitable for human consumption.

| [Goterra](https://goterra.com.au/) | startup | Australian robotic BSF modules ('MIBs') placed at supermarkets and waste sites to process food waste autonomously. | Contracts with Woolworths and Australian councils; venture-backed |
| [Entocycle](https://www.entocycle.com/) | startup | Sells BSF breeding technology and turnkey farm design so waste companies can build their own insect bioconversion capacity. | London demonstration facility; UK government grant backing |
| [⚠️ Ynsect](https://agfundernews.com/judicial-liquidation-for-ynsect-as-insect-farming-sector-struggles-to-become-competitive) | scaleup | French mealworm pioneer that built a giant vertical insect 'farm of the future' (Amiens) for feed and food proteins. | Raised $600M+ but entered receivership Mar 2025 and judicial liquidation Dec 2025; flagship plant closed — only EUR 656k revenue in 2023 vs EUR 80M losses · **☠ shut down** |
| [⚠️ AgriProtein](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S235255092400191X) | scaleup | South African early mover feeding true mixed food waste to BSF at industrial scale for feed protein. | Raised ~$105M at ~$200M valuation, then collapsed (~2021) — variable waste substrate at scale proved unworkable · **☠ shut down** |

> **White space:** The two biggest players failed on unit economics — insect meal costs 2-10x fish/soy meal and EU/US feed rules bar most true post-consumer food waste as substrate, which strands the cheapest feedstock. Openings: small modular on-farm/at-store units that skip central logistics (Better Origin, Goterra), co-location with processors for clean byproduct streams (InnovaFeed), and regulatory change permitting former-foodstuffs substrates.

Companies that plant or re-establish forests faster and cheaper using drone/aerial seeding, industrialized native-seed banking and nurseries, and (in a few cases) biotech-enhanced trees, so degraded and burned land can be restored at the scale climate goals require.

| [Dendra Systems](https://planettools.org/8-drone-planting-systems-2026/) | scaleup | Oxford UK drone seeding carrying 50+ native species at once plus an AI ecology/monitoring platform for large-scale restoration | ~$15.7M raised; April 2025 World Bank partnership for Sahel RESILAND aerial reforestation |

| [American Forests](https://www.americanforests.org/project/racp/) | incumbent | Century-old US conservation nonprofit running the Reforest America Carbon Program (RACP) to connect climate-smart reforestation to carbon finance | RACP active in 2025 to bridge high upfront cost / long tree-growth timelines for landowners |

> **White space:** Capital is now abundant for marquee Brazilian/US developers, but ARR still carries 30-60 year delivery risk and thin track records; the gap is bankable insurance/guarantee structures and standardized non-recourse project finance (Chestnut's JPMorgan facility is a first-of-kind) that let mid-size developers scale without dilutive equity.

**Forest / biomass carbon MRV (satellite, lidar, AI)** · `🟡 scaling`

Measurement, reporting and verification firms that use satellite imagery, airborne/terrestrial lidar and machine learning to estimate forest carbon stocks and change, replacing slow and expensive field plots and underpinning credit integrity.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Pachama](https://www.esgtoday.com/carbon-direct-acquires-carbon-project-mrv-platform-pachama/) | startup | Satellite + lidar + AI MRV platform that verifies forest conservation and reforestation projects | ~$79M raised (Breakthrough, Amazon, Lowercarbon); ACQUIRED by Carbon Direct in Nov 2025 to bolster its MRV stack · **acquired** |
| [Chloris Geospatial](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/chloris-geospatial-raises-8-5-million-series-a-to-scale-satellite-based-forest-carbon-monitoring-302498338.html) | startup | Satellite-based measurement of forest carbon stock-change and ecosystem change for project and portfolio MRV | $8.5M Series A (Jul 2025) led by Future Energy Ventures, with AXA IM Alts, At One Ventures, Cisco Foundation |
| [CTrees](https://ctrees.org/) | startup | Science nonprofit using AI + satellite + lidar to estimate carbon in every tree on Earth and run an open jurisdictional MRV (JMRV) tool | AWS Imagine Grant (2024); released open aboveground-biomass data 2000-2025; widely cited as reference layer |
| [Kanop](https://www.kanop.io/) | startup | Paris startup measuring forest carbon and ecosystem services from high-res satellite + AI for project developers | Early stage (~$1.15M raised); selected for the EU CASSINI space accelerator in 2025 |
| [Space Intelligence](https://spaceinsider.tech/2024/08/21/space-intelligence-secures-series-a-funding-to-expand-global-forest-mapping-efforts/) | scaleup | Edinburgh firm producing high-accuracy global forest-cover and biomass maps (Habitat/Carbon mapping) for project MRV and nature monitoring | Series A (2024) led by AzurX Space Ventures with Intercontinental Exchange participating |

**Deforestation & conversion monitoring (incl. EUDR compliance)** · `🟡 scaling`

Platforms that detect deforestation and land conversion via radar/optical satellite and turn it into supply-chain due-diligence, especially for EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) compliance where importers must prove goods are deforestation-free.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Satelligence](https://satelligence.com/eudr/) | scaleup | Netherlands radar+optical (Sentinel-1/2, Landsat) deforestation and land-use monitoring positioned as Europe's largest EUDR data provider | Grew from 3 to ~40 staff in 5 years; engaged in EU pilots; Fairtrade and Prewave partnerships |
| [osapiens](https://osapiens.com/solutions/eudr/) | scaleup | Germany EUDR compliance SaaS automating due diligence, traceability, DDS generation and TRACES submission | Trusted by 700+ industry leaders for EUDR |
| [IntegrityNext](https://www.integritynext.com/esg-solutions/eudr-deforestation-regulation) | scaleup | Germany ESG/supplier platform with an EUDR module running supplier-data upload through DDS and direct TRACES submission | Large supplier ESG network targeting the Dec 2025 EUDR deadline |
| [Prewave](https://supplychaindigital.com/sustainability/supply-chain-transparency-tools-tackling-eudr) | scaleup | Austria AI supply-chain risk platform automating supplier engagement and EUDR monitoring (built with Satelligence and Taylor Wessing) | ~€63M Series B (2024) |
| [Global Forest Watch (WRI)](https://www.globalforestwatch.org/) | incumbent | WRI-run open platform whose GLAD/RADD deforestation alerts are the free data backbone under many commercial EUDR tools | Foundational, free near-real-time alert layer used industry-wide |
| [Orbify](https://orbify.com/blog/navigating-eudr-compliance-the-best-saas-solutions-for-deforestation-monitoring) | startup | No-code Earth-observation platform offering EUDR deforestation-monitoring and due-diligence SaaS | Featured in 2025 EUDR-SaaS roundups; early-stage geospatial player |

> **White space:** Demand is almost entirely regulation-driven, so repeated EUDR timeline slippage and political 'simplification' pressure (application now phased from Dec 2025 for large operators) is the key risk; vendors that diversify into voluntary deforestation-free sourcing and Scope-3 monitoring are less exposed than pure compliance plays.

**Supply-chain traceability & sourcing platforms** · `🟡 scaling`

Software that maps multi-tier agricultural supply chains down to plot/origin and attaches verifiable chain-of-custody and claims data, enabling deforestation-free sourcing for commodities like cocoa, coffee, palm, soy and timber.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Sourcemap](https://www.sourcemap.com/) | scaleup | MIT-born platform mapping products to raw-material origin with transaction-level traceability and EUDR-grade due diligence | Used by large global brands (e.g. AG1); 2024 partnership with Provenance for end-to-end traceability |
| [Provenance](https://www.sourcemap.com/blog/supply-chain-mapping-meets-blockchain-tracking-provenance-partners-with-sourcemap-to-power-end-to-end-robust-traceability-for-consumer-goods) | startup | UK platform producing verified product claims (regenerative, low-carbon, fair trade) backed by chain-of-custody evidence | Strong food/beauty adoption via retailer supplier-engagement programs; Sourcemap partnership |
| [TraceX](https://sti-portal.fao.org/innovations/tracex-supply-chain-traceability-platform) | startup | India blockchain agri-supply-chain traceability connecting participants and supporting EUDR, ESPR, CSRD and DPP | Users include Rainforest Alliance and Organic India; listed on the FAO STI innovations portal |
| [Rainforest Alliance](https://www.fairtrade.net/en/why-fairtrade/why-we-do-it/deforestation.html) | incumbent | NGO certifier whose deforestation-free standard and farm/cooperative traceability underpin cocoa, coffee and tea sourcing | Global certification scheme integrating satellite partners (e.g. Satelligence) for risk assessment |
| [osapiens](https://osapiens.com/solutions/eudr/) | scaleup | Also serves as a traceability layer, bundling multi-tier mapping with EUDR due-diligence and reporting in one platform | 700+ customers spanning compliance and traceability use cases |

> **White space:** The hard, unsolved layer is reliable first-mile/plot-level origin data from millions of smallholders who lack resources to collect and own it; affordable producer-side data capture (not just importer-side dashboards) is the opening, otherwise traceability stays approximate at the farm gate.

**Forest carbon credit ratings, registries & marketplaces** · `🟡 scaling`

The integrity-and-transactions layer: independent rating agencies that score credit quality, the standards/registries that issue and track credits, and marketplaces that let buyers procure them.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Sylvera](https://www.sylvera.com/state-of-carbon-credits) | scaleup | UK carbon-credit rating agency (AAA-D scale) combining satellite, lidar and project data, plus market analytics | ~$96M raised (Index Ventures, Balderton); publishes State of Carbon Credits |
| [BeZero Carbon](https://carbonherald.com/carbon-ratings-agency-bezero-will-boost-its-efforts-with-a-new-32m-funding/) | scaleup | UK rating agency scoring VCM credits (AAA-D) and expanding into CORSIA and Article 6 compliance markets | $32M Series C; ~$90M+ raised total |
| [Calyx Global](https://calyxglobal.com/research-hub/commentary/ratings-differences-1-categorization-of-risks/) | startup | US rating agency that moved to the AAA-D scale in Jan 2025 and absorbed the Renoster team to deepen forestry coverage | VC-backed; converged on market-standard methodology and scale in 2025 |
| [Verra](https://verra.org/programs/verified-carbon-standard/) | incumbent | Runs the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), the world's largest credit registry and the dominant forestry/REDD+ standard | Largest issuer of credits; ARR methodology VM0047 v1.1 received ICVCM CCP approval Oct 2025 |
| [Gold Standard](https://www.marketsandmarkets.com/ResearchInsight/carbon-credit-validation-verification-certification-market.asp) | incumbent | WWF-founded Swiss non-profit standard and registry certifying high-integrity carbon and SDG-impact projects | One of the two leading global certification/registry bodies alongside Verra |
| [Patch](https://carbonherald.com/patch-and-cloverly-partner-to-streamline-carbon-credit-procurement/) | startup | API/enterprise carbon-procurement marketplace for buyers to access, evaluate and buy credits | ~$55M raised (a16z-led Series B); 2025 strategic partnership with Cloverly |
| [Cloverly](https://cloverly.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-carbon-project-registries) | startup | Self-serve carbon marketplace and API for procuring and retiring credits, including forestry | Partnered with Patch in 2025 to streamline corporate buyer access |

**Peatland & wetland conservation / restoration** · `🟠 demonstration`

Protecting and rewetting carbon-dense peat swamp forests, mangroves and wetlands, whose disproportionate carbon stocks make them high-value but high-risk credit sources prone to reversal and tenure disputes.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Permian Global](https://permianglobal.com/projects/katingan-mentaya-project/) | scaleup | UK developer managing tropical peatland REDD+, including the 149,800 ha Katingan Mentaya peat-swamp project in Central Kalimantan | Katingan averages ~7.5M VCUs/year; triple-gold VCS+CCB rated |
| [PT Rimba Makmur Utama (Katingan)](https://www2.cifor.org/redd-case-book/case-reports/indonesia/katingan-peatland-restoration-conservation-project-central-kalimantan-indonesia/) | scaleup | Indonesian project owner/developer of the Katingan peatland conservation project (with Permian Global) | 41M+ Verra credits issued since 2013 |
| [PT Rimba Raya Conservation](https://www.spglobal.com/commodity-insights/en/news-research/latest-news/energy-transition/051024-wide-swathe-of-carbon-market-exposed-to-indonesias-rimba-raya-project-revocation-risks) | scaleup | Developer of the Rimba Raya peat-swamp REDD+ project, once the world's largest avoided-deforestation project | 33.6M credits issued, but Indonesia revoked its license Mar 2024; a Jakarta court voided the revocation Jul 2024 (under appeal), leaving CCB status in legal limbo · *status unverified* |
| [Carbon Streaming Corp](https://www.carbonstreaming.com/news/carbon-streaming-announces-further-update-on-rimba-raya-project/) | incumbent | Carbon-credit streaming/financier that prepaid for Rimba Raya volumes and absorbed the fallout from its revocation | Issued multiple investor updates / write-down risk on Rimba Raya through 2024 |
| [IUCN Peatland Carbon Code](https://bezerocarbon.com/insights/could-non-tropical-peatlands-create-some-of-the-most-valuable-nature-based-credits-for-the-vcm-a-dive-into-the-iucn-peatland-carbon-code) | incumbent | Standard for temperate/non-tropical degraded-peatland restoration (rewetting), opening a new credit class beyond the tropics | First ex-post credits expected to verify around June 2025; still nascent issuance |

> **White space:** Credible supply is concentrated in a handful of Indonesian mega-projects exposed to political tenure and reversal risk (Rimba Raya's license fight), while temperate-peat MRV (water-table and flux measurement) is immature; the opening is robust rewetting MRV plus aggregation of many small parcels into financeable temperate-peatland portfolios.

**Wildfire-resilience forest management & post-fire reforestation** · `🟠 demonstration`

Technology to reduce wildfire risk to forests, the carbon they store and the grid that runs through them, plus replanting after fires, addressing wildfire as both a forest-loss and emissions driver.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [BurnBot](https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/29/climate-change-ignited-las-wildfire-risk-these-startups-want-to-extinguish-it/) | startup | Robotic prescribed-burn / mechanical fuel-treatment machines that clear hazardous fuel loads safely | $20M VC + $30M in fuel-treatment contracts; targeting ~15 machines and 3,000 acres treated by end of 2025 |
| [Kodama Systems](https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/climate-crisis/a-new-wave-of-startups-is-tackling-a-huge-emissions-source-wildfires) | startup | Retrofits forestry equipment for remote/autonomous thinning to cut fuel loads, and buries felled timber for durable carbon credits | $5.95M seed (Tahoe Fund and others); selling biomass-burial removals to Frontier/Stripe |

| [Overstory](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/overstory-closes-43m-series-b-to-scale-ai-driven-wildfire-prevention-and-grid-resilience-302625548.html) | scaleup | AI vegetation-intelligence from satellite imagery for wildfire prevention and grid/vegetation-management for utilities | $43M Series B (Nov 2025) led by Blume Equity with Energy Impact Partners |
| [Pano AI](https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/29/climate-change-ignited-las-wildfire-risk-these-startups-want-to-extinguish-it/) | startup | AI-powered mountaintop camera network for ultra-early wildfire detection and situational awareness | Series B (2024); deployments across western US and Australia, featured among LA-fire response startups |

> **White space:** The category splits into detection (Pano, Overstory), fuel treatment (BurnBot, Kodama) and post-fire replanting (Mast) with little integration; the gap is a single risk-to-remediation loop and, critically, durable revenue beyond episodic state/utility grants, since most fuel-treatment economics still lean on credits or public money.

**REDD+ avoided-deforestation & improved forest management (IFM) developers** · `🟢 mature`

Developers that earn credits by keeping standing forests standing (REDD+) or improving harvest regimes on managed forests (IFM) — the single largest forestry credit category, and the one most damaged by over-crediting and baseline scandals.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [South Pole](https://www.ftm.eu/articles/south-pole-kariba-carbon-emission) | scaleup | Once the world's largest carbon developer/trader; originated and marketed REDD+ at scale | Kariba REDD+ over-crediting scandal led it to terminate the contract (Oct 2023), overhaul leadership (new CEO May 2024) and restructure |
| [Wildlife Works](https://www.wildlifeworks.com/) | scaleup | Community-based REDD+ pioneer (e.g. the Kasigau Corridor, Kenya) tying avoided deforestation to local livelihoods | Long-running Verra-registered REDD+ portfolio; a defining template for the model |
| [Everland](https://www.southpole.com/blog/south-pole-reaction-to-criticisms-of-redd-and-the-vcm) | incumbent | Marketing/distribution arm for REDD+ credits (including Wildlife Works projects) and a vocal defender of REDD+ integrity | Issued public rebuttals to 2023 REDD+ over-crediting criticism |
| [Permian Global](https://permianglobal.com/projects/katingan-mentaya-project/) | scaleup | Tropical forest + peat REDD+ developer (Katingan Mentaya) emphasizing high-integrity avoided-deforestation | Katingan ~7.5M VCUs/year, triple-gold rated |
| [Finite Carbon](https://www.finitecarbon.com/) | incumbent | North America's leading forest carbon developer, mostly IFM projects on private and tribal land | 60+ projects since 2009; majority-owned by bp |
| [Anew Climate](https://northeastforestcarbon.org/forest-carbon-financial-markets/) | incumbent | Large US carbon-project originator (formed from Bluesource + Element Markets) active in IFM and environmental commodities since 2001 | One of the largest US offset suppliers/originators |
| [EFM (Ecotrust Forest Management)](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/microsoft-to-purchase-3m-carbon-removal-credits-from-forest-management-firm-efm/) | scaleup | US forestland investment manager running improved-forest-management funds that generate carbon removals | Microsoft agreed to purchase ~3M IFM carbon-removal credits from EFM |

> **White space:** Although crowded and high-volume, avoided-deforestation baselines were systematically over-credited (Kariba, multiple Verra REDD+ projects), collapsing buyer trust and prices; the reset opportunity is jurisdictional REDD+ (ART/TREES) and re-issuance under Verra's consolidated allocated-baseline methodology (VM0048) with third-party ratings baked in, rather than project-by-project self-reported baselines.

### Blue Carbon & Coastal Ecosystems

**Mangrove restoration & conservation** · `🟡 scaling`

Replanting and protecting mangrove forests, which lock carbon into waterlogged soils at rates far above terrestrial forests while buffering coasts from storms, financed largely through blue carbon credits.

| [Indus Delta Capital (Delta Blue Carbon)](https://deltabluecarbon.com/) | scaleup | Develops and operates the world's largest blue carbon project: 350,000 ha of mangrove restoration in Pakistan's Indus Delta with the Sindh government. | 60-year project targeting ~124 Mt CO2; multiple Verra issuances sold to corporate buyers via Respira and others. |
| [Conservation International (Vida Manglar / Cispata)](https://www.conservation.org/projects/vida-manglar-carbon-project) | incumbent | NGO that pioneered the first Verra-registered blue carbon mangrove project and the first to credit the full mangrove soil-carbon stock, in Colombia. | 7,500 ha conserved/restored; ~1 Mt CO2 expected over 30 years. |
| [Sumitomo Corporation](https://www.sumitomocorp.com/en/jp/news/topics/2025/group/20250401_2) | incumbent | Japanese trading house entering mangrove blue carbon via reforestation projects in Madagascar and Mozambique, selling credits into Europe, the Americas and Asia. | Announced 2025; among Africa's largest, targeting ~34 Mt of credits over 21+ years. |
| [Vlinder Climate](https://vlinderclimate.com/vlinder-kenya-blue-carbon) | startup | Netherlands-based developer building community-led, investable mangrove restoration projects (e.g. Papariko in Kwale/Kilifi/Tana River, Kenya). | Multiple African mangrove projects in development. |

| [Apple (Restore Fund)](https://www.conservation.org/projects/vida-manglar-carbon-project) | incumbent | Corporate investor/buyer financing mangrove conservation (Cispata, Colombia) through its nature-based Restore Fund. | Part of a multi-hundred-million-dollar restoration fund anchoring early blue-carbon demand. |

**Seagrass & tidal salt-marsh restoration** · `🔵 pilot`

Re-establishing seagrass meadows and tidal salt marshes that bury carbon in seabed and marsh sediments and rebuild fish nurseries, though the carbon-finance pathway is still nascent.

| [Project Seagrass](https://www.projectseagrass.org/carbon-and-biodiversity-credits-for-seagrass/) | startup | Largest dedicated seagrass-restoration NGO; running the Accelerate Seagrass programme with Deloitte and the UK National Oceanography Centre to build a UK seagrass carbon code. | Large-scale seed-collection and restoration programmes across the UK. |
| [EcoAct (an Atos company)](https://carboncredits.com/first-carbon-credit-methodology-for-seagrass-developed-in-france/) | incumbent | Climate consultancy that co-developed Europe's first seagrass carbon-credit methodology (Promethee-Med, with Calanques National Park, Schneider Electric, Digital Realty). | Method approved by French DGEC in 2023; ~24,000 tCO2e/yr potential. |
| [The Nature Conservancy + Virginia Institute of Marine Science](https://e360.yale.edu/features/why-the-market-for-blue-carbon-credits-may-be-poised-to-take-off) | incumbent | NGO/academic partnership that restored 9,000+ acres of eelgrass in Virginia's coastal bays, now the first seagrass project to apply for Verra carbon certification. | World-first seagrass Verra application; decades-long restoration dataset. |
| [Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust (with Boskalis)](https://www.hiwwt.org.uk/seagrass-restoration) | incumbent | Runs the Solent Seagrass Restoration Project with dredging major Boskalis Westminster as restoration partner. | Volunteer-driven seed collection and survey programme expanded in 2025. |

| [⚠️ AKUA](https://civileats.com/2024/09/05/will-seaweeds-farming-fulfill-its-potential-as-a-climate-change-solution/) | startup | Kelp-burger and kelp-jerky consumer brand that tried to build retail demand for US-grown kelp. | Raised ~$4.5M (2020-24); shut down August 2024, assets taken over by a Maine farmer co-op. · **☠ shut down** |

> **White space:** The bottleneck is demand, not biology: US seaweed funding fell from ~$100M (2022) to ~$8M (2024) and consumer-food plays like AKUA failed. The durable opening is high-volume industrial offtake (biostimulants, feed, bio-materials), not consumer food brands.

**Seaweed feed additives for livestock methane reduction (Asparagopsis)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Growing red seaweed (Asparagopsis) or synthesizing its active compound bromoform to add to cattle feed, cutting enteric methane burps by up to ~90% and abating a potent greenhouse gas rather than storing carbon.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CH4 Global](https://ch4global.com/2025/01/29/ch4-global-begins-production-at-worlds-first-commercial-scale-asparagopsis-growing-facility-setting-new-benchmark-for-cost-effective-livestock-methane-reduction/) | scaleup | Opened the first commercial-scale Asparagopsis 'EcoPark' (Louth Bay, South Australia) producing the Methane Tamer feed additive via low-cost ponds. | Commercial production began January 2025; claims up to 90% methane cut and 90% lower production cost. |
| [Symbrosia](https://agfundernews.com/symbrosia-nets-5-8m-to-scale-most-cost-effective-cultivation-method-for-methane-busting-seaweed-additive) | startup | Land-based Asparagopsis cultivation (photobioreactor-to-pond) producing the SeaGraze additive; building what it bills as the world's largest land-based seaweed farm in Kona, Hawaii. | $5.8M Series A-1; FDA data submitted; 15-acre site targeted for mid-2027. |
| [Sea Forest](https://agfundernews.com/methane-busting-feed-supplements-are-beginning-to-scale-but-who-will-foot-the-bill-and-what-will-drive-widespread-adoption) | scaleup | Cultivates Asparagopsis in Tasmania for the SeaFeed oil and pellet supplement. | Raised ~$34M; operates a large Tasmanian seaweed farm. |
| [Blue Ocean Barns](https://www.pbs.org/video/cutting-methane-1744664894/) | startup | Grows Asparagopsis on land in filtered seawater (farm in Mexico) for the Brominata feed additive supplied to dairies. | Early commercial supply; one of the first US Asparagopsis additive makers. |
| [Rumin8](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/rumin8) | startup | Synthesizes and stabilizes bromoform pharmaceutically (no seaweed farming) for a low-cost, scalable feed additive. | ~$18M+ raised, including Breakthrough Energy / Bill Gates and Prelude Ventures. |
| [Volta Greentech](https://agfundernews.com/red-seaweed-was-billed-as-a-gamechanger-for-livestock-methane-reduction-so-when-will-it-deliver) | startup | Swedish maker that began with Asparagopsis but has pivoted away to an undisclosed, more-scalable methane-reducing molecule. | ~$2M seed; pivot away from Asparagopsis announced 2024-25. · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Crowded on supply but the unsolved problem is who pays: there is no value chain that funds the per-animal premium, dosing for grazing herds is hard, and Asparagopsis bromoform is costly to grow at scale (hence Volta's pivot and Rumin8's synthetic route). An opening exists for whoever pairs cheap, stable dosing with a credible enteric-methane crediting/insetting mechanism.

**Seaweed / biomass carbon sequestration & sinking** · `🔵 pilot`

Growing or collecting macroalgae and sinking or burying the biomass (or converting it to biochar) so its carbon leaves the fast carbon cycle for centuries, a high-ambition but scientifically contested removal pathway.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [⚠️ Running Tide](https://carbonherald.com/running-tide-shuts-down-citing-lack-of-demand-from-the-voluntary-market/) | startup | Flagship ocean carbon-removal firm that pivoted from kelp to sinking limestone-coated wood chips off Iceland and selling the removals as credits. | Raised >$50M (Lowercarbon et al.); sold credits to Microsoft and Shopify; shut down June 2024 citing collapsed voluntary-market demand. · **☠ shut down** |
| [Seafields](https://oceannews.com/news/science-technology/carbon-removal-company-completes-world-s-first-seaweed-bailing-and-sinking-test/) | startup | Plans open-ocean sargassum farms using artificial upwelling, then bales and sinks the biomass in the South Atlantic gyre. | Sank test bales at ~3,483 m in 2024 (with Running Tide and the Alfred Wegener Institute); pre-commercial, targeting the early 2030s. |
| [Carbon Kapture](https://carbonkapture.com/) | startup | Builds networks of kelp farms and converts harvested kelp into biochar for durable, on-land carbon storage. | Early UK/European pilots; participant in EU ocean-restoration projects. |
| [Brilliant Planet](https://carbonherald.com/brilliant-planet-lands-first-large-scale-carbon-removal-deal-via-watershed-marketplace/) | startup | Grows marine microalgae (not macroalgae) in coastal desert ponds, then solar-dries and buries the biomass on site. | >$25M raised (Toyota Ventures et al.); ~100 t/yr demo; sold removals to Block; targeting 270k t/yr by 2030. |

> **White space:** Thin and high-risk: open-ocean biomass sinking has no scientific consensus or accepted MRV, permitting is fraught (London Protocol/Convention), and the voluntary market shrank, which is exactly what killed Running Tide. The credible openings are on-land/biochar pathways and rigorous, measurable MRV rather than dumping biomass in the deep sea.

**Coastal / blue carbon MRV & credit methodologies** · `🟡 scaling`

The standards, measurement-reporting-verification (MRV) tooling and ratings that turn coastal-ecosystem carbon into credible, sellable credits, the financial plumbing the rest of the bucket depends on.

| [BeZero Carbon](https://www.sylvera.com/blog/what-is-a-carbon-credit-agency) | scaleup | Carbon-credit risk-ratings agency; the only major rater to publish its topline ratings free. | Founded 2020; widely used by corporate buyers to screen blue-carbon credits. |

| [Plan Vivo](https://www.senken.io/academy/blue-carbon) | incumbent | Standards body running PV Blue, a community-focused blue carbon standard used by smallholder mangrove/seagrass projects. | Long-running standard with a dedicated blue-carbon module. |

**Shellfish / bivalve reef restoration** · `🟡 scaling`

Rebuilding oyster and mussel reefs that filter water, protect shorelines and create fish habitat, valuable coastal restoration whose role as a carbon sink is scientifically contested.

|---|---|---|---|

| [Billion Oyster Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oyster_reef_restoration) | startup | Nonprofit restoring oyster reefs in New York Harbor via public-school education and restaurant shell-recycling networks. | 100M+ oysters restored toward a one-billion-oyster goal. |
| [The Nature Conservancy](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/chesapeake-bay/oyster-reef-restoration-chesapeake-bay-were-making-significant-progress) | incumbent | Leads large global shellfish/oyster reef restoration programs and ran the SOAR shellfish-buyback initiative during COVID. | Dozens of reef restoration projects across the US, Europe and Australia. |
| [Puget Sound Restoration Fund](https://restorationfund.org/programs/olympiaoysters/) | startup | Nonprofit restoring native Olympia oysters and pinto abalone across Puget Sound. | 140+ acres of Olympia oyster habitat restored by early 2025. |
| [Chesapeake Bay Foundation](https://www.cbf.org/blogs/save-the-bay/2025/04/harnessing-the-little-bivalve-to-produce-big-results-for-the-bay.html) | incumbent | Runs oyster-gardening and reef-building programs across the Chesapeake with partner agencies. | Helped reach the 2025 10-tributary restoration goal. |

> **White space:** Almost no for-profit players, because the carbon case is weak: shell calcification releases CO2, so bivalves are excluded from blue carbon and mCDR frameworks and earn no credits, leaving restoration dependent on grants and public funds. An opening would require a defensible net-removal MRV (recent PNAS work hints at organic-carbon co-benefits) or stacking biodiversity, coastal-protection, water-quality and nutrient-trading credits into a revenue model.

## Carbon Removal & Capture

Pulling CO2 back out of the air and smokestacks and locking it away — or turning it into products. The clearest innovation gap in climate: the IEA pathway needs ~1,000 Mt/yr of removal by 2050 and today's installed base captures a rounding error of that, at $100–1,000/tonne. Almost the entire sector currently lives off voluntary buyers and tax credits.

*9 solution areas · 90 variations · 437 company entries (376 unique companies; 10 marked dead, 11 acquired, 26 unverified)*

**Maturity at a glance (variations per stage):** Direct Air Capture (3 demonstration, 7 pilot, 1 lab) · Biochar & Bio-oil (5 scaling, 5 demonstration) · Biomass Storage & BECCS (2 scaling, 7 demonstration, 1 pilot) · Enhanced Weathering & Mineralization (land) (4 demonstration, 4 pilot, 1 lab) · Ocean-Based CDR (4 demonstration, 6 pilot, 1 lab) · Point-Source Capture (1 mature, 1 scaling, 6 demonstration, 2 pilot) · CO2 Transport & Geologic Storage (4 scaling, 3 demonstration, 2 pilot) · CO2 Utilization: Fuels, Chemicals & Bio-products (3 scaling, 3 demonstration, 6 pilot) · CO2 Utilization: Built Materials (3 scaling, 3 demonstration, 2 pilot)

**Solution areas:** [Direct Air Capture](#direct-air-capture) · [Biochar & Bio-oil](#biochar-bio-oil) · [Biomass Storage & BECCS](#biomass-storage-beccs) · [Enhanced Weathering & Mineralization (land)](#enhanced-weathering-mineralization-land) · [Ocean-Based CDR](#ocean-based-cdr) · [Point-Source Capture](#point-source-capture) · [CO2 Transport & Geologic Storage](#co2-transport-geologic-storage) · [CO2 Utilization: Fuels, Chemicals & Bio-products](#co2-utilization-fuels-chemicals-bio-products) · [CO2 Utilization: Built Materials](#co2-utilization-built-materials)

### Direct Air Capture

**Liquid solvent DAC (hydroxide capture + calciner regeneration)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Giant fan-driven contactors absorb CO2 into a potassium hydroxide solution that is regenerated through a 900C calcium-looping calciner, favoring very large centralized plants that can leverage oil-and-gas engineering and economies of scale.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1PointFive (Occidental)](https://www.1pointfive.com/projects/stratos) | scaleup | Operates Stratos in Ector County, TX — the world's largest DAC plant (up to 500 ktpa design) using Carbon Engineering's hydroxide/calciner process — and develops the South Texas DAC hub on King Ranch. | Stratos started up mid-2025; first-ever EPA Class VI permits for DAC storage; leads DAC market with ~1.3 Mt credits sold (52% of all DAC tonnes contracted 2020-H1 2025) to Microsoft, Airbus, AT&T and others |
| [Carbon Engineering](https://carbonengineering.com) | startup | Invented the KOH-capture/calcium-loop DAC process and air-to-fuels variant, proven at its Squamish, BC pilot since 2015 before becoming Oxy's technology engine. | Acquired by Occidental for $1.1B (Aug 2023) — the largest DAC exit to date · **acquired** |
| [Occidental / Oxy Low Carbon Ventures](https://heatmap.news/climate-tech/occidental-buys-holocene) | incumbent | Oil major rolling up DAC technology (Carbon Engineering 2023, Holocene 2025) and bankrolling plant buildout, pairing capture with its CO2 sequestration and EOR infrastructure. | DOE confirmed retention of South Texas DAC hub funding (part of $1.2B, Apr 2026); BlackRock invested $550M in Stratos JV |
| [Worley](https://www.worley.com) | incumbent | Global EPC firm that delivered engineering, procurement and construction for Stratos, making it the de facto constructor for gigascale liquid-solvent DAC. | Completed Stratos EPC 2025; positioned for follow-on DAC hub work |

> **White space:** The 900C calciner loop only pencils at mega-scale, so entry requires billions and oil-major balance sheets — effectively an Oxy monopoly today; openings are in component/EPC supply, licensing efficiency improvements to operators, and lower-temperature regeneration chemistries rather than new vertically integrated entrants.

**Liquid amino-acid / non-caustic solvent DAC** · `🔵 pilot`

Benign liquid solvents (amino acid salts, carbonate solutions) absorb CO2 at ambient conditions and are regenerated at low temperature (80-120C) or electrochemically, avoiding caustic chemicals and enabling use of waste heat instead of high-grade energy.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Holocene](https://techcrunch.com/2025/04/17/carbon-removal-startup-holocene-bought-by-oil-and-gas-giant-occidental/) | startup | Amino-acid solution capture combined with guanidine crystallization so CO2 is released from a solid at just 80-120C, based on ORNL chemistry. | Signed $10M/100kt deal with Google at ~$100/t (Sept 2024) — lowest disclosed DAC price — then acquired by Occidental in April 2025 · **acquired** |
| [AirMyne](https://carbonherald.com/airmyne-eneos-direct-air-capture/) | startup | Berkeley YC-backed developer of a low-temperature-regenerable liquid sorbent designed for replication with off-the-shelf industrial equipment and supplying CO2 to local users (including air-captured beverage CO2). | Strategic investment from Japan's ENEOS (Mar 2026); California Energy Commission-backed commercial pilot planned; ~18 employees |
| [Greenlyte Carbon Technologies](https://partechpartners.com/news/greenlyte-secures-multi-million-euro-funding-to-reach-commercial-inflection-point-by-building-its-foak-1-facility) | startup | Potassium-based liquid sorbent that precipitates bicarbonate and releases CO2 via electrolysis while co-producing hydrogen, feeding an integrated DAC-to-methanol plant at the Marl chemical park. | Raised >$40M total; 60+ employees; NRW/EU grant for FOAK DAC-to-e-methanol facility (2025); pre-study with Evonik and Max Planck Institute |

> **White space:** ORNL-derived amino-acid chemistry regenerates with low-grade heat, but Holocene's quick sale to Oxy despite a landmark Google deal shows the venture-funded path is thin; the opening is co-locating with industrial waste heat or geothermal and selling sub-$200/t removals, or licensing solvent chemistry to existing liquid-solvent operators (exactly what Oxy is now doing with hybrid Holocene-Carbon Engineering systems).

**Solid amine sorbent DAC (temperature-vacuum swing)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Air is blown through amine-functionalized solid filters that grab CO2 and release it when heated under vacuum to ~100C; the dominant modular DAC architecture because units can be factory-made and deployed incrementally.

**Advanced/novel sorbent DAC (MOFs, zeolites, thin-film structured sorbents)** · `🔵 pilot`

Next-generation engineered materials — metal-organic frameworks, zeolites, and thin-film structured laminates — promise faster CO2 uptake, lower regeneration energy, and longer sorbent life than first-generation amines, attacking the single biggest DAC cost driver.

Gore & Associates](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carboncapture-inc-unveils-first-us-direct-air-capture-system-designed-for-mass-production-modular-units-to-be-manufactured-at-new-high-volume-facility-in-mesa-arizona-302179051.html) | incumbent | Materials giant co-developing structured sorbent laminates for CarbonCapture Inc.'s mass-produced DAC modules. | Sorbent partnership disclosed with CarbonCapture's 2024 US-manufactured system unveiling |

> **White space:** Sorbent lifetime under real humid, oxidizing, SO2-laden air is the unsolved moat — most MOFs degrade or cost too much per kg; the opening is for chemical majors (BASF already supplies sorbents to the AirJoule JV) to commoditize robust sorbents and sell them across all DAC OEMs, decoupling materials risk from machine risk.

**Electrochemical pH-swing DAC (bipolar membrane electrodialysis, acid-base regeneration)** · `🔵 pilot`

Electricity, not heat, drives capture: electrodialysis or electrolyzer stacks swing a solution between basic (absorbs CO2) and acidic (releases CO2), enabling all-electric, modular, renewables-friendly DAC that piggybacks on the falling cost curves of electrolyzers.

| [Mission Zero Technologies](https://tech.eu/2025/05/02/mission-zero-technologies-opens-first-direct-air-capture-plant-in-norfolk-uk/) | startup | Electrodialysis-based pH-swing recovering CO2 from a carbonated solution at room temperature; first DAC company with three operating plants across different industrial uses (SAF at Sheffield, carbon-negative aggregates at O.C.O Norfolk, storage at Deep Sky). | £21.8M Series A (Mar 2024, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, World Fund, Fortescue, Siemens FS); UK government FEED for 10 ktpa system; 250 tpa Norfolk plant opened 2025 |
| [Phlair](https://frontierclimate.com/writing/phlair) | startup | Munich startup whose 'hydrolyzer' electrochemical acid/base cycle runs DAC entirely on intermittent renewable electricity. | €14.5M seed (2024, Extantia); $30.6M Frontier offtake (2025) — first electrochemical DAC deal by Frontier buyers; deployment at Deep Sky and German BIK federal grant |
| [Capture6](https://capture6.com/news/capture6-completes-27-5-million-series-a-and-project-funding-round/) | startup | Splits waste desalination brine via electrodialysis into NaOH capture solvent plus fresh water, bundling carbon removal with water utilities' brine-disposal problem. | $27.5M Series A + project funding (Mar 2025, Tetrad, Hyundai ZER01NE); Project Monarch demo in Palmdale, CA (~25 ktpa at Phase 2); largest CEC grant in its round (>$8M); follow-on project financing 2026 |
| [Parallel Carbon](https://www.parallelcarbon.com) | startup | Combines iridium-free water electrolysis with a mineral pH-swing loop so every unit co-produces green hydrogen and captured CO2. | ~$3.6M seed (2023) incl. Aramco Ventures; Frontier prepurchase reported |
| [Carbon Atlantis](https://www.carbonatlantis.com) | startup | Munich startup using PEM-electrolyzer-style stacks for acid/base swing capture, supplying CO2 to Paebbl for mineralized building materials. | Seed-stage (~€5-6M); 'Alpha' pilot plant delivering CO2 to industrial offtakers |
| [Ucaneo](https://techfundingnews.com/ucaneo-6-75m-seed-funding-co2-removal-technology/) | startup | Berlin startup with a biomimetic electrochemical membrane (enzyme-inspired) capture cell targeting high energy efficiency. | €6.75M seed (Sep 2024); German federal BIK funding for a Berlin demonstration plant operating by 2027 |

**Electro-swing adsorption DAC (redox-active quinone electrodes)** · `🔵 pilot`

Battery-like cells with redox-active electrodes (quinones) that chemically grab CO2 when charged and release it when discharged, promising near-thermodynamic-minimum energy use with no heat, water, or solvent losses.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Verdox](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251110789998/en/Verdox-Demonstrates-Electrochemical-Carbon-Capture-From-Aluminum-Smelting) | startup | MIT spinout commercializing quinone electro-swing capture; uniquely effective on very dilute streams, demonstrated on 1%-CO2 aluminum smelter exhaust with Hydro before full DAC. | $80M raised (2022, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Prelude, Lowercarbon); pilot-scale unit commissioned Oct 2025; customer pilots 2026, demo unit 2027, commercial target 2029 |
| [RepAir Carbon](https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/repair-carbon-capture) | startup | Israeli startup with a battery-like electrochemical cell shuttling carbonate ions between electrodes for continuous capture at ~600 kWh/t with no thermal step. | Venture-backed Series A (~$15M, 2024); pilot-scale stacks; partnerships incl. geothermal/energy players |

> **White space:** Effectively a Verdox monopoly built on MIT's quinone patent estate; the physics barrier is that redox sorbents degrade in oxygen-rich ambient air — which is why Verdox is wedging in via 1-4% industrial streams first — so an O2-tolerant redox chemistry that survives millions of cycles in real air would reopen the field.

**Moisture-swing DAC and hybrid atmospheric-water-harvesting systems** · `🔵 pilot`

Sorbents that bind CO2 when dry and release it when wetted (or that co-harvest water from air) eliminate most regeneration energy, trading thermal input for water flux — uniquely suited to arid regions and water-co-product business models.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Avnos](https://www.axios.com/2025/11/06/avnos-direct-air-capture-shell-mitsubishi) | startup | 'Hybrid DAC' using moisture-swing sorbents that need no external heat and produce ~2 tons of clean water per ton of CO2 captured — the only water-positive DAC. | >$100M in combined funding secured incl. up to $17M Shell + Mitsubishi project financing (Nov 2025) for Project Cedar (3 ktpa CO2 + 6 kt water, online end-2026); Bakersfield pilot since 2023; US Navy ONR demo 2026 |
| [Carbon Collect](https://carboncollect.com/mechanical-tree/) | startup | Commercializes Klaus Lackner's passive 'MechanicalTree' — wind-fed sorbent discs using moisture-swing regeneration, no fans required. | Gen-II MechanicalTree installed 2025 at ASU; partner in $11.2M Southwest regional DAC hub grant (Jan 2025) |
| [AirJoule Technologies](https://www.gevernova.com/news/press-releases/ge-vernova-and-montana-technologies-close-joint-venture-to-manufacture) | scaleup | Public company (NASDAQ: AIRJ) making MOF-coated-contactor sorbent systems that harvest water and dehumidify air at low energy — sold as the water/dehumidification front end for DAC and data-center cooling. | 50/50 JV with GE Vernova closed Mar 2024 with BASF sorbent supply agreement; $15M follow-on GE Vernova investment |
| [GE Vernova](https://www.gevernova.com/news/press-releases/ge-vernova-and-montana-technologies-close-joint-venture-to-manufacture) | incumbent | Contributes proprietary sorbent materials and manufacturing scale to the AirJoule JV, its beachhead in sorbent-based air harvesting. | JV closed 2024; exclusive manufacturing rights for the Americas, Africa, Australia |
| [Carbominer](https://carbominer.com) | startup | Ukrainian startup using humidity-swing sorbents to capture field CO2 for greenhouse enrichment, operating through wartime. | Grant/angel-funded; pilot units delivered to greenhouse customers |

> **White space:** Moisture-swing regeneration is nearly free energetically but works poorly in humid climates, consumes water in dry ones, and yields dilute CO2 — which is why VCs stayed away and Lackner's concept took 20 years to field; the credible wedge is water-positive hybrids (Avnos) selling water and dehumidification value alongside carbon, especially for data centers and arid-region utilities.

**Calcium/lime-looping DAC (limestone carbonation-calcination)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Cheap, abundant lime or limestone passively carbonates in air and is then calcined to release pure CO2 and regenerate the sorbent — swapping exotic chemistry for the world's most commoditized mineral and existing kiln industry know-how.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Heirloom](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20241204489244/en/Heirloom-Raises-%24150-Million-Series-B-to-Rapidly-Scale-Commercial-Direct-Air-Capture) | scaleup | Spreads calcium hydroxide on stacked trays that carbonate in days, regenerated in Calix-derived electric kilns; opened the first US commercial DAC facility (Tracy, CA, Nov 2023). | $150M Series B (Dec 2024, Future Positive + Lowercarbon, with JAL, Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Siemens FS); two Louisiana plants — 17 ktpa operational from 2026 and a 100 ktpa Project Cypress phase for 2027; DOE hub funding ($1.2B combined) retained Apr 2026; Microsoft offtakes |
| [8 Rivers (Calcite)](https://8rivers.com/portfolio/calcite/) | scaleup | Calcite process reacts hydrated lime with air in low-energy contactors and regenerates it in an oxy-fired kiln; anchor technology of the Southeast DAC hub. | DOE DAC hub FEED for 50 ktpa in Mobile County, AL; Project Cardinal first commercial deployment FEED from 2025; JX Nippon strategic investment; majority-owned by SK Inc. |
| [Origen](https://energiesmedia.com/8-rivers-moves-forward-with-calcite-direct-air-capture-technology/) | startup | UK developer of ZerCaL flash oxy-calcination producing zero-carbon lime as the consumable for DAC and ocean/enhanced-weathering removals, partnered with 8 Rivers on calcite air contactors. | Pilot-scale calciner demos in UK; 8 Rivers partnership |
| [Heimdal](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/heimdal-celebrates-launch-of-bantam-americas-largest-operational-direct-air-capture-facility-302220498.html) | startup | Ultra-cheap DAC from off-the-shelf kit plus crushed limestone, sited next to CO2 users; built Bantam in Osage County, OK — largest constructed US DAC at launch (~5 ktpa). | YC and Sam Altman-backed; Bantam launched Aug 2024 with CapturePoint taking CO2 for EOR; claims path to hundreds of kilotons before 2030 |

**Passive and piggyback contactors (mineralizing surfaces, HVAC/cooling-tower air streams)** · `🔵 pilot`

Instead of paying for fans, these systems borrow air that is already moving — through cooling towers, building HVAC, or wind across passive sorbent structures — cutting capture capex and energy at the cost of small, distributed volumes per site.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Spiritus](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250306128973/en/Spiritus-Unleashes-a-Golden-Era-of-Carbon-Removal-to-Power-Americas-Explosive-Growth-%2430M-Series-A-to-Scale-Direct-Air-Capture) | startup | Passive 'carbon orchard' sorbent structures that soak up CO2 with no forced air, plus a low-cost desorption chamber, targeting $100/t. | $30M Series A (Mar 2025) led by Aramco Ventures with Khosla, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries America, TDK Ventures; Aramco partnership for Saudi deployment; New Mexico pilot |
| [⚠️ Noya](https://www.qcintel.com/carbon/article/us-based-direct-air-capture-developer-ceases-operations-46385.html) | startup | YC-backed pioneer of retrofitting industrial cooling towers into DAC devices, later pivoted to standalone activated-carbon DAC. | Raised ~$14.5M (YC, Union Square Ventures); ceased operations in 2025 amid DAC funding collapse · **☠ shut down** |
| [NeoCarbon](https://techcrunch.com/2022/09/14/neocarbon-pre-seed/) | startup | Berlin startup retrofitting DAC kits inside operating industrial cooling towers, using their airflow and waste heat to cut DAC costs up to 10x. | €1.25M pre-seed (2022) + €3.2M seed (2023, Speedinvest, PT1); pilots with German industrials |
| [Soletair Power](https://www.soletairpower.fi) | startup | Finnish, Wärtsilä-backed maker of building-HVAC-integrated DAC that scrubs CO2 from ventilation air and feeds utilization (including demonstration synthetic fuel chains). | Units deployed in office buildings in Finland and Germany; Wärtsilä strategic investor |
| [Carbon Reform](https://www.carbonreform.com) | startup | 'Carbon Capsule' retrofit for commercial HVAC that captures CO2 from indoor air and mineralizes it to calcium carbonate while cutting ventilation energy. | Seed-stage; pilot installations in US commercial buildings |
| [enVerid](https://enverid.com) | scaleup | Sells sorbent-based HVAC Load Reduction modules that scrub CO2/VOCs from indoor air so buildings can slash outside-air intake — proving the only currently profitable business model for air-scrubbing hardware (energy savings, not removal credits). | Deployed in hundreds of buildings globally; >$40M raised |

> **White space:** Borrowed airflow slashes contactor cost but each site yields only tens to hundreds of tons a year, so MRV, logistics, and sales overhead swamp the unit economics — Noya's shutdown after $14.5M is the cleanest evidence; the surviving opening is bundling capture with paid co-benefits (HVAC energy savings like enVerid, or onsite CO2 supply), where carbon revenue is gravy rather than the business.

**Integrated DAC-to-fuel/material plants** · `🔵 pilot`

Vertically integrated systems that capture CO2 from air and immediately convert it — with green hydrogen or solar heat — into gasoline, methane, jet fuel, methanol, or building materials, selling a product rather than a removal credit.

|---|---|---|---|
| [Aircela](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/05/15/3082353/0/en/Aircela-Unveils-Machine-That-Turns-Air-into-Fossil-Free-Gasoline.html) | startup | Fridge-sized machine integrating DAC, electrolysis, and methanol-to-gasoline synthesis to make ~1 gallon/day of fossil-free gasoline onsite. | First working US air-to-gasoline demo (Manhattan rooftop, May 2025); initial off-grid/commercial deployments from fall 2025; backed by Maersk Growth and Chris Larsen |
| [Terraform Industries](https://terraformindustries.com) | startup | Containerized 'Terraformer' converting cheap solar power plus DAC CO2 and electrolytic H2 into pipeline-grade synthetic natural gas. | ~$38M seed at $150M valuation; delivered carbon-neutral synthetic methane to two utility partners (2024) earning a green premium |
| [Sora Fuel](https://www.sorafuel.com/news/sora-fuel-closes-14-6m-round-to-scale-air-to-jet-fuel-technology) | startup | Captures CO2 into bicarbonate and electrochemically converts it to syngas in one integrated step, claiming <$50/t captured carbon en route to <$5/gal SAF. | $14.6M round (closed 2025/2026) to build a pilot scaling SAF output from gallons to barrels per day within ~18-24 months; earlier $6M seed (2024) |
| [Synhelion](https://synhelion.com) | scaleup | Swiss solar-thermochemical fuel producer whose concentrated-solar reactors turn CO2 and water into syngas/fuels; built the DAWN industrial demonstration plant. | DAWN plant operating in Jülich, Germany (2024); >CHF 70M raised; partnerships with SWISS/Lufthansa and Climeworks heritage on DAC-sourced CO2 |
| [HIF Global](https://www.hifglobal.com) | scaleup | Largest e-fuels project developer (Haru Oni demo in Chile); contracted Baker Hughes' Mosaic MOF DAC to supply atmospheric CO2 for its planned Matagorda, TX e-gasoline plant. | >$1B raised (Porsche, EIG, others); Haru Oni producing since 2022; Matagorda in development with DAC integration |
| [Prometheus Fuels](https://www.prometheusfuels.com) | startup | Promised direct air-to-gasoline via aqueous CO2 electroreduction and carbon-nanotube membrane separation at fossil-parity prices. | Raised at a $1.5B valuation (2021, BMW i Ventures, Maersk); no verified product deliveries since, public communications gone dark · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Stacking DAC, hydrogen, and synthesis multiplies capex and failure modes — Prometheus's $1.5B-valuation silence is the cautionary tale — and air-captured fuel can't yet compete with point-source or biogenic CO2 feedstocks; the openings are price-insensitive niches (off-grid sites, islands, military, motorsport) and EU e-fuel mandates (ReFuelEU) that explicitly reward atmospheric CO2 feedstock.

**Early-stage membrane and cryogenic DAC** · `⚪ lab`

Membranes that passively filter CO2 from air and cryogenic systems that freeze it out promise solvent-free, chemical-free capture, but at 420 ppm both fight brutal thermodynamics and remain at lab/early-pilot stage.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Carbon Xtract](https://c-xtract.com/en/news/340/) | startup | Kyushu University spinout commercializing m-DAC nano-separation membranes — the first claimed membrane-only system to capture and concentrate atmospheric CO2 — initially for greenhouses and urban installations. | Founded May 2023 by Sojitz; Kyushu University's first-ever direct business investment; Tokyo Metropolitan GX demonstration installation; joint development with Tokyo Ohka Kogyo; Japan Moonshot program targets devices by 2030 |
| [Sojitz](https://www.sojitz.com/en/news/article/20231124.html) | incumbent | Japanese trading house incubating and commercializing m-DAC, lining up agriculture co-ops and MUFG for greenhouse and distributed deployments. | Co-founded Carbon Xtract (2023); MOU with Kyushu Electric for DAC-utilization systems |
| [Revcoo](https://carbonherald.com/revcoo-pushes-solvent-free-carbon-capture-toward-industrial-scale/) | startup | French startup freezing CO2 out of gas streams by cryogenic reverse-sublimation using only electricity and nitrogen cold — today on lime-kiln flue gas, the nearest commercial stepping stone toward cryogenic air capture. | Pilot running since late 2024 at an Eiffage lime kiln; seeking growth funding |
| [Air Liquide](https://www.digitalrefining.com/news/1003771/air-liquide-inaugurates-its-co2-cold-capture-system-cryoca) | incumbent | Owns the industrial cryogenic CO2 capture toolkit (Cryocap) and air-separation expertise any cryogenic DAC would be built on; has not productized ambient-air capture. | Cryocap operating at hydrogen plants since 2015; active CCUS portfolio |
| [NuAria](https://www.startus-insights.com/innovators-guide/direct-air-capture-companies/) | startup | US early-stage developer of sorbent-filled membrane DAC modules cited in 2025 startup scouting reports. | Pre-seed/seed stage; minimal public verification · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Physics keeps this lane empty: at 420 ppm a membrane needs extraordinary selectivity-permeance plus multistage vacuum/compression, and freezing CO2 from air means refrigerating ~2,500x its volume of N2/O2 — so no Western pure-play has been venture-funded and Japan's consortium model (university + Sojitz + Moonshot money) is the only serious bet; openings are membrane pre-concentrators feeding sorbent systems, and cryo-DAC piggybacking on free cold from LNG regasification or cold-climate winters.

### Biochar & Bio-oil

**Industrial slow-pyrolysis biochar plants** · `🟡 scaling`

Continuous industrial reactors bake forestry and agricultural residues without oxygen into stable biochar plus usable process heat/power, locking ~2-3 tCO2 per tonne of char for centuries while producing a saleable soil product; this route delivers the large majority of all durable carbon removal credits retired to date.

| [Novocarbo](https://techfundingnews.com/novocarbo-raises-e25m-to-build-up-to-200-carbon-removal-parks-across-europe/) | scaleup | Develops 'Carbon Removal Parks' across Europe that co-locate pyrolysis with industrial customers buying the waste heat | €25M from SWEN Capital Partners (2024); roadmap of up to 200 parks across Europe |

**Mobile and village-scale pyrolysis units** · `🟠 demonstration`

Small transportable carbonizers, tractor-mounted units and trained smallholder kiln networks convert dispersed agricultural and forestry residues into biochar at the field edge, avoiding open burning and biomass haulage costs — the cheapest feedstock in the world, but the hardest to monitor.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Takachar](https://earthshotprize.org/winners-finalists/takachar/) | startup | MIT spinout making low-cost, tractor-mountable units that convert crop residue to char/bioproducts in-field to stop residue burning | Earthshot Prize 2021 winner; Takavator Mini (~100 kg/hr) deployed in southern India, US West Coast and British Columbia |
| [Applied Carbon](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/31/applied-carbons-farm-robot-turns-plant-waste-into-biochar-to-capture-co2/) | startup | Self-propelled in-field pyrolyzer trailers (ex-Climate Robotics) that pick up crop residue, char it, quench it and spread it on the field in one pass | $21.5M Series A (Aug 2024) led by TO VC with Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund participation |
| [Biochar Life](https://biochar.life/) | startup | Trains smallholder farmers in Kenya, Malawi and Thailand to make artisanal biochar (Kon-Tiki/trench kilns) and aggregates C-Sink credits | Sells via Carbonfuture; deploying WasteX semi-automated carbonizers across its network from 2025 |
| [WasteX](https://climateinsider.com/2024/04/04/wastex-secures-450k-to-expand-biochar-solution-in-indonesia/) | startup | Singapore/Indonesia startup selling small semi-automated carbonizers to rice and poultry mills with credit revenue sharing | $450k from P4G (2024); trials showing 38-95% yield gains with halved fertilizer in Philippines/Indonesia |
| [HUSK](https://www.atmosfair.de/en/cambodia-biochar-rice-husks/) | startup | Cambodia/Vietnam venture turning rice husks into biochar-based fertilizers for smallholders, now adding a dedicated pyrolysis plant with atmosfair | Mekong Capital investee; Kampong Thom plant commissioned Nov 2025 (~3 t char/day from 6 t husks) |
| [Air Burners](https://airburners.com/) | incumbent | Florida maker of mobile air-curtain burners whose CharBoss model (developed with USDA Forest Service) converts forestry slash to char on-site | CharBoss units sold to utilities and forestry agencies for wildfire-fuel reduction |
| [Tigercat](https://www.tigercat.com/) | incumbent | Canadian forestry-equipment manufacturer producing the 6050 Carbonator, a tracked mobile carbonizer for slash disposal | In serial production within an established global forestry equipment line |

**Hydrothermal carbonization of wet wastes (hydrochar)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Pressurized hot water (~180-250C) 'cooks' wet feedstocks like sewage sludge, manure and food waste into coal-like hydrochar without energy-intensive drying, solving a disposal problem and enabling phosphorus recovery — though hydrochar's lower carbon permanence limits its carbon-credit value versus pyrolysis char.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [TerraNova Energy](https://www.terranova-energy.com/en/applications/) | startup | German HTC technology (TerraNova Ultra) for sewage sludge with integrated phosphorus recovery; industrial reference plant in Jining, China | Operating industrial references in Germany and China; licenses to utilities |
| [Ingelia](https://ingelia.com/) | startup | Spanish pioneer running continuous industrial HTC at Naquera since 2010 and licensing plants internationally | Longest-running industrial HTC plant; licensees including CPL in the UK |
| [C-Green](https://www.c-green.se/) | startup | Swedish OxyPower HTC modules that use wet oxidation to make sludge-to-hydrochar nearly energy self-sufficient | First commercial unit at Stora Enso's Heinola mill (Finland); further Nordic deployments |
| [HTCycle](https://www.openpr.com/news/4105102/exponential-growth-expected-for-hydrothermal-carbonization) | startup | German sewage-sludge HTC plant at Relzow with phosphorus recovery as the revenue anchor | Consistently ranked among the top HTC players in 2025 market surveys |
| [CPL Industries](https://www.openpr.com/news/4105102/exponential-growth-expected-for-hydrothermal-carbonization) | incumbent | UK smokeless-fuel incumbent operating an Ingelia-licensed HTC line (Immingham) to make waste-derived briquettes | Decades-old solid-fuels business; listed among leading HTC companies 2025 |
| [AVA-CO2 (AVA Biochem)](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/17/8/1918) | startup | Built the world's first industrial-scale HTC plant (Karlsruhe, 2010) before exiting HTC to pivot to 5-HMF biochemicals | Early-mover cautionary tale: HTC business wound down in the mid-2010s for lack of offtake economics · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Hydrochar is less recalcitrant than pyrolysis char so registries award few or no durable-CDR credits, leaving plants to live off sludge tipping fees; EU bans on sludge landspreading and phosphorus-recovery mandates create a utility-partnered niche that remains thinly served — an opening for waste majors (Veolia/SUEZ-style) to roll up the licensors.

**Bio-oil and bio-slurry deep-well injection for permanent storage** · `🟠 demonstration`

Biomass is converted to a pumpable carbon-rich liquid (fast-pyrolysis bio-oil) or slurry and injected into regulated deep disposal wells, where it solidifies for 1,000+ year storage — trading biochar's soil co-benefits for maximum permanence and verifiability.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Charm Industrial](https://carbonherald.com/charm-industrial-raises-100m-in-series-b-ramp-up-bio-oil-sequestration/) | scaleup | The category creator: mobile fast pyrolyzers convert crop residue and wildfire-risk biomass into bio-oil injected into EPA-regulated disposal wells | $100M Series B (2023); $53M Frontier offtake, Google and JPMorgan purchases, TD Bank deal with Canada expansion (2025); tens of thousands of tonnes delivered |
| [Vaulted Deep](https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/17/microsoft-is-buying-tons-of-carbon-removal-from-xprize-startup-vaulted-deep/) | startup | Injects slurried organic wastes (biosolids, manure, paper sludge) into deep geologic formations using oilfield slurry-injection IP — same storage logic without the pyrolysis step | $32M Series A (Prelude); won $50M XPRIZE grand prize... ($8M category, Apr 2025); Microsoft 4.9 Mt 12-year deal (Jul 2025); CNBC Disruptor 50 (2026) |
| [MASH Makes](https://www.nefco.int/news/mash-makes-secures-financing-from-nefco/) | startup | Danish-Indian company whose containerized pyrolysis lines yield biochar plus carbon-negative bio-oil, proven as drop-in marine fuel and a candidate storage feedstock | Nefco financing; Karnataka plant processes ~23,700 t agri-waste/yr (~3,400 t bio-oil); world-first vessel trial on its biofuel; second plant tripling capacity |
| [Carba](https://esgnews.com/microsoft-signs-44000-tonne-carbon-removal-deal-with-carba-using-biochar-burial/) | startup | Minnesota startup using low-temperature pyrolysis (torrefaction) then burial of the carbon in engineered landfill-style pits — a low-cost storage cousin of injection | $7M DOE Carbon Negative Shot grant; Microsoft 44,000-credit 5-year deal; $6M round (Rusheen, CanopyGen) for US and Asia expansion |

> **White space:** Charm is still the only company injecting pyrolysis bio-oil at scale — bio-oil is corrosive, costs run several hundred dollars per tonne, and injection-well permitting is slow — so the opening is regional pyrolysis hubs feeding shared disposal wells and oilfield-services incumbents (who already drill and permit these wells) offering 'storage as a service' to any bio-oil producer.

**Biochar soil-application networks and credit aggregators/registries** · `🟡 scaling`

Registries, MRV platforms and project aggregators certify that char is actually produced, tracked and applied to soils or materials, turning fragmented biochar production into bankable carbon credits — the connective tissue that made biochar ~90% of delivered durable CDR.

| [Carbonfuture](https://www.carbonfuture.com/magazine/exomad-green-announces-worlds-largest-biochar-carbon-removal-agreement-with-microsoft-tracked-by-carbonfuture-mrv) | startup | German digital MRV ('MRV+') and marketplace tracking char from kiln to end use; infrastructure behind the largest supplier programs | Tracks the Exomad-Microsoft 1.24 Mt deal and Swiss Re's 70,000 t biochar program |
| [Isometric](https://registry.isometric.com/protocol/biochar) | startup | Science-first CDR registry whose Biochar Production & Storage protocol was ICVCM-approved in 2025, used by quality-focused corporate buyers | $25M seed (Lowercarbon, Plural); biochar protocol live alongside Frontier-aligned buyers |
| [Varaha](https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/16/google-strikes-worlds-largest-biochar-carbon-removal-deal-with-indian-startup-varaha/) | startup | Indian developer aggregating smallholder and industrial biochar projects (incl. Gujarat facility) across South Asia | Google offtake of 100,000 t (Jan 2025) — world's largest biochar deal at signing; only Indian supplier listed on Puro.earth at the time |
| [Carbon Standards International](https://www.carbon-standards.com/) | startup | Swiss certifier running the EBC (European Biochar Certificate) and Global C-Sink standards covering both industrial and artisanal char sinks | De-facto EU biochar quality standard; artisanal C-Sink methodology used across the Global South |
| [Pacific Biochar](https://trellis.net/article/seven-biochar-companies-you-should-know/) | startup | Retrofits idle California biomass power plants for char production and routes it through compost and farm soil-application networks | Early Microsoft biochar supplier (1,500 t CO2 in 2021); multiple California facilities |
| [Verra](https://www.sylvera.com/blog/biochar-carbon-credits) | incumbent | World's largest voluntary carbon registry; its VM0044 biochar methodology brings biochar into the mainstream VCM | VM0044 v1.2 ICVCM-approved in 2025 alongside Isometric and CAR biochar methodologies |

**Biochar-embedded materials (concrete, asphalt, plastics, filtration media)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Biochar is blended into concrete, asphalt, polymers and filtration media as a lightweight carbon-storing filler that can also cut cement content, turning buildings and roads into carbon sinks and stacking embodied-carbon savings on top of sellable removal credits.

| [ecoLocked](https://carbonherald.com/ecolocked-secures-e4m-in-seed-funding-for-biochar-carbon-removal/) | startup | Berlin startup making biochar-based admixtures that replace part of the cement binder in ready-mix concrete | €4M seed (Matterwave, Climentum, 2023) on top of €1.8M pre-seed; pilots with concrete producers |
| [Glanris](https://www.glanris.com/applications) | startup | Memphis company converting rice hulls into patented biocarbon water-filtration media, with concrete and asphalt applications | Patented rice-hull media; certified carbon-removal claims; commercial filtration sales |
| [Made of Air](https://www.madeofair.com/) | startup | German maker of HexChar, a biochar-filled thermoplastic for facades and retail interiors (used by Audi, H&M pilots) | Raised ~$5-6M (2022); little public activity since 2024 — commercial status unclear · *status unverified* |
| [Verde Resources](https://biochar-international.org/news/biochar-as-a-diversified-carbon-dioxide-removal-pathway-research-and-technology-integration-update-2023-2025/) | startup | US-listed developer of BioAsphalt/BioFraction putting biochar into net-zero road construction, working with NCAT test tracks | Named by the International Biochar Initiative (2025) as the pioneer of biochar asphalt R&D and pilot roads |
| [Myno Carbon](https://mynocarbon.com/biochar-carbon-for-concrete-and-asphalt/) | startup | Washington-state producer building mill-co-located biochar plants and marketing char specifically for concrete and asphalt | First plant sited at a WA pulp mill; targets 5 Mt CO2/yr across facilities by 2030 |

> **White space:** Construction codes and conservative mix-design specs make adoption slow, and biochar must beat near-free fillers like fly ash on cost; Made of Air's stall shows the product risk — the opening is code-approved, EPD-backed admixtures sold through ready-mix incumbents that stack embodied-carbon reductions with CDR credit revenue.

**Pyrolysis reactor OEMs and technology licensors** · `🟡 scaling`

Equipment makers and licensors supply the kilns, screws and carbonization modules every biochar project depends on, monetizing the boom through capex sales and royalties rather than carbon credits — the 'picks and shovels' of the sector.

**Fast-pyrolysis bio-oil production for fuels and chemicals** · `🟠 demonstration`

Rapid high-temperature pyrolysis maximizes the liquid fraction, producing pyrolysis oil that is co-processed in refineries, burned as renewable heating fuel, or upgraded to chemicals — the industrial bio-oil base that the carbon-removal injection pathway now builds on.

| [Pyrocell](https://www.setragroup.com/en/pyrocell/about-pyrocell/) | incumbent | Setra-Preem joint venture converting sawmill sawdust to pyrolysis oil at Gavle for co-processing at Preem's Lysekil refinery | Producing since autumn 2021 (~25,000 t/yr design); first sawdust-to-refinery value chain in Sweden |
| [Twence (Empyro)](https://www.btg-bioliquids.com/plant/pyrocell-gavle-sweden/) | incumbent | Dutch waste-and-energy utility that owns and operates the Empyro fast-pyrolysis oil plant in Hengelo | Empyro running commercially since 2015 (~20 ML/yr design), acquired by Twence in 2019 |
| [Green Fuel Nordic](https://www.ieabioenergy.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/WP3.3-DTL-Final.pdf) | startup | Operates the Lieksa, Finland fast-pyrolysis bio-oil plant on BTG-BL technology for industrial heating fuel | Commercial production since 2020; listed as commercial in IEA Bioenergy's direct-liquefaction status report |

> **White space:** Pyrolysis oil as fuel struggles against fossil parity and depends on a handful of refinery co-processing partners, which is why the plant fleet has barely grown since 2015; the visible opening is redirecting output to higher-value uses — carbon-removal injection feedstock (Charm's model) or specialty chemicals — rather than competing in heating fuel.

**Metallurgical and industrial biocarbon (fossil carbon substitution)** · `🟡 scaling`

Engineered high-purity biocarbon from wood residues replaces fossil coal and coke as reductant and energy carbon in steel, ferroalloy, silicon and battery-material production — an enormous emissions-reduction market that pulls pyrolysis to true heavy-industrial scale.
