| [Aperam BioEnergia](https://www.regreener.earth/blog/the-5-best-biochar-carbon-credit-and-offset-projects-of-2026) | incumbent | Stainless-steel group Aperam's Brazilian eucalyptus charcoal operation, decades-scale supplier to its own 'green steel' mills and now a Puro-certified biochar credit issuer | ~10,000 t/yr certified biochar in 2025, tripling by 2026 — among the largest Puro.earth projects |
| [Weyerhaeuser](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/weyerhaeuser-and-aymium-enter-agreement-to-rapidly-scale-biocarbon-market-302638368.html) | incumbent | US timber REIT entering biocarbon production and guaranteed fiber supply through the TerraForge Biocarbon Solutions JV with Aymium | MOU announced Dec 2025 to produce and sell 1.5 Mt/yr of biocarbon for metals |

> **White space:** Steel, ferroalloy and silicon demand for fossil-coal substitutes dwarfs current biocarbon supply, but smelter qualification cycles and securing multi-decade fiber supply are brutal for startups — openings favor forestry incumbents and licensors who control feedstock (Weyerhaeuser's entry is the tell), and a credible European/Asian counterpart to Aymium is still missing.

### Biomass Storage & BECCS

**Engineered terrestrial biomass burial (dry casks, vaults, trenches)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Waste biomass (forestry/ag residues, wildfire-killed wood) is dried below the moisture threshold for decomposition, compressed and sealed in impermeable barriers, then buried in engineered underground chambers so its carbon cannot return to the atmosphere for centuries.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Graphyte](https://www.eenews.net/articles/exclusive-worlds-largest-carbon-removal-plant-is-about-to-open/) | startup | Carbon Casting: dries and compresses timber/ag residue into sealed blocks buried in monitored underground sites; first BiCRS firm to earn a BeZero 'AA' rating. | Breakthrough Energy-backed; ~$30M raised; first commercial Pine Bluff AR plant operating (250k t/yr target), ~6,000 t sequestered year one, ~50k t capacity by early 2026; expanding to BC, Canada. |
| [Mast Reforestation (Mast Wood Preserve)](https://www.renewableenergymagazine.com/biomass/mast-reforestation-sells-out-mt1-biomass-burial-20260415) | startup | Buries wildfire-killed trees in engineered underground chambers as part of post-wildfire restoration, pairing reforestation with biomass burial credits. | Sold out 100% of its 4,277-credit MT1 Montana project within ~6 weeks of issuance; >10M lbs of biomass buried. |
| [Boomitra](https://boomitra.com/biomass-carbon-removal/) | startup | Selectively removes invasive woody species, dries and seals biomass into dense bales, then buries them at secure sites for 100+ year storage. | Operating biomass-burial program alongside its soil-carbon MRV business; XPRIZE-recognized soil carbon team. |
| [Carbon Sequestration Inc.](https://www.carbonsequestration-inc.com/) | startup | Markets terrestrial storage and biomass burial as durable sequestration solutions. | Early-stage; limited public traction disclosed. · *status unverified* |

**Subsurface slurry / bio-oil injection of organic wastes** · `🟠 demonstration`

Non-hazardous organic wastes (biosolids, paper-mill sludge, manure, crop residue) or biomass-derived bio-oil are pumped thousands of feet underground into porous rock or salt formations, locking biogenic carbon away permanently while solving a waste-disposal problem.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Vaulted Deep](https://www.canarymedia.com/articles/emissions-reduction/frontier-bets-58.3m-on-carbon-removal-startup-vaulted-deep) | startup | Injects organic-waste slurry (biosolids, sludge, manure, crop residue) >3,000 ft underground using established geologic-disposal engineering. | $32.3M Series A; won $8M as XPRIZE Carbon Removal second runner-up (Apr 2025); $58.3M Frontier offtake; delivered ~9,986 net tonnes in demo; processed waste up 225% 2024-2025. |
| [Charm Industrial](https://www.axios.com/2025/11/14/boeing-carbon-removal-charm-industrial-startup) | scaleup | Pyrolyzes biomass into stable bio-oil, then injects it into Class-I disposal wells; also delivering biochar removals. | $100M Series B (General Catalyst); $20M JPMorgan venture debt; Boeing offtake up to 100k t; TD Bank 10-yr deal; ~12,000 t sequestered to date. |

**BECCS retrofits on biomass power and district-heat plants** · `🟠 demonstration`

Existing biomass-fired power and combined-heat-and-power plants are retrofitted with post-combustion CO2 capture so the biogenic CO2 they emit is permanently stored geologically, turning renewable heat/power into net carbon removal.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|

| [Drax Group](https://www.edie.net/drax-scales-back-carbon-capture-funding-and-staffing/) | incumbent | Plans to retrofit BECCS onto its converted biomass power station (planning permission for two units, phased conversion of four). | Scaled back BECCS spend and cut roles in 2025 amid UK policy uncertainty (~GBP1M H1 2025 vs GBP2M prior); Ember estimates up to GBP30bn subsidy could exceed entire UK CCUS budget; timeline slipped to early 2030s. · *status unverified* |

**Purpose-built biomass carbon removal & storage (gasification to hydrogen/power + CO2 storage)** · `🟠 demonstration`

New-build plants gasify or combust biomass specifically to co-produce energy (hydrogen, power, or fuels) and a concentrated biogenic CO2 stream that is captured and geologically stored, designed from the ground up to be carbon-negative rather than retrofitted.

**Waste-to-energy CO2 capture (biogenic fraction)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Municipal waste-to-energy (energy-from-waste) plants add CO2 capture so that roughly the half of their emissions that are biogenic (food, garden, waste wood) become net carbon removal, while the fossil-plastic half is captured as avoided emissions.

| [Hafslund Oslo Celsio](https://frontierclimate.com/writing/hafslundcelsio) | incumbent | First-ever carbon-capture retrofit on a WtE plant (Oslo Klemetsrud), capturing both biogenic and fossil CO2 for Northern Lights storage. | Up to 350k t CO2/yr (175k biogenic); world's first commercial WtE-CDR offtake (Frontier, $31.6M / 100k t 2029-2030, Apr 2025); capture construction from spring 2026, ops Q3 2029. |
| [Encyclis](https://www.ieabioenergy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/IEA-Bioenergy_Intertask_BECCUS_Phase2_Oslo_WtE_final-report.pdf) | incumbent | UK/European energy-from-waste operator developing carbon capture across its WtE fleet (e.g. Protos) under the UK CCUS cluster programme. | Part of UK HyNet/track-1 CCUS plans; multiple WtE capture projects in development. |

> **White space:** Few movers because WtE-CDR depends on accurate biogenic-fraction accounting, CO2 transport/storage networks (e.g. Northern Lights), and willingness to retrofit municipal utilities; an opening exists for capture-tech vendors and aggregators who can standardize biogenic MRV and bundle many mid-size municipal plants.

**Ethanol & fermentation biogenic CO2 capture and storage** · `🟡 scaling`

Corn-ethanol and other fermentation plants emit a nearly pure biogenic CO2 stream that is cheap to compress and inject underground, making fermentation-source CCS among the lowest-cost biogenic carbon storage available.

**Biogas/RNG upgrading CO2 capture for removal credits** · `🔵 pilot`

When raw biogas from anaerobic digestion is upgraded to pipeline-quality renewable natural gas, the separated biogenic CO2 (normally vented) is instead captured and permanently stored or mineralized, generating durable carbon-removal credits on top of the RNG.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [neustark](https://www.neustark.com/en/news/neustark-secures--69-million-in-funding-to-expand-carbon-removal-solution-globally) | scaleup | Liquefies biogenic CO2 captured at biogas/RNG-upgrading plants and mineralizes it into recycled demolition-concrete granules and mineral wastes for permanent storage. | $69M round led by BlackRock/Temasek's Decarbonization Partners (Holcim, Siemens backing); targeting 1M t CO2 removed by 2030; CHF50M Swiss climate-fund awards; aiming for 4,000 t/yr UK projects from 2025. |
| [Green Gas / RNG project developers (sector)](https://adbioresources.org/newsroom/engineered-removal-of-carbon-is-creating-opportunities-for-the-biogas-sector/) | incumbent | RNG producers increasingly monetize the biogenic CO2 byproduct of biomethane upgrading as carbon-removal credits. | US RNG facilities grew from ~30 (2011) to >300 by 2023, expanding the addressable biogenic-CO2 base; ADBA/CCC flag engineered removal as a new biogas-sector revenue stream. |

> **White space:** The vented CO2 is biogenic and already separated, so capture is technically easy, but each digester emits only small, dispersed volumes that are uneconomic to truck to storage individually; the opening is aggregation models and onsite mineralization (e.g. into concrete) that avoid long-distance CO2 transport.

Kraft pulp mills and similar biogenic-heavy industries capture the large, concentrated biogenic CO2 streams from their recovery boilers and lime kilns for permanent storage, leveraging existing biomass supply chains and large point sources.

Hafslund Celsio engagement). |

**Biogenic CO2 mineralization into building materials (added)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Concentrated biogenic CO2 from biogas or other biomass sources is permanently fixed as carbonate minerals inside recycled concrete granules, demolition aggregate, and mineral wastes, giving durable removal that doubles as a low-carbon construction input.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [neustark](https://carbonherald.com/neustark-secures-69m-to-scale-promising-carbon-removal-technology/) | scaleup | Injects liquefied biogenic CO2 into recycled-concrete granules and mineral waste (slag, slurry) for permanent mineral storage, also yielding a construction material. | $69M BlackRock/Temasek-led round; backing from Holcim and Siemens; goal of 1M t CO2 removed by 2030. |

> **White space:** Still a thin field: it requires both a biogenic CO2 source and nearby mineral-waste/recycling feedstock, and credit volumes per site are small; the opening is co-locating mineralization at construction-and-demolition recycling hubs in dense urban markets where CO2 transport distance is minimal.

### Enhanced Weathering & Mineralization (land)

**Cropland enhanced rock weathering (crushed basalt spreading)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Finely crushed basalt is spread on farm fields where it dissolves in rainwater, capturing atmospheric CO2 as stable bicarbonate that drains to the ocean while raising soil pH and crop yields, making it one of the most scalable and co-beneficial land-based carbon removal methods.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Lithos Carbon](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251202793450/en/Lithos-Carbon-Delivers-5160-Registry-Certified-Tons-of-Carbon-Removal-in-Worlds-Largest-Enhanced-Rock-Weathering-Issuance-to-Date) | startup | Basalt spreading on US row-crop farms with soil-chemistry models to optimize dose and measure removal | Issued 5,160 registry-certified tons in Dec 2025 (largest single ERW issuance to date, ~7x prior record); Frontier/Microsoft offtakes |
| [Mati Carbon](https://www.mati.earth/mati-carbon-is-the-grand-prize-winner-of-the-xprize-carbon-removal-competition/) | startup | Nonprofit deploying basalt to smallholder farms in India/Africa (Global South), monetizing via carbon credits | Won $50M XPRIZE Carbon Removal grand prize April 2025; demonstrated >1,000 t/yr removal |
| [Terradot](https://www.ccarbon.info/insight/carbon-dioxide-removal-series-enhanced-weathering-and-mineralization-market-compass-august-2025/) | startup | Quarry-sourced silicate rock crushed and spread on cropland at scale, primarily in Brazil | ~$58.2M equity raised (largest ERW equity round); Microsoft 12,000-ton deal; ~290K-ton deal volume |
| [InPlanet](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/microsoft-to-purchase-28500-tons-of-co2-removal-credits-from-brazils-inplanet/) | startup | Basalt application on tropical farmland in Brazil and Germany with MRV verified under Isometric protocol | Delivered world's first independently verified ERW credits (Dec 2024, BeZero 'A'); 28,500 t contracted to Microsoft 2026-2028 |
| [UNDO Carbon](https://un-do.com/resources/blog/undo-named-one-of-four-global-winners-in-100m-xprize-carbon-removal-competition/) | startup | Basalt and other silicate spreading across UK, Canada and India farmland at large acreage | XPRIZE $5M third-runner-up (2025); >54,000 acres enriched, ~69,000 t CO2; Microsoft 15,000-ton deal |
| [Alt Carbon](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/11/microsoft-taps-alt-carbon-in-sign-of-indias-growing-rile-in-carbon-removal/) | startup | Crushed Rajmahal-Traps basalt spread on West Bengal farmland (Darjeeling Revival Project) with smallholder network | $12M seed (Lachy Groom, 2025); Microsoft ~37,000-ton 3-yr deal June 2026; ~10,000 credits issued |

Instead of basalt, faster-weathering silicate minerals or alkaline construction wastes (olivine, wollastonite, brucite, milled returned concrete) are spread on land to accelerate CO2 uptake, trading higher reactivity against trace-metal and supply considerations.

| [Silicate](https://carbonherald.com/silicate-to-undertake-first-ever-enhanced-weathering-trial-u-s/) | startup | Milled returned (waste) concrete spread on US farmland (Illinois) as a fast-weathering carbonate-rich feedstock | XPRIZE 2024 finalist; applied 500 t to 50 ha at Schott Farms, Illinois; Northwestern MRV collaboration |
| [greenSand](https://greensand.com/en) | startup | Mines, grinds and distributes olivine sand for gardens and projects in the Netherlands | Long-running Dutch olivine commercializer; modeled 200-250k t/yr NL potential; small commercial sales |

**Mine tailings carbonation (ultramafic mining waste)** · `🔵 pilot`

Reactive magnesium-silicate tailings at nickel, diamond and platinum mines are actively churned, aerated or exposed to flue gas so they passively absorb CO2 and mineralize it, turning mine waste liabilities into on-site permanent storage.

**In-situ mineralization via dissolved CO2 injection into basalt** · `🟠 demonstration`

CO2 is dissolved in water and injected into reactive basaltic formations, where it reacts with the rock to form solid carbonate minerals within months to a couple of years, delivering verifiably permanent geologic storage.

| [IISER Bhopal / CSIR-NGRI (DeCarbFaroe)](https://www.cognitud.com/news/india-launches-first-storage-well-in-basalt-to-tackle-climate-challenge) | incumbent | Research consortium drilling India's first CO2 injection well into Deccan Traps basalt for in-situ mineralization | First Indian basalt storage well launched 2025 under international DeCarbFaroe programme |

**In-situ mineralization in peridotite/ultramafic formations** · `🔵 pilot`

CO2 (often dissolved in seawater and captured via DAC) is injected into highly reactive peridotite/ultramafic rock that naturally carbonates extremely fast, enabling permanent storage in regions like Oman and the UAE with vast ultramafic geology.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [44.01](https://esgnews.com/adnoc-and-44-01-to-scale-up-carbon-to-rock-project/) | startup | Mineralizes CO2 in Omani/UAE peridotite by dissolving captured CO2 in seawater and injecting it underground, powered by renewables | ~$37M (EUR 33.9M) Series A led by Equinor Ventures; ADNOC pilot mineralized 10 t in <100 days, scaling to >300 t; world-first commercial peridotite concession in Oman's Hajar mountains |
| [ADNOC](https://www.agbi.com/sustainability/2024/11/adnoc-and-omans-44-01-scale-up-carbon-to-rock-project/) | incumbent | National oil company co-developing and hosting peridotite carbon-to-rock scale-up in Fujairah, UAE | Completed 10-t pilot with 44.01; backing first scale-up phase as part of $15B decarbonization investment |

> **White space:** Few players because suitable obducted peridotite is geographically rare (Oman, UAE, parts of California/Cyprus) and injectivity into tight rock is hard; opening is proving reliable flow and reaction rates at scale in a small number of concession-rich geographies.

**Ex-situ accelerated carbonation reactors (acid-recycle loops, pressurized carbonation to storable or cementitious minerals)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Engineered reactors crush and react silicate rock or wastes with CO2 under pressure or via acid/base recycle loops to rapidly produce storable carbonates and cementitious or industrial co-products, decoupling carbon removal from slow field weathering.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Paebbl](https://carbonherald.com/paebbl-launches-worlds-first-continuous-co2-mineralization-demo-plant/) | startup | Continuous reactor mineralizing crushed olivine with industrial-captured CO2 into a carbonate powder usable as a construction filler | $25M (EUR 22.8M) Series A Oct 2024; world-first continuous CO2-mineralization demo plant running since Mar 2025; first commercial facility targeted 2028 |
| [Travertine Technologies](https://www.worldfertilizer.com/sulfur/10102025/travertine-starts-demonstration-plant/) | startup | Electrochemical acid-recycle platform (salt-splitting + caustic DAC + mineralization) upcycling sulfate waste into sulfuric acid, carbonate and green hydrogen | $8.5M round 2024 (Holcim MAQER, Grantham, CEV) + NYSERDA $3.2M; demonstration plant operating since Oct 2025 (with Sabin Metal) |
| [MCi Carbon](https://carbonherald.com/cop30-mci-carbon-launches-breakthrough-co2-to-material-plant-at-cop30/) | startup | Mineral carbonation reactors converting industrial CO2 plus feedstocks into building materials and refractory inputs at its 'Myrtle' demo plant | Myrtle demo plant launched at COP30 (Nov 2025); RHI Magnesita US$10M investment + first customer; AUS-Austria $12M decarbonization program recipient |
| [Exterra Carbon Solutions](https://cleanenergyventures.com/clean-energy-venture-capital/exterra-20m-series-a-to-transform-mining-waste-into-low-carbon-critical-minerals/) | startup | Reactive-Oxide-to-Carbonate reactors processing asbestos mine tailings into MgO for carbon sequestration plus nickel and silica co-products | C$20M Series A May 2025 (CEV, BDC; C$32M total); BASF OASE partnership; Frontier pre-purchase; Hub I (300,000+ t/yr) construction targeted 2027 |
| [neustark](https://www.esgtoday.com/microsoft-signs-deal-to-capture-and-store-carbon-in-recycled-concrete-with-startup-neustark/) | scaleup | Modular plants injecting biogenic CO2 into recycled demolition-concrete aggregate where it mineralizes permanently | Largest disclosed sector equity ~$69M; 14 plants operating (DE/CH) + 20 under construction; Microsoft 27,600-t 6-yr offtake; 1 Mt/yr 2030 goal |

**Microbial/biotic acceleration of soil mineral weathering** · `⚪ lab`

Microbes, fungi or isolated enzymes (e.g. carbonic anhydrase) and microbial iron-chelating siderophores are used to speed the dissolution of silicate minerals in soil, aiming to shorten enhanced-weathering carbon-capture timelines from decades to a few years.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [FabricNano](https://carbonherald.com/fabricnano-is-revolutionizing-enhanced-rock-weathering-with-enzymes/) | startup | Immobilizes carbonic-anhydrase enzyme on large-particle basalt as a protein powder to accelerate rock-weathering CO2 capture | World-first enzyme-treated ERW trial with Veolia (2024); pre-commercial |
| [Andes (Andes Bio)](https://verra.org/methodologies/methodology-for-microbial-carbon-mineralization-mcm/) | startup | Introduces soil microorganisms alongside crop seeds to expedite conversion of CO2 into soil inorganic carbon (microbial carbon mineralization) | Released first-ever MCM methodology, but Verra put the methodology on hold Dec 2024; company continues with soil-carbon products · *status unverified* |
| [Veolia](https://www.veolia.co.uk/press-releases/veolia-uses-enzymes-world-first-trial-remove-carbon-dioxide-enhanced-rock-weathering) | incumbent | Waste/water major partnering on enzyme-accelerated enhanced-rock-weathering field trials | Co-ran world-first enzyme ERW trial with FabricNano (2024) |

> **White space:** Very few credible players and no certified credits: the carbon-removal mechanism is hard to additionally attribute and measure (MRV), Verra put the microbial-mineralization methodology on hold (Dec 2024), and durability claims are unproven. Opening is rigorous field MRV that isolates the biotic acceleration signal, most likely as an add-on enzyme/inoculant layered onto an existing basalt-ERW deployment.

**Alkaline wastewater enhanced weathering (point-source mineral dissolution)** · `🔵 pilot`

Alkaline minerals are dosed into wastewater-treatment flows where engineered pH/alkalinity conditions rapidly dissolve them and convert dissolved CO2 into stable bicarbonate, co-locating measurable carbon removal with existing water infrastructure for tighter MRV.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CREW Carbon](https://www.esgtoday.com/crew-carbon-raises-25-million-for-technology-combining-wastewater-treatment-carbon-removal/) | startup | Adds alkaline minerals into wastewater-treatment systems, tuning pH/alkalinity to accelerate mineral weathering and lock CO2 as bicarbonate | $25M raise 2025; Frontier EUR 31M / 71,878-t purchase (2025-2030); $2.35M Colorado Energy Office award |

> **White space:** Emerging niche with essentially one lead player; opening is that wastewater plants offer enclosed, monitorable flows (easier MRV than open fields) and existing alkalinity-dosing operations, so incumbents in water treatment could fast-follow.

### Ocean-Based CDR

**Electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement (acid extraction from seawater)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Electrochemical cells split seawater into an alkaline stream that is returned to the ocean to absorb more atmospheric CO2 and an acidic stream managed separately, giving precise, mining-free control over how much carbon the sea draws down.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Ebb Carbon](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251210046603/en/Ebb-signs-initial-carbon-removal-offtake-agreement-with-Google-to-accelerate-innovation-for-ocean-alkalinity-enhancement) | startup | Bipolar-membrane electrochemistry bolted onto desalination/industrial seawater outfalls to make alkalinity and split off acid; pursues co-located deals with desal plants. | ~$40M raised; 350,000-tonne 10-yr offtake with Microsoft (Oct 2024); Google offtake (Dec 2025); Saudi Water Authority MoU for up to 85 Mt/yr at full deployment. |
| [Equatic (UCLA spinout)](https://www.equatic.tech/articles/equatic-secures-11-6mm-series-a-funding-to-advance-permanent-carbon-removal-and-green-hydrogen-production) | startup | Seawater electrolysis that co-produces solid carbonates plus green hydrogen, neutralizing the acid stream by mineralizing CO2; sells CDR + H2 bundles. | $11.6M Series A closed Aug 2025 (Temasek Trust C3H, Kibo); Equatic-1 demo plant in Tuas Singapore live Q1 2026 with PUB; Boeing pre-buy of 62,000 t + 2,100 t H2; ~$500/t. |
| [Captura](https://capturacorp.com/carbon-removal-firm-captura-expands-series-a-funding-to-us45-3m/) | startup | Direct Ocean Capture via bipolar-membrane electrodialysis that strips gaseous CO2 out of seawater (rather than dosing alkalinity); see direct ocean capture variation — straddles both. | $45.3M Series A (Apr 2024, Eni/Equinor/Maersk/Aramco); Kona 1,000 t/yr pilot; Equinor validated for commercial 30,000-50,000 t/yr facility Nov 2025. |
| [Vycarb](https://carbonherald.com/italian-startup-limenet-is-fighting-ocean-acidification-while-sequestering-co2/) | startup | Brooklyn-based CO2 neutralization plus in-situ carbon sensing to make fully-measured, dose-controlled alkalinity additions at the waterline. | Founded 2022; early-stage; cited among credible US OAE developers but pre-large-offtake. |
| [Capture6](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/capture6-completes-27-5-million-series-a-and-project-funding-round-to-scale-the-production-of-fresh-water-and-carbon-removal-302397891.html) | startup | Turns desalination waste brine into a solvent that mineralizes CO2 in one step while recovering >50% freshwater; electrochemically derived alkalinity loop (also in brine variation). | $27.5M Series A + project funding Mar 2025 (Hyundai ZER01NE, Energy Capital Ventures); Palmdale Water District (CA), plus WA Australia and South Korea projects. |

**Mineral ocean alkalinity enhancement (lime/olivine/carbonate dosing at outfalls and from vessels)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Finely ground alkaline minerals (magnesium hydroxide, hydrated lime, or processed limestone) are dosed into seawater at power-plant/wastewater outfalls so dissolved CO2 converts to stable bicarbonate, locking carbon away for millennia while countering ocean acidification.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Planetary Technologies](https://carboncredits.com/frontiers-31-3m-offtake-with-planetary-signals-a-new-era-for-ocean-carbon-removal/) | startup | Doses magnesium hydroxide slurry into power-plant cooling-water and wastewater outfalls (Halifax, Norfolk VA) and verifies removals; the volume leader on credits delivered. | Delivered world's first independently verified OAE credits (625.6 t) to Stripe/Shopify/British Airways Jun 2025; $31.3M Frontier offtake (Aug 2025) for 115,211 t; ~$271/t; $11.3M Series A Oct 2024. |
| [Limenet](https://carbonherald.com/italian-startup-limenet-is-fighting-ocean-acidification-while-sequestering-co2/) | startup | Calcines limestone and reacts the resulting lime + recovered CO2 with seawater in a reactor to produce pH-neutral calcium bicarbonate dosed to the sea; world's largest OAE pilot plant. | Italian plant operational since Sept 2023, ~800 t CO2/yr scaling to 2,000 t/yr (2025) and 100,000 t/yr target by 2028; raised EUR 5M Sept 2024; first blockchain OAE credits via Carbonmark. |
| [CREW Carbon (formerly CarbonRun spinoffs / Yale)](https://www.theinvadingsea.com/2026/05/12/marine-carbon-dioxide-removal-ocean-storage-climate-change-power-plants-planetary-technologies/) | startup | Adds alkalinity at municipal wastewater treatment plants to enhance carbon uptake in receiving waters; US East Coast deployments. | Early-stage; cited among credible US OAE developers (Vycarb, Vesta, CREW); pre-large-offtake. |

**River and watershed liming (river alkalinity enhancement)** · `🔵 pilot`

Crushed limestone is dosed into acidified rivers via automated dosers, simultaneously repairing acid-rain damage and boosting the river's natural ability to pull CO2 from the air before the alkalinity reaches the sea.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CarbonRun](https://frontierclimate.com/writing/carbonrun) | startup | Canadian spinout (Dalhousie) running automated limestone dosers on rivers, pioneering 'river alkalinity enhancement' as a distinct CDR pathway with a credible sub-$100/t trajectory. | $25.4M Frontier offtake (Stripe, Shopify, McKinsey, Meta, Google) to remove 55,442 t 2025-2029; generated world's first river alkalinity enhancement credits; +$1M Stripe R&D grant. |

> **White space:** Nascent and effectively single-player: river liming is cheap and ecologically familiar (long used for fish habitat), so the physics are de-risked, but measurement/verification of incremental CO2 uptake in flowing freshwater is the hard part and the regulatory/credit category is brand new. An opening exists for credible MRV-first entrants in geographies with many acidified or neutral-pH rivers (Scandinavia, Appalachia, Canada).

**Coastal enhanced weathering (olivine sand placement)** · `🔵 pilot`

Olivine sand is placed in the nearshore where wave energy grinds and dissolves it, generating bicarbonate alkalinity that captures CO2 while doubling as shoreline-erosion protection — marine enhanced rock weathering powered by free wave action.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Vesta (Project Vesta)](https://carbonherald.com/vesta-reaches-milestone-with-ocean-carbon-removal-project-in-north-carolina/) | startup | Integrates olivine 'carbon-removing sand' into coastal construction and beach-nourishment projects (Coastal Carbon Capture), harnessing wave energy for marine enhanced rock weathering. | Flagship pilot placed 7,000 cubic yards of olivine sand at Duck, North Carolina (Jul 2024); trials in Caribbean, Hawaii, India; pilot targets >=5,000 t CO2; backed by Stripe Climate, TreadRight. |

> **White space:** Thin field with one clear lead. Slow, hard-to-measure dissolution kinetics in cold/low-energy water and trace-metal (nickel/chromium) permitting concerns deter entrants, and MRV is contested. Opening: integration with publicly funded coastal-resilience/beach-nourishment budgets (which dwarf carbon revenue) could subsidize deployment and de-risk the model.

**Direct ocean capture (seawater CO2 stripping via electrodialysis/vacuum)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Rather than dosing alkalinity, these systems acidify a seawater stream (or apply vacuum) to convert dissolved bicarbonate into gaseous CO2 that bubbles out for permanent storage or reuse, then return the CO2-depleted water to re-absorb atmospheric carbon.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Captura](https://capturacorp.com/equinor-and-captura-validate-doc/) | startup | Caltech spinout using bipolar-membrane electrodialysis to split seawater and strip out pure CO2 gas; the most commercially advanced DOC player, targeting ~$100/t. | $45.3M Series A (Eni Next, Equinor, Maersk Growth, Aramco, National Grid, JAL); Port of LA (100 t/yr) + Kona Hawaii (1,000 t/yr) pilots; Equinor validated for 30,000-50,000 t/yr commercial plant (Nov 2025). |
| [SeaO2](https://www.eu-startups.com/2024/11/amsterdam-based-seao%E2%82%82-secures-over-e2-million-to-advance-its-co%E2%82%82-removal-technology/) | startup | Amsterdam-based DOC using electrochemistry plus vacuum to shift the carbonate equilibrium and extract CO2 gas from North Sea water; proposes Europe's first standalone DOC field test. | Raised >EUR 2M (Nov 2024); pilot plant in Scheveningen Harbor targeting 250 t CO2/yr launched summer 2025; field-validated with real North Sea water 2025; BlueInvest-backed. |
| [Equinor (incumbent partner)](https://capturacorp.com/equinor-and-captura-validate-doc/) | incumbent | Norwegian energy major running a joint technology-qualification program to validate and scale DOC for commercial offshore deployment, supplying engineering and offshore siting. | Completed DOC qualification with Captura Nov 2025; designing 30,000-50,000 t/yr facility with European/UK/APAC sites; also a Captura equity investor via Equinor Ventures. |

**Brine-based capture and mineralization (desalination brine alkalinity loops)** · `🔵 pilot`

Desalination reject brine is intercepted and processed electrochemically to extract alkalinity or mineralize CO2 into solid carbonates, simultaneously solving desal's hypersaline-waste problem and recovering extra freshwater plus saleable chemical co-products.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Capture6](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/capture6-completes-27-5-million-series-a-and-project-funding-round-to-scale-the-production-of-fresh-water-and-carbon-removal-302397891.html) | startup | Converts desal waste brine into a CO2-mineralizing solvent in a single step while recovering >50% of freshwater; co-locates at water utilities to share economics across water + carbon. | $27.5M Series A + project funding Mar 2025 (Tetrad, Hyundai ZER01NE, Energy Capital Ventures); Palmdale Water District (CA) eliminating ~100 acres of brine ponds; projects in WA Australia, South Korea, NZ. |
| [Ebb Carbon](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251210046603/en/Ebb-signs-initial-carbon-removal-offtake-agreement-with-Google-to-accelerate-innovation-for-ocean-alkalinity-enhancement) | startup | Intercepts desalination brine discharge and runs it through an electrochemical system to produce ocean-bound alkalinity plus chemical co-products and higher freshwater yield. | ~$40M raised; desal-integration strategy anchored by Saudi Water Authority partnership (up to 85 Mt/yr potential at full deployment). |
| [IDE Technologies](https://ide-tech.com/en/blog/from-sustainable-to-self-sustained-the-future-of-seawater-desalination-merges-sustainability-with-profitability/) | incumbent | Global desalination EPC that patented a sustainable desalination process recovering calcium and CO2 from seawater to cut external chemical purchases and enable mineralization. | Established desalination incumbent (multi-decade, global plants); 'Desalination Brine Mining' commercialization program; representative example of incumbent brine-valorization. |

**Macroalgae/sargassum cultivation and deep-ocean sinking** · `🔵 pilot`

Fast-growing seaweed (kelp or pelagic sargassum) is cultivated or collected, then sunk to the deep ocean (>1,000 m) so the fixed carbon is locked away for centuries — appealing because seaweed needs no land, fertilizer, or freshwater, though sinking permanence and MRV remain contested.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [⚠️ Running Tide](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/environment-sustainability/carbon-removal-company-running-tide-shuts-down-operations) | startup | Sank limestone-coated wood waste seeded with kelp ~200 miles off Iceland to >1,000 m, bundling biomass sinking with alkalinity; once the highest-profile seaweed-sinking venture. | Shut down June 2024 citing lack of voluntary-market demand; raised ~$50M (2017-2024); laid off remaining 32 staff (peak 120); generated controversial woodchip credits. · **☠ shut down** |
| [Seafields](https://carbonherald.com/seafields-is-gathering-funds-to-turn-coastal-seaweed-crisis-into-a-cdr-solution/) | startup | Aims to farm pelagic sargassum in stationary open-ocean aquafarms off West Africa (using artificial upwelling for nutrients) and bale/sink it for durable storage. | ~$3.9M in grants/equity/debt by Mar 2025 plus a 2025 crowdfunding round (~$226K from 140+ investors); unveiled a $1B project concept; partners with MacroCarbon; pre-commercial. |
| [Carbonwave](https://thefishsite.com/articles/sargassum-upcycler-raises-5-million-carbonwave) | startup | Upcycles Caribbean sargassum blooms into biomaterials (cosmetic emulsifier, fertilizer); a co-product-first model where carbon is secondary, hedging against thin CDR markets. | Raised $5M round bringing total to ~$12M; building large-scale emulsifier production in Puerto Rico. |
| [Kelp Blue](https://blog.sintef.com/ocean/cultivated-kelp-and-blue-carbon-hype-or-opportunity/) | startup | Cultivates giant kelp in deep offshore waters (Namibia) for biostimulants and other products while studying blue-carbon sequestration; product-led rather than pure-sinking. | Operating offshore Namibia; partnering with Wageningen University and Algaia on the SeaSolv seaweed-processing project; pre-large-offtake on carbon. |

> **White space:** High-churn, low-survivor variation. The economics are brutal: seaweed CDR credits are expensive and seaweed can't be readily monetized on existing carbon markets, and recent in-situ studies show sunk kelp degrades rapidly, undercutting permanence claims. Running Tide's collapse chilled buyers. Opening favors players that pair biomass with a saleable co-product (biomaterials, feed) so carbon is upside, not the whole business case.

**Terrestrial biomass sinking in anoxic basins** · `🔵 pilot`

Agricultural and forestry residues (woodchips, bagasse, corn stalks) that already captured CO2 on land are sunk into oxygen-free deep basins where decomposition is extremely slow, aiming to lock the carbon away for centuries to millennia.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Rewind](https://www.planetech.org/climatetechstories/rewind) | startup | Israeli venture sinking woody/agricultural residue into the anoxic Black Sea seabed (2,300 m), arguing near-zero decomposition; the largest dedicated anoxic-basin biomass player. | Tested in Sea of Galilee, Germany, and off Trabzon Turkey; permitting with Romania for 100 t at 600 m; targets 1 Mt/yr by 2030 and 50 Mt long-term; Stripe/Activate R&D grant. |
| [Carboniferous](https://theconversation.com/a-deep-ocean-climate-plan-wins-rare-epa-approval-but-is-sinking-plants-in-the-sea-the-answer-282361) | startup | Sinks sugarcane bagasse and other crop residue into the hypersaline, anoxic Orca Basin in the Gulf of Mexico (Anoxic Biological Carbon Sequestration); won rare US EPA research permit. | EPA MPRSA research permit (applied May 2025) to sink 20 sacks of sugarcane residue at 2,200 m; $250K Frontier R&D grant + $500K Stripe/Activate grant; faces Friends of the Earth opposition. |

**Microalgae cultivation with terrestrial/desert storage** · `🟠 demonstration`

High-growth microalgae are grown in open coastal ponds using seawater, then harvested, dried into hypersaline flakes, and buried on land in arid regions for ~1,000+ years — moving the storage step onshore to sidestep ocean-permanence and MRV uncertainty.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Brilliant Planet](https://carboncredits.com/brilliant-planet-carbon-capture-with-algae/) | startup | Grows engineered microalgae in open-air seawater ponds on coastal desert (Morocco), then dries and buries the biomass onshore as hypersaline flakes for ~1,000-year storage. | $12M Series A (Union Square Ventures, Toyota Ventures), >$25M total; 70,000 m2 demo site (~100 t/yr) targeted early 2025; sold 1,500 t to Block via Watershed; 270,000 t/yr commercial plant goal by 2030. |

> **White space:** Sparse, capital-intensive niche dominated by one credible scaler. It needs cheap flat coastal desert land plus seawater plus burial sites — a rare geographic combination — and competes with cheaper enhanced-weathering and DAC on cost. Opening: co-siting with desalination or solar in MENA/North Africa where all three inputs coincide, and where buried biomass MRV is simpler than ocean sinking.

**Iron and nutrient ocean fertilization** · `⚪ lab`

Adding trace iron (or other limiting nutrients) to iron-poor surface waters stimulates phytoplankton blooms that absorb CO2 and, when the plankton die, export carbon to the deep ocean as 'marine snow' — historically the most studied and most controversial marine CDR pathway.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS)](https://oceaniron.org/) | incumbent | Non-commercial international research consortium (60+ scientists, 37 institutions) designing transparent, permitted iron-fertilization field experiments to resolve efficacy and ecosystem impacts. | Planning multi-region trials (off Alaska/Canada, Pacific upwelling zones, Southern Ocean) over a 5-10 yr horizon; estimated first-of-kind LCOC ~$200/t; research stage, not selling credits. |
| [Gigablue](https://fortune.com/2025/07/03/ocean-technology-startup-200000-carbon-credits-scientists-doubts-gigablue/) | startup | Israeli startup deploying patented particles meant to grow algae then sink rapidly to the seafloor; markets it as distinct from iron dumping though scientists dispute that. | Claimed sale of 200,000 carbon credits (2025) despite little public technical data; NZ EPA found a planned 1,000 t particle deployment amounted to illegal ocean dumping; credibility widely questioned. · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Almost no commercial players because the pathway is heavily stigmatized (London Protocol restrictions, the 2012 Haida rogue-dumping episode) and ecological side-effects plus verification of permanent export remain deeply uncertain. The serious activity is research consortia, not startups; the one venture that flirted with it (Gigablue) drew accusations of de-facto fertilization. An opening exists only behind rigorous, permitted, MRV-heavy science — and only if governance frameworks legitimize it.

**Artificial upwelling/downwelling** · `🔵 pilot`

Wave- or pump-driven systems bring cold, nutrient-rich deep water to the sunlit surface (upwelling) to trigger photosynthesis and carbon export — or push surface water down (downwelling) — aiming to enhance the ocean's natural biological carbon pump.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [The Sea Upwelling Company (formerly Ocean-Based Climate Solutions)](https://news.mongabay.com/2025/06/marine-artificial-upwelling-problematic-climate-solution-slow-to-advance/) | startup | Builds wave-powered open-ocean upwelling pumps that lift nutrients to the surface to trigger photosynthesis and food-web restoration alongside CO2 removal. | Deploying east of Bermuda with Bermuda Institute of Ocean Sciences — billed as the first open-ocean upwelling CDR project worldwide; early/demonstration scale. |
| [Sea-Up](https://www.sea-up.life/) | startup | Designs, deploys, and operates wave-driven sea-upwelling pumps that deliver deep-water nutrients to the sunlit upper ocean to stimulate photosynthesis and restore sea life. | Early-stage developer building/operating pumps; pre-commercial, small-scale field activity. |
| [Seafields](https://carbonherald.com/seafields-is-gathering-funds-to-turn-coastal-seaweed-crisis-into-a-cdr-solution/) | startup | Uses artificial upwelling specifically to feed stationary sargassum aquafarms (overlaps the macroalgae variation) rather than for standalone bloom export. | ~$3.9M raised by Mar 2025 plus crowdfunding; partners with MacroCarbon on stationary aquafarms; pre-commercial. |

> **White space:** Barely past the theoretical stage with only micro-scale tests; engineering durable wave-driven pumps in the open ocean is unproven at scale and modeled CDR efficiency is low (likely capping around ~100 Mt/yr, far below gigaton hopes), so few investors commit. Opening is narrow: ecosystem-restoration/fisheries co-benefits may fund early pumps where carbon alone cannot, but the carbon thesis itself is weak.

### Point-Source Capture

**Amine solvent capture (incumbent licensors plus next-gen low-energy amines)** · `🟢 mature`

Flue gas is bubbled through liquid amine solutions that chemically bind CO2 and release it when heated, the benchmark capture route used in nearly every operating commercial CCS plant today.

**Non-amine solvents (potassium carbonate, chilled ammonia, amino acids, ionic liquids, enzyme-catalyzed)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Alternative liquid chemistries (hot potassium carbonate, ammonia, enzymes, alkali hydroxides) absorb CO2 with cheaper, non-degrading, non-toxic solvents, trading some kinetics for lower lifetime cost and cleaner emissions.

> **White space:** Ionic liquids and amino-acid salts still have no venture-scale champion - viscosity, solvent cost, and oxygen degradation have kept them in the lab - so the field is effectively three chemistries (HPC, ammonia, enzyme); an opening exists for oxygen-tolerant, dirt-cheap solvents for dirty flue gases and for a second enzymatic player beyond Saipem.

**Membrane separation (polymeric and hybrid membrane-cryogenic)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Selective polymer films let CO2 permeate faster than nitrogen or methane, separating gases with electricity alone - no steam, solvents, or chemicals - and pair naturally with cryogenic polishing for high purity.

| [Air Liquide](https://www.airliquide.com) | incumbent | Runs commercial hybrid membrane-plus-cryogenic capture (CryoCap H2) on SMR hydrogen offgas at Port-Jerome since 2015 and sells Medal CO2 membranes for gas processing. | CryoCap commercial reference >100 ktpa; global membrane franchise |
| [Honeywell UOP](https://uop.honeywell.com) | incumbent | Separex membrane systems are a decades-old workhorse for bulk CO2 removal in natural gas sweetening, with hundreds of installed units worldwide. | Mature commercial fleet in gas processing |

| [Aqualung Carbon Capture](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250423800926/en/Aqualung-Carbon-Capture-Successfully-Closes-Phase-1-2025-Financing-Round) | startup | Norwegian NTNU-heritage facilitated-transport membranes operating without feed compression, piloted on natural gas processing, lime kilns, and waste-to-energy flue gas. | Closed Phase 1 of 2025 financing with a top-3 global membrane maker, LGE, Tupras Ventures and Delek (Apr 2025) |

> **White space:** At 4-15% CO2 flue concentrations membranes need multi-stage compression, so they lose to solvents on energy at large scale - hence few players; the opening is hybrid membrane-cryogenic trains, steam-less retrofits at mid-size sites, and high-CO2 industrial streams (biogas, ethanol, gas processing) where membranes already win.

**Cryogenic capture (CO2 desublimation/frost)** · `🔵 pilot`

Flue gas is chilled until CO2 freezes out as solid frost or condenses to liquid, yielding ultra-pure, pipeline-ready CO2 using only electricity and refrigeration hardware instead of chemical solvents.

| [Chart Industries](https://www.chartindustries.com/News-And-Events/Baker-Hughes-to-Acquire-Chart-Industries) | incumbent | Owns Cryogenic Carbon Capture (CCC) desublimation technology (from SES acquisition) and the cryogenic boxes, tanks, and liquefiers used across the CO2 chain. | Being acquired by Baker Hughes for $13.6B all-cash, closing targeted mid-2026; shareholder approval secured |
| [Sustainable Energy Solutions](https://www.chartindustries.com/News-And-Events/Baker-Hughes-to-Acquire-Chart-Industries) | startup | BYU spinout that invented the CCC desublimation process demonstrating ~30% energy savings vs amines on coal/cement slipstreams; bought by Chart in December 2020. | Acquired by Chart Industries, Dec 2020 · **acquired** |
| [Carbon America](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240806990204/en/Carbon-Americas-FrostCC-Technology-Demonstrates-Ultraclean-Carbon-Capture) | startup | Vertically-integrated developer whose FrostCC freezes CO2 from flue gas (99% capture, 99.97% purity in 1,000-hour NCCC pilot) while self-developing CCS at three Colorado ethanol plants (~525 ktpa). | NCCC pilot completed 2024; first standard commercial module in fabrication |
| [REVCOO](https://revcoo.com) | startup | French startup capturing CO2 by cryogenic separation of flue gas into liquid CO2 onsite, targeting cement and lime kilns with containerized units. | Seed-stage; industrial pilot with French lime/cement partners |
| [Air Liquide](https://www.airliquide.com) | incumbent | CryoCap family applies cryogenic purification and liquefaction to high-CO2 streams (H2 PSA tail gas, oxyfuel flue), the commercial anchor of cryogenic capture today. | Commercial since 2015 at Port-Jerome |

> **White space:** Physics keeps the field thin: refrigeration energy penalties and dry-ice fouling only pencil where CO2 is concentrated or cold is cheap, so credible players cluster around ethanol/biogas and hydrogen tail gas; an opening exists in coupling capture to LNG regasification cold and in steam-less modular units for sites with no boiler.

**Oxy-fuel combustion and Allam-Fetvedt supercritical CO2 power cycles** · `🟠 demonstration`

Burning fuel in pure oxygen instead of air produces an exhaust of nearly pure CO2 (no nitrogen to separate), making capture inherent to the combustion or power cycle itself.

**Pre-combustion and inherent-capture routes (gasification, chemical looping, molten carbonate fuel cells)** · `🟡 scaling`

CO2 is separated before or during fuel conversion - from concentrated syngas in hydrogen/ammonia plants, via oxygen-carrier solids in chemical looping, or inside molten carbonate fuel cells - where high CO2 partial pressure makes capture far cheaper than from dilute flue gas.

**Calcium looping and indirect calcination for cement/lime kilns** · `🔵 pilot`

Lime-based or molten-salt sorbents absorb CO2 at kiln temperatures, or limestone is calcined in an externally heated vessel, releasing pure process CO2 - approaches purpose-built for cement and lime where two-thirds of emissions come from the rock itself.

| [Mantel Capture](https://news.mit.edu/2025/mantel-develops-new-take-carbon-capture-1119) | startup | MIT spinout using molten borate salts that capture CO2 at ~600C inside boilers and kilns while returning high-grade heat, roughly halving the energy penalty; first industrial demo at Kruger's Wayagamack pulp mill (mid-2025). | $30M raised; FEED started Dec 2025 for commercial-scale SAGD project in Alberta |
| [Heidelberg Materials](https://www.heidelbergmaterials.com/en/pr-2025-06-18) | incumbent | Industrial anchor for indirect calcination as Leilac-2 JV partner and host plant owner, alongside its portfolio of amine and oxyfuel capture builds. | Brevik CCS operating; Leilac-2 hosted at its Ennigerloh plant |

> **White space:** Kiln integration risk plus cement's decade-long capital cycles deter startups, leaving roughly three credible technology owners worldwide; the nearer opening is lime (smaller kilns, purer limestone, simpler retrofit) and electrically heated calciners that double as flexible load - a slot Calix only partially occupies.

**Modular small-emitter capture (containerized units, building exhaust, gensets)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Factory-built, skid- or container-sized capture units (typically 1-100 kt/yr) cut site engineering to weeks, opening capture to waste-to-energy plants, gas engines, buildings, and other emitters too small for bespoke megaprojects.

Hafslund Celsio (2025); first mover in serial production |

> **White space:** Below ~1 kt/yr (gensets, small boilers) there is still no credible player - parasitic load, footprint, and CO2 logistics destroy economics at that scale - so the open play is capture-as-a-service with centralized CO2 aggregation, viable mainly where the gas has onsite reuse value.

**Mobile and maritime onboard capture (ships, trucks, locomotives)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Compact capture systems ride on the vehicle itself - scrubbing CO2 from ship, truck, or locomotive exhaust and storing it onboard as liquid CO2 or solid carbonate for offload in port or at depots - decarbonizing engines that cannot easily switch fuels.

### CO2 Transport & Geologic Storage

**CO2 trunk pipelines and regional aggregation networks** · `🟡 scaling`

Large-diameter pipelines (new-build or converted natural gas lines) gather CO2 from clusters of emitters and move it in dense phase to storage hubs; pipelines are by far the cheapest way to move large CO2 volumes onshore, making them the binding constraint on most CCS buildouts — and the most politically contested piece (eminent domain, siting).

Cortez) feeding Permian EOR, the template for CO2 trunk economics. | Decades of operations moving >1 Bcf/d of CO2; positioning network for 45Q sequestration service |
| [ExxonMobil (Low Carbon Solutions)](https://corporate.exxonmobil.com/news/news-releases/2024/10102024_exxonmobil-secures-largest-carbon-offshore-storage-site-in-the-us) | incumbent | Owns the ~1,300-mile Denbury CO2 pipeline system on the Gulf Coast and is building it into an open CCS-as-a-service network for industrial emitters. | Acquired Denbury for $4.9B (Nov 2023); >5 Mtpa of third-party CO2 offtake contracts (CF Industries, Linde, Nucor) |
| [Summit Carbon Solutions](https://northdakotamonitor.com/2026/03/10/summit-permit-for-co2-storage-voided-as-second-judge-finds-north-dakota-law-unconstitutional/) | scaleup | Developing a ~2,500-mile Midwest trunk network aggregating CO2 from 50+ ethanol plants for North Dakota storage — the largest proposed CO2 pipeline in the world. | Raised >$1B (Continental Resources, TPG Rise, SK); Iowa permit 2024 but SD permit denied twice + 2025 SD eminent-domain ban; ND storage permit voided by court Mar 2026; rerouting west via Nebraska to Wyoming (May 2026) |

**CO2 shipping (liquefied CO2 carriers with port liquefaction/buffer terminals)** · `🟠 demonstration`

CO2 is liquefied and buffered at port terminals, then moved in pressurized refrigerated carriers to offshore storage hubs — giving dispersed coastal emitters access to storage without dedicated pipelines, and creating a flexible cross-border CO2 market (now recognized under the EU ETS).

**Rail, barge, and truck CO2 logistics** · `🔵 pilot`

Cryogenic tank trailers, rail tank cars, and inland-waterway barges move liquefied CO2 in small parcels — already routine in the merchant (food-grade) CO2 business and now the bridge for emitters too small or stranded to justify a pipeline, or while pipelines are stuck in permitting.

| [Air Liquide](https://www.airliquide.com) | incumbent | Runs merchant CO2 liquefaction and truck distribution networks across Europe/US and is building port-side CO2 liquefaction capacity for CCS export chains. | Multiple CO2 liquefaction units tied to North Sea CCS export projects announced 2023-2025 |

| [Chart Industries](https://www.chartindustries.com) | incumbent | Builds the hardware layer of small-parcel CO2 logistics: cryogenic storage tanks, road trailers, ISO containers and liquefaction skids. | Acquisition by Baker Hughes (~$13.6B, announced Jul 2025) pending/closing 2026, folding CO2 logistics kit into an oilfield major |
| [HGK Shipping](https://www.globalccsinstitute.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Global-CCS-Institute-Needs-Opportunities-and-Prospects-for-CO2-Shipping-in-CCS-Projects.pdf) | incumbent | Europe's largest inland-waterway operator, designing dedicated LCO2 barges to feed Rhine/ARA-region CO2 to Rotterdam/Antwerp export terminals. | Classification-approved inland LCO2 vessel designs unveiled 2023-2024 for German industrial CCS chains |

> **White space:** Few credible CCS-dedicated players because rail/truck costs ~2-4x pipeline at scale, so the mode stays niche (<100 ktpa sources); the opening is standardized LCO2 railcar fleets and transload terminals serving stranded ethanol/biogas plants in the post-Navigator Midwest, and inland-barge feeder systems into Rotterdam/Antwerp hubs — currently served only by food-grade incumbents with no pure-play startup.

**Onshore saline aquifer storage developers (Class VI projects)** · `🟡 scaling`

Developers characterize sites, obtain Class VI (or state-primacy) injection permits, and drill wells into deep saline formations — the largest and most widely distributed storage resource — selling pore space as a fee-per-tonne disposal service backed by 45Q's $85/t.

**Offshore storage hubs (subsea saline formations and depleted fields)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Hub operators combine shared transport (pipelines or ships) with subsea injection wells beneath the seabed, selling open-access storage-as-a-service to industrial clusters — avoiding onshore landowner conflict and serving Europe and Asia where onshore storage is constrained.

**Storage site characterization, modeling, and monitoring tech (seismic, fiber-optic, downhole, satellite)** · `🟡 scaling`

Seismic imaging, distributed fiber-optic sensing, downhole gauges, satellite InSAR and reservoir simulation that prove CO2 stays in the storage complex — mandatory for Class VI/EU permits and 45Q/credit MRV, and the main lever for cutting storage cost and earning public trust (the ADM leak made MMV a board-level issue).

**CO2 injection well services and specialty well engineering** · `🟡 scaling`

CO2 wells need corrosion-resistant alloys, CO2-tight cements, dedicated wellheads and subsea injection systems because wet CO2 forms carbonic acid and cold dense-phase injection thermally shocks casing — a specialty niche the oilfield service majors are productizing as Class VI drilling ramps.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |

| [Baker Hughes](https://www.bakerhughes.com/surface-pressure-control/carbon-capture-and-injection-wellhead-solutions) | incumbent | Carbon capture and injection wellhead systems, CO2 compression trains, and CCS well completions. | Dedicated CCS wellhead product line; Frontier Infrastructure partnership (2025) bundling wells + storage development |
| [Expro](https://www.expro.com) | incumbent | CCS well testing, CO2 flow metering and well-integrity services adapted from gas well testing — a key niche since CO2 metering underpins 45Q claims. | CCS contracts on UK and US storage projects 2024-2025 |
| [Vallourec](https://www.vallourec.com) | incumbent | Premium CO2-tight tubulars and casing connections qualified for dense-phase CO2 service, supplied to European CCS wells. | CCS-qualified OCTG product line with deliveries to North Sea storage projects |
| [Aker Solutions](https://www.akersolutions.com) | incumbent | EPC specialist that delivered the Northern Lights receiving terminal and offshore injection infrastructure — the reference build for CO2 injection facilities. | Northern Lights Phase 1 delivered 2024-2025; follow-on CCS EPC backlog in Norway/UK |
| [TechnipFMC](https://www.technipfmc.com) | incumbent | Integrated subsea (iEPCI) CO2 injection systems for offshore storage hubs, adapting subsea production hardware to CO2 service. | Subsea CCS awards on UK/North Sea storage developments 2024-2025 |

> **White space:** Almost no pure-play startups: oilfield incumbents already own the rigs, cements and metallurgy, and CCS well counts (~10s/year) are too small to support independents yet. Openings exist in Class VI-specialist drilling contractors, CO2-rated P&A/legacy-wellbore remediation around storage complexes (every depleted-field project must fix old wells), and independent CO2 flow metering/verification as 45Q audit scrutiny rises.

**Novel storage media (in-situ mineralization, CO2 hydrates, enhanced coal-bed storage, engineered caverns)** · `🔵 pilot`

Alternatives to sedimentary pore space: reacting CO2 into solid carbonate in basalt/peridotite (permanent within ~2 years), locking it as solid hydrate under deep-sea pressure/temperature, adsorbing it in coal seams, or engineered caverns — extending storage to geographies without sedimentary basins and offering permanence beyond conventional trapping.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Carbfix](https://www.carbfix.com/codaterminal) | scaleup | Icelandic pioneer of dissolved-CO2 injection into basalt, mineralizing >95% of injected CO2 within about two years; stores for Climeworks' Orca/Mammoth DAC plants. | Injecting since 2012; Coda Terminal cross-border shipping + mineral storage hub won a large EU Innovation Fund grant (3 Mtpa design, ~€13/t target storage cost) |
| [44.01](https://adnoc.ae/en/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/adnoc-and-4401-to-scale-up-carbon-torock-project-following-successful-pilot) | startup | Omani/UAE startup mineralizing CO2 in peridotite — the most reactive rock on Earth — via water-dissolved injection, targeting low-cost permanent removal. | $37M Series A (Jul 2024, led by Equinor Ventures); ADNOC Fujairah scale-up to 300+ tonnes after a 10-tonne pilot mineralized in under 100 days; Earthshot Prize winner |
| [Cella Mineral Storage](https://frontierclimate.com/portfolio) | startup | Developing basalt mineralization storage wells in the Kenyan Rift Valley to pair with East African DAC and geothermal energy. | Seed-stage; partnered with Octavia Carbon on Kenya's first DAC+storage pilot with early Frontier-ecosystem buyer interest |
| [CO2 Lock Corp](https://co2lock.com) | startup | FPX Nickel spinout targeting CO2 mineralization in brucite-rich serpentinite bodies in British Columbia. | Field pilot stage circa 2023-2024; little public progress confirmed since · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Outside mineralization, this is open field: CO2 hydrate storage has zero commercial players (only academic work and PFLOTRAN modeling through 2025) because formation kinetics, monitoring and deep-sea logistics are unsolved; enhanced coal-bed storage died with its 2000s pilots (swelling kills injectivity); salt caverns are unsuitable for permanent CO2 (creep/economics favor storing H2 instead). The realistic opening is geography-driven mineralization — basalt/peridotite provinces in Iceland, Oman/UAE, Kenya, India's Deccan and offshore Cascadia — co-sited with DAC, where conventional saline basins do not exist; a credible hydrate demonstration in Arctic/deepwater sediments would be genuinely novel but needs patient capital.

### CO2 Utilization: Fuels, Chemicals & Bio-products

**Thermocatalytic e-fuels (RWGS + Fischer-Tropsch SAF & e-diesel)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Green hydrogen and captured CO2 are combined via reverse water-gas shift into syngas and then Fischer-Tropsch-synthesized into drop-in synthetic aviation fuel and diesel, offering a fossil-free liquid fuel for hard-to-electrify aviation and shipping.

> **White space:** First commercial plants are opening (Twelve, Infinium) but the economics are brutal: e-SAF costs several times fossil Jet A, each plant needs EUR 1-2B, and at least 16 large-scale EU e-SAF projects were paused/cancelled and Liquid Wind went bankrupt in 2026. The opening is cheap green H2 + cheap biogenic CO2 co-location plus long-dated offtake/mandate certainty; whoever cracks bankable project finance for Nth-of-a-kind plants wins.

**CO2-to-methanol and methanol derivatives (e-methanol)** · `🟡 scaling`

Captured CO2 is hydrogenated with green hydrogen over catalysts into methanol, the most commercially mature CO2-utilization fuel/chemical, usable directly as marine fuel or as a feedstock for olefins, formaldehyde and other chemicals.

SOEC electrolysis) technology to multiple developers' plants. | Selected for Forestal del Atlántico's Triskelion e-methanol plant in Galicia, Spain (~40,000 t/yr, FID expected mid-2025, operation 2028) and other e-methanol projects. |
| [Celanese](https://bioenergyinternational.com/2025-a-watershed-year-for-renewable-and-low-carbon-methanol-projects/) | incumbent | Chemicals major operating the Fairway Methanol CCU unit (Clear Lake, TX) that captures industrial CO2 and converts it into low-carbon methanol at large scale. | Completed early 2024 at ~130,000 t/yr of low-carbon methanol from captured CO2, described as the world's largest CO2-to-methanol production site. |
| [⚠️ Liquid Wind](https://global-efuels.com/news/liquid-wind-declares-bankruptcy/) | startup | Swedish developer of standardized commercial-scale e-methanol plants (FlagshipONE, planned Örnsköldsvik) targeting marine fuel offtake. | Filed for bankruptcy May 2026; the failure cast doubt on e-methanol supply for shipping decarbonization. · **☠ shut down** |
| [Mitsui & Co.](https://www.mitsui.com/jp/en/topics/2025/1251209_14859.html) | incumbent | Trading/industrial house co-developing and offtaking commercial e-methanol (Kassø with European Energy) and investing across the e-fuels value chain. | Partner in the world's first commercial e-methanol plant (Kassø, 2025) and investor in Infinium (2025). |

**Power-to-methane (synthetic natural gas / e-methane)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Green hydrogen and CO2 are combined via catalytic or biological methanation into synthetic methane that is fully interchangeable with fossil natural gas, letting existing gas grids, appliances and LNG infrastructure run on renewable carbon.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Tokyo Gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power-to-gas) | incumbent | Japanese city-gas utility developing e-methane (synthetic methane) synthesis to decarbonize its existing gas grid, testing in Yokohama. | Plans to scale e-methane testing to a facility ~30x its pilot, using recycled water and CO2 from a nearby waste-treatment plant. |
| [Osaka Gas / Daigas Group](https://www.daigasgroup.com/en/rd/topic/1768546_56103.html) | incumbent | Develops CO2 methanation technology (incl. SOEC co-electrolysis 'methanation') to produce synthetic methane for city gas. | Running a demonstration spanning H2 2024 through FY2025 to produce synthetic methane. |
| [Uniper](https://www.uniper.energy/news/methanation-plant-in-falkenhagen-starts-operation-and-supplies-synthetic-methane--another-step-towards-a-successful-energy-transition) | incumbent | Energy company that operated the Falkenhagen power-to-gas methanation plant feeding synthetic methane into the German gas grid. | Falkenhagen methanation plant commissioned to supply synthetic methane to the grid as a demonstration of the energy transition. |
| [NaTran (formerly GRTgaz)](https://www.natrangroupe.com/en/new-gas/e-methane-production) | incumbent | French gas transmission operator running the Jupiter 1000 industrial power-to-gas demonstrator that produces e-methane at Fos-sur-Mer. | Jupiter 1000 operating since 2022 as an industrial-scale methanation/e-methane demonstrator. |
| [Electrochaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power-to-gas) | startup | Provides biological methanation using archaea microbes to convert H2 + CO2 into grid-quality biomethane (BioCat process). | Has run grid-connected biomethanation demonstration plants (Denmark, Hungary, Switzerland) and licenses its power-to-gas technology. |

> **White space:** Technically proven for years but stranded by economics: e-methane costs far more than fossil gas and loses energy versus using H2 directly, so it survives mainly where utilities need a drop-in grid gas and value molecule fungibility (notably Japanese city-gas firms). Opening is cheap surplus renewable power + concentrated CO2 (biogas upgrading) and policy that credits e-methane in gas mandates.

**Direct CO2/CO electrolysis to syngas and chemical intermediates** · `🔵 pilot`

Electrochemical cells reduce CO2 (or water + CO2) directly into carbon monoxide, syngas, ethylene, formate or other building blocks at ambient conditions, replacing fossil-derived feedstocks for the chemical industry with electricity-driven 'electro-refineries'.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Twelve](https://cleantech.com/decarbonizing-the-chemical-industry-the-role-of-co2-electrolysis/) | startup | Built a proprietary CO2 electrolyzer (membrane electrode assembly) producing CO/syngas, ethylene and downstream e-chemicals and fuels. | ~$645M raised (2024); electrolysis platform now feeding its AirPlant One SAF plant (operational June 2026). |
| [Dioxycle](https://dioxycle.com/dioxycle-raises-17m-to-turn-co%E2%82%82-emissions-into-sustainable-chemicals/) | startup | Develops modular electrolyzers that convert industrial CO2 directly into ethylene (and CO). | ~$37M total funding incl. a $17M round co-led by Lowercarbon and Breakthrough Energy Ventures Europe; lab unit converts ~10 kg CO2/day, first large industrial prototype targeted 2026. |
| [OCOchem](https://www.geekwire.com/2025/ocochem-prepares-to-flip-the-switch-on-tech-for-turning-captured-co2-into-industrial-chemicals/) | startup | Operates a Carbon Flux Electrolyzer converting CO2 + water directly into formic acid / formate (H2 and potassium formate) as a hydrogen carrier and chemical feedstock. | Commissioned the first multi-cell industrial-scale pilot in Eastern Washington (~$5M, 60 t/yr formate); ~$7.5M private + ~$8.3M grants raised. |
| [Sunfire](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acsenergylett.4c00955) | scaleup | German maker of high-temperature solid-oxide co-electrolyzers that produce syngas (CO + H2) from CO2 and steam for downstream Fischer-Tropsch fuels. | Supplies SOEC co-electrolysis to e-fuel projects (e.g. Norsk e-Fuel, Concord/Total studies); raised large rounds for electrolyzer scale-up. |
| [CERT Systems](https://greyb.com/blog/electrochemical-conversion-startups/) | startup | Canadian startup (Toronto) commercializing electrochemical CO2 conversion to ethylene and other C2+ products; grew out of the NRG COSIA Carbon XPRIZE. | Carbon XPRIZE finalist scaling a CO2-to-ethylene electrolyzer at pilot scale. |

**Solar thermochemical fuel synthesis (sun-to-liquid)** · `🟠 demonstration`

Concentrated solar heat drives high-temperature thermochemical reactions that split CO2 and water (or reform biogenic methane) into syngas, which is then converted into drop-in solar kerosene and gasoline, using sunlight rather than electrolysis as the primary energy input.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Synhelion](https://synhelion.com/solar-fuels-and-plants/solar-fuel-plants) | startup | Swiss spinout (ETH Zurich) running the full solar 'sun-to-liquid' chain: solar tower, thermochemical reactor and thermal storage producing solar syngas then kerosene/gasoline. | DAWN plant (Jülich, Germany), the world's first industrial-scale solar fuels plant, producing fuel since late 2024 near nameplate; first commercial plant planned in Spain (~1,000 t/yr). |
| [Heliogen](https://www.solarpaces.org/researchers-create-a-digital-twin-to-run-dawn-synhelions-solar-fuels-plant/) | scaleup | US concentrated-solar company developing AI-calibrated heliostat fields and high-temperature solar process heat that can drive thermochemical fuel/hydrogen production. | Publicly listed; pivoted toward solar process heat and storage; CSP-for-fuels remains pre-commercial. |

> **White space:** Essentially one credible commercial player (Synhelion) plus academic spinouts; the physics (very high-temperature receivers, reactors, thermal storage) is hard and capital-intensive, and it competes with cheaper electrolysis-based PtL. The opening is high-DNI desert sites where round-the-clock thermal storage beats electrolysis economics, and licensing the reactor/receiver IP rather than owning plants.

**Gas fermentation and microbial CO2/CO conversion (ethanol, acetate)** · `🟡 scaling`

Engineered acetogenic microbes ferment CO/CO2-rich gases (steel off-gas, syngas, or captured CO2 + H2) into ethanol, acetate and other chemicals, turning waste industrial emissions into fuels and chemical feedstocks at commercial scale.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [LanzaTech](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843724/000162828025058573/ex991_lanzajetshareholde.htm) | scaleup | Pioneer of gas fermentation, licensing its bioreactors that convert steel-mill and other waste gases (CO/CO2) into ethanol and chemicals; spun out LanzaJet for ethanol-to-SAF. | Multiple commercial plants licensed in China/India; LanzaJet Freedom Pines (GA) began commercial ethanol-to-jet production Nov 2025; won EUR 40M EU Innovation Fund grant (Nov 2025) for a Norway CCUS ethanol facility (~23.5 kt/yr). |
| [LanzaJet](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843724/000162828025058573/ex991_lanzajetshareholde.htm) | scaleup | Alcohol-to-jet company (LanzaTech spinout) turning ethanol, including CO2-derived ethanol, into ASTM-certified SAF and renewable diesel at its Freedom Pines plant. | World's first commercial-scale ethanol-to-jet plant fully operating Nov 2025 (Soperton, GA); LanzaTech holds ~36% equity. |
| [Jupeng Bio](https://renewable-carbon.eu/news/gas-fermentation-another-promising-biobased-technology/) | startup | Gas-fermentation company (formerly INEOS Bio lineage) converting syngas/CO-rich gases into bioethanol via proprietary microbes. | Holds INEOS Bio-derived gas fermentation IP; pursuing licensing and project development in Asia. · *status unverified* |
| [Synata Bio](https://renewable-carbon.eu/news/gas-fermentation-another-promising-biobased-technology/) | startup | Acquired the Coskata syngas-fermentation technology, producing ethanol and chemicals from waste-gas/biomass syngas. | Holds legacy Coskata gas-fermentation assets; limited public deployment activity. · *status unverified* |

**CO2-to-food: single-cell protein from gas fermentation** · `🔵 pilot`

Hydrogen-oxidizing or methylotrophic microbes are fed CO2 (or methane), hydrogen and minerals and grown into edible single-cell protein, decoupling protein production from agriculture and land use.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Solar Foods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_Foods) | startup | Makes Solein, a single-cell protein grown by feeding CO2 + hydrogen to a hydrogen-oxidizing microbe; operates Factory 01 in Finland. | Nasdaq First North listed; >$47M equity + EUR 10.6M EC grant; received US FDA GRAS (self-affirmed) and is approved for sale in Singapore; ESA space-food project. |
| [Air Protein](https://stellarix.com/insights/blogs/air-derived-proteins-the-next-step-in-circular-food-economy/) | startup | US startup using hydrogenotrophic fermentation to convert CO2 into protein for whole-cut meat alternatives. | Raised ~$32M to date; building pilot/'Air Protein Farm' production. |
| [Deep Branch](https://stellarix.com/insights/blogs/air-derived-proteins-the-next-step-in-circular-food-economy/) | startup | Uses gas fermentation of CO2 + H2 to make Proton, a single-cell protein aimed at animal feed (aquaculture, poultry). | EU/UK grant-backed pilot scale-up targeting feed-grade protein from industrial CO2. · *status unverified* |
| [Arkeon](https://stellarix.com/insights/blogs/air-derived-proteins-the-next-step-in-circular-food-economy/) | startup | Austrian startup using archaea to convert CO2 + H2 directly into all 20 proteinogenic amino acids for food ingredients. | Seed/Series A backed; pilot-stage gas fermentation to amino acids. · *status unverified* |

> **White space:** Promising but pre-scale: only a handful of players, high green-H2 cost, and slow novel-food regulatory approval keep volumes tiny. The opening is co-locating with cheap renewable H2/CO2 and winning GRAS/EU novel-food clearances so the protein can sell into mainstream food rather than niche supplements.

**CO2-to-food: synthesized fats and ingredients (thermochemical)** · `🔵 pilot`

Rather than fermentation, CO2 + hydrogen are chemically built into fat molecules (or other ingredients) that are molecularly identical to dairy or plant fats, producing animal- and agriculture-free butter, oils and lipids.

| Company | Type | What they do | Signal / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Savor](https://vegconomist.com/ingredients/savor-develops-dairy-plant-free-butter-from-co2-hydrogen/) | startup | Builds fat molecules chemically identical to dairy butter from CO2 and hydrogen via a thermochemical (non-fermentation) process; launched animal- and plant-free butter. | ~$33M backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures (Bill Gates); commercial butter launch March 2025. |
| [Solar Foods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_Foods) | startup | Beyond protein, explores CO2-fed microbial routes to food ingredients/fats as an extension of its gas-fermentation platform. | Core CO2-to-protein platform commercial; ingredient/fat extensions early-stage. |

> **White space:** Very thin field distinct from precision-fermentation fats: only Savor uses a genuinely CO2/thermochemical route at present, so it is early and capital-light but unproven at scale and facing food-regulatory and consumer-acceptance risk. Opening is cost parity with palm/dairy fat plus clean-label approvals; most 'animal-free fat' rivals still use sugar-fed fermentation, not CO2.

**CO2-derived polymers and polyols** · `🟡 scaling`

CO2 is copolymerized into polyols, polycarbonates and surfactant precursors, embedding 20-50% captured carbon into plastics, foams and coatings, which both lowers product carbon footprint and reduces fossil feedstock use.

|---|---|---|---|

| [Econic Technologies](https://www.econic-technologies.com/changhua-begins-commercial-production-of-co2-polyols-based-on-econics-technology/) | startup | UK catalyst licensor enabling CO2-based polyols (PCE 'Carnol' polyols) and CO2-derived surfactants for third-party producers. | Partner Changhua Chemical opened the first commercial-scale CO2 PCE polyol plant (~80,000 t in 2026, scaling toward 1M t); 2025 launched Recreaire CO2 surfactants. |

| [Econic / Changhua Chemical](https://carbonherald.com/econic-and-changhua-launch-first-commercial-co2-based-polyols-plant/) | scaleup | Taiwanese chemicals producer commercializing Carnol CO2-based PCE polyols at the world's first commercial-scale site using Econic's catalyst. | Plant producing ~80,000 t Carnol in 2026 with a stated path to >1M t, ~30% lower carbon footprint vs conventional polyols. |
| [Avantium](https://avantium.com/products-technologies/co2-based-polyesters-chemicals/) | scaleup | Dutch renewable-chemistry company developing CO2-based polyesters and chemicals (incl. electrochemical routes to glycolic acid for PLGA polymers). | Operates an FDCA/PEF flagship plant and runs CO2-to-chemicals programs (Volta technology); EU-grant supported. |

**CO2-to-solid-carbon products (carbon black, graphite, nanotubes, nanofibers)** · `🔵 pilot`

CO2 (often together with methane) is split into valuable solid carbon, such as carbon black, graphite, carbon nanotubes/nanofibers, locking carbon into durable materials for tires, batteries, composites and construction while displacing fossil-derived carbon.

| [Bergen Carbon Solutions](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/bergen-carbon-solutions-publishes-2025-annual-report) | startup | Norwegian producer making carbon nanofibers/nanotubes from CO2 using renewable electricity. | Listed on Euronext Growth Oslo; published 2025 annual report; small-scale commercial CNF output. |
| [Solid Carbon Products](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/solidcarbonproducts/__ziLFeUkcwdBcH3ghPC7Xx-N6DFotZnL8YN81Ww8_CUw) | startup | Converts CO2 into solid carbon products such as nanotubes, carbon black and nanofibers. | Raised ~$17.5M over two rounds. · *status unverified* |

Bill Gates-linked funds); pilot methane-to-solid-carbon + H2. |

> **White space:** Most credible players actually feed methane/natural gas (with CO2 as co-feed) rather than pure captured CO2, because direct CO2-to-solid-carbon is energetically expensive; volumes are small and funding rounds modest. Opening is the high-value end (battery-grade graphite, conductive CNTs) where product price tolerates the energy cost, plus tapping CO2/CH4 co-streams at industrial sites.

**CO2-to-specialty chemicals (formic acid, oxalic acid, surfactants)** · `🔵 pilot`

CO2 is converted, mostly electrochemically, into higher-value specialty chemicals such as formic/formate, oxalic acid, glycolic acid and surfactants that serve as hydrogen carriers, polymer precursors and industrial reagents.
