| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Cultivated Meat & Novel Protein Sources | Cultivated pet food | Pet food is widely seen as the most realistic near-term cultivated-meat market because owners are less squeamish, the regulatory bar is lower, and inclusion rates can start small — but it is still a handful of small, lightly funded players, and even the leader operates at tiny volumes and gross prices. Opening: B2B cultivated-meat ingredients sold into existing pet-food brands (rather than standalone products) so cultivated cells need only be a premium topper or inclusion, not the whole bag. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Cultivated Meat & Novel Protein Sources | Cultivation enabling tech (cell lines, growth media, bioreactors, scaffolds, CDMOs) | This is arguably the most defensible niche in the bucket — media and bioreactor cost are the binding constraints, so a supplier that genuinely cuts them sells to every meat company regardless of which products win. But it is exposed: demand depends on cash-strapped customers who keep failing, and global bioreactor capacity must grow ~300-500x to matter. Opening: animal-free media at commodity (not biopharma) prices, off-the-shelf food-grade bioreactors, and shared CDMO infrastructure that lets thin startups avoid capex. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Cultivated Meat & Novel Protein Sources | Insect protein & farming (black soldier fly, mealworm, cricket) | The most mature novel-protein category by tonnage, yet 2025 was a bloodbath: the global 'leader' Ÿnsect (>€600M raised) entered judicial liquidation, and ENORM, Agronutris, Aspire and Inseco all failed. Root cause is structural — insect meal costs 2-10x soy or fishmeal and high-temperature rearing is energy-intensive, so it cannot compete in commodity feed; human-food acceptance is low. The surviving model (Protix, Innovafeed, Entobel) is large single sites co-located with feedstock and aquafeed/pet-food offtake. Opening is narrow: only high-value applications (aquafeed, pet food, petfood-grade oils) where a sustainability or functional premium covers the cost gap. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Cultivated Meat & Novel Protein Sources | Microalgae & duckweed protein | Microalgae (spirulina/chlorella) is genuinely commercial with established incumbents, but mostly as supplements and specialty nutrients (DHA, astaxanthin) rather than bulk protein, where it remains too costly. Duckweed protein is earlier but advancing on a functional-ingredient angle (RuBisCO as an egg-white-like protein). Opening: functional, label-friendly protein isolates (gelling, foaming, neutral color/taste) that command an ingredient premium, rather than competing with soy/pea on commodity protein price. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Cultivated Meat & Novel Protein Sources | Gas fermentation / single-cell protein (CO2, H2, methane feedstocks) | Two very different stories. Methane-to-protein for FEED is reaching real industrial scale (Calysta's 20,000 t/yr China JV; Unibio's Saudi plant), because cheap stranded gas plus aquafeed offtake can pencil out. The CO2+H2 'protein from air' route for FOOD is in crisis: green-hydrogen cost and slow regulatory/scale timelines killed Arkeon (insolvent), NovoNutrients (asset sale), and pushed Calysta to wind down its 'from air' pilots. Opening on the food side: only where cheap renewable electricity/H2 and a final investment decision converge (Solar Foods' Factory 02), so it is a capex-and-energy game, not a science game. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Cultivated Meat & Novel Protein Sources | Molecular farming (animal proteins grown in crops) | Conceptually attractive because field-grown crops are far cheaper than steel fermenters, but the field is small and early: extraction/purification of low-titer proteins from plant biomass is unproven at scale, and GMO-crop regulation and consumer perception add friction. Most players are at pilot/stealth stage and several are pivoting feedstock crops (potato, oats, safflower) to chase titer and cost. Opening: high-value, low-volume animal proteins (chymosin/rennet, dairy caseins for cheese, egg/heme proteins) where even modest titers beat incumbent supply economics; bulk commodity protein is not viable yet. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Fertilizer & Crop Inputs | Nitrogen-fixing microbes / biological nitrogen fixation | Despite ~$1B cumulative VC, no product reliably replaces more than ~25% of nitrogen; biological N is dosage-limited by microbe colonization and oxygen sensitivity of nitrogenase, and farmers won't pay for an input they must still backstop with urea. Opening: strains that fix N even under high soil-nitrate conditions (the ammonia 'switch-off' problem) and verifiable yield-or-money-back guarantees to overcome trust gap. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Fertilizer & Crop Inputs | Green, distributed & on-farm ammonia / nitrogen production (ag-side) | Economics are brutal at small scale: distributed green ammonia only pencils where renewable power is cheap and fertilizer imports are expensive (sub-Saharan Africa, remote Midwest, Brazil). Electrochemical 'ammonia without Haber-Bosch' remains pilot-stage on energy efficiency. Opening: hybrid models that co-locate with existing ethanol/renewable plants (Tsubame-Atvos) or convert almond/biomass waste to fertilizer (Nitricity), sidestepping pure-play electrolysis cost. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Fertilizer & Crop Inputs | Microbial biostimulants, biofertilizers & mycorrhizae | Funding to the category fell ~86% from its 2023 peak; efficacy is highly variable across soils and seasons, and many products are sold on agronomic 'activation' claims that are hard to verify, eroding farmer trust. Opening: outcome-based pricing (paying growers to cut fertilizer) and pairing biostimulants with carbon-credit revenue (mycorrhizae) to monetize beyond yield. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Fertilizer & Crop Inputs | Biopesticides, biocontrol & RNAi crop protection | RNAi sprays are at most demonstration-stage commercially (one registered foliar product), constrained by RNA stability, delivery cost, and slow EPA pathways; pheromones only recently became cheap enough for row crops. Opening: low-cost biomanufacturing (Provivi-style biocatalysis) and platform RNAi to compress the cost-per-acre that has blocked broad-acre adoption. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Fertilizer & Crop Inputs | Recovered / circular nutrients (struvite, nutrient recapture) | Recovery only captures a slice of nutrients (Ostara cites ~45-50% of inflow P) and depends on host wastewater/digester economics, so it is a complement, not a replacement, for mined/synthetic supply. Pure-play bio-based fertilizer makers that tried to scale on waste upcycling (Anuvia) failed on cost. Opening: tighter integration with utilities' phosphorus-discharge compliance needs and manure/agri-waste streams where disposal cost subsidizes the fertilizer. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Food Loss & Waste | Upcycled ingredients & byproduct valorization | Consumer 'story brands' keep stalling on distribution and price premiums, and capex-heavy vertically integrated models are fragile (Do Good Foods' 2023 bankruptcy is the cautionary tale); the credible opening is B2B ingredients that win on cost and functionality at parity, co-located with large processors for free feedstock (the EverGrain model), rather than selling the upcycled story at a markup. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Food Loss & Waste | Post-harvest loss reduction & off-grid cold chain / storage | The physics is solved; the economics aren't — smallholders can't pay upfront for cold rooms, so deployment still leans on donors and DFIs and few players reach VC scale. The opening is cooling-as-a-service with embedded finance (pay-per-crate, loss-linked or carbon-linked payments) bundled with market aggregation, the model SokoFresh and ColdHubs are proving, plus first-loss capital to crowd in commercial debt. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Food Loss & Waste | Home & consumer food-waste tech (countertop digesters/composters) | Net climate benefit is contested — drying isn't composting, devices embed energy and materials, and output often still lands in the trash — while $300-1,000 price points cap the addressable market. The defensible openings are municipally subsidized diversion where curbside organics collection is impractical (the FoodCycler model) and verified end-use of output (Mill's feed pathway), not more DTC gadgets. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Food Loss & Waste | Freshness sensing, smart labels & shelf-life prediction | Adoption is throttled by static date-label regulation and by per-unit label costs that don't fit penny-margin packaged food, so most players stay pilot-scale point solutions; EU date-marking reform or retailer shrink mandates tying markdowns to measured freshness (pairing sensing with dynamic pricing engines like Wasteless) would crack the market open. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Food Loss & Waste | Insect bioconversion of food waste | The two biggest players failed on unit economics — insect meal costs 2-10x fish/soy meal and EU/US feed rules bar most true post-consumer food waste as substrate, which strands the cheapest feedstock. Openings: small modular on-farm/at-store units that skip central logistics (Better Origin, Goterra), co-location with processors for clean byproduct streams (InnovaFeed), and regulatory change permitting former-foodstuffs substrates. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains | Reforestation / afforestation tech (drone seeding, seed & nursery tech, native species) | Pure drone-seeding remains seed-efficiency- and survival-limited (DroneSeed's original credits 'failed to materialize', pushing Mast toward biomass burial), so the durable economics sit in seed/nursery supply and credit-funded full-service planting rather than the aircraft themselves. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains | Restoration project developers & forest carbon project origination (ARR) | Capital is now abundant for marquee Brazilian/US developers, but ARR still carries 30-60 year delivery risk and thin track records; the gap is bankable insurance/guarantee structures and standardized non-recourse project finance (Chestnut's JPMorgan facility is a first-of-kind) that let mid-size developers scale without dilutive equity. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains | Deforestation & conversion monitoring (incl. EUDR compliance) | Demand is almost entirely regulation-driven, so repeated EUDR timeline slippage and political 'simplification' pressure (application now phased from Dec 2025 for large operators) is the key risk; vendors that diversify into voluntary deforestation-free sourcing and Scope-3 monitoring are less exposed than pure compliance plays. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains | Supply-chain traceability & sourcing platforms | The hard, unsolved layer is reliable first-mile/plot-level origin data from millions of smallholders who lack resources to collect and own it; affordable producer-side data capture (not just importer-side dashboards) is the opening, otherwise traceability stays approximate at the farm gate. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains | Peatland & wetland conservation / restoration | Credible supply is concentrated in a handful of Indonesian mega-projects exposed to political tenure and reversal risk (Rimba Raya's license fight), while temperate-peat MRV (water-table and flux measurement) is immature; the opening is robust rewetting MRV plus aggregation of many small parcels into financeable temperate-peatland portfolios. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains | Wildfire-resilience forest management & post-fire reforestation | The category splits into detection (Pano, Overstory), fuel treatment (BurnBot, Kodama) and post-fire replanting (Mast) with little integration; the gap is a single risk-to-remediation loop and, critically, durable revenue beyond episodic state/utility grants, since most fuel-treatment economics still lean on credits or public money. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Forests & Deforestation-Free Supply Chains | REDD+ avoided-deforestation & improved forest management (IFM) developers | Although crowded and high-volume, avoided-deforestation baselines were systematically over-credited (Kariba, multiple Verra REDD+ projects), collapsing buyer trust and prices; the reset opportunity is jurisdictional REDD+ (ART/TREES) and re-issuance under Verra's consolidated allocated-baseline methodology (VM0048) with third-party ratings baked in, rather than project-by-project self-reported baselines. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Livestock & Rice Methane | Enteric feed additives — seaweed / Asparagopsis | Hyped as a gamechanger but delivery has lagged: bromoform stability/safety, seaweed cultivation cost, and unclear who pays the on-farm cost premium are slowing adoption. Opening: cheaper land-based or synthesized-bromoform formulations and bankable carbon/insetting revenue to cover the farmer cost gap. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Livestock & Rice Methane | Methane-reducing vaccines | Very few credible players because the science is hard: antibodies must survive the rumen and durably suppress methanogens without harming the animal or digestion, and no candidate has yet shown large, lasting reductions in field trials. Opening is enormous (it is the only solution that scales to pasture-based herds), so the first team to demonstrate durable 20%+ reductions in animals captures a huge market — but it is still pre-commercial (best estimates put launch at 2027-2028+). |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Livestock & Rice Methane | Livestock & herd emissions monitoring / MRV | Outside the dominant feeder-station incumbent the field is thin: continuous, low-cost per-animal measurement (especially on pasture) is physically hard, so direct in-vivo sensors and proxy/model-based MRV are still early. Opening: a cheap, durable wearable or in-rumen sensor plus a credit-grade modeling layer that works at herd scale on grazing systems. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins | Plant-based meat (ground, whole-cut, 3D-printed) | The ground/burger segment is mature but in retail decline in the US/EU as the early flexitarian wave fades; the credible opening is premium whole-cut (steak, bacon, chicken filet) at sub-conventional price and clean labels, where texture and ingredient-deck simplicity, not novelty, win shelf space. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins | Plant-based dairy, cheese & yogurt | Plant milks are mature, but plant cheese still trails dairy on melt/stretch/flavor and shelf economics; the opening is a plant casein-mimic (e.g. Bettani's Caseed) that delivers true mozzarella performance without precision fermentation's bioreactor cost. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins | Plant-based eggs & seafood | Plant seafood is the weakest segment: low repeat purchase, thin margins, and a string of closures/asset sales (New Wave). The opening is whole-muscle, nutritionally fortified analogues (omega-3, B12) for high-value species rather than crumb/surimi formats that compete on price. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins | Precision fermentation of dairy proteins (whey, casein) | Bioreactor capacity and unit cost remain the binding constraints; several leaders have paused or pivoted to contract manufacturing rather than build their own mega-plants. The opening is asset-light protein supply through CDMOs plus regulatory-cleared GRAS ingredients sold B2B to legacy dairy brands. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins | Precision fermentation of egg, heme & specialty proteins (collagen, etc.) | Heme has effectively consolidated into one player (Impossible) after Motif's collapse, leaving little competition; the opening is regulatory-cleared, GRAS-affirmed egg-white and specialty proteins sold B2B into bakery, sports nutrition and cosmetics where animal supply is volatile. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins | Animal-free fats & oils (fermented or synthetic) | Fats are a high-value, under-served leverage point: a 1% animal-fat inclusion can transform plant-meat flavor, so B2B 'designer fat' suppliers win without needing to own the finished product. The constraint is fermentation cost; carbon-to-fat thermochemistry (Savor) is a novel, capacity-light alternative still proving cost at scale. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins | B2B plant-protein ingredients, isolates & texturization tech | This is a crowded, incumbent-dominated commodity layer; differentiation is shifting to clean-label, neutral-tasting isolates and high-moisture textured proteins with chicken-like fiber, where formulation know-how rather than raw tonnage creates pricing power. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Plant-Based & Fermentation Proteins | Fermentation scale-up infrastructure & contract manufacturing (CDMOs) | Dedicated food-grade large-scale fermentation capacity is acutely scarce, only a handful of players have committed to 100,000 L+ food plants, so capital intensity and offtake risk keep entrants few. The opening is purpose-built food CDMOs (vs. repurposed pharma capacity) financed by sovereign and strategic capital with anchor offtake contracts. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Precision Ag, Robotics & Controlled-Environment Ag | Ag robotics & autonomous machinery (weeding, harvesting, tractors) | Harvest robotics specifically keeps failing (Tortuga, FarmWise; earlier Abundant and Traptic) — high capex and seasonal utilization break against thin farm margins; the opening is robotics-as-a-service priced per acre with OEM/dealer distribution, or selling autonomy software into incumbent equipment rather than building machines. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Precision Ag, Robotics & Controlled-Environment Ag | Electrified & alternative-fuel farm equipment | Few credible players because battery energy density can't yet match the duty cycle of full-size field tractors, farms lack charging infrastructure, and both dedicated US e-tractor startups are in distress despite ~$300M raised — the realistic openings are compact/orchard electric tractors, retrofit electrification, and biomethane tractors paired with on-farm digesters, mostly led by incumbents. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Precision Ag, Robotics & Controlled-Environment Ag | IoT sensors & smart irrigation / water-efficiency tech | Hardware incumbents (Netafim, Lindsay, Valmont) own distribution and pure-software irrigation startups stall at low contract values; the open ground is cheap actuation — automated valves for the majority of specialty acreage still turned by hand (Lumo's wedge) — and financed flood-to-drip conversion in emerging markets where the biggest water/methane savings sit. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Precision Ag, Robotics & Controlled-Environment Ag | Controlled-environment agriculture (vertical farms, greenhouse automation, container farms) | Physics, not execution, killed pure vertical farming — paying for photons that sunlight provides free only pencils for premium crops; 14 CEA bankruptcies in 2025 alone. The durable opening is automation, vision AI and breeding for existing sun-fed greenhouses (retrofit software/robotics) rather than new electricity-hungry farms, plus consolidation plays buying distressed assets at cents on the dollar. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Precision Ag, Robotics & Controlled-Environment Ag | Precision & land-based aquaculture (RAS, monitoring) | RAS grow-out has consumed ~$5B across 150+ projects with repeated biology (mortality, off-flavor) and capex blowouts — Atlantic Sapphire, AquaBounty and Nordic all stumbled — so the economics favor selling shovels instead: monitoring/feeding AI, modular mid-scale RAS for high-value species, and rebuilding farmer-platform trust in Southeast Asia after eFishery's fraud vacated the field. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Precision Ag, Robotics & Controlled-Environment Ag | Precision livestock monitoring & virtual fencing | Only about four credible virtual-fencing vendors exist globally; collar cost (~$300+/head plus subscription) and patchy rural connectivity limit adoption on low-margin US beef rangeland — openings are lower-cost collars for extensive beef systems, satellite-connected devices, and bundling virtual fencing with grazing-based soil-carbon and methane programs. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Regenerative Agriculture & Soil Carbon | Managed / rotational grazing & rangeland carbon | Rangeland soil-carbon credit science is contested (high spatial variability, reversal risk, slow accrual) and 2025 deal activity in the sector fell ~21%, so few developers can underwrite grazing credits buyers trust; an opening exists for cheaper, denser in-situ measurement (e.g. probe networks) paired with outcome-based contracts that pay for verified ecological improvement rather than modeled tonnes. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Regenerative Agriculture & Soil Carbon | Agroforestry, silvopasture & tree intercropping | Capital stays thin because trees impose a multi-year biological lag before any return, split incentives plague leased/rented land, and there's no standardized, high-integrity agroforestry carbon methodology, so most activity is grant- or NGO-funded rather than venture-scale; an opening exists for de-risked establishment financing bundled with guaranteed timber/nut + carbon offtake that lets landowners borrow against future tree cash flows. |
| Food, Agriculture & Land Use | Regenerative Agriculture & Soil Carbon | Perennial & cover-crop seed/genetics (e.g., perennial grains) | Perennial-grain genetics remain pre-commercial in the West: yields still lag annual crops, breeding cycles run decades, and the work sits almost entirely with nonprofit/academic breeders plus a handful of demand-pull food brands, with no venture-scale seed-genetics company productizing the trait. An opening exists for a gene-editing/genomics-driven perennial-grain breeder that closes the yield gap and pairs varieties with guaranteed offtake and seed-licensing economics, mirroring how China's public sector already commercialized perennial rice. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Hydrometallurgical lithium-ion recycling at scale (incl. LFP-specific routes) | Crowded for NMC chemistries, but LFP, graphite anode and electrolyte recovery remain thin in the West because low contained-metal value breaks the leach-and-sell-salts revenue model — openings for LFP-tolerant flowsheets (cylib, tozero, Ace Green are early) and anode/electrolyte valorization; Li-Cycle's and Northvolt's failures show capex discipline and feedstock contracts matter more than nameplate capacity. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Direct cathode recycling and upcycling to pCAM/CAM | Few players because direct recycling needs chemistry-sorted, format-consistent feedstock and OEM re-qualification of regenerated powder, while target chemistries keep churning (NMC to high-Ni to LFP) — an opening for chemistry-agnostic regeneration tied to cell-maker production scrap, where feedstock is clean and qualification loops are short. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Electrochemical and novel-solvent metal recovery | Sparse because electrochemical routes must beat brutally cheap incumbent solvent-extraction refining in China, and scale-up is capital-hungry (Aqua Metals' going-concern struggles are the cautionary tale) — the opening is modular, distributed refining that monetizes intermediates like MHP near scrap sources in tariff-protected markets, as Nth Cycle is attempting. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Second-life EV battery systems, diagnostics, and state-of-health analytics | The economics are being squeezed from both sides — new LFP cell prices keep falling while recyclers bid up end-of-life packs — so pure repurposers struggle; the durable openings are cell-level electronics and bankable SOH certification (diagnostics + warranty + insurance) that make second-life assets financeable, plus captive OEM/fleet supply deals like Waymo-B2U. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | E-waste urban mining and precious-metal recovery | Smelting capacity is ample; the real bottleneck is feedstock — only ~20% of global e-waste reaches formal recycling — so the opening is collection/reverse-logistics and automated PCB liberation rather than more refining chemistry; clean-chemistry players win where local processing avoids export of boards to distant smelters. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Magnet and rare-earth recycling | China refines ~90% of rare earths and its 2025 export controls turbo-charged demand for Western alternatives, yet collection of dispersed small magnets and the lack of Western sintering capacity keep the field thin — openings in automated magnet harvesting from motors/HDDs and OEM-backed closed loops (the VAC-Cyclic and CREEM models). |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Solar panel recycling and reuse | Volumes are still early (the big end-of-life wave hits ~2030) and recycling margins lean on tipping fees plus tariff-protected glass demand — Solarcycle's 2025 construction pause over federal tax-credit uncertainty shows policy sensitivity; the open ground is high-purity silver/solar-grade silicon recovery at cost, and reuse certification for the booming used-panel trade. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Wind blade and fiber-composite recycling | Recovered glass fiber is worth little relative to the cost of moving and cutting 70-meter blades, so cement co-processing wins on economics and high-value routes stay subscale (GFS's stockpiles are the cautionary tale) — openings in mobile/on-site blade sectioning logistics, resin-recovery chemolysis as repowering accelerates through 2030, and higher-value carbon-fiber streams. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Advanced alloy scrap sorting and metals recovery | Thin because it demands simultaneous depth in sensors, ML and physical metallurgy plus plant capex, and incumbents sell equipment rather than operate — Sortera is nearly alone as an operator; tightening scrap-export flows and aluminum tariffs create an opening for more own-and-operate alloy upgrading hubs and for copper/steel alloy-level sorting beyond aluminum. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Battery & Materials Recycling | Materials traceability and battery-passport software | Everledger's collapse showed standalone blockchain provenance doesn't monetize without a regulatory forcing function — the EU battery passport (mandatory Feb 2027) now provides one, but data onboarding from thousands of small suppliers is the unsolved pain; the opening is ERP/MES-integrated passports with automated supplier data capture rather than another ledger. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Clean Hydrogen Production | AEM electrolyzers | Only a handful of credible players because pure-water-fed AEM membranes still degrade too fast for 60,000-hour industrial duty — the physics bottleneck is hydroxide-induced polymer breakdown; whoever proves a long-life membrane (Ionomr-class chemistry plus a stack integrator) captures PEM performance at alkaline cost, with no iridium supply ceiling. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Clean Hydrogen Production | Stimulated (orange) and subsurface-biological hydrogen | Barely three credible players because the chemistry is unproven at field scale: serpentinization kinetics are slow, catalyst delivery and hydrogen recovery from the same wellbore is an unsolved engineering loop, and there is no offtake infrastructure at remote sites. ARPA-E seeded the science in 2024; the opening is for oilfield-services-grade execution (drilling, stimulation, downhole separation) married to geochemistry — a natural play for service majors or well-capitalized spinouts. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Clean Hydrogen Production | Biomass and waste-to-hydrogen (gasification and non-combustion reforming) | Waste gasification has a 20-year graveyard (capex blowouts, feedstock contamination, syngas cleanup), and the two US flagships illustrate it — SGH2 stalled post-permit and Ways2H went quiet. The economics only close when tipping fees, LCFS/45V credits and hydrogen revenue stack; the opening is modular, non-combustion designs at existing landfill/utility sites with a creditworthy waste partner (the Raven SR–Republic–Chevron template). |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Clean Hydrogen Production | Biological, photocatalytic, solar-thermochemical and metal-water hydrogen routes | Sparse because the physics is brutal: photocatalysis sits at ~1-5% solar-to-hydrogen versus ~10% needed to beat PV-plus-electrolysis, fermentation rates cap out on microbial kinetics, and solar thermochemical cycles (Sandia/DLR-class) remain lab projects with no dedicated commercial player after Heliogen's collapse. Credible openings are niche-first: distributed ag-waste hydrogen for fertilizer-dependent farms (HydGene's wedge) and aluminum-water systems for defense/remote power where logistics, not $/kg, set the bar — evidenced by the US Army's $20M program. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Lithium from clay and unconventional hard-rock processing | Capital intensity ($1-3B per project) and unproven first-of-kind flowsheets restrict this to a handful of mega-projects that only advanced once DOE loans and automaker equity de-risked them; the open lane is low-capex, low-acid chemistry (CO2 or chloride leaching) that can work at smaller deposits without a billion-dollar acid plant. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Copper extraction innovation (catalytic heap leaching, electrochemical reduction, in-situ recovery) | Chalcopyrite passivation defeated heap leaching for 40 years; catalytic leaching now has several funded players, but direct electrochemical reduction of concentrate has essentially one startup (Still Bright) — hard electrochemistry, but the prize is replacing the world's copper smelters (and their geographic concentration in China), so credible second entrants would find capital. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Cleaner nickel and cobalt supply (hydromet refining, low-carbon laterite processing, tailings handling) | Indonesian HPAL oversupply crashed nickel prices and froze nearly all western projects — BHP suspended Nickel West (2024) and BASF/Eramet scrapped their Sonic Bay HPAL JV — so few startups attack primary nickel processing; the opening is not new chemistry but verified low-carbon 'green premium' nickel qualifying for IRA/EU rules, plus carbon-mineralizing tailings that monetize CO2 storage alongside metal. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Deep-sea polymetallic nodule collection | Regulatory limbo (ISA stalemate vs. a contested new US permit path) plus ESG-driven investor flight (Loke bankrupt, Impossible Metals delayed, automakers pledging no deep-sea metals) leaves effectively one funded developer; openings are picks-and-shovels — selective harvesting robotics, environmental monitoring/baselining tech, and onshore nodule processing — rather than new license holders. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Critical-material substitution (rare-earth-free magnets, cobalt-free and PGM-thrifted materials) | Physics caps substitutes — iron nitride and ferrite give up energy product versus NdFeB, so they only address mid-performance motors — and magnet manufacturing scale-up is slow, capital-heavy, and incumbent-dominated, which is why credible players are scarce; AI-accelerated alloy discovery plus the post-2025 China export-control panic (and US price floors) create the best entry window this decade. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Battery-grade refining and midstream chemical conversion (lithium hydroxide, HPMSM, CAM precursors, reagent regeneration) | China's scale plus the 2023-25 lithium/nickel price collapse made western conversion plants uneconomic without policy support — even Albemarle walked away — so the field thinned to electrochemical flowsheets that structurally cut reagent, energy, and waste costs (Mangrove, Aepnus) and to projects wrapped in automaker/government offtakes; price floors and Section 232-style tariffs are now creating bankable demand for whoever can finance first plants. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Synthetic and bio-based graphite for battery anodes | China's Dec 2024 export controls exposed near-zero western anode capacity, yet Chinese price undercutting keeps margins brutal — Graphjet's going-concern and Syrah's force majeure are the cautionary tales; 2025 US anti-dumping duties (effective rates in the hundreds of percent) plus DOE loans finally give first-plant economics a floor, favoring whoever locks fixed-price automaker offtakes. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Tailings and mine-waste reprocessing for metals recovery | The barrier is legal, not technical: acquiring tailings means acquiring perpetual environmental liability, and feedstock chemistry varies dam to dam, which scares generalist capital; DoD/DOE rare-earth-from-waste funding and liability-transfer deal structures with majors (the Regeneration model) are the wedge, and failures here are scarce because so few have tried. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Bio-mining and phytomining | Microbial kinetics are slow and phytomining is land- and time-hungry, so economics only close on nickel-rich ultramafic soils and on waste streams where remediation budgets or CO2-removal credits stack with metal revenue; the field is thin enough that a player proving stacked-revenue unit economics at one site could own the category. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Critical Minerals Extraction & Refining | Low-impact and precision mining (surgical extraction, ore sorting, clean process chemistry) | Mining's conservatism and first-of-kind operational risk keep adoption slow even when sensors are proven, and few startups survive the 5-10 year sales cycle; the opening is outcome-priced mining-as-a-service on stranded small/high-grade deposits (Novamera's model) and reagent circularity tied to acid supply security, both of which sidestep the 'sell tech to a skeptical miner' problem. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Ammonia & Fertilizers | Gigascale green ammonia (electrolytic H2 + Haber-Bosch) | Economics, not physics: green ammonia lands at roughly 2-3x grey cost, so projects live or die on subsidized offtake and dedicated shipping. A wave of 2025-26 FID failures (BP exiting AREH, Fortescue abandoning Queensland, Murchison's shipping deal collapsing) shows the bottleneck is bankable long-term buyers and logistics, not technology. Opening: aggregated demand/offtake vehicles (H2Global-style auctions) and merchant import terminals that de-risk the buyer side. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Ammonia & Fertilizers | Electrochemical & lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction | Physics-limited: lithium-mediated and direct N2 reduction still post low Faradaic efficiency, modest rates, and energy use that trails optimized Haber-Bosch, so all credible players remain lab-to-bench. The opening is a continuous, high-current-density, stable electrolyzer (especially Li recovery/regeneration) — whoever cracks durability at industrially relevant rates first leapfrogs the field. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Ammonia & Fertilizers | Plasma nitrogen fixation & on-farm nitrate | Energy efficiency is the wall: plasma N-to-NOx still consumes far more energy per kg N than Haber-Bosch, which is why Nitricity pivoted from plasma nitrate to waste-derived organic fertilizer. Plasma survives where the value isn't bulk N but logistics/co-benefits (slurry enrichment, on-site liquid nitrate, ammonia-emission abatement); the opening is selling the avoided-transport and manure-management value, not commodity N. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Ammonia & Fertilizers | Green urea & alternative nitrogen products (green AN, CO2-to-urea) | Green urea carries a double penalty — it needs both green ammonia AND a clean CO2 source — so levelized costs (~$1000/t with DAC) sit far above grey until ~2030, leaving almost no pure-play. Green ammonium nitrate is further along because miners/explosives buyers (Orica) will pay a green premium and volumes are smaller. Opening: green AN for mining and civil works as the beachhead, with green urea waiting on cheap captured CO2 co-located with green ammonia. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Ammonia & Fertilizers | Low-carbon phosphate/potash processing & recovered-nutrient fertilizers | Recovered nutrients are real but tiny against mined phosphate/potash, and phosphogypsum valorization is mostly still research; struvite economics depend on wastewater-plant gate fees and local fertilizer offtake. Opening: regulatory tailwinds (EU nutrient-recovery mandates, P-runoff limits) plus rare-earth co-recovery from phosphogypsum could turn waste liabilities into byproduct revenue. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Chemicals & Bio/CO2-Based Materials | Chemo-enzymatic & cell-free biomanufacturing | Cell-free and chemo-enzymatic routes are hard at commodity scale because of enzyme cost, cofactor regeneration and stability; the credible opening is high-value specialty/cosmetic actives, or pairing enzymes with cheap metal catalysis as Solugen does to reach larger commodity volumes. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Chemicals & Bio/CO2-Based Materials | Electrified synthesis beyond CO2 & catalyst-discovery platforms | Electro-organic synthesis at scale and AI catalyst discovery are nascent: few standalone companies exist because incumbents capture most value through internal R&D and economics hinge on cheap clean power and proven electrode durability. The opening is modular electrochemical reactors for high-value pharma/specialty intermediates and AI catalyst-discovery offered as a service to chemical majors. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Iron, Steel & Metals | Molten oxide electrolysis (MOE) of iron ore | Effectively a one-company field: inert anodes must survive 1,600°C corrosive oxide melts and the process needs very cheap firm clean power, so nobody else has followed Boston Metal out of the lab. Openings are alternative anode materials/chemistries and Boston Metal's own playbook — monetizing high-margin ferroalloys and critical metals first, where $/tonne tolerance is far higher than commodity steel. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Iron, Steel & Metals | Low-temperature aqueous/electrochemical ironmaking (iron electrowinning) | Electrowinning's low current densities mean enormous cell area and capex per tonne — the physics that kept it out of ironmaking for a century — so only three credible players exist. The opening is pairing cells with cheap curtailed renewables (the process tolerates intermittency, unlike furnaces) and selling ultra-pure iron into premium niches like powders and electrical steel before attacking bulk steel. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Iron, Steel & Metals | Flash and single-step novel ironmaking reactors | Only ~4% of seaborne ore is DR-pellet grade, so fines-tolerant single-step reactors attack a real $50-80/t pellet-premium gap — yet the field is tiny because high-temperature fines handling and product consistency are unforgiving, and the University of Utah flash-ironmaking lineage (DOE-funded since the 2010s) still has no commercial operator. Room remains for new reactor entrants with capital-light pilots, as Hertha's $17M-to-1tpd economics demonstrated. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Iron, Steel & Metals | Hydrogen plasma, smelting reduction and electric smelting furnaces (ESF) | No startups operate here — smelting furnaces only pencil when bolted onto existing mills and need hundreds of MW of firm power, so the field is incumbent consortia. The strategic opening (and why BHP/Rio/BlueScope fund it) is unlocking mid-grade Pilbara ores for green steel; a licensable, ore-flexible ESF design would ride that need. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Iron, Steel & Metals | Alternative chemical reduction routes: sodium-cycle ironmaking and biocarbon/biochar reductants | Sodium-cycle ironmaking has exactly one player (Helios) — alkali-metal handling risk and the energy round-trip of regenerating sodium deter investors, but a proven closed loop at oven temperatures could enable small modular iron plants. Biocarbon is land-constrained (Brazil-style charcoal cannot scale to 2 Gt of global steel), so it stays a regional niche — Rio Tinto's BioIron pause underlines the engineering risk. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Iron, Steel & Metals | CCUS retrofits on BF-BOF/DRI, top-gas recycling, and steel offgas-to-products | Only one commercial-scale capture system exists on steel worldwide (Al Reyadah — and on clean DRI gas, not dirty dilute BF gas), because thin steel margins cannot absorb capture costs without strong carbon pricing. The opening is modular capture plus utilization on Asia's young blast-furnace fleet (Baowu's HyCROF shows incumbent appetite), while LanzaTech's distress is a warning that offgas-to-chemicals must work without subsidy. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Iron, Steel & Metals | Green aluminum: inert-anode smelting, low-carbon alumina refining, and low-carbon smelting/remelt | Inert anodes are a 40-year graveyard of failed attempts (anode materials corrode at ~960°C in cryolite), so only deep-pocketed incumbents and state champions play — there is essentially no startup presence in primary aluminum. The under-explored opening is low-carbon alumina refining (MVR, electric calcination), which is ~25% of aluminum's footprint and has almost no dedicated companies. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Green Iron, Steel & Metals | Other low-carbon structural metals: magnesium from brines, low-carbon titanium, green silicon/ferroalloys | China produces ~90% of world magnesium via coal-fired Pidgeon retorts, and the 2025 US Magnesium bankruptcy erased North America's only primary supply — a wide-open, DoD-subsidized lane for electrolytic brine magnesium where Magrathea is nearly alone. The same import-dependence logic (and Kroll-process energy intensity) keeps low-carbon titanium underpopulated despite IperionX's traction. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Industrial Heat & Process Electrification | Molten-salt, molten-hydroxide, and phase-change industrial heat storage | Salts and PCMs carry corrosion, freeze-protection and balance-of-plant costs that dirt-cheap brick/rock/sand systems avoid - Azelio's 2023 bankruptcy and 1414 Degrees' slow grind show the squeeze; the defensible niche is compact isothermal discharge and direct >500C steam where solid media and steam quality struggle (Hyme's hydroxide bet), plus retrofit of existing CSP salt supply chains. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Industrial Heat & Process Electrification | Electric resistance and electrode boilers for process steam | The hardware is commoditized century-old technology held by a handful of boiler makers, so differentiation has moved to economics: the open ground is grid-interactive 'boiler-as-battery' dispatch software, demand-charge management, and heat-as-a-service wrappers that make electric steam pencil against cheap gas - not new steel. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Industrial Heat & Process Electrification | Advanced electric heating: induction, infrared, microwave, plasma, e-beam, and rotodynamic heaters | Beyond mature induction/IR niches, plasma, microwave and e-beam stay confined to high-value applications because capex per MW, electrode/magnetron lifetime, and RF coupling physics limit general-purpose heat; the wedge that is working is drop-in burner-replacement retrofits inside existing furnaces (PyroGenesis' aluminum play, Coolbrook's kiln heater) rather than whole-furnace rebuilds. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Industrial Heat & Process Electrification | Electrified steam crackers, calciners, and glass/metal furnaces | Only deep-pocketed incumbent consortia can fund e-cracker and e-furnace demos, and each design is a bespoke one-off tied to a single site; the open ground is licensable modular electric furnace/calciner packages (SaltX's licensing model) and grid-integration layers that let multi-MW furnaces flex against power prices. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Industrial Heat & Process Electrification | Concentrated solar industrial heat and steam | Serial failures - GlassPoint 1.0's 2020 bankruptcy, Heliogen's ~$10M fire-sale off a ~$2B SPAC - show that land, capex and intermittency rarely beat cheap PV feeding electric heat batteries; the surviving opening is very high-DNI geographies with expensive fuel and giant steady steam loads (Saudi alumina, MENA mining/desalination), and heat-purchase-agreement business models that remove customer capex. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Industrial Heat & Process Electrification | Geothermal direct-use heat for industrial and district process loads | Physics keeps this thin: most accessible hydrothermal resources sit below ~120C while industrial steam needs >150C, and heat cannot be shipped, so projects only work where industry happens to sit on the resource and drilling capex is front-loaded; the openings are closed-loop wells serving low-temperature food/drying/aquaculture loads on sedimentary basins, co-production economics (lithium + heat, a la Vulcan), and develop-finance-operate models that take drilling risk off industrial hosts (a la Innargi). |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Industrial Heat & Process Electrification | Waste-heat recovery and upgrading: ORC, sCO2, thermoelectric and thermoacoustic conversion | Heat-exchanger reuse is mature and MW-scale ORC is crowded, but conversion below ~1 MW and all solid-state routes (thermoelectric, thermoacoustic) remain uneconomic - Alphabet Energy's shutdown closed that chapter; openings are zero-capex heat-to-power-as-a-service for mid-size factories and proving sCO2 at >10 MW where its compactness beats steam. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Industrial Heat & Process Electrification | Fuel-flexible decarbonized combustion: hydrogen-ready and biogas burners, oxyfuel | The burner market is locked up by incumbents and a burner swap is cheap insurance compared to full electrification, leaving startups little room - ClearSign's decade-long struggle as a listed microcap is the proof; the realistic openings are certified 100%-hydrogen retrofit packages, combustion sensing/AI tuning layers, and oxyfuel-plus-capture integration rather than new burner hardware. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Low-Carbon Cement & Concrete | Electrochemical and low-temperature cement/lime synthesis | Physics works but economics are brutal — these routes trade cheap coal heat for electricity plus first-of-a-kind capex against a ~$100-130/t commodity, and the May 2025 DOE rescissions removed the leading US demonstrations; the opening is small modular plants sited on cheap clean power and underwritten by green-premium offtakes (Microsoft-style EAC deals from data-center builders) rather than head-to-head commodity competition. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Low-Carbon Cement & Concrete | Biogenic and microbial cements | Biology's slow precipitation rates and nutrient/water logistics cap biocement at premium precast, masonry and defense niches rather than ready-mix; the opening is high-margin architectural products, coastal/erosion hardening, and DoD expeditionary construction where cost-per-ton matters less than logistics. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Low-Carbon Cement & Concrete | Kiln decarbonization hardware (electric kilns/calciners, solar calcination, oxyfuel, micro-modular kilns) | Kilns are 40-year assets needing 24/7 ultra-high-grade heat, so few startups attack the hardware directly and Heliogen's distressed sale shows pure-play solar heat struggled; the opening is electrified calciners that double as capture enablers by producing pure process-CO2 streams, sold through incumbent EPCs. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Low-Carbon Cement & Concrete | Recycled cement and concrete circularity | Hardened paste is only ~20-30% of demolition concrete, its reactivity is low, and virgin aggregate is nearly free, so standalone economics are weak and pure-plays are scarce; EU end-of-waste rules, rising landfill costs and the EAF steel boom create the opening — steel-cement symbiosis (the CEC model) and carbonation of recycled fines integrated into existing recycler networks. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Low-Carbon Cement & Concrete | Alternative fuels and waste co-processing in cement kilns | Mature and incumbent-locked — kilns, permits and waste streams are controlled by cement majors and waste utilities, so the startup opening is limited to fuel-prep logistics, AI sorting, and biogenic-content certification rather than the combustion step itself. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Enzymatic depolymerization of PET, nylon and polyolefins | Enzymes work well on ester/amide bonds (PET, nylon) but struggle with carbon-carbon backbones of polyolefins (PE/PP), which dominate plastic waste; an enzyme or hybrid system that economically cracks polyolefins remains the major open prize. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Microwave-assisted and room-temperature PET depolymerization | These are first-of-a-kind energy-saving angles on a crowded PET-chemolysis field; the bet is that lower energy intensity finally beats virgin PET on cost, but none has yet proven full commercial-scale economics. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | PMMA, polycarbonate and polyurethane chemolysis | Beyond PET, monomer-recovery chemistry is fragmented and mostly pre-commercial; PMMA-to-MMA is closest to viability while PU and PC chemolysis remain economics-challenged, leaving room for a player that nails feedstock logistics and monomer purity. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Pyrolysis and catalytic cracking of mixed polyolefins | Despite heavy investment, polyolefin pyrolysis is the epicenter of sector failures (Brightmark default, Freepoint shutdown, Viridor/Quantafuel exit) because virgin plastic is cheaper and feedstock prep is hard; the surviving model appears to be asset-light technology licensing plus tight integration with a downstream cracker/offtaker. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Microwave-assisted pyrolysis and depolymerization to monomers | Microwave/electrified pyrolysis promises modularity and lower carbon but is unproven at commercial scale; polystyrene-to-styrene is the most differentiated niche (clean monomer recovery) and the least crowded. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Hydrothermal and supercritical-water recycling | Only a handful of players hold viable hydrothermal IP (Licella's Cat-HTR underpins Mura; Aduro is independent); high-pressure reactor capex and scale-up risk are the barrier, so the opening is a partner with deep petrochemical engineering and offtake (as Dow is for Mura). |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Dissolution and purification recycling (without depolymerization) | Dissolution is energy-light but solvent recovery and feedstock purity drive economics; the field thinned after APK's insolvency, so a player that proves cheap, recyclable solvent loops on high-value streams (PP, multilayer flexibles) has room. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Polyolefin upcycling to higher-value products | Upcycling sidesteps the 'cheaper-than-virgin' trap by targeting premium chemicals, but each product market is small; scaling requires multiple offtakes and the field is thin, leaving room for platforms that flexibly tune output to whatever specialty market pays most. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Textile fiber-to-fiber recycling | Sorting and separating blended polycotton is the hard part, and the sector's first generation (Renewcell) went bankrupt before relaunching; survival now hinges on multi-year brand offtakes (H&M, Inditex, Nike) underwriting capex - so the opening is reliable feedstock collection/sorting infrastructure feeding these plants. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Carbon fiber and composite reclamation | Recovered fiber loses some mechanical performance and faces qualification hurdles in aerospace; supply of clean end-of-life feedstock is also lumpy, so the field is small - an opening exists for processes (like cold-plasma) that preserve fiber strength and for firms that lock up aerospace/wind scrap streams. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Wind-blade and thermoset epoxy chemolysis for industrial composites | Epoxy chemolysis for blades is still lab-to-pilot and driven mainly by an OEM consortium (Vestas/Olin/Stena) rather than independent startups; with tens of thousands of tonnes of blades reaching end-of-life yearly, there is wide-open space for a dedicated commercial-scale operator once the chemistry proves out economically. |
| Industry & Manufacturing | Plastics & Polymer Circularity | Mixed-plastic feedstock aggregation and pre-processing | Feedstock prep is the quiet linchpin of the whole bucket: pyrolysis plants failed partly for lack of clean, consistent input. Cyclyx is nearly alone at scale, so there is white space for independent aggregators that de-risk advanced recyclers by guaranteeing engineered feedstock. |
| Transport | Aviation Decarbonization | Gasification & Fischer-Tropsch SAF from waste/biomass | Two flagship failures (Fulcrum 2024, Red Rock ~2022) prove the chokepoint is feedstock prep and syngas cleanup at scale, not FT chemistry — yet waste feedstock remains the largest untapped SAF resource; the opening is for modular FT (Velocys/Ineratec-style) paired with already-proven gasifiers or with clean point-source syngas, and for developers who de-risk the front end before scaling. |
| Transport | Aviation Decarbonization | Emerging SAF routes: pyrolysis, HTL, algae, CO2-to-ethanol chains | Algae has now failed twice at corporate scale (Exxon exit 2023, Viridos Chapter 11 2025) — biology plus harvesting economics remain unsolved physics-of-cost; meanwhile wet-waste HTL has gate-fee-negative feedstock at every city wastewater plant and essentially one credible player (Firefly), so process developers that partner with water utilities face an almost empty field. |
| Transport | Aviation Decarbonization | Battery-electric fixed-wing aircraft | The 9-19 seat pure-battery commuter segment has been gutted (Eviation paused, Bye stalled) because ~250-300 Wh/kg pack-level density cannot close the payload-range business case; trainers (Pipistrel) and cargo feeders work today, and the opening reopens only when 400+ Wh/kg cells (solid-state/silicon-anode) reach aviation qualification — battery suppliers, not airframers, hold the bottleneck. |
| Transport | Aviation Decarbonization | Hybrid-electric propulsion & retrofits | Incumbent engine makers have retreated (Rolls-Royce sold off its electric-propulsion unit; Pratt & Whitney slowed its Dash 8 hybrid demo), and Heart's downsizing shows clean-sheet regional hybrids strain venture funding — certification cost versus a small regional market is the chokepoint, so retrofit STCs on existing airframes (Ampaire-style) are the nearest-term wedge and remain thinly contested. |
| Transport | Aviation Decarbonization | Hydrogen fuel-cell & H2-combustion aircraft plus airport H2 fueling | Universal Hydrogen's collapse and the Airbus ZEROe slip to the 2040s froze airline and airport H2 investment — the chicken-and-egg between aircraft and fueling infrastructure is the binding constraint, not the fuel cell; the credible near-term openings are sub-regional retrofits certified under existing rules and airport cryogenic ground equipment (Fabrum is nearly alone), which monetize before any H2 airliner exists. |
| Transport | Aviation Decarbonization | Flight-ops efficiency & contrail avoidance | Fuel-efficiency software is crowded, but contrail avoidance — arguably the cheapest large climate lever in all of aviation — has almost no independent commercial players left after SATAVIA sold to GE: there is still no regulatory or market mechanism that pays airlines for avoided contrails (EU non-CO2 MRV only began 2025), so whoever builds the verification-and-credit layer when regulation lands inherits the category. |
| Transport | Aviation Decarbonization | Ultra-efficient airframes & next-gen engines (BWB, open fan, laminar flow) | The Boeing-Airbus duopoly has no clean-sheet aircraft before ~2035 and Boeing even paused its own X-66 efficiency demonstrator, leaving a rare structural opening that JetZero is testing via military-funded demonstrators — but the $10B+ certification-and-industrialization moat means the realistic startup path is defense/cargo first, and almost no one else is attempting it. |
| Transport | Aviation Decarbonization | Low-emission airships & hybrid lighter-than-air cargo | A century of failed revivals (CargoLifter, Lockheed's exited LMH-1) plus helium cost, weather sensitivity, and unsolved variable-buoyancy ground handling keep credible players to three; the opening is narrow but real in remote logistics where the alternative is building roads or flying helicopters — and certification authorities have no modern airship rulebook, so the first type certificate effectively defines the category. |
| Transport | Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries | Challenger & regional cell manufacturers | Northvolt, Britishvolt and FREYR show that standalone Western cell startups rarely survive the capital intensity and Chinese cost curve; the openings that remain are OEM-anchored ventures with guaranteed offtake (PowerCo, Amplify) and distressed-asset plays like Lyten's Northvolt takeover. |
| Transport | Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries | Lithium-metal & anode-free cells | This space is thinning, not crowding: Northvolt shut its Cuberg li-metal unit (2024) and SES pivoted to software/drones, evidence that dendrite suppression plus manufacturable yield remains unsolved economics; the opening is defense- and aviation-funded niches where $/kWh matters less than Wh/kg, and anode-free architectures that piggyback on solid-state separators (Ion Storage, QuantumScape). |
| Transport | Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries | Silicon-anode cell makers | Full silicon-anode cells at EV scale remain open territory — current players profitably serve drones/defense/consumer niches while EV silicon arrives mainly as anode-material blends from suppliers (Sila, Group14, in the Components bucket); whoever cracks automotive-grade cycle life and GWh cost first inherits a large premium-EV and eVTOL market. |
| Transport | Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries | Lithium-sulfur cells | Barely a handful of credible players because polysulfide shuttle and lithium-metal anodes compound two unsolved problems; OXIS's collapse and Lyten's pivot toward conventional li-ion (via Northvolt assets) show the funding gap — the opening is weight-critical aviation, drone and defense markets that tolerate 200-500 cycle lives while cycle life improves. |
| Transport | Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries | Sodium-ion for mobility | Outside China the field is nearly empty — Natron's liquidation and Faradion's quiet absorption into Reliance show sodium-ion's cost advantage only materializes at giga-scale when lithium prices are high; the opening is Western low-cost regional EVs, two/three-wheelers and cold-climate fleets if anyone can finance a plant before CATL's exports set the price floor. |
| Transport | Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries | LFP/LMFP & manganese-rich cell innovation | Chinese incumbents own LFP innovation end-to-end; the Western gap is stark — ONE's retreat from automotive leaves GM/LG's 2028 LMR program as the main non-Chinese bet, so an opening exists for US/EU LFP-LMFP cell capacity insulated by tariffs and defense/rail demand rather than head-on EV price competition. |
| Transport | Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries | Extreme-fast-charge & niobium/LTO cells | Standalone XFC startups are being squeezed from above — CATL's 4C-6C Shenxing and BYD's 10C flash-charge LFP now ship at giga-scale, which is exactly why StoreDot is on the brink; the surviving opening is high-cycle-count niche duty cycles (robotics, mining, ports, charging buffers) where niobium/LTO chemistry's 10x cycle life justifies its $/kWh premium, as Nyobolt and Echion are proving. |
| Transport | Battery Cells & Next-Gen Chemistries | High-power specialty cells for e-aviation & performance | Cuberg's shutdown and the insolvency of anchor customers like Lilium left e-aviation cell supply concentrated in Molicel; aerospace certification costs and tiny volumes deter giga-scale incumbents, so the opening is defense- and certification-funded specialty lines (the Amprius/NanoGraf playbook) selling Wh/kg and C-rate at 5-10x automotive cell prices. |
| Transport | Battery Materials, Components, Powertrain & Recycling | Electrolytes, separators & inactive cell components | Asian incumbents control ~90% of separator and electrolyte capacity at brutal commodity cost points, so almost no startups attack the category head-on; the opening is policy-driven localization (ENTEK is the lone US-owned separator maker) and step-change chemistries like liquefied-gas or solid electrolytes rather than cost competition. |
| Transport | Battery Materials, Components, Powertrain & Recycling | Packs, modules, enclosures & thermal management (cell-to-pack, immersion cooling) | Cold plates are good enough for mainstream passenger EVs, so immersion cooling has few players despite better physics; the opening is fast-charge heavy-duty trucks, defense vehicles and AI data-center backup units where extreme duty cycles justify the fluid's cost and weight — exactly where XING and Carrar are pivoting. |
| Transport | Battery Materials, Components, Powertrain & Recycling | Battery manufacturing equipment & dry-electrode processing | Manz's insolvency shows Western toolmakers cannot beat Wuxi Lead and peers on cost or speed for conventional wet lines; the credible wedge is dry-electrode processing, which resets the capex stack (no NMP solvent ovens or recovery) and is still young enough that no equipment incumbent owns the standard. |
| Transport | Battery Materials, Components, Powertrain & Recycling | Direct & cathode-to-cathode recycling | Direct recycling stays thin because it needs clean, single-chemistry feedstock and the regenerated cathode must still match market demand — recovered NMC risks obsolescence as the fleet shifts to LFP. The opening is LFP and manufacturing scrap: metal values there are too low for hydromet to pencil, so structure-preserving regeneration is the only route that creates value, which is why PNE's LFP-capable SC plant matters. |
| Transport | Commercial, Heavy-Duty & Off-Road EVs | Agricultural tractors & farm equipment | Field agriculture is brutally hard for batteries (multi-day harvest peaks at 200+ hp, remote fields, thin dealer/service networks), and the VC route just failed publicly — Monarch and Solectrac both collapsed despite ~$300M combined raised — leaving incumbents to stage 75-130hp launches. The opening is depot-based specialty fleets (orchard, vineyard, dairy, municipal) with swappable packs, autonomy-bundled TCO, and low-cost compacts for India/Africa rather than head-on row-crop competition. |
| Transport | Commercial, Heavy-Duty & Off-Road EVs | Truck & bus repower/retrofit conversions | The graveyard here (pepper, Lightning eMotors, Lunaz, SEA, e-troFit) shows the economics: one-off engineering and certification on aging chassis can't beat falling new-BEV prices in rich markets. The credible openings are standardized kits for captive high-utilization fleets whose chassis outlive powertrains (refuse, terminal tractors, transit buses), retrofit-friendly regulatory regimes (France's décret rétrofit, India), and battery-swap conversions like Janus where charging infrastructure is the binding constraint. |
| Transport | Commercial, Heavy-Duty & Off-Road EVs | Electrified trailers & range-extending add-ons | Very few credible players because powered trailers sit in a regulatory grey zone (weight allowances, braking rules) and the industry splits incentives — tractor owners buy fuel while trailer owners buy trailers. An opening exists for per-mile leased range-extension that leaves the tractor and its warranty untouched, bridging fleets to electrification years before Class 8 BEVs and megawatt charging are ubiquitous. |
| Transport | Commercial, Heavy-Duty & Off-Road EVs | Battery-swap heavy trucks & swap ecosystems | Outside China this approach is nearly empty (Australia's Janus Electric is the lone notable player) because swap needs pack standardization across OEMs — a chicken-and-egg no western truck maker will start. The opening is corridor consortia (drayage lanes, mining/port shuttles) adopting a standard pack with battery-as-a-service financing, potentially importing CATL's proven 75# model. |
| Transport | EV Charging & Grid Integration | Megawatt charging systems (MCS) for heavy trucks | Hardware now exists, but multi-megawatt grid interconnections take 3-7 years in the US/EU — the opening is in battery-buffered or flexible-interconnect MCS hubs and in financing structures that de-risk utilization before electric long-haul truck volumes arrive. |
| Transport | EV Charging & Grid Integration | Battery swapping (cars and 2/3-wheelers) | Passenger-car swapping only works where one player controls pack standardization at scale — China's CATL/NIO advantage; the Western opening is not consumer cars (Ample's failure confirms it) but standardized commercial fleets and 2/3-wheeler markets in emerging economies. |
| Transport | EV Charging & Grid Integration | Wireless/inductive charging & electric road systems | Physics and cost keep this thin: inductive transfer adds $/kW and efficiency loss versus a cable, and no OEM factory-fits at volume; the credible opening is hands-free static charging for autonomous and transit fleets where eliminating charging labor justifies the premium — not consumer cars or long highway segments (Sweden postponed its permanent e-road). |
| Transport | EV Charging & Grid Integration | Battery-buffered, off-grid, solar-canopy & mobile chargers | Demand charges and multi-year interconnection queues create the niche, but hardware capex plus battery degradation crushed FreeWire even with $200M+ raised — the viable models pair the battery with a second revenue stack (ADS-TEC's ancillary services, Jolt's ad financing) rather than selling boxes alone. |
| Transport | EV Charging & Grid Integration | Curbside & pole-mounted urban charging | Outside the UK this is wide open: US curbside barely exists because utility make-ready costs and curb permitting kill L2 economics — models that bypass interconnection via building or streetlight power (itselectric, Voltpost) are the wedge, and no one yet owns the US city-franchise playbook. |
| Transport | EV Charging & Grid Integration | Robotic & automated charging | Almost nobody is at commercial stage here — Rocsys is nearly alone — yet the demand driver is compounding: robotaxi fleets (Waymo et al.) still charge with human labor, and autonomous trucking depots will need hands-free megawatt charging; a focused player that standardizes robot-ready connectors with OEMs could own the category. |
| Transport | Electric Two/Three-Wheelers & Micromobility | Electric motorcycles (on-road and off-road) | Player count is high but financial credibility is thin: Western consumer demand never materialized at premium prices (Energica, Cake, Fuell, Sondors all failed 2023-25) because range/price economics at highway speed favor ICE; the proven openings are profitable performance niches with vertical integration (Stark model) and low-cost commuter bikes in motorcycle-first markets (India, SE Asia, LatAm). |
| Transport | Electric Two/Three-Wheelers & Micromobility | Cargo e-bikes & electric delivery trikes/quads | The van-replacement e-quad niche remains thin: hardware is capex-heavy, fleet procurement cycles are slow, and quality failures (Babboe) show the durability bar; the opening is fleet-grade serviceable vehicles bundled with financing/maintenance (the Zoomo-style as-a-service model) rather than one-off hardware sales. |
| Transport | Electric Two/Three-Wheelers & Micromobility | Two-wheeler electric conversion & retrofit kits | Genuinely sparse: per-model homologation (RTO/ARAI type approval) is slow and expensive, kit-plus-battery cost approaches a cheap used EV, and liability/battery certification scares installers — so only a handful of credible players exist; the opening is B2B fleet retrofits (delivery fleets, boda-boda cooperatives, municipal fleets) where one approved model covers thousands of identical vehicles and TCO math is decisive. |
| Transport | Electric Two/Three-Wheelers & Micromobility | Emerging-market electric moto-taxis (Africa & SE Asia commercial two-wheelers) | Few players have scaled beyond one country because the model is triple-capital-intensive (vehicles + energy infrastructure + rider credit) in weak-currency markets; the opening is OEM partnerships with dedicated financiers/energy providers and pan-African battery standardization rather than fully vertically integrated plays. |
| Transport | Electric Two/Three-Wheelers & Micromobility | Standing e-kickscooters & personal light EV OEMs | Consumer kickscooter manufacturing is locked up by Chinese electronics-scale incumbents competing on price, leaving little room for hardware startups; remaining openings are regulatory-compliance niches (UL 2272-certified batteries, EU type approval) and durable fleet-spec hardware with repairability guarantees. |
| Transport | Maritime Decarbonization | Green methanol vessels, engines & fuel supply | Ships have outrun fuel: one commercial e-methanol plant (42 kt/yr) versus megaton-scale fleet demand, and developers die without bankable offtakes (Liquid Wind bankruptcy, Ørsted's FlagshipONE cancellation). The opening is for producers who can lock long-term offtakes and shrink the green premium, plus FuelEU-compliance structures that monetize it. |
| Transport | Maritime Decarbonization | Ammonia propulsion & ammonia-to-power | Engine supply is consolidating with the three incumbent engine houses; the open gaps are port-side bunkering networks, crew safety/training systems and N2O abatement — whoever industrializes safe ammonia transfer owns the bottleneck. |
| Transport | Maritime Decarbonization | Hydrogen & fuel-cell vessels | Two flagship failures (Future Proof Shipping, TECO 2030) plus Norled's heavy losses show green-hydrogen cost and missing infrastructure kill the economics wherever batteries suffice; the defensible niche is routes too long for batteries with captive or subsidized hydrogen supply — or onboard methanol reforming that dodges hydrogen logistics entirely. |
| Transport | Maritime Decarbonization | Primary-sail cargo shipping lines | Small capacity and ~11-knot speeds cap the addressable market to premium, time-tolerant cargo; FuelEU/CSRD-driven demand for verified low-CO2 freight is the opening, but nobody has cracked container-scale sail economics yet — Veer and France's Windcoop are first attempts. |
| Transport | Maritime Decarbonization | Onboard carbon capture | Capture is proven but the loop is open: there is no standardized port CO2 offload/storage chain and IMO/EU accounting for captured CO2 is still pending, so value hinges on regulation — first movers locking port logistics and cement/CCU offtake (the Seabound-Heidelberg model) own the gap. |
| Transport | Maritime Decarbonization | Nuclear maritime propulsion | Physics is proven by navies, but civilian port access, insurance/liability frameworks and IMO rules don't yet exist, so credible players are few and capital-heavy; the near-term opening is floating nuclear power for ports and islands (regulated like land assets) before propulsion, plus licensing/class-rule tooling. |
| Transport | Passenger & Light-Duty EVs | Solar-integrated EVs | Both flagship solar-car startups failed (Lightyear bankrupt, Sono's Sion canceled) and Aptera is still pre-revenue after years — physics caps on-vehicle PV near 1 kW, so a standalone 'solar carmaker' only pencils with extreme lightweighting. The credible opening is solar as a feature: OEM roof options, retrofit kits for fleets, and sun-rich-market microcars/LSVs where 20-40 km/day of free range covers most trips. |
| Transport | Passenger & Light-Duty EVs | Microcars, quadricycles & low-speed EVs | Crowded in Europe and China but nearly empty in the US, where no federal quadricycle class exists and the 25 mph low-speed-vehicle rule strands products between golf carts and cars — a regulatory void that helped kill Arcimoto and ElectraMeccanica. An opening exists for whoever cracks US homologation (a 35-45 mph 'medium-speed' class or state-level carve-outs) with a sub-$12k product like Eli's. |
| Transport | Passenger & Light-Duty EVs | EV skateboard platforms & contract manufacturers | Pure skateboard startups keep dying (Canoo Ch7 2025, Arrival 2024) and contract plants keep losing anchors (Magna-Fisker, VDL-MINI) because credible volume customers barely exist — incumbents own factories and startups die before reaching volume. The model that works is Foxconn's: regional assembly inside tariff walls plus white-label platforms for legacy brands that lack EV R&D (Mitsubishi-Foxtron), and Chinese platform licensing (Geely SEA, CATL) is the likely consolidation path. |
| Transport | Passenger & Light-Duty EVs | ICE-to-EV passenger conversions & classic-car retrofits | Mass-market retrofit has repeatedly failed (Transition-One liquidated despite French subsidies and a regulation written around it) because kit-plus-labor cost rivals a used BEV; only luxury restomods clear margins. The opening is standardized, type-approved kits for a handful of iconic high-volume models installed through OEM dealer networks (the Renault/R-FIT pattern), or subsidy-backed fleet retrofits where duty cycles are predictable. |
| Transport | Rail, Hydrogen for Transport & E-fuels | Autonomous battery railcars & rail freight innovation | Effectively a two-startup US field: FRA certification, railroad operating-rule conservatism, and Class I labor agreements make entry brutal, while the prize (the ~70% of US freight ton-miles on trucks) is huge. Openings exist for European/Asian equivalents on lighter-regulated networks and for retrofit propulsion/automation kits for existing railcar fleets. |
| Transport | Rail, Hydrogen for Transport & E-fuels | Locomotive repowering & hybrid retrofits | Thin field for zero-emission repowers: railroads sweat 30+ year assets and CARB's in-use locomotive rule was withdrawn from EPA waiver consideration in early 2025, gutting the regulatory driver. An opening exists for financing-wrapped repower-as-a-service priced against fuel savings rather than emissions mandates. |
| Transport | Rail, Hydrogen for Transport & E-fuels | E-fuels & low-carbon road fuels (e-gasoline, e-diesel, rDME) | Few players because green-H2 + DAC economics put e-gasoline at multiples of fossil prices, and most e-fuel capital is being diverted to aviation where SAF mandates guarantee demand. The EU's 2035 e-fuels carve-out for combustion cars creates a future certified e-gasoline supply-chain niche (certification, blending, distribution) that is nearly empty today. |
| Transport | Rail, Hydrogen for Transport & E-fuels | Freight logistics optimization & intermodal shift software | General freight software is crowded, but software purpose-built for road-to-rail modal shift (carbon-priced routing integrated with rail/intermodal capacity APIs) is nearly empty — most TMS tools optimize within trucking. A credible intermodal-shift engine pairing Class I capacity with shipper Scope 3 targets is an open seam. |
| Transport | Rail, Hydrogen for Transport & E-fuels | Hydrogen passenger cars (light-duty FCEVs) | Retail FCEV cars are in retreat — Shell closed all California light-duty stations in 2024 and Mirai resale values cratered — because chicken-and-egg station economics fail at low vehicle density. The viable opening is captive fleets with depot fueling (taxis, government fleets) as HysetCo demonstrates, not retail. |


---

## The graveyard — what failure teaches about white space

| Company | Sector | What they attempted | What happened (year) | Signal for the field |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Northvolt | Batteries | Europe's homegrown gigafactory champion to rival CATL/BYD, vertically integrated from cathode to recycling | Filed for bankruptcy in Sweden (Mar 2025) with ~$5.8B debt after raising ~$12B; had lost a €2B BMW order over delivery delays [1][2] | Scale-up execution, not cell chemistry, is the kill zone; parallel megaprojects on venture/debt capital outran operating capability |
| Moxion Power | Batteries | Mobile battery units to replace diesel generators on film sets, festivals, construction | Abrupt shutdown (Jul 2024) after raising $110M+; scaled manufacturing before product validation [3] | Hardware that skips iteration to chase manufacturing scale dies of its own capex; "demand anticipated, not validated" |
| Ambri | Batteries | Liquid-metal long-duration storage (MIT spinout, Gates-backed) | Chapter 11 (May 2024); assets sold to a lender consortium incl. Gates Frontier and Paulson (Jul 2024) [4] | Novel chemistries can't outrun lithium-ion's cost curve; survival came only via creditor takeover, not markets |
| Natron Energy | Batteries | Sodium-ion cells for data centers and industrial power | Ceased operations (Sep 2025), closing its $40M Michigan plant and shelving gigafactory plans [5] | Alt-chemistry needs committed anchor offtake before factory buildout; policy/tariff whiplash removed the bridge |
| Powin | Grid storage | Third-largest US battery energy storage (BESS) integrator | Chapter 11 (Jun 2025), eight months after a $200M KKR credit facility [6] | Integrators are margin-squeezed between Chinese cell makers and EPCs; tariff uncertainty broke the model |
| Lordstown Motors | EVs | Electric pickup (Endurance) built in an ex-GM plant | Chapter 11 (Jun 2023) after Hindenburg exposed faked reservations and the Foxconn deal collapsed [7] | SPAC-era "reservations" were demand fiction; shell survived only as a litigation vehicle |
| Proterra | EVs | Electric transit buses plus battery systems and charging | Chapter 11 (Aug 2023) after aggressive three-business expansion drained capital [7] | Running multiple capital-hungry lines on municipal sales cycles is incompatible with venture timelines |
